The two-time Pro Bowler didn't have a monster game, finishing with less than 100 scrimmage yards for the first time this season, but he was still highly impactful by picking up several key first downs to extend drives. He led the team with nine targets and eight receptions for 53 receiving yards and picked up 13 rushing yards and a first down on the first play from scrimmage of the game. He would've finished as the team's leading receiver on a play where he picked up 26 yards, but since he drew a defensive pass interference three yards deeper downfield, the team accepted the penalty.

Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle was in his bag all night and turned up even more for the game-tying and winning drives with how he sequenced and dialed up plays to exploit matchups and put his players in a position to succeed. Minter called some timely blitzes and pressures to come up with key stops in the fourth quarter, including holding the Falcons to a short field goal after an eight-plus-minute drive.

title: 4 Major Issues Ravens Must Still Fix On Defense
full_text:
The Ravens may have forged a new identity under rookie head coach Jesse Minter Sunday night, finding a way to comeback and beat the Falcons in Atlanta in primetime despite lacking their highest-paid player on offense and defense.
Baltimore was without two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson and without $30M/year pass rusher Trey Hendrickson and trailed throughout the game, and still came away with the win, 30-23, in overtime . Minter funneled more manpower to the line of scrimmage than ever before this young season to try to tamp down elite running back Bijan Robinson, and it worked expertly. And, yes, while doing that will leave you a little exposed on the back end , this secondary is also supposed to be the strength of the team, and a young quarterback just back from his third ACL surgery shouldn’t be able to repeatedly convert on third-and-10 or longer as Michael Penix did throughout the course of this game (Atlanta was 9/17 on third down in regulation despite being in long situations).
Tavius Robinson’s late sack, which effectively knocked Penix from the game and forced washed back-up Tua Tagovailoa into the contest, proved huge, but if this defense is going to be Super Bowl quality there remain significant areas that must be improved and cleaned up.
“Obviously, you kind of know when you play a lot for the run you may give up a few things in the passing game,” Minter said late Sunday night. “But again, I thought we could have played some third downs better, from both schematical (approach) and just playing the plays. But man, I am just really, really proud of our guys.”
Hybrid defensive back Kyle Hamilton, who put the game away by picking off Tagovailoa in overtime, kept it real as always: “I don't think we played well, for real. The third-down stuff was crazy … Third down, we have to do better. But it obviously feels a lot better fixing those mistakes with a win. I might be a little too cynical or critical, but we can be better."
Here’s what needs to improve:
Minter will always want to flood the field with defensive backs, and he played a 3-4 base throughout the first half t o mitigate Bijan Robinson and it worked expertly (17 carries and just three for five yards or more), but Penix converted seven first downs passing against Minter’s dime defense on 14 dropbacks and did so from these distances: 3 yards, 6, 10, 10, 10, 11 and 15.
Penix had a 101.7 rating throwing against dime Sunday, Baltimore has faced 95 dropbacks vs it (21 is NFL average; Rams are second with 71 and they play Monday). The Ravens rank 20th in opposing QB rating vs dime (89.5) and 20th in completion percentage (66%) and 21st in yards/attempt (8.3).
Baltimore’s dime coverage is even worse on third-and-fourth down, allowing a 94.4 rating and 9.5 yards/attempt. Minter needs to find the right mix back there or be willing to use more nickel. Overall the Ravens are just 14th in the NFL in opposer passer rating; outside of Dak Prescott have not faced a top QB.
The hope is that Hendrickson’s return will mean everything. That’s always been the hope.
After his finger surgery, the Ravens need him to look like his Week 1 version. The Ravens are just 20th in pressure rare through five gams and Minter continued to have to blitz on one of every three plays, which is not his comfort level or preference. His blitz rate was around 22% with the Chargers.
Ravens edge players had just two total QB hits in Sunday night’s game despite Penix not really trusting his repaired knee to take off and run nearly as much he did coming out of college as a first-round pick. Merely re-inserting Hendrickson needs to be a cheat code for Minter; if this becomes a scheme-reliant thing we’ve got problems. Former All-Pro defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike is back to being a menace on the inside following neck surgery and getting him and Hendrickson going at the same time will be vital.
Top receivers continue to take games over against this secondary. I strongly believe lack of pass rush in critical moments has a lot to do with that, but they also are going to need top corners Nate Wiggins (who has problems with Drake London Sunday) and Marlon Humphrey to make plays on the ball.
The Ravens have been thrown on 171 times – ninth-most in the NFL – and their cornerbacks do not have a single interception. They don’t have many pass breakups. They don’t get their hands on the ball much at all and haven’t for years.
Here’s what No. 1 receivers have done against them since Week 2 (Carnell Tate of the Titans hasn’t looked like a top wideout against any other team, but he’s as good as it gets for that suspect operation):
London (ATL): 7/11, 118 yards, 7 1st D
Tate (TEN): 9/12, 145 yds, 6 1st D
CeeDee Lamb (DAL): 7/8, 112 yds 5 1st D
George Pickens (DAL): 7/11, 82 yds, 4 1st D
Chris Olave (NO): 8/10, 86 yds, TD, 6 1st D
Minter has a lot more on his plate than ever before having to run a sideline and manage a game, which is brand new to him, and also call the defense. His early-game plans have generally been stout but as games go along this defense tends to wilt, the fourth-quarter collapse gene is still in there and the second half in general has not been good enough.
The Ravens are 26th in the NFL allowing 2.64 points/drive in the second half. QBs – again, not very good ones by and large – complete 69% of their passes (21st) with a 102.7 rating (21st). Baltimore allows 5.6 yards/play (20th) and 129 passing yards (26th) and they rank just 18th in third-down defense in the second half.
In the fourth quarter the Ravens are allowing 5.9 yards/play (26th) and 94 passing yards (31st) and 3.83 points/drive (tied for 31st) and a 42% TD rate (30th). Atlanta rolled up 126 yards in the fourth quarter Sunday and this remains a very real issue; the Ravens holding them to two field goals after marching down the field late was vital.
The Ravens have allowed 46 points in the fourth quarter, tied (with the Eagles) for second most in NFL (only Washington is worse).

title: Critical Takeaways From Wild Ravens Comeback, OT Win In Atlanta
full_text:
The Ravens overcame a bevvy of injuries, including two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson missing the game, rallied to force overtime with a two-minute drive, went ahead in overtime and sealed a huge win over the Falcons with Kyle Hamilton's interception.
Rookie head coach Jesse Minter and novice offensive coordinator Declan Doyle managed the game expertly, knowing what they were up against with Atlanta boasting the best rushing attack in the NFL to go with the top rushing defenses and the best pass rush in terms of pressure rate. Backup quarterback Snoop Huntley is very limited in the downfield passing game but saved his best work for late in two TD drives and secure a 30-23 win at Mercedes-Benz Stadium to surge to 4-1.
Baltimore’s pass rush was tepid for most of the night, the secondary gave up repeated big plays on third downs (four of third-and-10 or longer), and went 9/19 on that down in regulation, but got key goal-to-go stops late again. Tight end Mark Andrews, who has been in major decline for years, had a rough game that took points off the board but caught a key pass in overtime.
The offense, which finally cut down on its penalty issues, mustered it's crispest drive of the night to tie the game at 23 in the dying seconds, with Huntley (24/32 for 201 yards with a rushing TD and two passing TDs) looking at ease and finally using the middle of the field, throwing a short TD pass to Devontez Walker, then Derrick Henry converted a Wild Cat two-point conversion that sent the game to overtime.
"Snoop is just one of the coolest dudes," Minter said after the game. "He doesn't get rattled."
Here are the key takeaways from Week 5:
The Falcons pass rush was a problem most of the night and the Ravens had trouble sustaining things, but the drive to tie the game was masterclass - going 71 yards in six plays in 1:51. The operation was smooth and in sync.
Minter opted to take the ball after winning the toss in overtime and the Ravens reconstructed offensive line continued to take the game over. They had a helluva second half and, facing a defense that came in allowing 2.7 yards/carry, the Ravens got Henry over 100 yards and they ran for 209 yards as a team.
The Ravens mustered a 14-play drive in overtime that erased over seven minutes from the clock to give them their first lead since 3-0. Atlanta backup QB Tua Tagovoalia had to replace Penix late in the game after he took a big hit and Hamilton read him perfectly to end the game with a pick after the Falcons had started to drive.
"It could be a launch point to really get us going," Minter said of the way his team finished the game.
The overpaid tight end was horrible a few hours after the best tight end on the Ravens roster the last two seasons, by far, Isaiah Likely, comminated Washington for the Giants as he has been doing all season. Andrews cannot separate anymore, he can’t run routes downfield, he is good for about eight yards a catch and he continues to drop easy passes early in games.
Andrews basically cost Baltimore 14 points in the first half of this game. And really 16 because he needed to make a better effort on a two-point conversion that came his way, too.
He dropped a touchdown pass early in the game, a play that simply has to be made, and then had a terrible fumble deep in Baltimore territory that was returned for a touchdown. General manager Eric DeCosta has a nasty habit of letting the wrong people walk, and giving Andrews $13M when he couldn’t land a fourth round pick for him back after his terrible drop in the 2024 playoffs to spite Likely will have major ramifications for this season as he runs low on anyone besides Zay Flowers to make plays downfield. Likely making about the same money as Andrews is even sillier.
The Ravens’s pressure peaked early in the game and they were unable to pressure jittery young QB Michael Penix Jr., coming off his third ACL surgery, as the game worse on, especially on obvious pass-rush situations. He had far too much time to operate in general on second-and-long and third-and-long and the Ravens need $30M edge rusher Trey Hendrickson back from his finger surgery ASAP.
Atlanta went up, 14-6, late in the first half when Penix picked up 13 yards to Kyle Pitts on second-and-16, the Drake London for 25 on third-and-three, and Jahan Dotson for 36 on third-and-six, and then Pitts for a touchdown on third-and-five.
In the fourth quarter, Penix had all day to hit London for 14 yards on third-and-two from the Atlanta 18 and then he hit London again for 19 yards on a third-and-15 in which no one could get anywhere close to making the QB concerned.
The Ravens vaunted secondary got picked apart. Minter doesn’t want to blitz but he had to Sunday night (43%) with very shaky results and Penix converted a third-and-10 inside of six minutes that was a backbreaker. There was not nearly enough winning going on up front and Baltimore’s fourth-quarter defense will remain among the worst in the NFL until some real closers emerge.
It would take a commitment from the offensive and defensive game plans to be synced to keep this game close given Baltimore’s injury issues, including, of course, no Jackson. It would take a willingness from young offensive coordinator Declan Doyle to keep it simple here and he did.
The best way to stop Falcons dominant running back Bijan Robinson is to keep him off the field and prevent him from getting a volume of plays on the ground to get going. That’s what we got. Jesse Minter played a loaded line of scrimmage, as was required, and Baltimore’s makeshift offensive line helped them sustain possession.
The Ravens ran 40 plays in the first half. They ran the ball 19 times. They were using over 41 second of wall clock time per play in the first half and that helped them keep the ball for 19:28 in that opening half. So even without scoring any touchdowns they were very much in the game at 14-9.
Atlanta held the ball for nearly as much time in the second half, however, with Baltimore’s defense wilting. But overall Minter applied heavy attention to the line, sticking with heavy fronts, and they bottled up Bijan Robinson (17 rushes for 86 yards) outside on one long blast on an outside zone play.
"Overall, I thought we played Bijan very well," Minter said.
Minter boasted about hunting explosives with Huntley this week but thankfully that was just talk. Well done.
You don’t want Huntley, with a 5.9 yards/attempt average for his career, trying to be something he’s not on the road against a defense that is getting a lot of pressure and with an offensive line that has never played together before. Minter cut down on the motion, the ball was designed to come out quickly and too the flats and with the offensive line so experimental in the interior, the Ravens attacked the perimeter of the field as they needed to .
He leaned into the screen game and horizontal passes, and the designed screens for Derrick Henry we told you were coming, one of which went for a touchdown. And the biggest offensive play of the game came in a “Pony Package” with Henry and running back Justice Hill on the field with Hill taking a draw 47 yards to set up Henry’s touchdown .
The Ravens got a defensive stop on the opening drive of the first half, to keep the deficit at 17-9 and not greater, continuing a recent trend of holding teams to three at critical times even after giving up some yards previously.
The Falcons got cute and called a pass to a tackle eligible rather than just hammer the ball on the ground. Safety Malaki Starks and corner Marlon Humphrey were excellent in run support in goal-to-go defense in general on the night and it was going to take defensive backs being very active in that regard to corral Atlanta’s rushing attack.
Humprey, who had a rough start to the season and missed most of practice with a calf injury, provided sound tackling and also had a great blitz on a fourth-and-short play to force a pressure and get Atlanta off field late in the third quarter.
Vega Ioane…

title: Ravens Inactives For Sunday Night In Atlanta
full_text:
The Ravens activated top receiver Zay Flowers and top-paid corner Marlon Humphrey for their Sunday night game at Atlanta, with both players listed as questionable. Baltimore is an underdog for the first time this season and is facing a Falcons team playing very good football.
The Ravens already ruled out two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson on Friday. His ankle injury could keep him out for Week 6 in Cleveland as well, and will be monitored closely this week. And top pass rusher Trey Hendrickson, signed to a $30M/year deal this offseason to jumpstart a poor pass rush, was also ruled out after having a procedure on his finger prior to Week 4 and he is expected back shortly as well.
The Ravens made a risky trade for Eagles offensive lineman Cam Jurgens early in the week, knowing he remained in concussion protocol and would not play Week 5, but head coach Jesse minter indicated on Friday that they believe Jurgens could be back next week. Jurgens will back to center with Baltimore, while some believe he was about to be benched by the Eagles , after the Ravens opted to deal two picks including a 2028 second-round selection for him in a deal that drew skepticism around the league .
Flowers has been the only consistent cog in the downfield passing game, with twice as many receiving yards as anyone on the team. But his production with back-up Snoop Huntley is above half of that it is with Jackson in terms of yards per catch and air yards per target, and the Ravens simply must alter the scope of their game plan and offensive attack against a Falcons defense that has the top pressure rate in the NFL and is also No. 1 against the run (2.7 yards/carry).
The Ravens also made receiver Elijah Sarratt (fourth-round pick) inactive for Sunday night as well as defensive lineman Aeneas Peebles. Guard Andrew Vorhees (foot) was also inactive.
Last week, with Hendrickson out, undrafted rookie free agent linebacker Ethan Burke, a Baltimore native, stepped up and made an impact after being limited to special-teams duty previously. He stands to see more work tonight and the Ravens will very likely be leaning on much heavier run fronts than we have seen so far this season against Atlanta’s potent rush attack. Bijan Robinson is generally considered the most complete back in the NFL and Brian Robinson has proven to be a powerful drive finisher as well.

title: Ravens Three Keys to Victory vs. Falcons
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens are slight underdogs to come out on top in their road interconference matchup against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5 of the 2026 regular season.
Coming off the team's first regular-season home victory under new head coach Jesse Minter, they'll be playing in primetime for the first time on Sunday Night Football. With a win, they'll improve to 4-1 before hitting the road for their first primetime game against the Atlanta Falcons next week.
In this showdown between two teams looking to take control of the top spot in the standings of their respective divisions, the Ravens can emerge victorious if they follow these keys.
The Ravens are going up against a Falcons team that has the top-ranked run defense and the second-ranked rushing offense through the first four weeks of the season. However, some of those figures are a little inflated because of how the last two weeks transpired, as they can against Green Bay Packers and New Orleans Saints defensive fronts that were missing multiple key starters and banged-up offensive lines on the other side of the ball.
To pull off an upset despite being without their highest-paid and most integral players on both offense and defense , quarterback Lamar Jackson and outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson, the Ravens will have to own the line of scrimmage in the trenches . Defensively, they can't get blown off the ball along the defensive line and provide unimpeded paths to the second level for star running back Bijan Robinson. On the offensive line, they need to be able to impose their will and open lanes in the ground game for Derrick Henry and provide backup quarterback Tyler Huntley with ample time to throw in key moments.
With Jackson under center, the Ravens were able to dig themselves out of moderate to long down-and-distances because of his uncanny ability to extend and make plays downfield. They won't have that kind of leeway, as their margin of error with Huntley is much smaller because, while he's an impressive dual-threat in his own right, it's not to the same electrifying and seemingly inevitable degree as the two-time league MVP, who is truly one-of-one.
This means the Ravens need to turn their discipline sliders all the way up and try not to get in their own way to the same or even a similarly high rate that they've been doing as one of the most penalized teams in the league over four weeks , especially on offense. A Huntley-led offense can't operate from a negative game script or afford to fall behind the sticks consistently because he's at his best throwing at the short and intermediate levels of the field.
Falcons third-year quarterback Michael Penix Jr. has been a big catalyst for the renewed success of their offense, not because he hands the ball off better to Robinson than Cooper Rush, but for his ability to deliver an accurate ball in rhythm and push it downfield. Most of the time, when the former goes deep, it's on passes outside the numbers and hashes and rarely over the middle of the field unless he has a target streaking wide open.
This tendency could lead to opportunities for the Ravens' defensive backs to jump and undercut some of those intended passes for clutch turnovers on interceptions, maybe even a pick-six if they catch it in stride with nothing but green grass in front of them. With a trio of Georgia natives in the secondary , it'll be especially meaningful if either cornerback Nate Wiggins or safeties Kyle Hamilton or Malaki Starks makes one of those big plays in this game.

title: Four Ravens X-Factors For Clash vs. Falcons
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens will continue the 2026 regular season with the first leg of a two-game road stint against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5 on Sunday Night Football , and the difference in the game could come down to how an individual player performs when it matters most or over the course of the game by capitalizing on their opportunities when presented with them.
With a win, the Ravens improve to 4-1 and could tie for or sit atop the AFC North division standings, but a loss would, at worst, tie them for second place with either the Pittsburgh Steelers or the Cincinnati Bengals if they both win on Sunday.
Here are four players who could wind up tilting the scales in favor of the Ravens and first-year head coach Jesse Minter.
With franchise quarterback Lamar Jackson out with an injury for his game, the former Pro Bowl reserve will be making his 17th career regular-season start and his 12th in place of the two-time league MVP. While the Ravens likely plan on having the offense flow through and leaning heavily on five-time Pro Bowl running back Derrick Henry, there will be times when they will need Huntley to step up and make a play with either his arm or his legs in crucial situations. He has shown an ability to rise to the occasion in his previous starts, especially the two most recent from last year, where he averaged just under 150 passing yards, a passing touchdown and just over 56 rushing yards in massive wins over the Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers.
The second-year pro has seen his playing time on defense increase each week since he made his 2026 debut in Week 3 after fully recovering from the torn ACL that ended his promising rookie season last December. Although he won't be supplanting four-time Pro Bowl veteran Roquan Smith or fourth-year breakout Trenton Simpson in the starting lineup, he'll almost certainly see another uptick in his defensive snaps going up against such a dominant and potent rushing attack as the one they'll face in Atlanta and star running back Bijan Robinson .
After losing veteran blocking specialist Durham Smythe for the rest of the season to a torn Achilles, the Ravens signed another veteran, Nick Vannett, from the practice squad to the active roster for depth. However, the fifth-round rookie could still wind up seeing an uptick in offensive snaps played for the third week in a row, particularly as a blocker, where he can fill the role Smythe did as a lead blocker in the backfield at times and an underneath target on play-action passing plays.
Since the Falcons' running game is heavily predicated on stretch and outside zone concepts, being able to set a strong edge and stay gap sound will be paramount to the success of Minter's unit in this game. Robinson is the Ravens' best run defender on the edge and leads the team with two sacks and six quarterback hits. With fourth-time Pro Bowl veteran Trey Hendrickson out for a second straight game while he recovers from finger surgery , he will be instrumental to their game plan both on early downs and as a pass rusher in obvious passing situations, whether he's lined up inside or on the edge.

title: Five Pivotal Ravens Matchups to Watch vs. Falcons
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens' Week 5 bout against the Atlanta Falcons could ultimately be decided by battles between specific position groups or individual players outperforming their counterparts on the other side of the ball.
It'll take place in the Mercedes-Benz Stadium under a national spotlight as it'll mark the Falcons' third straight primetime game of 2026 and the first for the Ravens. With two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson out for this game with an ankle sprain , they're entering this matchup as slight underdogs.
If the Ravens prevail, they will improve to 4-1 and could be in a two-way tie for first in the AFC North standings, depending on how the Cleveland Browns fare on the road against the New York Jets this week. Here are the five matchups that can either make or break this game.
While Falcons All Pro running back Bijan Robinson has garnered most of the headlines for the offense's success on the ground, their offensive line has been the driving force propelling him to back-to-back monster games. Even after franchise left tackle Jake Matthews left last week's game, they didn't miss a beat and kept steamrolling the New Orleans Saints defense.
The Ravens are going to need their vaunted interior defensive line, featuring a pair of Pro Bowlers in Calais Campbell and Nnamdi Madubuike and rising star Travis Jones, to step up in a big way in this game. They've gotten blown off the ball far too often by some of the worst rushing offenses in the league in the first month of the season as they've been gelling and getting healthier after long ramp-ups during training camp and preseason. They'll need to dominate at the point of attack to keep their linebackers clean and get penetration into the backfield themselves.
In a similar way that limiting Robinson is a total team effort for the Ravens' defense, guarding Baltimore's homegrown two-time Pro Bowl receiver won't solely fall on the shoulders of one or two Falcons defensive backs. Since Flowers lines up in a multitude of spots , ranging from all three receiver spots to even in the backfield to create and exploit favorable matchups, face off with any of the players in their secondary.
With a Jackson out, offensive coordinator Declan Doyle might not try to push the ball down the field to Flowers in the same ways as with backup signal caller Tyler Huntley, who is more proficient at throwing underneath and at the intermediate level. Thankfully, Flowers is even more dangerous moving horizontally in space than he is as a traditional vertical threat, meaning that he is just as likely to turn a shallow or quick pass. The Falcons have allowed a 100-plus-yard wide receiver in three straight games, and they don't have anyone on their team who can stop Flowers from extending that streak.
Whether they're mostly kept clean by their compatriots in the trenches or not, the responsibility of getting both Robinsons, Bijan and Brian, on the ground at, behind and beyond the line of scrimmage will fall to likes of Roquan Smith, Trenton Simpson and Teddye Buchannan more often than not. They'll need to be both disciplined and decisive when shooting and filling gaps created by the Falcons' offensive line. Bijan, in particular, can make a defense pay dearly for not being gap-sound on any given down and turn a play that should be a loss of yardage or minimal gain into an explosive play and even a house call.
Despite not having two of their best returning players due to injury and off-field behavior, Atlanta's front seven has surprisingly been one of the best in the league thus far this season. Since recently acquired two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens won't be making his debut this week, the Falcons will be going up against a reshuffled Baltimore offensive line that will be starting first-round rookie guard Olaivavega Ioane
 out of position for the second week in a row and one of either Andrew Vorhees or Emory Jones Jr.
Atlanta won't have sack leader and former Raven Za'Darius Smith available after he was downgraded to out with a concussion/neck injury , but defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich's unit still has several of the league's leaders in pressure rate both on the edge and along the interior. The Ravens will likely look to get the ball out of Huntley's hands quickly in the passing game while leaning heavily on star running back Derrick Henry to carry a lot of the offensive load on the ground, so being able to own the line of scrimmage when they need to will be key.
The Ravens traditionally have their outside cornerbacks play sides, but head coach Jesse Minter should make an exception in this case and have Wiggins follow the Falcons' top wideout early and often because he's the best man for the job. Four-time Pro Bowler Marlon Humphrey is listed as questionable with a hamstring and calf injury that kept him out of practice for most of the week and had him as a limited participant in Friday's session. Fellow 10th-year Chidobe Awuzie struggled in relief of Humphrey in last week's win over the Tennessee Titans, leaving Wiggins as their best possible option to limit, if not neutralize, London's impact in this game.

title: How Can Ravens Stop Bijan Robinson? Film Analyst Greg Cosell Suggests A Radical Change
full_text:
The goal of Ravens head coach Jesse Minter most weeks is to defend the run with as little manpower as possible.
That needs to change in a very fundamental manner tonight in Atlanta. And after watching every snap the Ravens and Falcons have played this season, longtime NFL analyst Greg Cosell from ESPN/NFL Films who studies every matchup, agrees with me that Minter will have to delve into some looks we have not seen all season in an attempt to mitigate the Falcons dynamic run game, specifically Bijan Robinson, the best back in the NFL, running outside zone stretch plays (7.4 yards/carry).
Minter enters Week 5 having used a four-man front just five times all season and being in nickel or dime (five or more defensive backs) over 90% of the time. That won’t work against this Atlanta scheme and offensive line and a pair of running backs (Brian Robinson also) and requires a total rethink of how they plan to operate up front, especially knowing the offense is limited with Snoop Huntley at quarterback and not Lamar Jackson and with new center Cam Jurgens on the concussion list and carrying serious injury red flags.
In fact, Cosell believes that with top pass rusher Trey Hendrickson out (he is not good against the run, anyway) that Minter could look into using anchors Tavious Robinson and Zion Young on the edge in base looks and lean into perhaps three defensive tackles at times. Minter also has flexibility to deploy hybrid defensive back/linebacker Kyle Hamilton in a multitude of ways at the line of scrimmage.
“They could play a 5-2 front, too, you know, and get the wider defender for the outside zone run game,” Cosell explained in detail on “The Daily Flock Show” this week. “Because that's where it starts with the Falcons with Bojan Robinson and outside zone. I think Bijan Robinson is the best back in the league. So you've got to be able to stop outside zone.”
Minter wants to flood the field with defensive backs of all shapes and sizes and responsibilities but that’s not going to play here. Tight end Kyle Pitts is a glorified outside receiver and he still doesn’t look fully vested in Atlanta’s pass game, Drake London is a bigtime receiver but young quarterback Michael Penix Jr is still feeling his way back from his third ACL surgery and it’s doubtful coach Kevin Stefanski wants him dropping back a ton if he doesn’t have to.
Cosell believes that Minter will devise a plan to get both linebackers Teddye Buchanan and Trenton Simpson on the field at the same time on some early-down looks; Simpson replaced Buchanan as a starter after Buchanan suffered an ACL tear late last season, and is playing the best football of his career by far, with him popping off the film for Cosell, along with Robinson in the front defensive front.
Here’s how some of the new base looks might shape out in a 5-2 framework:
“Hamilton would then be a (box) safety with (free safety Malaki) Starks as opposed to the big nickel where (Jaylinn) Hawkins is the third safety,” Cosell suggested. “So I think you're going to see more of that. But again, it also depends on the personnel. the Falcons put out there.
“You know, if they run out of base personnel (one back and two tight ends), you'll see that. If they run out of 11 personnel, then Jesse Minter has to decide how he wants to play that. Now, they don't have a big-time receiving core. So, you might feel that you can still play in your base even if they put 11 out there depending on distance and field location.
“Nothing, as you know, is 100% in an NFL game. So, other than Drake London, you're probably not necessarily believing that there's someone like, ‘Oh, we better stop that guy or else.’ So we'll see. But if you can widen your front, you have a better chance of setting the edge and dealing with that outside zone run game.”
On the other side of the ball, how will the Ravens try to muster a passing attack without Jackson and with their OL issues? A full breakdown of the Ravens and Falcons game can be found below.

title: Five Winners, Four Losers From Bills Exciting Win Over Rams in Week 5
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills just won a thriller in overtime against the Los Angeles Rams.
It was a low scoring first half, with Buffalo going into the break with a 13-7 lead. While both defenses were making plays during the first 30 minutes, that all changed in the second half. There was a stretch of six consecutive drives that ended in touchdowns as the two teams played to a 34-34 tie in regulation.
In overtime, there was more back-and-forth as the Rams ended the Bills' first drive by forcing a turnover. Buffalo responded by blocking a field goal attempt, setting themselves up for a game-winner of their own. Tyler Bass ended up knocking his attempt through the uprights, giving Buffalo a thrilling 37-34 win.
With that exciting game in the books, let's see which players stood out as both winners and losers for the Bills in Week 5.
Ray Davis got things off to a hot start for the Bills, taking the opening kickoff back 70 yards. He was eventually pushed out of bounds, but gave the offense the ball at the Los Angeles 26. The offense lost five yards on their first drive, but thanks to Davis, they took a 3-0 lead despite the three-and-out.
On the second offensive snap of the game, Josh Allen fired a bullet over the middle of the field and hit Dawson Knox in the end zone for what should have been a 23-yard touchdown. That wasn't the case, as Knox dropped the pass , forcing the Bills to settle for a field goal after Ray Davis gave them the ball at the 26-yard-line thanks to his 70-yard kick return.
After the Rams went up 7-6, the Bills needed something to click on offense. That happened as they went 69 yards on five plays to take the lead right back. James Cook ran in a 17-yard touchdown to cap off the drive, but it was Ty Johnson who made the big play on that drive.
On second-and-nine, Johnson took a screen pass from Allen and followed an excellent block from center Connor McGovern. Johnson turned the short pass into a 40-yard gain , finally being pushed out of bounds at the 17-yard line.
Cole Bishop has developed into a trusted starter, but he had a gaffe on Monday that helped set up the Rams for a touchdown. Bishop was beaten on a route by tight end Tyler Higbee and was guilty of pass interference. That gave the Rams the ball at the one-yard line, and Blake Corum ran in a touchdown on the following play, giving them a 14-13 lead.
Trailing 14-13, the Bills nearly gave the ball right back to the Rams. James Cook lost the ball when linebacker Nate Landman punched it out and the officials initially said Los Angeles recovered. After discussion, that was changed and Buffalo kept possession. On replay, it was clear that the Rams had a shot at the recovery, but right guard O'Cyrus Torrence wrestled it away. Buffalo ended up scoring a touchdown on a nine-play, 61-yard drive, which wouldn't have been possible without Torrence.
This wasn't a good day for C.J. Gardner-Johnson. He was flagged for unnecessary roughness on a second-and-16 play, which gave the Rams a fresh set of downs and 15 yards. He was beaten for a touchdown by Davante Adams. He also suffered a lower-body injury in the third quarter , but was able to get back into the game. Unfortunately, when he did, Gardner-Johnson promptly gave up an 18-yard pass to Tyler Higbee. On that play, he simply let the tight end go behind him without any help over the top.
Josh Allen had just four completions in the first half, but turned it on during the second. He still completed just 12-of-19 passes, which is uncharacteristic. Still, he made the plays when they mattered the most, oftentimes doing so with his legs. Allen finished with 121 yards and one touchdown, and had some fourth-quarter and overtime fireworks on the ground.
During their final drive, Allen had a 15-yard gain on third-and-five and then ran 21 yards on second-and-17, moving the ball to the Rams' five-yard line with 1:48 to play, setting James Cook up for the go-ahead touchdown.
In overtime, he had a 19-yard and a 13-yard run to help set up Tyler Bass for a 45-yard game-winning kick. He finished with the second-highest rushing yardage total of his career, and it was the highest since his rookie season in 2018.
James Cook was nearly the one to lose this game for Buffalo, fumbling it away in overtime. It was his second fumble of the game and while O'Cyrus Torrence recovered the first, Aaron Donald of the Rams got this one. Thankfully for Cook, he was bailed out by one of his teammates.
Greg Rousseau walked out of Week 5 as the biggest winner for the Bills. After the Cook fumble, the Rams moved the ball 50 yards and were set up for a game-winning field goal from 48 yards out. The attempt was blocked , however, by Rousseau, which gave the Bills the ball back. That was all they needed, as Allen used his legs to set up a game-winning field goal by Tyler Bass.

title: Alaric Jackson Punches Bradley Chubb in Postgame Altercation After Bills vs. Rams
full_text:
After the Buffalo Bills pulled off a wild win over the Los Angeles Rams in the Week 5 game on Monday night, there was an altercation between Alaric Jackson and Bradley Chubb.
The altercation occurred as players were talking on the field after the final whistle. Jackson was doing a jersey exchange with a Bills player when Chubb appeared to say something to the Rams offensive lineman.
Chubb then walked away, but Jackson followed him, got in his face and punched the Bills edge rusher before the two were separated.
Chubb attempted to get after Jackson once it was broken up, but he was held back by teammates while having more to say to Jackson. Check out the full exchange below.
Alaric Jackson threw a punch at Bradley Chubb after Bills-Rams. pic.twitter.com/diJunklKBe
Not a good look for Jackson, who is likely going to face a fine and a suspension from the NFL for his actions. We would expect the decision to come down in the next day or so.
We saw tempers flaring throughout the contest, as players on both teams got into some scuffles, but nothing escalated to anything close to the level we saw after the game, which amounted to a Monday Night Football classic.
There wasn't much excitement over three quarters, with Buffalo staking itself to a 19-14 lead going into the fourth.
However, the fireworks came from there, with the Rams and Bills exchanging touchdown drives throughout the final frame, which pushed the game to overtime.
Then, there was a wild sequence of events.
The Bills drove 51 yards to the Rams' 22-yard line before James Cook coughed up the football. The Rams then managed to drive 50 yards before Harrison Mevis' 48-yard field goal was blocked, with Greg Rousseau coming up with the rejection.
From there, the Bills drove 35 yards and Tyler Bass booted the game-winning field goal from 45 yards out to secure the 37-34 victory for Buffalo.
With the victory, the Bills are now sitting at 4-1 and keep the razor-thin distance between themselves and the New England Patriots, who moved to 3-2 after their Week 5 win, in the AFC East.
Meanwhile, the preseason Super Bowl champion Rams are now a disappointing 2-3 and in third place on the NFC West behind both the 5-0 San Francisco 49ers and 3-2 Seattle Seahawks.
The Bills will meet with the Las Vegas Raiders on a short week in Week 6 and the Rams draw the Arizona Cardinals, and will likely square off with their division rival without their left tackle.

title: Biggest Takeaways From Bills Resilient Week 5 Win Over Rams
full_text:
Two juggernauts met on Monday Night Football with the Buffalo Bills visiting the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5. The game got off to a hot start, with Ray Davis taking the opening kickoff back 70 yards to give Buffalo the ball at the Los Angeles 26.
Things slowed down from there, with both defenses playing well. That led to a low-scoring first half, with the Bills going into intermission with a 13-7 lead. In the second half, both teams found their rhythm, with multiple touchdowns each in the final quarter.
In overtime, both teams made huge plays. First, Nate Landman forced a fumble by James Cook, but Greg Rousseau blocked the game-winning field goal attempt . That gave the Bills one final chance, and Tyler Bass knocked in a 45-yard field goal to give them the win. Here are some big takeaways from the huge win.
Buffalo had a couple of chances to take a commanding lead in the first quarter, but couldn't capitalize. Ray Davis set them up near the red zone, taking the opening kickoff 70 yards to the Los Angeles 26. They had a chance at a touchdown, but Dawson Knox dropped a pass in the end zone. Josh Allen was sacked on the following play, leading to a field goal from Tyler Bass.
The Rams then missed a 50-yard field goal of their own, and the Bills responded with a strong drive. Leaning heavily on James Cook, they went 55 yards on 10 plays but stalled at the Los Angeles five, again settling for a field goal. Two golden opportunities for a touchdown were missed, meaning they went into the second quarter with a 6-0 lead instead of 14-0. That also allowed the Rams to take the 7-6 lead with their first score of the game, which happened right at the eight-minute mark in the second quarter.
We all expected fireworks in this one, but that wasn't the case in the first half. Instead, it was a defensive battle with the Bills going into the break with a 13-7 lead. What was more shocking than the score was the stat line. Josh Allen completed just 4-of-7 passing attempts for 60 yards and an interception, compared to 16-of-23 for 99 yards and a touchdown for Matthew Stafford. Buffalo moved the ball well on the ground, with James Cook rushing for 55 yards and Allen going for 21 in the first half, but seeing just four completions was shocking.
The Bills took the lead back in the second half when Keon Coleman caught a seven-yard pass to give them a 19-17 advantage. That play would have never happened if not for O'Cyrus Torrence.
Early on that nine-play, 61-yard drive, James Cook fumbled the ball and the Rams were there for the recovery. The officials even signalled that Los Angeles recovered it, but changed the ruling as it was revealed that Torrence was able to wrestle the ball away from everyone under the pile. His fight allowed Buffalo to keep some much-needed momentum and their offense looked completely different after his play.
Buffalo took a lead on a five-yard touchdown courtesy of James Cook, but there was enough time on the clock for the Rams to move down the field and tie the game. It was a disappointing drive as the secondary allowed completions of 14 yards, 16 yards, 15 yards, and nine yards before Kyren Williams ran it in from one-yard out to force overtime. That was the third consecutive touchdown drive for the Rams, all in the fourth quarter.
Buffalo was undisciplined all night, getting hit with 13 penalties for 112 yards. That was a problem for them, as it gave the Rams far too many free yards while also putting their offense in tough situations all night.
Fumbling has been an issue for James Cook throughout the past couple of years, and that's continued this season. He had two fumbles against the Rams, and while Torrence made a great play to get the ball back, the Bills weren't as lucky with his second.
Following a 57-yard reception from Khalil Shakir in overtime, Buffalo was in range to take the lead. That was until Nate Landman (who also forced the first fumble) punched the ball out. Aaron Donald made the recovery, allowing the Rams to get in range for a field goal that nearly won them the game.
As we saw with O'Cyrus Torrence, good things happen when you don't give up. All hope seemed lost following the overtime turnover and ensuing Los Angeles drive, but then Greg Rousseau came through with a huge blocked kick.
Of course it's Greg Rousseau with the FG BLOCK 👋🏈 pic.twitter.com/C7hzQEnvR6 https://t.co/xBcXpdzMQd
He has had a fantastic season and saved the game here for his team. Now, the Bills will turn their attention to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6.

title: C.J. Gardner-Johnson Injury Update: Latest on Bills S After Leaving Week 5 Game
full_text:
In a game that was expected to be a shootout, the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams have found themselves in a fight. The Buffalo defense has held its own, going into the half surrendering just seven points to the high-powered Rams' offense.
During the second half, both teams have found more room to operate, and for the Bills, stopping the Rams just got a lot more difficult. During a drive at the end of the third quarter, safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson tackled running back Blake Corum following a 34-yard play.
While going to the ground, Gardner-Johnson suffered an apparent lower-body injury , pointing to his right knee as soon as he was on the ground. He was able to get up on his own power, but had to limp off the field in obvious pain.
UPDATE : Gardner-Johnson was able to get back into the game during the fourth quarter.
During the first half, Gardner-Johnson appeared to have made a huge play when he broke up a pass from Matthew Stafford to tight end Tyler Higbee. Gardner-Johnson got there as soon as the ball did and delivered a crushing hit.
Unfortunately, the officials ruled that he made forcible contact to the head and neck area, giving the Rams 15 yards and a fresh set of downs. He was also beaten in the end zone by Davante Adams for a touchdown, although that was a tough matchup for any safety.
Gardner-Johnson has six tackles in this game, giving him 24 on the season to go along with one interception and two pass defenses. This isn't the first time Gardner-Johnson has suffered an injury for the Bills. During training camp, the veteran safety suffered a calf injury during practice and was carted to the locker room . He was able to suit up by Week 1, dodging a bullet with that one.
The Buffalo secondary has had health issues this season. Christian Benford missed the Week 4 loss to the New England Patriots with a toe injury. Against the Rams in Week 5, they had to go without Dee Alford, their nickel back, who is dealing with an ankle injury.
This is in addition to losing Jordan Hancock, a defensive back capable of playing safety and nickel, to a hamstring and quad injury.

title: Bills Cut 2x Super Bowl Champ, Sign  NCAA D3 All-American for Monday Night Debut
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills made a player-for-player roster swap prior to their Monday Night Football kickoff against the Los Angeles Rams in Inglewood.
In addition to their two practice squad elevations , the Bills announced the signing of practice squad cornerback Anthony Kendall to the active 53-man roster. In a corresponding move, Buffalo created a spot for Kendall by releasing veteran edge rusher Mike Danna.
Joining the Bills this past offseason, Danna, a two-time Super Bowl champion with the Kansas City Chiefs , was a game day inactive for three of the season's first four weeks. He played eight defensive snaps in Week 2 when Ed Oliver suffered an injury during pregame warmups.
It wouldn't be surprising to see Buffalo bring Danna back in a practice squad capacity, considering Kendall's promotion has created an opening there .
Meanwhile, Kendall joined the Bills during training camp . The 26-year-old Division III product has 16 games of NFL experience from the 2023 season with the Tennessee Titans.
Kendall has been added as emergency insurance in the Bills' banged-up secondary.
Although top cornerback Christian Benford is back in the lineup after an one-game absence due to injury, slot cornerback Dee Alford is unavailable after tweaking his ankle in Week 4. Furthermore, backup nickel cornerback Jordan Hancock is on Injured Reserve, and practice squad defensive back Te'Cory Couch, who was elevated last week, is also banged up.
Despite playing in 16 games for Tennessee, Kendall saw only three total defensive snaps while logging 323 special teams reps. Still, he'll be expected to contribute for the Bills as a member of the active roster.
“If you're on our roster, if that's an opportunity, whether it's practice squad, whether it's inactives, there's a reason you're here. If an injury happens, and we don't feel comfortable with a guy that's been inactive playing, or a guy that's been on the practice squad calling him up, then you start to question, why are they here?" said Bills' head coach Joe Brady earlier this month.
Kendall is on Buffalo's active game day roster, and he saw his first defensive snaps in the second quarter on Monday night. It's his first live NFL regular season game action since December 31, 2023 when he recorded one tackle and 23 special teams snaps against the Houston Texans.
The Baldwin Wallace product, who earned 2022 Division III All-America honors, was waived by the Titans in October 2024. He spent a brief time on the Baltimore Ravens' practice squad.

title: Will DJ Moore Be Back in Week 6? Injury Update, Return Timeline For Bills WR
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills do not have the services of wide receiver DJ Moore for the Week 5 game against the Los Angeles Rams.
That's because Moore was ruled inactive for the contest with the Rams after failing to overcome his shoulder injury before kickoff.
Moore was listed as questionable after getting in only one limited practice in the days leading up to the Week 5 game. Now, Moore will have another week to get his shoulder right before possibly returning to action in Week 6.
Here's what we know about Moore's injury and return timeline.
Moore suffered an AC joint sprain in the Week 2 win over the Detroit Lions that forced his early exit from the contest.
However, the Bills wideout was able to play in Week 3 and Week 4, although he ended up re-aggravating the injury in the latter game and was once again forced from a contest early.
The following day, ESPN's Adam Schefter confirmed Moore had re-aggravated the issue, but added that the injury wasn't considered "a long-term issue."
On Monday night, NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe said the hope is "more rest will help (Moore) with shoulder throughout the season," so it appears this issue is going to linger, which is concerning for his rest-of-season outlook.
After seeing Schefter's report, it's fair to assume that Moore has at least a decent chance to return in Week 6.
Adding to the optimism for his outlook in the short term, the fact that Moore was able to be a limited participant on Saturday before drawing a questionable tag suggests he isn't too far off from being back in action.
One thing that could complicate matters for Moore in Week 6 is the short week, which will give the veteran less time to recover before the game against the Las Vegas Raiders.
Then, there's the bye in Week 7, which will only tempt Buffalo to sit him in Week 6 more because Moore can get three weeks worth of rest and only miss two games.
The Bills will put out their first injury report of Week 6 on Wednesday afternoon, so we'll have more info then.
With Moore in and out of the lineup this season, it has been Keon Coleman who has stepped up big time for Buffalo.
In Week 2, when Moore made his first early exit from a game, the former second-round pick racked up six catches for 63 yards. In Week 4, when Moore left early again, Coleman reeled in six receptions for 116 yards and one touchdown.
In four weeks, Coleman's future has gone from bleak to promising, although there is still a long way to go before he cements himself in Buffalo for the long haul.

title: Bills' Wide Receivers DJ Moore, Josh Palmer Headline Monday Night Inactives at Rams
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are sitting wide receiver DJ Moore down in Week 5.
Fighting through an AC joint sprain, and officially questionable on the final injury report , Moore was tabbed as one of the Bills' seven game day inactives for Monday Night Football against the Los Angeles Rams on October 12.
Scratched from the lineup, Moore sees his 91-game consecutive appearance streak snapped. He made 12 receptions for 178 yards and one touchdown over his first four games as a Bill.
Josh Palmer, who was ruled out on Saturday due to a practice injury , is also inactive, meaning the Bills are down two wide receivers. Veteran Trent Sherfield is active as a practice squad elevation .
It was thought that Moore would be available to play when he practiced in a limited fashion on Saturday. Although pain tolerance is the main issue , it appears as if the Bills don't want to risk another reaggravation .
Additionally, defensive linemen Ed Oliver and Landon Jackson along with starting slot cornerback Dee Alford are game day scratches. Both linemen suffered knee injuries last time out against the New England Patriots while Alford tweaked his ankle.
Rookie offensive linemen Jude Bowry and Ar'maj Reed-Adams round out the seven inactives for October 12.
With Palmer out, Bills' fourth-round rookie wide receiver Skyler Bell is active for the first time this season.
"Skyler’s going to be up, and it was good because early in the week, he's taking DJ's [Moore] plays in practice as we kind of go through it," said Bills' first-year head coach Joe Brady after Saturday's practice in Orchard Park.
Bell, the No. 125 overall selection this past April, missed the Bills' first two preseason games due to an August 8 groin injury. He finally saw action in the exhibition finale against the Pittsburgh Steelers , making seven catches for 49 yards.
With Bell, Greg Dortch and Sherfield being three of Buffalo's five active wide receivers, expect a heavier than usual workload for Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir. We projected a big game for both Coleman and tight end Dalton Kincaid.
Also of note, fifth-round rookie safety Jalon Kilgore is making his debut on Monday Night Football. Buffalo, which is undermanned in the secondary with Jordan Hancock on Injured Reserve and Alford inactive, were not able to elevate practice squad defensive back Te'Cory Couch due to injury.

title: Four Bills' Player Prop Bets for Monday Night: Back Josh Allen, James Cook vs. Rams
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills take center stage on Monday Night Football in Week 5, visiting the high-powered Los Angeles Rams in what could be a Super Bowl LXI preview at SoFi Stadium.
Offensively, the Bills have had massive success against the Rams with Josh Allen at quarterback. They faced off against Los Angeles in 2020, 2022 and 2024, and they scored 35, 31 and 42 points, respectively. Interestingly enough, their only loss was the 42-point showing.
Even with the Rams owning the NFL's No. 1 ranked defense entering the game, there's a good chance the Bills will get theirs so to speak.
Here are four player prop bets that bank on the Bills piling up the yards and points on primetime. All odds are provided by DraftKings and are subject to change.
Allen, who bas thrown for at least 204 yards in every game thus far, has hit the 250 mark twice through four weeks.
He went 23-of-33 passing for 253 yards in the Week 4 loss after going 20-of-29 passing for 334 yards in the season opener. In Week 2, Allen passed for 248 yards as the Bills tamed the Detroit Lions.
Although past results do not guarantee future success, it's hard to ignore the numbers that Allen has produced in his last two road games against the Rams.
Allen passed for 342 yards and three touchdowns in a 44-42 loss on his way to the 2024 NFL MVP award. Two years prior, in what was the Rams' first game following their Super Bowl LVI victory, Allen keyed a 31-10 win by throwing for 297 yards and three touchdowns.
Furthermore, despite rumors that he's dealing with an unreported injury, Allen claimed to be fully healthy this week.
Cook ranks second amongst NFL leaders in yards per carry (6.0), and he's been highly efficient each of the past three weeks.
After rushing for 135 and 154 yards, respectively, in Weeks 2 and 3, the Bills mistakenly moved away from Cook at times during the Week 4 loss. Having totaled 45 rushes over the prior two games, he carried only 12 times for 75 yards against the Patriots.
As a result, I'm expecting the Bills to feed Cook as often as possible against the Rams, who allow 102.0 rush yards per game. He went over the 100-yard mark in more than 50 percent of games last season, and I'm looking for him to repeat that feat on Monday night.
Coleman stepped up in a big way when DJ Moore was forced out of the game against the Patriots. He caught six of seven targets for 116 yards and one touchdown.
When Moore left in Week 2 against the Detroit Lions, Coleman finished that win with six catches for 63 yards in six targets.
He has at least one 20+ yard reception in each of the past three games, and his big play ability makes the 50-yard mark even more attainable. Additionally, Coleman, who has Allen's trust, should be a significant factor for an offense that will be without wide receiver Josh Palmer and potentially Moore, too.
Maybe I'm a glutton for punishment, considering I also took Kincaid to score 8+ touchdowns for the season, but I'm not giving up yet.
With his first, and only, touchdown this season coming on primetime against the Detroit Lions in Week 2, let's back Kincaid to find pay dirt again on Monday Night Football. It also seems as if the Bills will make it a point to target Kincaid as often as possible after failing to get him into the flow against the New England Patriots in Week 4.
"Anytime Dalton comes away with two targets and one of them being in the last drive of the game, obviously, I didn't do a good enough job," said first-year head coach Joe Brady in the wake of the 29-26 loss.
Even with only three combined receptions over the past two weeks, Kincaid remains the Bills' receiving leaders (270 yards). It also worth noting, he caught touchdowns in five of 12 regular season games last year and one in each playoff appearance as well.

title: One of Bills' Practice Squad Elevations May Be Bad News For DJ Moore's Week 5 Status
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are calling up two players from the practice squad ahead of kickoff of the Monday night contest against the Los Angeles Rams and one of them might be bad news for DJ Moore.
The Bills announced they are elevating wide receiver Trent Sherfield and defensive lineman Phidarian Mathis for the showdown against the Rams.
Sherfield, who was with the Bills during the offseason and spent time in Buffalo in 2023, failed to make the team's 53-man roster out of training camp before he returned on Buffalo's practice squad. He has not appeared in a contest yet this season.
As for Mathis, he started off the season suspended , was cut loose by Buffalo after he was activated from the ban and then was brought back on the practice squad right after that.
If he plays, this will be his 2026 debut.
Moore's status for Week 5 remains uncertain as of this writing. All we know is Moore is questionable to play with his shoulder injury that he initially suffered in Week 2 but re-aggravated in Week 4 . Moore has been diagnosed with an AC joint sprain.
The elevation of Sherfield may simply be a precautionary measure just in case Moore isn't good enough to go, but it could also be an indication the Bills do not expect him to play.
We know it's not a move to cover for the loss of the injured Joshua Palmer, who was ruled out on Saturday . The Bills already have rookie Skyler Bell to cover for him.
We will know soon enough what the deal is with Moore. He will get in a pregame workout to test his shoulder and then the Bills will drop their list of inactives around 6:45 p.m. ET, which is an hour and a half before kickoff.
On Friday, the Bills ruled out star defensive tackle Ed Oliver, who is dealing with a knee injury. Oliver is now missing his second game of the season after he was a surprise scratch in Week 2 right before kickoff.
A former 2022 second-round pick of the Washington Commanders, Mathis will add more depth to the Bills' front.
Over 29 games (zero starts) during his career, Mathis has tallied 38 tackles, including two for loss, one QB hit, one pass defensed and one fumble recovery. This won't be his first game with the Bills, though, as he appeared in six contests with Buffalo in 2025.

title: Panthers Could Make Rare Trade With Eagles Before Playing Them
full_text:
NFL teams typically don't trade players to teams right before they play them, especially when the trade deadline is about a month away. There is no urgency for one team to give up a player who could immediately hurt them on the other side .
That said, the Carolina Panthers are desperate, and they could call up the Philadelphia Eagles this week and trade for cornerback Kelee Ringo, who has largely become a special teams player.
The Eagles would be taking a risk by giving up a player with intimate knowledge right before a huge NFC battle. But the Panthers need help as soon as possible, which could reflect an increase in the price.
Regardless, CBS Sports' Jordan Dajani pitched the Panthers as an ideal landing spot for Ringo, and he's spot on.
The Panthers lost Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson to injuries in Week 3. Neither is going to be back any time soon, though both are expected to return before the season is over. In the meantime, things are bad.
The Panthers may have beat the Detroit Lions in Week 4, but they were honestly lucky. Jared Goff tossed for over 400 yards, and Akayleb Evans was in coverage for about 200 of them. It was abuse at the highest level.
The Panthers won't face the Lions, arguably the NFL's best offense, again, but they can't afford to have a walking mismatch in coverage on every single snap. They need some sort of reinforcement. Enter, perhaps, Kelee Ringo.
Now, as mentioned, the Eagles might be very hesitant to do a deal now, but the fit makes too much sense to ignore.
"Kelee Ringo needs a change of scenery and is in the final year of his rookie deal. The former fourth-round pick out of Georgia has the physical makeup you want at 6-foot-2, 207 pounds," Jordan Dajani wrote.
That makes him the ideal short-term replacement while Carolina navigates who should be its CB2 opposite Horn in 2027 and beyond. Plus, physically, Ringo is similar to Horn. They're both big, strong corners.
Dajani continued, "He's started in just eight of 55 career games played with the Eagles, and he has played only on special teams this season. However, there are multiple teams out there that need cornerbacks right now to come in and contribute immediately."
The Panthers are one of those teams. In fact, they might be the team most in need. The Panthers had arguably the best cornerback duo in the NFL, and both of them are out. It's an unfathomable situation, but the Eagles just might hold the answer.

title: Panthers K Ryan Fitzgerald Hasn't Missed a Field Goal — So Explain This
full_text:
I don't think I've ever been this confused by a kicker.
Ryan Fitzgerald hasn't missed a field goal all season. He can line up from 53 yards, and honestly, I feel pretty good about it. Then Carolina scores a touchdown, Fitzgerald comes out for the extra point and I'm sitting there wondering what's about to happen.
Through four games, Fitzgerald is 9-for-9 on field goals . He's 3-for-3 from 40 to 49 yards, made his only attempt from 50-plus and has a long of 53. If I stopped right there, we'd be talking about how reliable Carolina's kicker has been.
But I can't stop there because he's 10-for-13 on extra points. Fitzgerald missed one against Chicago and then missed two against Detroit. Somehow, the kick that's supposed to be easier has been the one making me nervous.
The Cleveland game is where this really started standing out to me. Carolina couldn't get into the end zone for most of the afternoon, so Fitzgerald basically became the offense. He went 4-for-4 on field goals , including a 53-yarder, and scored Carolina's first 12 points.
And here's the weird part: I wasn't really worried when he came out there to kick them. Even when Fitzgerald lined up from 53, I felt pretty good about his chances. That's probably not how I'm supposed to feel about a 53-yard field goal, but he's given me a reason to trust him.
Then we get to Detroit. Fitzgerald made both of his field-goal attempts but missed two extra points. Carolina still won 32-26, so those points didn't end up deciding the game, but I definitely don't want to keep finding out how many missed extra points the Panthers can get away with.
I'm not saying Carolina has a kicker problem, either. How can I say that when the guy hasn't missed a field goal? Fitzgerald also showed as a rookie that pressure doesn't seem to bother him much, going 4-for-4 on game-winning field-goal attempts last season.
That's why I'm having such a hard time figuring this out. If Fitzgerald were missing everything, this would be an easy conversation. He's not. He's perfect on the kicks that are supposed to make me nervous and 10-for-13 on the ones I barely used to think about.
Maybe the extra points get cleaned up after the bye, and we never talk about this again. I hope that's what happens because Fitzgerald has been too good on field goals for three missed extra points to become the story of his season. But Carolina is going to play close games, and eventually one point could be the difference.
For now, I guess this is where I'm at with Fitzgerald.
Fifty-three yards? I'm good.
Extra point? I'm watching.

title: Jalen Coker, Taylor Moton Among Positive Monday Injury Updates From Panthers
full_text:
The arrow is pointing up when it comes to Carolina Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker returning from injury in Week 6.
Coker suffered a quadriceps injury during the Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns and was ruled out for the Week 4 contest against the Detroit Lions.
The Panthers had a bye in Week 5 , so Coker had some extra time to get right without having to miss another game. And, based on an injury update from head coach Dave Canales, it looks like the time off did him a lot of good.
On Monday, head coach Dave Canales revealed that Coker is now "on track" to play in Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles, but he cautioned that Carolina needs to see how he gets through a week of practice first.
"Dave Canales: WR Jalen Coker (quad) is 'on track' but has a couple of big days of practice ahead of him this week heading into Sunday's game at PHI," The Athletic's Joe Person relayed.
The Panthers will release their first injury report of the week on Wednesday afternoon, so we'll know more about Coker then.
If the veteran wideout can turn in even a limited practice, that will be a good sign for his chances of playing. A full practice would almost guarantee he'll return in Week 6.
While he has posted one great game and one good game in 2026, Coker has also dealt with injury issues. On top of his quad issue, Coker also battled an ankle injury before that.
Coker wasn't the only positive injury news for the Panthers on Monday, as Canales revealed that both offensive tackle Taylor Moton and defensive lineman Turk Wharton had their practice windows opened .
Moton was placed on the non-football illness list before the start of the season after it was discovered he had a blood clot in his lung. Wharton had an offseason procedure on his neck that resulted in him landing on the PUP list.
Canales said that the return of Moton is "certainly timely," as his replacement, Monroe Freeling, is dealing with a knee injury. The Panthers coach called Wharton's impending return a "breath of fresh air."
While both players are close, there is no guarantee they will make their returns this week. Both will likely need some time to ramp up, so it could be even more than one more week until they get back into the lineup. That said, for a team that has gotten nothing but terrible injury news this year, it's just nice to hear they're close.
The Panthers have time, too, as they're in first place in the NFC South going into Week 6 despite a 2-2 record. Carolina grabbed that spot during its bye week.
"It's playing out really nicely. It has nothing to do with how we perform," Canales said of the Panthers taking over the lead in the division during the bye.
One of the worst divisions in the NFL, every team in the NFC South has been on the struggle bus this season, but Carolina has looked like the best of the group through five weeks.

title: 5 Hail Mary Cornerback Moves Panthers Just Have to Consider Now
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers badly need a cornerback. With Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson both out, special teamer Akayleb Evans got picked on badly by the Detroit Lions last time out. These moves would be desperate, but after seeing what happened to Evans, we may be well past desperate.
The Packers may have earned a win in Week 5, but they're still facing an uphill battle to relevance this year. It might be wise to move a fringe player who is heading to free agency next season, and the Panthers would probably be happy to bring in Keisean Nixon.
The Panthers need anyone at cornerback so Akayleb Evans can go back to special teams, and Nixon has starting experience. Carolina can work with that while they wait for Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson to come back.
There's a reason Marshon Lattimore is still available even now, and that should concern the Panthers. However, at this stage, anyone is better than Akayleb Evans for another game at cornerback. Even Lattimore.
Plus, he knows how to defend NFC South wide receivers, and maybe after some time off, he will have a little left in the tank. The Panthers have done well dumpster diving already (Darren Waller, Bobby Okereke), so why not try again?
The Panthers and Buccaneers don't do business very often, especially in a season where both are fighting for the NFC South crown. Now, the Buccaneers are hanging on by a thread, so it might be wise to go ahead and trade someone like Zyon McCollum.
"McCollum enjoyed a tremendous start to the 2024 season, but since then, his production has certainly waned. Over the first four games of 2026, McCollum sports just a 58.3 PFF coverage grade, although his passer rating against (80.4) and forced incompletion rate (13.3%) are both in at least the 60th percentile," PFF's Bradley Locker explained.
The New York Jets made Nahshon Wright a healthy scratch, so he's an obvious trade candidate. The Panthers should be all over that. Wright had eight takeaways last year and 11 passes broken up, so he'd be an outstanding replacement for Horn and/or Jackson.
The Eagles are decidedly not out of the NFC East race, and they face the Panthers this week, but Carolina should be calling about Kelee Ringo. According to CBS Sports' Jordan Dajani , he "needs a change of scenery and is in the final year of his rookie deal."
Dajani noted that Ringo has the ideal physical makeup for an NFL cornerback, which makes him a decent Jaycee Horn replacement. Horn is of similar stature and very physical, so Ringo could step up in his absence.

title: Panthers' Power Ranking Spot, Super Bowl Odds Rise Despite Not Playing
full_text:
The bye week was kind to the Carolina Panthers. Aside from a miraculous, stunning Tampa Bay Buccaneers win on Thursday, it went exactly to plan. The New Orleans Saints and Atlanta Falcons both lost, leaving the Panthers in first place.
They also got healthier. Though this week will be key, there's a good chance Jaelan Phillips, Monroe Freeling, and Jalen Coker will be back. Tershawn Wharton, Taylor Moton, and Trevor Etienne have a chance of joining them.
Plus, their next opponent, the Philadelphia Eagles, saw one offensive lineman retire, traded another, and then lost in unfathomable fashion in London before flying back to face the Panthers this Sunday.
It was as good an off week as you could ask for if you're the Panthers. And while they didn't play, those good vibes are reflected in their rising Super Bowl odds and Power Ranking placement.
Teams rarely move in NFL Power Rankings when they're not playing. They didn't do anything to earn it. Sometimes, though, teams get worse around them, pushing them up. And with these Power Rankings from Sports Illustrated's Peter Dewey , the rising Super Bowl odds pushed Carolina up.
The Panthers' odds rose likely because their division title odds rose with the Saints and Falcons losing. Since these rankings are based on Super Bowl odds, the spot went up from 20th to 18th, but there is a caveat.
"Bryce Young and the Panthers went from +9000 to +7400 to win the Super Bowl during their bye week, as they're 2-2 and in the mix to win the NFC South for the second season in a row," Dewey began.
But, he added, " Their defense needs to show more -- even with all the injuries -- before I really buy this team in the futures market."
This is true, although it's going to be hard for the defense to do anything as long as both Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn are out. That's an untenable situation, and the other nine players on the field can only do so much.
It is likely that what the Panthers did on SNF versus the Detroit Lions is the blueprint. They're going to have to live with Akayleb Evans being picked on, but they can shut down the run, get timely pressure, and make fourth-down stops when necessary.
Until Horn and Jackson return, that might be the best we can hope for, and it's the sort of thing that should inspire those like Dewey and see the Panthers continue rising up the ranks.

title: The Panthers Defense Makes Absolutely No Sense — And That's a Good Thing
full_text:
I really don't know what to make of the Carolina Panthers' defense right now. There are times when I watch them and think they still have a long way to go, and then they'll turn around and make a play that completely changes the game. Four games in, I'm still trying to figure this group out.
The numbers don't really help, either. Carolina is giving up 387.2 yards per game, which ranks 29th in the NFL, and its 11.8% pressure rate ranks 30th. There's really no way around it. Those aren't good numbers.
Then I got to the numbers that surprised me. The Panthers have eight takeaways through four games, second-most in the NFL, and they've stopped opponents five times on fourth down, tied for the most in the league. I had to look at that twice because it doesn't really match what I've watched at times.
How does a defense give up that many yards, get that little pressure, and still keep finding ways to end drives? I don't really have an answer. They just keep doing it.
The first four games haven't made much sense. Chicago ran for 291 yards and put 59 points on Carolina in the opener, and after that game, I wondered how this defense was going to stop anybody. Seven days later, Atlanta scored three points.
Then Carolina went to Cleveland and gave up only 21. A week later, Detroit rolled up 452 yards of offense , and Jared Goff threw for 412 yards on 52 attempts. If you had given me those numbers before the game and asked who won, I'd take Detroit every time.
Even the way that game ended fits with everything else. Detroit had moved the ball all night and had one last chance to go win the game. Carolina needed one stop, and Lathan Ransom and Will Lee III combined to make it on fourth down.
Maybe that's why I'm having such a hard time deciding what I think about this defense. I don't like giving up nearly 400 yards per game, and I definitely don't like being near the bottom of the NFL in pressure rate. Keep doing that, and eventually it's going to hurt you.
But I also can't ignore eight takeaways and five fourth-down stops. Those have certainly helped the siege of injuries Carolina has dealt with on that side of the ball.
