title: The Panthers Just Fixed a Problem That Haunted Them All Last Season
full_text:
There were plenty of things I wanted to see change with the Panthers offense this season, but one of the biggest was pretty simple. I wanted to see some plays where it didn't feel like Carolina had to fight for every single yard. Last year, there were way too many times when it felt like the Panthers needed almost everything to go right just to put together a scoring drive.
Apparently, Dave Canales felt the same way. Around this time last season, he talked about Carolina's "lack of big plays" and the need to create more of them in both the running and passing game. I remembered Carolina having that problem, but I didn't realize how much it had changed until I started looking at the numbers from this season.
Through four games, the Panthers have an explosive-play rate of 10.9% , which ranks sixth in the NFL. They were at 8.8% last season and ranked 23rd. Going from the bottom third of the league to the top six is a pretty big change, even if we're only four games into the season.
The Detroit game was probably the best example we've seen so far. Carolina put up 445 yards in the 32-26 win , and 11.4% of its plays were explosive. It felt like every time Detroit started getting comfortable, somebody on Carolina's offense made a play.
Tetairoa McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and two touchdowns. Bryce Young threw for 329 yards, and Chuba Hubbard ran for 122 yards and scored twice. We've talked about all three of those guys plenty already, but when you put what they're doing together, you start to see why the explosive-play numbers have changed so much.
That's probably what feels the most different to me. Last season, one holding penalty or one sack could put Carolina in a spot where I didn't know how they were going to get out of it. When you're constantly asking an offense to put together long drives, eventually something is going to go wrong.
This year, there are more ways to make up for it. McMillan can make a play downfield, Hubbard can break a run and suddenly Carolina is on the other side of the field, and Young has been more willing to push the ball when the opportunity is there. Carolina doesn't have to be perfect for 10 or 12 plays anymore just to get into scoring position.
I wondered if maybe Detroit was making these numbers look better than they really were. It wasn't. Carolina's explosive-play rate was 12.9% against Chicago, 10.2% against Atlanta, and 9.5% against Cleveland. The Panthers have been above last season's 8.8% mark in every game they've played.
Four games is still four games, so I'm not ready to say this offense has everything figured out. We've seen it stall, and there are still times when Carolina makes things harder on itself than it needs to. But explosive plays were something Canales specifically wanted more of last season, and so far, he's getting them.
Last year, the Panthers were searching for big plays.
This year, they're finally expecting them.

title: Tetairoa McMillan's Most Impressive Stat So Far Isn't His 385 Receiving Yards
full_text:
I thought I had pretty much said everything I needed to say about Tetairoa McMillan after what he did against Detroit. When a guy catches 14 passes for 192 yards and two touchdowns, there really isn't much left to add.
Then I started looking through PFF's latest wide receiver rankings , and one number got my attention. McMillan has had 26 catchable passes thrown his way this season, and he's caught every single one.
I know what some people are probably thinking. He's a wide receiver; isn't that what he's supposed to do? Sure, but going four games without dropping a single catchable pass is still pretty impressive, especially with how much Bryce Young has been looking his way.
There's more to it than just the catches, too. McMillan has 385 receiving yards through four games and is averaging 2.35 yards per route run, which ranks 12th among NFL receivers, according to PFF. They also have him ranked as the No. 8 receiver in football right now.
I expected McMillan to be good this season. I'm just not sure I expected us to already be having this conversation four games in.
That's what I'm starting to wonder about with McMillan . He had 1,014 receiving yards as a rookie, so we already knew Carolina had something. I thought another step forward this season probably meant establishing himself as one of the better young receivers in the league.
He might already be past that.
PFF had McMillan ranked No. 23 among NFL receivers before the season. Now he's eighth, and obviously the Detroit game had a lot to do with that jump. But I don't think you can look at 26 catches on 26 catchable passes and say this is all about one huge game.
That's probably what I like most about that stat. The 192 yards against Detroit are going to get your attention, and they should, but 26-for-26 tells you something else. Young has given McMillan plenty of chances through four games, and McMillan hasn't wasted them.
We've talked a lot about how different Young has looked through the first four games, and he deserves that. But I also don't think it's a coincidence that his jump is happening while McMillan is making one of his own. It has to make Young's job a little easier when he knows that if he gives McMillan a chance, chances are he's coming down with it.
There are still 13 games left, so I'm not ready to start putting McMillan in the same group as the very best receivers in football. I do think we're getting closer to having that conversation, though, and I probably wouldn't have said that before the season.
I came into the year thinking McMillan could become one of the better young receivers in the NFL.
Four games later, I'm starting to wonder if I set the bar too low.

title: Nobody Drafted This Panthers Rookie & That Already Looks Like a Mistake
full_text:
Coming into the season, Lee Hunter was the rookie defensive tackle I expected to be talking about. The Carolina Panthers took him with the 49th pick, and so far, he's given them plenty to feel good about.
Aaron Hall was a different story. He went through all seven rounds without hearing his name called, signed with Carolina out of Duke, and came into camp just trying to find a way onto the roster. Honestly, I wasn't paying much attention to him at the time.
Four games later, I am now.
Hall has played in every game, already has 10 tackles, and has even made a start. Six of those tackles came in Carolina's 34-3 win over Atlanta, and he also has a fumble recovery. That's a pretty good start for a guy nobody drafted.
The funny thing is, maybe the Panthers aren't nearly as surprised by this as the rest of us. After Hall made the 53-man roster, general manager Dan Morgan said the rookie "kind of blew us away" with his ability to handle double teams, rush the passer, and play with a high motor.
Turns out Morgan might have been telling us something.
What really made me take notice was NFL.com's early All-Rookie team . Hunter made the first team at defensive tackle, which is already a pretty good development for Carolina, considering how much they invested in him.
Then I kept reading, and there was Hall on the second team alongside Kansas City first-round pick Peter Woods. Think about how different those paths were just a few months ago. Woods heard his name called in the first round, Hunter went in the second, and Hall sat through the entire draft without getting picked.
Now all three are on the same list.
That's what makes Hall's first four games such a good story. This isn't just an undrafted rookie hanging around at the bottom of the roster. He's getting snaps, he's already started a game and he's showing that he belongs out there.
Hall had a pretty good résumé at Duke, too. He finished his final season with 44 tackles and 2.5 sacks and was a two-time team captain. He also grew up in North Carolina and watched the Panthers during the Cam Newton years, which makes the way this has started even better.
And Carolina might have gotten a little lucky here. Every team had a chance to draft Hall. Nobody did, and the Panthers were able to bring him in without using a pick.
Nobody knows what Hall's career is going to look like after four games, but that's not really the point of this story. Going from undrafted in April to making an NFL roster was already an accomplishment. Now he's playing meaningful snaps and getting recognized alongside some of the best rookies in the league.
Hall didn't hear his name called during the draft.
He's giving people a reason to remember it now.

title: The Panthers Have Suddenly Become a Defensive Coordinator's Nightmare
full_text:
I remember when the biggest question around Bryce Young was whether the Panthers had given him enough help. Actually, I feel like we've been asking that almost since the day Carolina drafted him.
I'm not sure we need to ask it anymore. I've watched this offense for four games now, and I'm starting to wonder about something completely different. If you're playing the Panthers right now, who are you trying to take away?
I guess the obvious answer is Tetairoa McMillan. After what he did against Detroit, I'd probably start there, too. I'm just not sure that fixes the problem.
McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit. He became the first player in Panthers history with at least 10 catches, 175 receiving yards, and two touchdowns in a game, and he was named NFC Offensive Player of the Week.
Panthers.com broke down McMillan's huge night , including how Carolina kept moving him around instead of letting Detroit know exactly where he'd be. Dave Canales credited the staff for “putting him in different situations, getting matchups right.”
So yeah, I'm probably making sure I know where No. 4 is before every snap. But if I'm spending that much attention on McMillan, now I've got Chuba Hubbard to worry about.
Hubbard just ran for 122 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit. I've complained plenty about Carolina getting away from him too quickly, but if he's running the ball like that, you can't spend the entire game worrying about McMillan and let Hubbard keep getting five or six yards at a time.
And then there's Jalen Coker. He didn't even play against Detroit, but we're only a few weeks removed from him catching eight passes for 138 yards and two touchdowns against Chicago. Hubbard has also caught 10 passes with two touchdowns this season, and Darren Waller caught two touchdowns against Atlanta.
I don't remember the last time Carolina had this many answers on offense.
I know it's only four games. I've also watched this team go from getting embarrassed by Chicago to beating Detroit on Sunday night, so I'm trying not to decide too much about the Panthers from one week to the next.
Still, 121 points is 121 points.
According to Panthers.com , that's the most points through four games in franchise history. Carolina has also scored at least 30 points three times, something no Panthers team had ever done in three of its first four games.
I definitely didn't see that coming.
Young has thrown for 1,268 yards and nine touchdowns. McMillan already has 385 receiving yards, Hubbard is coming off his best rushing game of the season, and Coker hasn't even been available the last couple of weeks.
Maybe I'm making this too simple, but isn't this what Carolina has been trying to give Young all along?
For most of his career, we've talked about what he didn't have. The offensive line wasn't good enough. He needed another receiver. The running game disappeared. It always felt like we were talking about what Carolina needed to add next.
I'm having a harder time doing that now.
I'm not ready to put this offense up there with the best in the NFL after four games. That's too far for me, especially with how different this team has looked from one Sunday to the next.
But I also don't think what we're seeing is nothing. McMillan just took over a game, Hubbard ran for 122 yards, Young threw for 329, and Coker wasn't even on the field.
For once, I'm not asking whether Young has enough help.
I'm trying to figure out who defenses are supposed to stop first.

title: What Bears Miss Most About Caleb Williams Can Rapidly Reverse Their Fortunes
full_text:
One loss to the Green Bay Packers and the world has ended for Bears fans.
Take a look at social media over the last day and Ben Johnson's great turnaround of the franchise might as well have never happened. His play calling, game plan and failure to get the team up emotionally so they could win one for the late Mike Ditka are all among reasons Johnson is being lambasted.
Cornerback Jaylon Johnson was probably cut on social media about 739,000 times on Monday for his coverage breakdowns.
Dillon Thieneman? A bust. Malik Muhammad? A bust.
Ryan Poles should be fired for the Montez Sweat trade in 2023. Ryan Poles should be fired, period.
I know one god damn thing.. We better be seeking a poor man’s Caleb Williams in the draft as a backup QB moving forward..
These are all out there floating around simply from one loss.
It all sounds like something Packer fans would say about the Bears, and ironically Packers fans were all saying something similar about their own team just a few weeks ago after their blowout loss to Atlanta.
I knew Tyson Bagent played really poorly yesterday, but after the dust settled, I can say that I didn’t realize he played one of the worst games I had ever seen from a Bears quarterback. And that’s saying something.
This is life in the NFL, where fans think the season depends on one game only to realize, "oh yeah, there's a game this week."
Tyson Bagent probably gets the most criticism just one week after a win.
People forget Ben Johnson is 2-1 vs Green Bay with Caleb pic.twitter.com/Tn1keWmlAl
There's nothing really wrong with the Bears that can't be fixed, especially by one simple thing about their play. Of course, this is Caleb Williams' return. With as much productivity as Johnson squeezed out of Case Keenum against the Eagles in his start, there's nothing like having your starter and especially one thing about Williams.
Bears fans saw it if they were watching Josh Allen send the Rams to their third loss in five games. Remember, this was the team everyone said was a lock to win it all. And they're 2-3. How does that make Bears fans feel about their team?  It's early and no one should be too caught up in a 3-2 record is the message.
Rome Odunze's falloff needs to be studied. pic.twitter.com/QI73kV5clg
What the Bear saw from Allen is something they have when they get Williams back, provided he really is healthy. It's that ability to take it upfield if everyone is covered. It's the great deodorizer for Johnson if the play call doesn't work or is sniffed out by the defense.
The Bears have had 15 runs for 107 yards from Williams in less than two games of action. He had a 29-yard long, ran for seven first downs and two touchdowns. He might have even scored a third against Minnesota when he went down with the hamstring injury. His 29-yard run five weeks into the season is still top 20 for fastest runs in the NFL (16th, 20.78 mph).
This is the defensive rookie of the year huh? Dillon Thieneman is actually buns 😭😭😭 pic.twitter.com/Q9YKTjHyoB
He moved the sticks, put points on the board with his legs and his arm.
Meanwhile, without him for three starts and the end of the Vikings game the Bears have had three less rushing attempts from their backup QBs combined. Bagent has seven scrambles for 18 yards, Keenum five for 10 yards. Both ran 7 yards for a long. They have only one first down and had one touchdown from the two on the ground combined. Bagent has no rushing first downs and Keenum one. Bagent averages. 2.3 rushes per game and Keenum 1.7. Williams averages 7.5 rushes a game. This is a major factor for a team that loves the concept of ball control, or wants that added dimension to complement the pass, or just wants the running ability to set up passes off platform.
Jaylon Johnson's completion percentage allowed by year. 2020: 56.4% 2021: 59.7% 2022: 58.8% 2023: 55.2% 2024: 66.1% 2025: 72.7% 2026: 83.3%* He's been trending down for quite some time but this is as bad as it gets.
Josh Allen beat the Rams this way. Williams does it to Bears opponents.
It's about passing but if you can complement it with the run the passer's skillset is all the more dangerous.
Who deserves the most blame today? Jaylon Johnson Tyson Bagent Dennis Allen Ben Johnson Montez Sweat Rome Odunze Everybody?
Williams even can help the defense by letting them play with a lead or with the ball because of his ability to run.  Williams is the answer to what ails them in so many ways.
Before succumbing and getting in step with the group throwing in the towel on this season, simply remember what the team looked like in Week 1 on offense and can again once Williams returns and is throwing to his wide receivers and tight ends, throwing it farther downfield than Bagent, or running it like a running back at times.

title: Austin Booker Expressed Frustration Over Role With Bears Before Week 4 Game vs. Jets
full_text:
Chicago Bears defensive end Austin Booker is apparently not happy with his role over five games of the 2026 season.
A few days before the Week 4 game against the New York Jets, Booker spoke to Bears beat writer, The Score's Herb Howard , and expressed frustration with his role.
Booker told Howard that he wanted more snaps on defense.
"Two days before the Jets game, Bears DE Austin Booker expressed to me that he wasn’t happy with his role on the team," Howard wrote. "He wanted more playing time. In the two games since then Booker has 3 sacks and 4 (tackles for loss)."
Howard said he asked Booker on Monday if he had changed his approach prior to the past two games, when Booker has notched three sacks and four tackles for loss, and Booker responded:
“No. When the snap count goes up, the production goes up," Booker said.
Well, Booker's desire for more snaps was met on Sunday, as the third-year edge rusher played a season-high 44.  In the game against the Jets, he only played 20, although that did equate to 62.5% of the defensive snaps in the game.
It isn't clear if the increase in snaps was Booker getting the "squeaky wheel gets the grease" treatment or a result of the injury to Dayo Odeyingbo , who left after 23 snaps with a quad injury.
Booker played 40 (58.8%) in Week 1, but then saw his playing time dip to 19 snaps (36.5%) the next week, and then he played 30 (60%) and 20 snaps, respectively, over the next two games. The 44 snaps in Week 5 amounted to 72.1% of the total plays on defense for Chicago.
Booker was an absolute menace against Green Bay. Along with his two sacks and three tackles for loss, Booker also added four run stops and his 85.3 overall grade was third-best among the Bears defensive players, per Pro Football Focus .
It was the second time in his career Booker has tallied two sacks in a game. The other time came in Week 15 of last season, when he had two sacks and two tackles for loss in the win over the Cleveland Browns.
With those two sacks, Booker is now up to four on the season and is just 0.5 shy of his career-high, which he achieved in eight games last season. He ultimately played in nine but did not tally a sack in the Bears' regular season finale. He did, however, post another sack in the playoff win over the Green Bay Packers.
It isn't clear if Odeyingbo is going to miss any time with his injury, but if he does, Booker will almost certainly be locked into more snaps until the veteran returns.
Even if Odeyingbo plays, it's clear after Sunday that the Bears need to figure out a way to get Booker more involved.

title: Packers' Matthew Golden Calls out Bears' Cairo Santos Over Sideline Incident
full_text:
There was no shortage of storylines to come out of the Chicago Bears' disastrous Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. For one thing, any talk of Tyson Bagent becoming an intriguing trade piece for the Bears should come to a screeching halt. On the flip side of that, Bagent proved the immense value that Caleb Williams brings to the Bears , and Bears fans are hoping that he'll be ready to go for Week 6 against the feisty Atlanta Falcons.
However, there was one incident from the game that went mostly unnoticed until postgame comments from the players became public. On an offensive play for the Packers late in the first half, wide receiver Matthew Golden ran out of bounds with the ball to stop the clock and knocked a Bears' assistant coach off his feet . Fans can watch the video to judge for themselves, but Golden seemingly made little effort to avoid running into the coach.
Kicker Cairo Santos saw this and appeared to stick his leg out to trip Golden as he made his way back to the field. After the game, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic asked Golden about this incident, to which Golden dismissively replied, "It's all good. I ain't got nothing to say to him."
This altercation could have potentially escalated into an all-out brawl on the sidelines, but it still goes to show the passion in this rivalry. These are two teams that genuinely dislike each other and tempers have been at a boiling point ever since the Bears' triumphant Wild Card victory over the Packers last year. Since then, several Packers players have gone to the media to express their disdain for the Bears, both in the offseason and in the week leading up to this matchup.
That's exactly how things should be in this historic rivalry. The Bears and Packers have been dueling for over 100 years, and there should be bad blood between them. Unfortunately, the Packers' one-sided domination of the Bears since 1992, especially during the 15-year Aaron Rodgers era, put the rivalry on ice. It can't truly be a rivalry if one team is always winning, after all.
Thankfully, that's all in the past. Including the playoffs, the score is now 2-2 since Ben Johnson arrived in Chicago and breathed new life into the rivalry. That leaves the Packers still with a substantial lead in the all-time series, but the Bears are clearly no longer their punching bag, and honest Packers fans will admit that Sunday's game could have easily been a loss for them if Caleb Williams had been healthy enough to play.
Unfortunately for the Bears, they won't get another crack at the Packers until Christmas Day. This will be just the third Christmas matchup between these two teams, and the Bears will have the opportunity to not only take another 2-1 series lead over the Packers but can also wash the taste of this brutal loss out of their mouths.
Until that day, however, the Packers have earned the right to talk their smack. All the Bears can do is flush this game after what will likely be a rough film review. On the bright side, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported on Monday morning that 'all signs point' to Caleb Williams returning for the Bears' Week 6 game in Atlanta, and you can bet your bottom dollar that he's itching to remind everyone of what he can do on the football field.

title: Key Observations From Bears Snap Count in Their Week 5 Loss Against Packers
full_text:
The Chicago Bears suffered a tough loss against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday afternoon. Very few things went right for Chicago on either side of the ball in the blowout 31-7 defeat to their hated NFC North foes.
The offense came out flat with backup Tyson Bagent under center ( until he got benched in the second half ). The defense also had easily their worst performance of the season, which is saying a lot considering the fact that they gave up 37 points to Carolina in the season opener.
Surprisingly, it was pretty even from a time-of-possession standpoint (largely because the Packers had a lot of chunk plays and struggled to run the ball). Chicago's offense ran 69 offensive plays , and the defense was on the field for 61 snaps.
The official snap count on both sides of the ball produced a few interesting developments.
The most noteworthy development for the offensive snap count is how much 11 personnel they ran. The game script definitely played a role there, but the fact that they didn't have Kyle Monangai at their disposal also factored into the pass-heavy approach. They clearly missed his presence.
Rookie receiver Zavion Thomas saw a career-high 15 offensive snaps, and he actually got involved with an 11-yard catch and an 11-yard run. On an offense that did virtually nothing right, he at least stood out as somewhat of a bright spot .
Running back Roschon Johnson (27 snaps) played Monangai's normal complement of snaps (before the Week 4 explosion against New York, anyway), but he didn't make the most of them. He finished the game with only five attempts for six yards. D'Andre Swift (40 snaps) clearly wasn't 100%, but he still looked like their best offensive weapon.
With them trotting out three receivers far more often, Cole Kmet (29 snaps) saw a season-low in playing time by a wide margin. Coming into the game, his 43 snaps played against Carolina and Philadelphia were the fewest of the year. Third-string TE Sam Roush (5 snaps) also saw a season-low by a wide margin ( his previous was 12 in the season opener ).
It's also worth noting that Case Keenum (23 snaps) threw for 21 more yards than Tyson Bagent (46 snaps) despite seeing exactly half as much playing time. Both players had ugly performances, but it's painfully obvious who should start if Caleb Williams isn't healthy next week.
The most stark observation for the defensive side of the ball is why they were in base defense so much against Green Bay's weak rushing offense. Based on the snap counts, it seems like they had three linebackers on the field for 32 of 61 snaps (unless they had four backers on the field at the same time at any point, which I don't think happened).
Any way you slice it, that's an odd decision on defensive coordinator Dennis Allen's part. The Packers came into the game with the league's worst rushing offense, and they were constantly destroying the secondary with deep shots over the top. Good for Noah Sewell for playing 22 snaps in his first game back from being activated off IR. They still should've had more speed on the field.
With that said, an injury to Tyrique Stevenson (31 snaps) may have played a role. It was interesting to see Clark Phillips IIInot see any action as a result. Malik Muhammad II (49 snaps) moved to the outside, and Cam Lewis (36 snaps) moved down to the slot. I know Ben Johnson has a vendetta with Kyler Gordon, but he can't return to the field soon enough.
Edge rusher Austin Booker (44 snaps) led the defensive line in snaps for the first time this season, and that was for good reason. He was the only true bright spot on either side of the ball.
Dayo Odeyingbo 's day getting cut short (22 snaps) probably was a slight factor in why Booker was on the field a bit more. His absence had a bigger impact on the defensive tackles, though. Kentavius Steet saw a season-high 30 snaps, and James Lynch 's 27 snaps were only one away from his season high. Seeing the latter get right back into the swing of things after being a healthy scratch last week was a good sign.

title: Jaylon Johnson's Decline Has the Bears Facing a Hard Call on His $76 Million Contract
full_text:
A popular saying in the football world is that the NFL stands for "Not For Long". It's a notoriously results-based league, with popular players and coaches getting the axe if a cold stretch runs too long. Unfortunately for the Chicago Bears, one such player has just about hit that point after their disastrous Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers .
Two-time Pro Bowl cornerback Jaylon Johnson, the longest tenured member of Chicago's defense, is playing on the third year of his four-year, $76 million contract extension . The cornerback who signed that contract in 2024, however, is not the cornerback that we see on the field anymore, and it cannot be tolerated for another season. Despite all the good he did for the Bears in the past, the time is nigh for Johnson and the Bears to part ways.
While this may have been an unthinkable opinion just one year ago, it has become a regrettable reality. Through five weeks of the 2026 NFL season, one that Johnson himself views as a contract year , he's allowing a 118.8 passer rating when targeted, according to Pro Football Focus (PFF). He's been charged with three missed tackles, which is good for 63rd out of 155 cornerbacks, and has allowed 18 receptions, 86th out of 155 cornerbacks.
And that's not all. According to Pro Football Network's impact rankings , Johnson has earned just a 57.9 grade. For reference, a 75.0 grade is considered league average. Tyrique Stevenson, another Bear in danger of losing his job, grades out at a 65.0 while fourth-round rookie Malik Muhammad is earning an impressive 77.3 grade.
As bad as he's been all season, however, Week 5 had to be rock-bottom. Johnson seemed to be a part of almost every Packers highlight, from this touchdown pass to Christian Watson , which was the dagger despite almost the entire second half left to go, to this big gainer by Matthew Golden . Even in the run game, Johnson got obliterated on this eight-yard touchdown run by Marshawn Lloyd .
It always sucks to see a player lose his mojo, but that's what has happened with Jaylon Johnson. One wonders if the groin injury that plagued him throughout 2025 never fully healed, and if his mobility has been permanently capped. Some Bears fans suspect that Johnson was only good in the zone-heavy defenses favored by Matt Eberflus and is now struggling in Dennis Allen's man-heavy scheme.
Whatever the reason, the Bears are paying Johnson an annual average of $19 million to be the second-team All-Pro cornerback that he was in 2023, and they're not getting anywhere close to a fair return on that investment. According to Spotrac , the Bears can free up $16 million in salary cap space for 2027 by releasing Jaylon Johnson either pre- or post-6/1, and that needs to be at the top of general manager Ryan Poles' to-do list in the offseason.

title: Bears Defense May Have Caught a Break with Michael Penix Injury
full_text:
The Bears defense looked like it could use a few breaks on Sunday at Green Bay and may have received one already for their next game.
Starting Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix suffered a rib injury in Sunday night's 30-23 overtime loss to the Baltimore Ravens and had to leave the game in the fourth quarter. The Bears are at Atlanta on Sunday.
Penix has had numerous injuries over the course of his brief career, and went down after a hit on the Falcons' last drive of regulation. He was on the field, then got up and went to the bench in obvious pain. Tua Tagovailoa finished the game at quarterback for the Falcons after Penix was 19 of 32 for 240 yards and a touchdown.
Penix has played in three of the Falcons' five games and has a 104.84 passer rating with 52 completions in 77 attempts and three touchdowns with an interception. He has 719 yards in those three games.
MICHAEL PENIX TAKEN DOWN HARD HE IS IN PAIN pic.twitter.com/Ref6DhrROW
The Falcons are fortunate to have a former starter as backup in Tagovailoa, although he threw a game-ending interception in overtime Sunday. He wasn't available to start the season when Penix was out injured, and they started Cooper Rush. The Falcons lost both games Rush started against Carolina and Pittsburgh.
Tagovailoa went 2-for-3 for 34 yards with the interception in the Sunday night loss. He finished his six seasons with Miami after last year and had a 96.4 career passer rating with 120 TD passes and 59 on 68% completions. The only time the Bears have faced Tagovailoa, he threw for three TDs in 2022 in a 35-32 win for Miami at Soldier Field.
NEW -- Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr tells Dave Archer of the Falcons radio network he is going to "get some imaging" after a rib injury ended his night, "but it's nothing season-ending." pic.twitter.com/580rSUk4So
After the game, Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said the injury was causing great discomfort for Penix and he'd need an MRI of the injury before they knew more about it.
“He was trying to work to get comfortable and could not," Stefanski said at his postgame presser.
The Bears are not strangers to facing backup quarterbacks this season. They faced Vikings backup Carson Wentz in Week 2 and the result was a 9-3 defeat at home.
Whether it's indecision about who starts or an actual change at QB it can be a disruption for the Falcons and their process and the Bears could benefit on Sunday in a noon game.

title: Austin Booker Stats vs. Packers: DL Secures Multi-Sack Performance in Bears Defeat
full_text:
The Chicago Bears had a very poor defensive performance against the Green Bay Packers during a 31-7 loss in Week 5 . Bears defensive end Austin Booker did not, though.
Booker had two sacks, three TFLs, and a forced fumble in the loss.
Booker was the lone bright spot in a game that Chicago would probably like to forget as soon as humanly possible.
Quarterback Tyson Bagent threw two interceptions and was benched for Case Keenum , who threw a pick himself.
Linebacker T.J. Edwards, defensive lineman Dayo Odeyingbo, corner Tyrique Stevenson, and safety Cam Lewis all left the game with injuries .
Roschon Johnson only exacerbated the Bears' running back problem without a healthy Kyle Monangai by amassing six yards on five carries.
Jordan Love diced up the Bears defense for 367 yards and two touchdown passes on 25-of-31 passing. Love had four 40-plus-yard completions. Two of those passes found the hands of receiver Christian Watson in the end zone.
If it weren't for Booker generating pressure, who knows how much more Love would've embarrassed Chicago's defense at Lambeau Field.
Booker is rising to the occasion as the starting defensive end opposite Montez Sweat so far this season.
Booker has 14 tackles, four sacks, and two forced fumbles through the first four games. His strongest performances came against Green Bay and a dominant 27-7 win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 3.
With Odeyingbo out for an unspecified timetable, Booker has an increased opportunity to set the edge and get the run defense back to previous levels.
Booker also has the chance to disrupt opposing quarterbacks so the injury-riddled secondary isn't subjected to performances like Love had in Week 5.
Losing Edwards hurts the pass defense as well. His non-contact hamstring injury is a scary thought for the defense's ability to limit strong passing performances.
The Bears don't have true hopes of contending if the pass rush doesn't continue being a force.
Booker is a major piece of that puzzle moving forward.
While the Atlanta Falcons offensive line's greatest strengths are in the interior, left tackle Jake Matthews will provide a veteran test for Booker.
Jawaan Taylor may be more vulnerable on the right side when Booker is lining up on that edge.
As a unit, Atlanta has held up well in pass-protection, ranking near the top of the league in Pass Block Win Rate.
That has a lot to do with snap distribution, though.
Against a Falcons offense heavily skewed toward the run, Booker's added size should serve him well trying to catch Bijan Robinson this coming Sunday at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

title: Ben Johnson Has a Rivalry Problem and There's No Clear Answer
full_text:
This has probably been a rough Monday morning so far for Chicago Bears fans. A disastrous Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers sucked all the air out of the room, so to speak, and with it all the momentum the Bears had built up after their 3-1 start to the season. If there's a silver lining to the game's outcome, it's that no one should ever again question how much Caleb Williams means to this offense, and luckily for Bears fans, there's hope that he can return for Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons .
However, Sunday's loss highlights an uncomfortable question that must be asked regarding head coach Ben Johnson: why does he struggle so much against his division rivals? Since becoming head coach of the Chicago Bears, Johnson is just 2-6 in games against NFC North opponents, and both of those wins came on walk-off scoring plays. On the flip side of that, in Johnson's six losses to his rivals, the Bears are losing by an average of 12.3 points.
As much as it fires up Bears fans, Johnson may want to spend some time looking in the mirror to determine whether his trash talk is getting him into trouble. For one thing, his rivals are more motivated to hit him with their absolute best shots, and so far those shots have been devastating haymakers to the kidney.
We saw this play out all last week. Multiple Packers players took shots at Ben Johnson ahead of their Week 5 matchup , and now they've earned the right to strut their stuff as the victors. They walked the walk while Johnson only talked. The Vikings earlier this year held Johnson's offense to just three points. Yes, the weather played a big role in that, but the scoreboard didn't lie. Last year, facing off against his former boss in Detroit for the first time, Johnson took a humiliating 31-point loss to the Lions in just his second game as head coach.
Meanwhile, Johnson doesn't seem to be benefitting from his trash talk. He's not getting in the heads of his opponents. If anything, he appears to be getting inside his own head. In both of Johnson's two losses this year, he appeared stymied, groping in the dark for answers and finding none. We saw neither hide nor hair of the ruthless efficiency we've come to expect from the Bears, nor the jaw-dropping explosives.
I'm not saying that Johnson should completely rework his persona, nor that the trash talk is definitely the cause of yesterday's loss. Outside of rivalry games, he's been exactly who we expected him to be: a gifted savant and a master of his craft. What he's been doing is working and producing results. But for some reason, it's not showing up consistently in rivalry games, and Johnson must leave no stone unturned to figure out why. That includes a long, hard look in the mirror.
In the interest of fairness, it must be admitted that at least three of Johnson's NFC North losses come with some context. One came in Johnson's very first game as a head coach. In the Bears' ugly Week 2 loss to the Vikings , Soldier Field was rendered a soggy, sodden swamp by constant rainfall. On Sunday, Johnson was without his starting quarterback. It doesn't excuse those losses, but the context can't be ignored.
Nevertheless, Johnson clearly has a rivalry problem, and neither the cause nor the answer is clear. The Bears don't face another NFC North opponent until Week 12, a road game against the Detroit Lions. That gives Johnson nearly two months to figure out how to notch his first win against his former team and keep the Bears from sliding any further down the division standings.

title: Bears Report Card for Week 5 Vs. Packers: Last in the NFC North Again
full_text:
After playing a quarter on Sunday — which seemed like much more than some members of the Bears secondary or their other backup quarterback played — third-string QB Case Keenum beat up one of the most overused phrases at Halas Hall in any given week.
He decided to talk about the team's "identity."
"This is a tough resilient group," Keenum told reporters at Lambeau Field. "We are fighters. We're a really good football team. I know it didn't show today. But gol-ly I think i know guys are going to come and get back to work, get their bodies back right, get their minds back right.
"It's a long season. There's a lot you find out about yourself at this point in the season, about you're becoming the team you're going to be. Your identity is forged, sometimes through fire. It was in fire today. It was in the fire today, so we will see what kind of identity we have coming out of the back end of this thing.”
Too often Sunday the Bears looked like their identity was what really does come out of the back end.
As a result, they are now in last place in the NFC North.
Chicago Bears fans already turning on Ben Johnson 😂😂😂 pic.twitter.com/GnqRXomvs1
At the risk of channeling everyone's inner Dennis Green, they are who we thought they were. Their identity was obvious long before Sunday. They're a running team, a ball-control team and they need to take risks on defense to make up for personnel deficiencies. When they don't have Caleb Williams, they're all struggling on both sides of the ball.
The deficiencies were apparent everywhere on Sunday and here are their grades for a throwback game in Green Bay — the kind you throw back and an effort similar to those games they would play in the bad old days at Lambeau when Aaron Rodgers was Packers QB.
A 3.4-yard average per carry made it quite apparent how much the Bears missed Kyle Monangai. Early on, some of the running lanes were there but they closed gradually and eventually the Bears abandoned the run anyway. Only nine rushes for 43 yards for D'Andre Swift as he made his rebound from his egregious game against the Jets. Sunday, the whole offense was egregious. The one rushing positive was Swift's 1-yard fourth-and-goal TD burst up the middle. It was a tough play to pull off. If only Swift had done that against Minnesota instead of fumbling in that game.
rome odunze fumble issue now? #dabears B U S T one of the worst chicago bears of my lifetime man pic.twitter.com/TYwsw0VE9J
Tyson Bagent's 27.4 passer rating places him first place for the Rex Grossman Sweepstakes this year (0.00). Bagent's two interceptions were similar, even if one was tipped. They were late, over the middle and his arm can't deliver that type of pass. Keenum didn't get great pass protection but at that point in the game it's difficult to keep the passer free of traffic because the defense knew he was passing. At least he didn't eat the ball and take a sack on the fourth-down interception he threw, the way Bagent did in Chicago against the Vikings. Another typically disappointing week for the Bears receivers, especially Rome Odunze.
This might be one of the worst passes I’ve seen a Bears QB throw and that says a lot pic.twitter.com/tuW2i63pTB
It would be easy to look bottom line and 2.7 yards per carry with 70 total rushing yards says they did a fantastic job. However, they gave up a key 10-yard run to MarShawn Lloyd and later a 23-yard run to Kaleb Johnson. If they could duplicate this effort the rest of the year they wouldn't mind it.
Bears defense lets Watson score with ease pic.twitter.com/kRKkGp19ze
Even Austin Booker's sacks of Jordan Love on consecutive second-quarter plays couldn't cover for a pass rush lacking much life. Montez Sweat was held without a penalty call on the first Packers pass of the game, and Green Bay then drove 91 yards to a TD. Dillon Thieneman allowed two long TDs and Malik Muhammad struggled once the Bears moved him outside after Tyrique Stevenson's hamstring injury. Those two rookies making mistakes are anticipated. Seeing Jaylon Johnson beaten twice deep and six Love completions of 31 yards or longer says they need to bring Kyler Gordon back this week full time even if their plan said to gradually work him into the mix.
Zavion Thomas finally broke a kick return for 61 yards but that 4.28-second speed didn't keep him from being caught from behind. He veraged a healthy 26.2 yards on his other five returns. Cairo Santos missing a 43-yard field goal just doesn't happen. The snap by Scott Daly was a bit high but it was easily a kick Santos normally makes blindfolded.
Packers WR Matthew Golden appeared to intentionally knock over a Bears coach on the sideline and Bears K Cairo Santos tried to trip him out of retaliation. (🎥: NFL on FOX) pic.twitter.com/wK4DqcuGs1
Ben Johnson's game plan probably wasn't the kind of problem the execution was, but it was Dennis Allen's game plan on the other side that really caused problems. Too many of their DB blitzes got picked up and the wound up exposing their young DBs to Packer big-play attempts. When the Packers really had no running game to speak of, it should have been much easier for the Bears to scheme up heat on Love in the passing game. They still couldn't do it without blitzing.
Luther Burden said this week the Bears wanted to make the #Packers quit. Zaire Franklin heard the comments. "He quit today, by the way. He didn't want to play anymore." pic.twitter.com/aA34RXZoFw
The final score doesn't say the Bears were in it at halftime but they really weren't not long after that. At least they didn't telegraph their weakness shutting down the running game because that's the way the Falcons will attack them next week.

title: NFL Insider: 'All Signs Point To' Caleb Williams Returning From Injury For Bears in Week 6
full_text:
If there's one thing clear after the Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers, it's that the Chicago Bears need Caleb Williams back.
After the debacle that was Tyson Bagent's showing on Sunday, all eyes are now on Williams, who is hoping to return for the Week 6 contest against the Atlanta Falcons.
On Monday, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport laid out the situation with Williams and he said that "all signs point to" Williams making his return after a three-week absence.
"My understanding at the beginning of this whole thing was three to four weeks with a hamstring. He has missed three weeks," Rap said. "All signs point to Caleb Williams being back on the field this week for Chicago, which considering the way it went this past Sunday, would be quite good news."
Rapoport is basing that on all of the evidence we've seen since last week that shows Williams is, at the very least, very close.
Optimism for Williams' Week 6 return has been building up since Friday, when the Bears signal-caller took part in his first practice since he suffered the Grade 2 hamstring strain in Week 2.
After the limited session, Williams was given the questionable tag before being made inactive on Sunday. However, the bigger note was how Williams was working out on the field before kickoff and seemed to be moving around perfectly fine.
#Bears QB Caleb Williams warming up pregame vs. Packers at Lambeau Field. Williams is questionable (hamstring) today. @fox32news pic.twitter.com/Y5KO7NDNdW
We also know, according to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo , that Williams is "pushing to play" this coming Sunday.
"Really good news for the Bears the other day, with Caleb Williams returning to practice with that hamstring injury," Garafolo said.
"Not good news for (Week 5), really for next week, because this is Williams starting to work his way back and pushing to play next week. That's what I am told by multiple sources here," Garafolo went on to add. "The team is going to see how he does through the course of the week, so we really don't know how this is going to go, but this is Williams trying to get back right on the timeline."
After the loss to Green Bay, even head coach Ben Johnson would not rule out Williams making his return against the Falcons.
"(Williams is) on track," Johnson said . "We'll see if that's Atlanta or after. I think it's going to be close."
Not hard to see why Rapoport is saying "all signs point to" Williams making his return in Week 6. Every key indicator tells us that.
Now, we wait for our next injury update on Williams, which could come from Johnson on Monday, or from the injury report on Wednesday.

title: Bengals Announce Linebacker Addition During 2026 Bye Week
full_text:
The Bengals announced a roster addition amidst Swayze Bozeman's move to injured reserve. Cincinnati is signing former Jaguars linebacker Jack Kiser off of waivers to help fill the special teams void.
The 2025 fourth-round pick played in 14 games for Jacksonville, totaling 10 defensive tackles and four special teams tackles last season. He spent one game on the Jaguars' practice squad and was inactive for three games earlier this season, before being waived over the weekend.
He played for Al Golden at Notre Dame and should be able to slide in quickly on that front. Bozeman broke his arm but is expected back this season.
"Swayze (Bozeman) broke his forearm, so he'll go to IR," Taylor said about the latest injury updates earlier today. "Tanner Hudson has a pec issue that we're gathering more information on. Kyle Dugger (quad) is still week to week. Those are really the main three right now in terms of guys that would be affected coming out of the bye."
Cincinnati won a grimy 31-24 game on Sunday, but the Bozeman arm injury is the only major issue that popped up from the Miami heat. Now, the whole team gets to reset for a few days and focus on Baltimore next week.
"We had a tremendous opportunity coming out of the bye with the divisional game to put ourselves to the top there, and so right in front of us. So opportunity to get healthy, get your legs back under us," Taylor said today. "I do think the heat really hits well after Miami. I mean, I've never coached there for four years, never really thought about that. But the heat really does drain you, to the point where I'm sure it affects you the next week.
"So I'm happy that it hit for guys to be able to recover and get that, and then get your legs out under us and start getting ready for some colder weather, which we're very familiar with, as the season gets going here."
Kiser figures to work into the special teams unit soon after Bozeman played 64 snaps on the kicking units this season. The new Bengals LB played 193 played snaps last season on ST and none this campaign in Jacksonville.

title: Zac Taylor Updates Bengals Injury Situation Entering 2026 Bye Week
full_text:
Zac Taylor and the Bengals are back from Florida, with no major injuries added to the ledger after a rough week on that front. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins got through the game without any setbacks, and Zac Taylor discussed the team's overall health before entering the official bye week window.
Cincinnati is 3-2 on the season for the first time since making the Super Bowl during Chase's rookie year in 2021. The Bengals beat Miami 31-24 and didn't have any huge issues pop up after the game.
"Swayze (Bozeman) broke his forearm, so he'll go to IR," Taylor said about the latest updates. "Tanner Hudson has a pec issue that we're gathering more information on. Kyle Dugger (quad) still week to week. Those are really the main three right now in terms of guys that would be affected coming out of the bye."
The Bozeman blow stings, he has played 63 snaps for the Bengals on special teams this season.
The Bengals kept up with the rest of the AFC contenders this week and didn't lose any ground in the division. A group that could get really shaken up after Cincinnati's second division game of the season on Oct. 25 against Baltimore.
Cincinnati has two AFC wins so far and needs to amass as many as possible.
"Glad we won. Hard to win in this league. We've certainly been in those games before where we let them slip away and didn't get the win," Taylor said on Sunday. "Credit to Miami. They fought us tooth and nail till the very end. I thought Jeff Hafley is doing a great job with these guys, man. He's got them believing. They fought us like they fought a lot of other teams. They gave themselves a chance. There are a lot of frustrating things on our end. We had two personal fouls. We fumbled twice in the red zone. We caught a kickoff on the four-yard line. We had a penalty on a field goal that led to a touchdown, gave them four points, and gave up over 200 yards rushing. Plenty to clean up.
"The bye hits us at a great time. I know these guys are worn out. We've had some down-to-the-wire games the last three weeks. I know how hot this one was today. The bye week comes at a great time for us to be 3-2. These guys will regroup. We know who we are. Today, there are a lot of things we have to clean up to be better when we go to Baltimore in two weeks."
The Bengals lick their injury wounds this week before preparing for Baltimore.

title: Jordan Battle, Dalton Risner And More Pop With Strong Pro Football Focus Grades Against Dolphins
full_text:
The Pro Football Focus grades are in for the Bengals' 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday afternoon. Cincinnati leaders like Joe Burrow and Zac Taylor weren't too thrilled with how the team played, and the grades reflect that.
Cincinnati had its third-lowest team grade of the season (72.7) and only had 11 players grade out at 70-plus or higher. Starting on offense, Tight end Tanner Hudson made the most of his call-up with a team-high 89.9 PFF grade on 19 snaps.
The rest of the top five went in this order: Guard Dalton Risner (84.6), Joe Burrow (76.3), WR Ja'Marr Chase (75), and RB Samaje Perine (70.7).
Risner is posting his best year of grading since entering the league in 2019. He has a career-high 81.7 offensive grade and a career-best 80.7 pass-blocking grade powering that mark. He's currently the sixth-highest graded NFL guard with at least 190 snaps.
At the bottom, A few skill position players rounded out the low offensive grades, including Drew Sample (46.1), Chase Brown (47.3), Mike Gesicki (55.3), Tee Higgins (56.5), and Mitch Tinsley (58.8).
Brown and Perine were pretty close in snap count, at 38 for Brown to Perine's 33, something to monitor in the final two-thirds of the season.
Moving to the defense, defensive end Boye Mafe had arguably the best performance of any Bengal and continues to prove the team right for pivoting to him instead of sticking with the Trey Hendrickson train this offseason.
Mafe notched a defense-high 88 grade on 49 snaps. Five other Bengals defenders logged 70-plus grades: LB Demetrius Knight Jr. (79.2), safety Jordan Battle (79.2), DE Shemar Stewart (71 on only eight snaps), DT B.J. Hill (70.9), and CB DJ Turner II (70.3).
Linebacker Oren Burks also just missed out on that group with one of his best games as a Bengal. He had a 69.5 grade on nine fill-in snaps.
At the bottom of the defense, defensive end Cashius Howell (45.4) checked in with the lowest grade, followed by safety Bryan Cook (45.9), defensive end Cedric Johnson (47.5), linebacker Barrett Carter (52.4), and cornerback DJ Ivey (54.1). Cook had one of the Bengals' six missed tackles in the game.

title: Joe Burrow Reflects on Dominant Play in One Area During Bengals Win Over Dolphins
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals' backs were up against the wall coming into Week 5. After back-to-back losses, it felt that a loss to the winless Miami Dolphins would have sparked even more uncomfortable conversations around the team.
It wasn't the cleanest performance, but the Bengals got back in the win column with a 31-24 victory over the Dolphins. There are certainly some things that need to be cleaned up, however, quarterback Joe Burrow was on his A-game.
After his impressive performance on Sunday, Burrow spoke with the media and was asked specifically about his effectiveness in the red zone.
"Our receivers did a good job of finding space. We didn't get a ton of man coverage, but when we did, we made them pay," Burrow explained. "We had good field position most of the day, and I think for the most part we took advantage of it. But we had some dumb mistakes, and we got to get those fixed if we want to be a great team."
Three of Burrow's four touchdowns on Sunday were in the red zone. Like Burrow stated, if a team is going to give this offense good field position for the majority of the game, the unit has to make them pay. That's exactly what Burrow did.
Along with their red zone success, the Bengals converted 69.2% of their third down conversions. Extending drives is the name of the game, and this offense will bruise any defense if they can stay on the field.
This offense can be the most dynamic unit in the league. They proved that on Sunday. But there is still a lot to clean up before they take the field again in two weeks.
In particular, running back Chase Brown had some struggles hanging on to the football. The Bengals running back had two fumbles on the day.
Waiting for the Bengals out of the bye week is the Baltimore Ravens, who picked up a dramatic win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday Night Football. With the Bengals already suffering a loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, the game against the Ravens will be pivotal for the AFC North race.
Early bye weeks are brutal, but a reset at this point in the season may not be such a bad thing for a team that has already seen injuries to key players.

title: Zac Taylor Praises Toughness of 2 Bengals Offensive Stars After Win Over Dolphins
full_text:
After dropping two straight games, the Cincinnati Bengals found themselves in a must-win scenario when they took on the winless Miami Dolphins on Sunday.
In one of the hottest games played in the month of October, the Bengals put the past in the rearview, beating the Dolphins 31-24.
Was it a pretty game? No. But no team should ever apologize for winning a game in the NFL. It was a total team effort, and thankfully the Bengals' offense was near full strength.
During postgame comments with the media, Bengals head coach Zac Taylor spoke about the toughness of wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, who suffered injuries in the team's Week 4 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
"Hats off to them. They wanted to play, and Ja'Marr had to clear protocol on Saturday. His mindset all along was, 'I'm playing,'" Taylor stated. " Now I hadn't seen him on the field enough to know. I appreciate him saying that, but I need to see him do it in practice, and he did. For those guys to go out there and make plays that they did for us is a big time. I don't ever question that."
Chase had to exit last week's game against the Jaguars after a dirty hit concussed him. For Higgins, it was an adductor injury that had him coming into the game with the Dolphins feeling less than 100%.
Both receivers made an impact on Sunday's game, but it was Chase who showed no signs of dealing with a head injury. The Bengals star receiver made an unbelievable touchdown grab on a 45-yard dime from Joe Burrow in the third quarter.
Chase finished Sunday's game leading the Bengals in receptions with six and receiving yards with 77. As for Higgins, it was a little bit of a quieter day. The seventh-year receiver finished the game with two receptions and 22 receiving yards.
With a bye week coming up, it's nice to see that two of the biggest concerns on the injury front got through Sunday's game. The goal now is to rest and gear up for a long stretch of games thanks to drawing an unfortunate early bye week.

title: 6 Winners and 3 Losers From Bengals' 31-24 Win Over Dolphins
full_text:
In a game that did not feel as close as the score indicated, the Bengals beat the Dolphins in Miami 31- 24 to improve to 3-2 on the season.
Here are six winners and three losers from the Bengals victory over the Dolphins.
Battle stepped up in a major way after his struggles last week. After calling out Malik Willis' tells as a quarterback early in the week, Battle delivered on the confidence he displayed with two key interceptions.
The secondary consistently limited Willis' options, making him force throws outside of his comfort zone. This kind of bounce-back performance is the exact one that Battle needed after a week filled with criticism.
Lawrence committed two costly back-to-back penalties to extend the Dolphins opening drive. The first happened on a field goal attempt where the referees called him for roughing the center, with the second coming directly after for holding.
The Bengals have found their return man for the foreseeable future. Meyers returned the opening kickoff for 81 yards, setting up a Mike Gesicki touchdown to take a seven point lead in only three plays. Despite his mistake later in the game where he accidentally stepped out of bounds on a kickoff deep in Bengals territory, Meyers has earned enough faith from the coaching staff to feel secure.
All has not changed the Bengals offense as much as many had hoped so far. Now after he had an opportunity to make that impact, it is fair to wonder if he will at this point. After committing a bone-headed penalty that negated a short kickoff, All had a fumble that Miami nearly recovered if not for the defenders toe hitting out of bounds.
Perine at this point looks to be the most trustworthy runner the Bengals have in their backfield. He caught a six-yard touchdown from Joe Burrow in the second-quarter, and gained more opportunities following a horrendous Chase Brown fumble in the red zone.
Perine finished with 16 touches for 78 yards, a touchdown, and an average of 4.9 yards per carry. After this performance, Zac Taylor has to dial up a more balanced attack between Brown and Perine as the former has been largely ineffective this season so far.
As mentioned above, Brown lost a fumble in the first-half in the red zone and failed to make any true impact as a ball carrier. He finished with 16 touches for 60 yards and 3 yards per carry. Brown has done little to show he is deserving a big extension with the Bengals in a contract year.
Burrow controlled the game from from start to finish. He finished the game with four touchdown passes and 23 completions for 190 yards, and looked as poised as ever. This is the performance everyone should expect from Burrow against a lesser opponent.
Mafe got to Willis often in the backfield and forced the Dolphins quarterback to make hasty decisions, and even got home for his 3rd sack of the season. He also hit Willis while throwing to force an interception early in the second-quarter. Mafe continues to look like the young ascending player that the Bengals wanted when they signed him in the offseason.
Allen had a critical strip-sack late in the fourth quarter that the Bengals recovered. The turnover gave the Bengals the chance to take a 31-18 lead late in what ended up being a one score margin of victory. He now has three sacks on the season and has played exceptionally in the role of a pass rusher.

title: 'Mr. Reliable' - Bengals RB Samaje Perine States Case for Bigger Role in Backfield
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals run game looked a lot different Sunday afternoon in Miami.
And in more ways than one.
Coming off last week’s historically bad performance, the Bengals not only upped the volume and the efficiency of the rushing attack, but they also leaned heavily into backup running back Samaje Perine on the way to a 31-24 victory against the winless Dolphins.
The Bengals had a season-high 31 rushing attempts, with Perine leading the team in both carries (14) and yards (68). He also caught a pair of passes, including a 6-yard touchdown that gave the Bengals the lead for good with 11:51 left in the second quarter.
Perine’s 4.9 yards per attempt were much better than Chase Brown’s numbers, which saw him carry 13 times for 39 yards.
“I think he was finishing an extra 2 or 3 (yards),” head coach Zac Taylor said of Perine. “Got a lot of confidence in Chase. Sometimes you got two great backs that you've got trust in. That's just the way it can go sometimes, and I don't think there's anything wrong with that.”
Brown has struggled to get going this season, and the heavier volume for Perine on Sunday could lead to more of a split load after the team returns from the bye week.
Perine’s 4.86 average Sunday was the fourth highest of his Cincinnati career in a game in which he had at least 10 carries.
“I think I am effective whenever my number is called, whenever I need to be,” Perine said. “As the game goes on, I feel like I do become a stronger runner, just because if the defense has been out there for a long time, I feel like I'm wearing on them a little bit.
“I'm a bigger back, so they don't want to hit bigger backs that often,” the 5-foot-11, 240-pounder added.
“I wouldn’t want to try to tackle him,” Bengals center Ted Karras quipped.
Perine’s 14 carries against the Dolphins are tied for his third most in a game as a member of the Bengals.
In back-to-back weeks in 2022, the year before the team drafted Brown, Perine had 22 carries against the Chiefs and 17 against the Titans.
And Sunday’s workload came on day that goes down as the hottest road game in Bengals history and hottest October game ever at Hard Rock Stadium, which opened in 1987.
“I feel fine,” Perine said. “A little tired. Dehydrated. But I feel decent.”
Overall, the Bengals finished with 32 passes and 31 rushes, although two of those were kneel downs by Burrow after the Dolphins’ last-ditch onside kick attempt failed.
That output comes after Taylor and quarterback Joe Burrow both extolled the need for a more balance in the wake of last week’s loss to the Jaguars.
It helped that the Bengals jump out to an early lead and were up by 14 at halftime and eventually led by 18.
“That's just the way the game was played out,” Taylor said of the heavier reliance on the running game. “They're trying to give you some underneath stuff and let you run the ball a little bit, when you're in the gun there. You got to take advantage of it and get some yards there. And take advantage of the shots when you get the favorable looks for them, which we did with (the touchdown to Ja’Marr Chase).
“Eventually, they got to come up if they're going to be in those shells, come up and make a play. I thought they did a great job. They're well coached on defense. I thought their guys tackled well and they gave us a run there. They made it hard.”
Had it not been for Perine’s effectiveness, the Bengals may not have been able to lean into the run as much as they did.
Part of the self-scouting that will go on during the bye week will no doubt involve discussions on whether to make Perine a bigger part of the rushing attack.
It sounded as though Burrow would be in favor of it with the praise he heaped on Perine after the game, both for what he brings in the run game and pass game.
“He's just Mr. Reliable, and he has been my entire time here since he's been on our team,” Burrow said. “You can count on him to fall forward and get us an extra two. You can count on him to win against the linebacker in coverage. He's such a valuable piece for us and certainly doesn't get enough credit for it.
“Downhill,” Burrow added when asked why Perine is such a good fit for the offense. “We count on him a lot in protection too on third down to go not just block linebackers, sometimes defensive linemen as well. And I feel really confident that if I get it to him in space on third down, he's going to go make it happen for us. He's just such a valuable piece for us.”

title: 'Not Good Enough All Around' - Joe Burrow Aiming Higher After Bengals Road Win Over Miami
full_text:
Joe Burrow got a win in the NFL on Sunday, but it didn't seem like it from his reserved press conference. He drove home the mistakes Cincinnati made multiple times in a 31-24 result over the now 0-5 Miami Dolphins.
Cincinnati is entering its bye week with another massive divisional game on the horizon against Baltimore.
Committing untimely penalties and sputtering out on three punting drives could be a losing recipe on the road again October 25.
"I think just not good enough all around," Burrow said. "Team-wide. I think if we want to be the team that we think we're going to be, we got to be better than that ... Our receivers did a good job of finding space. We didn't get a ton of man coverage, but when we did, we made them pay. They made a good play there on the last third down. We had good field position most of the day, an I think for the most part we took advantage of it. But we had some dumb mistakes, and we got to get those cleaned up if you want to be a great team."
It marked the 10th time in Burrow's career he's tossed four-plus touchdowns in a game (14th time with a 126-plus passer rating), but he's more worried about the big picture and clearly wants to keep moving forward and not dwell on any milestones like that.
He had big praise for the stars gutting through injuries to come back and make plays like Ja'Marr Chase and more did today.
"You see what number one can do whenever the ball's in the air," Burrow said about the crazy 45-yard TD catch and touching on his toughness. "Obviously, unbelievable play, but we don't want to take it for granted. But we're used to it at this point, you know. That's football, man. That's football. When you have great players that want to be great and want to be there for the team, that's what it's all about."
Cincinnati flies back tonight and disbands for a few days this week before getting back to it for the final two-thirds of the season.

title: 'Dead Tired' - Bengals, Zac Taylor  Navigate Fall Heat to Get Back on Track Entering Bye Week
full_text:
Zac Taylor's Bengals team worked its way through record heat in Florida today to get on the winning side of a 31-24 result entering the bye week.
Cincinnati is 3-2 on the season after taking on the Dolphins during a real-feel game of 104 degrees at kickoff (hottest in Hard Rock Stadium history). The big-time heat may have caused a few more of the controllable penalties and final-drive malaise to cut the score closer, but they are 3-2 entering a few days off.
They are still last in the division due to tiebreakers, but it was a huge win. According to RotoWire, No team in the past 10 seasons has started 2-3 and made the Super Bowl.
"Nothing really at this point in October gets you ready for this heat," Taylor said. "I mean, somebody told me it started as the hottest game here in October history, which I can attest to. I've coached here for four years, and pregame; I was worn out. And so our players fought through that.
"Yeah, I told them. I made that statement to them because I know they're dead tired right now, and I didn't want them to think that's just in their mind. They're like, 'What's wrong with me?' It was a hot day, and they battled through it, and they found a way to win. And I don't discount that at all."
Cincinnati got a strong, surgical-type day from Joe Burrow (190 yards, four touchdowns, 126.3 passer rating). Still they only posted 4.9 yards per play to Miami's 5.2.
He fed the offense the right way after a week of injury questions all over, while Jordan Battle had the team's first multi-INT game since 2023 to keep Miami under 25 points.
It wasn't clean, but a win is a win in a league as tough and closely competitive as this one.
"There are a lot of frustrating things on our end. We had two personal fouls. We fumbled twice in the red zone. We caught a kickoff on the four-yard line. We had a penalty on a field goal that led to a touchdown. Gave them four points. Gave up over 200 yards rushing," Taylor said. "So, plenty to clean up. The bye hits us at a great time. I know these guys are worn out. We've had some down to the wire games last three weeks.
"I know how hot this one was today. So the bye week comes at a great time for us to be 3-2. These guys will regroup. We know who we are today. There are a lot of things we have to clean up to be better when we go to Baltimore in two weeks."
Cincinnati gets an extended rest period before returning to practice for Baltimore game planning.

title: Joe Burrow Leads Bengals to Much-Needed Win Over Dolphins: Instant Takeaways
full_text:
The Bengals beat the Dolphins 31-24 on Sunday in Miami. Cincinnati never trailed in the contest, maintaining a double digit lead for most of the second half.
The Bengals are 3-2 on the season following the victory. They ended a 2-game losing streak and are back over
Here are our top takeaways from the Bengals' win:
Burrow was outstanding on Sunday. He completed 23-of-32 passes for 190 yards and a season-high four touchdowns. He found Mike Gesicki on Cincinnati's first possession for a 4-yard touchdown.
He connected with Samaje Perine on a 6-yard touchdown to give Cincinnati the lead for good. Tanner Hudson snagged Cincinnati's third touchdown of the game and then Ja'Marr Chase had one of the best catches you'll ever see in the third quarter to put the game out of reach.
Chase made a one-handed grab for a 45-yard touchdown. Watch the play here .
Chase led the Bengals with six catches for 77 yards and a score. Erick All had three receptions for 25 yards. Tee Higgns had two catches on four targets for 22 yards. Burrow completed passes to nine different players on the roster: four tight ends, two running backs and three wide receivers.
The Bengals leaned into their rushing attack on Sunday. Samaje Perine led the way with 14 carries for 68 yards. He also had two catches for 10 yards and a touchdown. Chase Brown had 39 rushing yards on 13 carries and three catches for 21 yards and a fumble.
Overall, the Bengals leaned into their shotgun running attack and were able to move the ball on the ground. Cincinnati finished wth 119 rushing yards.
Battle mentioned Malik Willis had a "tell" when throwing the ball. He took advantage of that and had two interceptions. He also had six tackles and two passes defensed.
The Bengals' defense responded well for most of the game after giving up a touchdown on the Dolphins' first possession. Battle has three interceptions on the season.
The Bengals forced a third turnover late in the game when they knocked the ball away from Willis. Jonathan Allen recovered to secure the victory. The Dolphins scored a touchdown in the final minute to cut the lead to single digits.
Evan McPherson made his 22nd consecutive field goal in the fourth quarter. That's a new franchise record, breaking Shane Graham's record (21 straight). McPherson is 9-for-9 this season and has been as good as any kicker in the NFL this year.
The Bengals desperately needed a win after back-to-back losses. There are plenty of things to clean up, from penalties to fumbles—especially in the first half, but Cincinnati went on the road and got a much needed win ahead of the bye week. They showed they could run the ball, their defense forced turnovers and Burrow played well without turning the ball over.
This Bengals team has a chance to be a real contender in the AFC. They have flaws, but there's a lot to like about this group.
The Bengals are on a bye in Week 6. They play the Ravens in Baltimore on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 1 p.m. ET.

title: How Adding Notre Dame Standout Audric Estime Gives the Browns RB Room A Boost
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are adding a bit of insurance to the running back room.
On Monday, Oct. 12, it was announced that former Notre Dame standout and early NFL journeyman Audric Estime would be signing with the Browns . The front office, amid countless injuries to the running back room, is hoping that Estime can provide the depth with some much-needed depth.
He joins the team from the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad.
Sources: The #Browns are signing RB Audric Estime off the #Vikings practice squad to their 53-man roster. The 23-year-old Estime brings 508 career rushing yards, 130 receiving yards and 3 TDs to Cleveland. pic.twitter.com/cN57eboBz3
After losing RB2 Dylan Sampson earlier in the season, the team was dealt a bad blow on Sunday following a loss to the New York Jets. Starting back Quinshon Judkins was banged up, eventually leaving the stadium in a walking boot.
Just hours before the signing of Estime was announced, Browns head coach Todd Monken confirmed that Judkins and Sampson were still injured , but didn't give any insight into whether or not the two would be ready to suit up this weekend against the Baltimore Ravens.
Instead, he opted to say that every injured Brown wouldn't be fully ruled out yet.
But the signing of Estime does show that the Browns are at least somewhat planning for a future where another back is needed.
The 23-year-old was drafted in the fifth round of the 2024 NFL Draft, playing for both the Denver Broncos and the New Orleans Saints since then.
He has rushed for a total of 508 yards, three touchdowns and roughly 4.2 yards per carry across the last two seasons, tacking on 130 receiving yards along the way.
With a heavier workload, or just a decent increase in general opportunities in both the passing and rushing attack, Estime could become a legitimate threat in the Browns' offense. After all, he showed just how impactful he could be while in college.
Just to also add, Estime is 5-11, 227 lbs, and is a physical north/south runner. He did run a 4.58 40 time at the combine, so he’s not a burner, but this reads to me like a Jud replacement while they sit him down for his health. Also, an Audric Estime & Jaleel McLaughlin… https://t.co/fEkZjtEoEL
In his 2024 junior season, he was one of college football's best running backs.
He took off for 1,341 yards and 18 touchdowns on a whopping 210 carries. He averaged 6.4 yards per attempt and rushed for over 110 yards per game.
While he was never really a big-time receiver in South Bend, he did haul in 26 catches for 277 yards across his sophomore and junior campaigns.
With Estime finding so much success while being a member of the Fighting Irish, there is a strong thought that with the right scenario, he can unlock that talent once again.
At the end of the day, a signing like Estime doesn't hurt the team at all.
He is not going to immediately come in and change the depth chart, but he does give the team another young option out of the backfield. While he will certainly have to prove himself, the strugglesome start to the season from Judkins and the rest of the room will give him a better path to reestablishing himself in the league.
If Judkins and Sampson end up missing Sunday's contest against the Ravens, the Browns will likely turn to Raheim Sanders and Jaleel McLaughlin to take over most of the workload.
Well it took a couple years, but the Browns finally got Audric Estimé. The Browns are signing Estimé to their active roster off the Vikings practice squad. Coming out of Notre Dame, Estimé (5-11, 230) was drafted in the 5th round by the Broncos in 2024. The bruising back has… pic.twitter.com/A9vJJ6GIIP
However, all it takes is a few good practices, a solid first impression or an injury to someone else to immediately thrust him up the ladder and onto the gridiron.
For now, though, Estime will make his way to Cleveland and begin preparing for the Ravens this weekend. The two sides will clash at Huntington Bank Field at 1:00 p.m. EST on Sunday, Oct. 18.
