title: Browns Sign Running Back in Wake of Struggling Run Game and Injuries
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are looking for any way possible to give their run game a boost moving forward.
After suffering a tough 17-12 loss to the New York Jets this past Sunday, and Cleveland’s run game being virtually non-existent, the Browns had to make a move.
On Monday, the Browns went out and signed another extremely young option to hopefully boost their running back room moving forward.
Sources: The #Browns are signing RB Audric Estime off the #Vikings practice squad to their 53-man roster. The 23-year-old Estime brings 508 career rushing yards, 130 receiving yards and 3 TDs to Cleveland. pic.twitter.com/cN57eboBz3
Estime last played for the New Orleans Saints before being cut from the injured reserve just a few weeks ago. He was their preseason rushing leader, and has totaled 508 yards rushing on 122 carries in the 20 NFL games he’s appeared in.
He was picked up by the Vikings and put on their practice squad a little over a week ago but was picked up by the Browns on Monday to join their 53-man roster. This move was made in response to Quinshon Judkins’ injury sustained on Sunday.
Here’s why the signing of Estime makes sense for the Browns:
Aside from the recent injury to Judkins, the Browns are already without their backup running back Dylan Sampson, who was put on the injured reserve after his opening week knee injury.
Cleveland does still have Raheim Sanders in the backfield, as well as Jaleel McLaughlin, but outside of McLaughlin’s touchdown against the Steelers, both have been uninspiring options to lead the Browns’ backfield.
It’s not a good sign when the second leading rusher on the team is a 31-year-old Deshaun Watson at quarterback, and he only trails Judkins as their lead rusher by 54 yards.
In steps Estime, who brings two years of NFL experience to the Browns running back room. After starting his career with the Denver Broncos for 13 games, Estime played in seven games with the Saints.
It won’t be a permanent solution to Cleveland’s struggling run game by any means , but it’s worth a shot giving Estime playing time as he’s shown he can be serviceable. If the Browns want to develop their run game at all, they’ll need production out of Estime.
It isn’t expected that Judkins will miss an extended period of time , but after his significant injury suffered last season limited his availability during the offseason, the Browns might take it slow getting him back on the field.
The Browns have time to prepare for the Baltimore Ravens this Sunday, which is a great time for Estime to get up to speed with Cleveland’s playbook to ensure he’s ready to go moving forward.

title: If Deshaun Watson Keeps Losing, It's Time To Make a Change
full_text:
The rain was pouring down, and the offense was sloppy in the Cleveland Browns' loss to the New York Jets. The offense had a difficult time running the ball and protecting Deshaun Watson en route to scoring only 12 points.
The loss dropped their record to 3-2 and the Jets improved to 2-3.
Watson did not have a good game as he held onto the ball too long, leading to eight sacks. His decision-making was slow, and he did not even get a throw off on the last play of the game. The Browns even surprised themselves with a 3-1 start, and the odds of them making the playoffs increase exponentially at 4-1. However, they lost and the season may have a different outlook.
They fell to second place and will have to play the 4-1 Baltimore Ravens next week to try to keep pace in the division. The Jets game was considered very winnable, and the Browns should have come out victorious to make the playoffs more possible.
If the Browns’ offense continues to play poorly and losses start to mount, then they need to make a change at quarterback. Outside of a miracle, the Browns can finally move on from him after the season. They have to decide the future of the most important position in all of sports.
Should losses start to stack up, then the Browns may be in a position to draft a top quarterback from college. They also have backup Shedeur Sanders on the roster and he has not had a chance to show what he can do in Todd Monken’s offense so far this season. If the playoffs are not in the fold for the season, they have to see what Sanders can bring to the offense.
NFL purgatory is being “in the hunt” without making the playoffs. As the playoff contention window gets closer to shutting, then the move has to be made to evaluate Sanders.
The Browns also have two more games before having to make a decision on activating Dillon Gabriel from the injured list or shutting him down for the season with the injury designation. In the next two games, the Browns play the Ravens and the Tennessee Titans.
If the Browns lose both games, their record would drop to 3-4, with losses to the one-win Jets and zero-win Titans. Being under .500 pummels the odds of making the playoffs, and they would have lost to two bad teams. Watson should then be benched, and the Browns would still have time to play Sanders; if he shows he cannot play, then they can also see what they have in Gabriel.
Although Watson has led three game-winning drives so far this season, he has still not been overly impressive. There have been long stretches in each game where the offense goes stagnant. The game against the Jets was not all his fault, as the offensive line was bad, the receivers dropped good passes, and there was no running game, but he did not do enough to win.
They are still over .500 and one game should not alter the season, but winning will get more difficult if the offense continues to look like it did on Sunday. Todd Monken claimed that Watson gives the team the best chance to win, which he did for the first quarter of the season. If he cannot continue to win, then the Browns have to move on.

title: Todd Monken Shares Positive Update on Browns Running Back Injuries
full_text:
Well, the Cleveland Browns learned they still have more to work on.
Losing 17-12 in a Sunday duel with the New York Jets , the Browns moved to 3-2 on the season. While a loss is always going to be difficult to swallow, especially when it ends a three-game winning streak, what followed made the entire road forward even bumpier.
#Browns HC Todd Monken said Quinshon Judkins "had a little tweak" in his ankle from yesterday's game, which is why he left in a medical boot. Monken described Judkins as "day-to-day."
Already without running back Dylan Sampson due to an injury occurring in the season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Browns found out starting back Quinshon Judkins was newly banged up as well.
After the loss to the Jets, Judkins was seen in a walking boot, casting doubt on his health.
On Monday, Oct. 12, head coach Todd Monken confirmed that Judkins was dealing with an ankle injury. However, he did say that he wouldn't rule out any of the team's injured players for the Browns' Week 6 clash with the Baltimore Ravens, which includes Judkins.
He is considered day-to-day, though.
Along with Judkins, Sampson's timetable to return to the gridiron is unknown. The team is considering opening up his practice window this week, but the possibility remains up in the air as he continues to recover from his early-season knee injury.
Browns coach Todd Monken said there is a “possibility” the team opens RB Dylan Sampson’s practice window this week. He’s missed the last 4 games with a knee injury.
For a team that was looking at potentially being without an RB1 and RB2, hearing that both are not officially counted out for Sunday's game against Baltimore is a positive sign.
With both Judkins and Sampson still not fully healthy, the Browns may have to turn to a backfield that features just Raheim Sanders and Jaleel McLaughlin as of now. And while both have shown little spurts of promise this season, there has not been a clear path ahead for anyone in the room.
As a team, the Browns have just 471 rushing yards on 126 attempts , finding the end zone twice along the way.
Through five games, that is less than 100 rushing yards an outing, a far cry from where the franchise has been in the past.
It's hard to blame one player in particular, especially considering the offensive line is still brand new and the whole unit is attempting to find its identity with starting quarterback Deshaun Watson leading the charge, but Judkins averaging just 3.0 yards per carry and Sanders and McLaughlin only receiving 11 combined handoffs to start the year, the Browns are going to be facing an uphill climb moving forward.
Both Sanders and McLaughlin, at least right now, don't feel like stomachable options out of the backfield for the next few weeks, especially as the Browns still look to establish a dynamic offense.
It wouldn't be shocking to see the front office go out and add a third option to the backfield if Judkins and Sampson both aren't ready to return by the weekend.
As the week continues on, Monken will certainly continue to provide updates on the two.
The Browns and Ravens clash at 1:00 p.m. EST from Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland for an in-division clash on Sunday, Oct. 18.

title: 24 Hours Later: My Thoughts on Lackluster Browns Performance in Week 5 vs. Jets
full_text:
In a few months, we may be looking back on this game as the reason the Cleveland Browns missed the playoffs.
24 hours later, here are my thoughts on the Browns week five loss to the Jets
. @TheOGPAW and @HammerNation19 are wondering how much blame should be put on Quinshon Judkins on the Browns lack of run game. pic.twitter.com/iBaG4EslnE
The Browns had countless chances to score on offense. I understand the rain made things a lot harder, but there's always a way to get things done.
The Jets came into the game with the NFL's 25th-ranked run defense . Despite this, the Browns failed to establish a run game. They finished the game with 96 rushing yards, with 40 of them coming from Deshaun Watson.
Outside of the ground game, the worst moment of the contest by far came with just 4:13 to play.
Cleveland had just scored a touchdown. On the next defensive drive, Carson Schwesinger strip-sacked Jets quarterback Geno Smith. This gave the ball back to the Browns with the lead, 4:13 left to go, and in Jets territory.
You would think Todd Monken and the Browns offense would simply want to burn as much clock as possible right?
Instead, Quinshon Judkins ran the ball out of bounds, and after back-to-back incompletions, the Browns only took 21 seconds off the clock. Of course, this led to the fumbled punt, which set up the Jets for the win.
Outside of the special teams error, this drive is what lost the Browns the game. The inability to take either time off the clock or timeouts away from the Jets was incredible. Instead, Monken got too cute with the football, trying to put an end to the game.
This season, when the opponent figures out how to stop the Browns offense , that has been it. The best example of this was the week four game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Cleveland scored 21 of their 27 points in the second quarter. After halftime, the Browns had a scoreless third quarter followed by a squeaked out win in the fourth after leading by 14 earlier in the game.
Todd Monken and Deshaun Watson need to find a way to reset the offense during bad times throughout games. When things go wrong, they need a formation or set of plays they can confidently run despite the circumstances.
Outside of some great film on situational failure to review, the Browns need to move on from this game.
This loss cannot take away from the incredible start the team had with three straight game-winning drives. Looking at the schedule, the Browns have some very winnable games coming up.
This week, they play the Baltimore Ravens at home. Lamar Jackson's status is unclear at the moment, but it should still be close, with the defense. After that game, the Browns play the 0-5 Tennessee Titans, the Steelers once again, and then the 1-4 New Orleans Saints.

title: 2 Glaring Holes in the Browns Offense that Need Addressed Now
full_text:
So far this season, we have seen the Cleveland Browns on display five different times. Clearly, there are two big things that need to be fixed on Offense
With the NFL Trade deadline less than a month away, these positions are two the Browns should aim for in potential trades.
Ever since Quinshon Judkins was injured against the Bills last season, we have yet to see him return to that rookie-year form.
It doesn't help that Dylan Sampson went down with an injury in week one, but the Browns still should be getting it done with the former Buckeye.
If Cleveland decides it wants to improve the running back room, I do not expect them to fully get rid of Judkins. Instead, I see a trade to either bring in help alongside Judkins or to block for him.
That brings us to the main position group that needs to be reworked.
This is such a complicated group because all five starters are brand new to the team this season.
Is it a lack of experience? Two of the five big men are rookies who are only five games in to their professional careers.
Is it a lack of playing time together as a unit? The line has had all offseason to mesh, so you would hope that would be enough time to learn assignments and how to work together.
Regardless, the unit ranks dead last in sacks allowed with 19 this season. At this rate, the Browns are on pace to allow 65 sacks this year.
In the run game, the Browns are averaging just over 94 yards per game. Most of the time, 20-30 of those yards are coming from Deshaun Watson on scrambles.
Would you trade Jerry Jeudy to the Titans for Tony Pollard? Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay proposed the two teams swap players to help bolster areas of weakness on each roster. "No other Browns back outside of starter Quinshon Judkins has garnered more than six carries or eclipsed… pic.twitter.com/aXaVm1VTie
The Tony Pollard, Jerry Jeudy swap has been thrown around for the past few weeks. If the trade is legitimate, it is something the Browns should absolutely consider with Tennessee.
Pollard could bring another aspect to the Browns' run game as a dynamic runner, while Jeudy could go in as a much-needed pass-catching option for Cam Ward.
As for the Offensive line, the name doesn't matter nearly as much as the experience. The Browns need to go after a strong run blocker who has had reps with a winning line in the past.
Overall, changes need to be made to the Cleveland offense if they truly want to go all in for a playoff push this season.

title: Deshaun Watson Takes Accountability After Browns’ Loss to Jets
full_text:
Deshaun Watson said the Browns’ difficult afternoon against the Jets was no excuse for an offense that struggled to protect him or sustain drives.
Cleveland fell 17–12, and Watson was sacked eight times while completing 15 of 33 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown. He credited New York’s defense for changing its pressure looks and attacking from different directions.
“ You just got to give the Jets credit . They did a good job of showing different pressures and bringing it from all over the place,” Watson said.
The conditions made throwing and catching difficult, and the Browns had several drops. Watson said Cleveland couldn’t use the weather as an excuse.
“We try not to make that an excuse. We just try to adjust to the elements as best as possible and try to make as many plays as we possibly can,” he said.
Deshaun also discussed the challenge of starting drives deep in Cleveland territory while the run game struggled. The Browns had to find ways to move the ball and escape those difficult situations.
“It’s always tough being backed up. Anytime we possess the ball, we try to put in a drive, regardless of where we’re starting. But it’s tough to go 90-plus yards versus any defense in this league, especially consistently,” Watson said.
The veteran QB also acknowledged how difficult it was to lose KC Concepcion early. The first-year wideout from Texas A&M had been a major part of the game plan, but Watson said Isaiah Bond did well stepping into a larger role. Bond finished with three catches for 74 yards.
Cleveland had a chance late. Watson connected with Denzel Boston for a touchdown, but the Browns couldn’t finish the comeback. A penalty and a sack derailed their final possession.
“There was still hope. There were still opportunities, and again, they capitalized on it better than us...not good enough to win. We didn’t get the W. That’s all that mattered for me," Watson said.
The Browns now turn to Baltimore. Watson said the offense needs to improve its communication and alignment, and he put some of that responsibility on himself as the quarterback.
“Being the quarterback, being a veteran guy, just making sure that before we break that huddle, we’re all on the same page. I think that’s the key,” Watson said. “Operation comes first, and communication comes right there with it.”

title: 3 Biggest Problems in Browns Loss Sunday vs. Jets
full_text:
Sunday was a rude reminder that the ebbs and flows of the NFL can make you feel like you’re on top of the mountain or in a deep valley.
The Browns came in at 3-1, on fire after a primetime divisional win against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and they were quickly put out by the rain in the Meadowlands.
New York outlasted Cleveland 17-12 in a wet, sloppy game all around. The young aspect of this team showed up in a big-time way, and while they have pulled out three games in a row in the fourth quarter, these struggles were too much to overcome.
In total, today Cleveland rushed for 96 yards on 24 carries; 40 of those yards came from Deshaun Watson, and Quinshon Judkins rushed for 44 yards on 14 carries (3.1 YPC). Even though Judkins is coming off an injury, he has still not been able to crack over 4 yards per carry through the first five games.
The run-blocking has not been up to par with the pass-blocking, as Cleveland ranked 30th in the league in run-block win rate (70%) coming into the week , and 17th in pass-block win rate (49%). Hopefully Judkins is healthy also after leaving the locker room in a boot, but the run game needs to be better in order to win these close games.
The Browns were able to force two lost fumbles, along with two more fumbles that were recovered by New York, but unlike last week, they could not do anything with the ball when they got it.
The fumbles that Cleveland took away came in crucial spots also, the first coming with the Jets threatening inside the Cleveland 15-yard line with under six minutes to go in the third quarter, where Quincy Williams forced the ball out, and Ronnie Hickman was there to recover. The Browns then went three-and-out on three run plays and punted it right back to the Jets.
The second fumble taken away came with 4:20 left in the game, after the offense was finally able to find the end zone and take their first lead of the game, 12-10. Cleveland needs to close the game out at this point; if they’re able to get a couple of first downs or just eat up some clock and flip the field, it will be a win for the offense.
But what do the Browns do? They take just 21 seconds off the clock and are forced to punt; Corey Bojorquez then mishandles a high snap, and New York gets the ball at the Cleveland 23-yard line.
The weather was obviously a huge factor in this game, as we saw many fumbles by both teams, along with lots of dropped passes. In total, though, the Browns mustered up 198 yards: 102 passing and 96 rushing.
Watson threw for 155 yards, but was sacked eight times for a loss of 53 yard s, which is subtracted from the team’s total passing yards.
Watson was sacked six times over the past three wins, but him going down eight times today was a mix of bad protection and him trying to extend plays with his legs.

title: I’m Most Concerned About This One Thing With the Browns Through Five Weeks
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns still have work to do.
After beginning the 2026 NFL regular season with a strong 3-1 record, the Browns returned right back down to reality.
On Sunday, Oct. 11, the Browns fell to the New York Jets on the road from MetLife Stadium by a final score of 17-12. While they entered the game as underdogs, that public perception became apparent as the offense struggled to get anything going.
"It comes down to making the other team play their best. And I don’t think we did that today," head coach Todd Monken said postgame.
The weather conditions in New Jersey certainly played a role in making such issues obvious, but there is a major concern following the organization.
And unfortunately, it hasn't gone away week after week.
For the first time since becoming a member of the Cleveland Browns, starting quarterback Deshaun Watson looks like a mobile quarterback. He is routinely moving around in the pocket, scrambling to pick up extra yards and connecting with receivers downfield on the run.
He finished Sunday's loss to the Jets with 15 completions for 155 yards and one touchdown.
However, he was sacked a whopping eight times and wasn't able to convert on third down 12 total times. With Watson being consistently pressured by the Jets' defense, they made the Browns' offensive line look abysmal.
“It’s coaching. It’s playing, it’s getting the ball out of our hands. It’s protection," Monken said when asked about the high number of sacks. "It’s all the above … We all gotta take a big freaking bite of this.”
4th and long and deshaun watson is stopped for a 1 yard gain pic.twitter.com/COpZ6QGehE
Now, on the season, Watson has been sacked 19 times.
In the Week 1 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on the road, he was sacked five times, before the offensive line somewhat turned things around as they held the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Carolina Panthers and Pittsburgh Steelers to just two sacks each.
Either way, with a less mobile quarterback, the Browns' line would likely be giving up even more sacks than the statistics show.
There are players who are obviously looking the part, most notably rookies Austin Barber and Spener Fano, elevating a position group that went through extensive changes in the offseason, but there are still plenty of improvements needed to be made.
And it isn't just Watson who is struggling due to the offensive line's inability to provide ample room to move.
The Browns' go-to rusher out of the backfield, Quinshon Judkins, has had an eye-poppingly slow start to the season.
He carried the ball 14 times on Sunday, rushing for just 44 yards, an average of 3.1 yards per carry. On the season, his total numbers see him with just 221 yards on 73 carries, with him finding the endzone just once. He is barely averaging north of 3.0 yards per carry.
If the Browns truly want to be a multi-dimensional offense, that ability to establish both the rushing and passing game comes from the line's protection.
“You’re going to put yourself in that position when you can't run the football," Monken continued when asked about the high sack count. "We weren't able to run the football today. We were behind the sticks the whole day and we made a few plays, some (to) get back on track and some third downs that gave us a chance...
"But we were never comfortable calling it or playing. And that's not a recipe for success.”
Monken: “You’re going to put yourself in that position when you can't run the football. We weren't able to run the football today. We were behind the sticks the whole day and we made a few plays, some (to) get back on track and some third downs that gave us a chance, but we were… https://t.co/drjFJxMPvG
Moving forward, it simply needs to be better. Not just for Watson, but for Judkins and the rest of the running back room, too.
The Browns return to the field on Sunday, Oct. 18, for a Week 6 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens at 1:00 p.m. EST.
And with hopes of maintaining the top spot in the AFC North, they'll have to make that one big change.

title: The Browns Have 3 Major Issues That Could Derail Their Season
full_text:
After the Cleveland Browns lost to the New York Jets 17-12 in week five, one thing is very clear about this team: They do not have what it takes to perform like a top team in the league.
The Browns need to clean up some aspects of their game and stop getting cute with the football.
Browns' Head Coach Todd Monken is in his first-ever season as an NFL Head Coach.
With some of the play calls and decisions the Browns made in a very winnable loss to the Jets , that lack of experience was very clear.
While the rain played a big factor in the matchup, mother nature is not the one with the headset on calling plays from the sideline.
It seemed as if everything Monken learned about play calling for Deshaun Watson through the first four weeks was thrown out of the window.
Rather than simple screens or quick passes, Monken tried to go for longer developing plays that ultimately failed miserably against New York's strong pass rush. In the game, Watson was sacked eight times.
Monken needs to realize he is no longer calling plays for Lamar Jackson, but Deshaun Watson.
At the end of the first quarter, KC Concepcion was ruled out with a concussion after a dirty hit from Jets' safety Minkah Fitzpatrick.
Without their first-round rookie, you would think Monken would focus the playcalling on trying to target the NFL's rookie receiving leader, Denzel Boston, or reliable tight end Harold Fannin Jr.
Instead, Boston and Fannin combined for only 11 targets throughout the entire game, while guys like Isaiah Bond and Jerry Jeudy split 14 targets.
As the head coach, you have to be able to recognize those guys who are able to make big plays and then find ways to get them the football.
Once again, Deshaun Watson is not a top-tier quarterback who will win games for you. While he may make some nice plays, offensive production heavily depends on the skill positions making plays themselves.
Carson Schwesinger forces a massive turnover, @Browns ball! @CLEvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FQHcn2V9Tc
With four minutes left to go in the game, the Carson Schwesinger strip-sacked Geno Smith. With the ball in Jets territory and the lead, you would think the Browns would try to drain the clock or maybe the Jets' timeouts. Instead, they ran the ball out of bounds and had back-to-back incompletions.
In that time, they only took nine seconds off the clock before the muffed punt from Corey Bojorquez. Clearly, it was that sequence that cost them the game just after taking their first lead.
Other than this moment, the Browns had multiple chances to make plays in a game they should have won.
If they can go back home next week, clean it up, and keep it simple, they will be in a much better spot trying to face off with the Baltimore Ravens.

title: Cowboys Monday Injury Report Leaves Dallas Thin at Cornerback
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys were back on the practice field on Monday, preparing for a Week 6 showdown with the Green Bay Packers. This was always going to be a tough game, but the Cowboys enter this one low on confidence following a disheartening loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday Night Football.
Their task could be even more challenging after seeing the number of injuries they were dealing with in the secondary.
Dallas didn't have DaRon Bland or Calean Carson, leaving them thin at cornerback. Both players were dealing with an illness , and were sent home, so there's a chance they could be fine by the time the weekend rolls around.
There were multiple defensive backs who were limited as well, with Ameer Speed and Shavon Revel Jr. sitting out of drills. There was no update on what injuries they had, but it's concerning to see so many key players out. Especially with Cobie Durant (hamstring) and P.J. Locke (foot) working with the rehab group.
Some notable absences at practice today in the Cowboys secondary. We didn’t see DaRon Bland or Caelen Carson. Ameer Speed and Shavon Revel Jr. weren’t participating in drills. Cobie Durant and PJ Locke were both working in the rehab group. At least Joey Porter Jr. was back. pic.twitter.com/aLQohfFp4d
There was one positive note for their secondary as Joey Porter Jr. was back after missing Week 5 with an illness . It was a shocking turn of events for Dallas to lose Porter right before the game, but he will be back to take on a talented Green Bay offense.
Here's a quick rundown of what the Cowboys were dealing with during Monday's practice.
OUT: DaRon Bland, CB (Illness) Caelan Carson, CB (Illness)
Limited: Shavon Revel Jr., CB Ameer Speed, CB P.J. Locke, S (Foot) Cobie Durant, CB (Hamstring) DeMarvion Overshown, LB (Hamstring)
Full Participant: Jaishawn Barham, LB (shoulder) Joey Porter Jr., CB (Illness) Tyler Guyton, LT (Back)
Dallas lost starting linebacker DeMarvion Overshown to a hamstring injury during their Week 1 loss to the New York Giants and have yet to get him back on the field. On Monday, Overshown said he was feeling great and is hopeful he can play this weekend.
"I feel better than when I felt when the injury happened," Overshown said via Tommy Yarrish of the team's official website. "I'm running around, I'm doing everything you can as a football player. These [hamstring injuries] are tricky. You can have six good days in a row and then out of nowhere, something happens. Right now I'm feeling great. I'm feeling like I can run around and do everything I could before the injury. At this point, it's just how practice goes throughout the week. How the [hamstring] handles all the stresses of a full 60 minutes of football."
Overshown has been a dynamic playmaker when he's on the field, but his injuries have kept him sidelined for much of his career. If he can return to full health and stay in the game, it would be a huge boost for a defense in desperate need of help.

title: Cowboys Tyler Guyton Lands Among NFL's Elite in One Major Category in Week 5
full_text:
Thursday was a bad game for the Dallas Cowboys , who lost 24-16 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday Night Football. There was very little to get excited about during that defeat, especially with Michael Irvin saying the sideline felt "hopeless" as they were being outperformed.
That doesn't mean there was nothing positive to take from the game. One example is the performance of Tyler Guyton, the Cowboys' starting left tackle who is in the midst of a breakout season. In Week 4, Guyton stood out for his stellar pass protection as he kept Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter from ruining their offensive game plan.
In Week 5, it was his run blocking that turned heads. According to Pro Football Focus, Guyton had the second-highest run-blocking grade, earning a 91.5. The only player ahead of him was Penei Sewell of the Detroit Lions, who earned a 93.4.
Highest run blocking grade so far in Week 5 Penei Sewell              93.4 Tyler Guyton              91.5 Christian Haynes     90.4 Ed Ingram                   88.7 Dalton Risner            87.9 pic.twitter.com/N8QVHQxdEV
There's still one game to go with the Los Angeles Rams hosting the Buffalo Bills, but it's hard to see anyone surpassing Guyton and Sewell. Even if they do, it won't take away from the dominant performance from the 2024 first-round pick.
For Guyton, this isn't wildly surprising. He's been one of the top offensive tackles in the league this year. He enters Week 6 with an overall PFF grade of 73.8, which is the 15th best at his position. He's been especially strong in the run game, earning a 90.0 which is the third highest .
Ahead of this season, Guyton was already seen as a strong run blocker, but his ascension in pass protection has been what's stood out. Through five games, he's allowed 12 pressures and zero sacks. He's also been incredibly disciplined, with just one penalty in 317 snaps.
With the performance of Guyton this year, it's hard to imagine that there was a time when his starting position was in question.
Ahead of training camp, head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Guyton would need to earn his job as he battled Nate Thomas. Guyton quickly secured the spot and by the beginning of the season, Thomas was no longer on the team, being traded to the Houston Texans.
Thomas was replaced as the swing tackle by Broderick Jones, who was added in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers.

title: Cowboys Hire Former Packers DC, Browns HC To Help Struggling Christian Parker
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are bringing in a reinforcement on the coaching staff to help defensive coordinator Christian Parker.
According to head coach Brian Schottenheimer on Monday, the Cowboys hired former Cleveland Browns head coach Mike Pettine to serve as a senior defensive assistant with the goal of helping Parker.
"Had a chance to work with Pettine for a number of years, along with the Jets, and he's gonna be here in a role to support everything that [Christian Parker] is leading and guiding, and we are really, really excited," Schottenheimer said. "They worked together in Green Bay, and this is actually something the C.P. and I talked about when we first hired him."
In 2019 and 2020, Parker was a defensive quality control coach under Pettine, who was the defensive coordinator of the Green Bay Packers, a job Pettine held in 2018, also.
Schottenheimer noted there was at least one other candidate for the job, but ultimately the Cowboys decided to go with Pettine because of his experience with the 3-4 defense.
I think Pet's experience, not only in football, but as experience in this system, of what we do, is understanding of the 3-4 family," Schotty said.
The hiring of Pettine comes amid the Cowboys having serious struggles on the defensive side of the ball . Despite a total revamp of the defense, Dallas has one of the worst units in the NFL.
But it isn't just about the play on the field, as Parker has looked overmatched in his first year as a play-caller and it's very clear Dallas could use another voice in the defensive room to help Parker figure out how to right the ship.
Pettine is a good choice to be that guy thanks to his wealth of experience. It also helps that Parker is familiar with Pettine, which will make this a more comfortable situation for the defensive play-caller.
This move also amounts to an admission that, for whatever reason they may believe, the Cowboys fully realize that Parker needs help. We definitely can't be mad at that.
Pettine has extensive experience as a defensive coach in the NFL. He started as a coaching assistant with the Baltimore Ravens in 2002 before being promoted to assistant defensive line coach in 2004 and then outside linebackers coach in 2005.
He then served as the defensive coordinator of the New York Jets, Buffallo Bills and Packers in the years that followed. In between those stints, Pettine was the head coach of the Cleveland Browns and a consultant with the Seattle Seahawks.
More recently, he was with the Chicago Bears as a senior defensive assistant in 2021, so he's familiar with his current role, and he was assistant head coach and outside linebackers coach with the Minnesota Vikings from 2022 through 2025.

title: Cowboys Legend Says Sideline Felt ‘Hopeless’ During Latest Loss
full_text:
Michael Irvin is usually the strongest supporter the Dallas Cowboys have. One of the key pieces of their three Super Bowl wins during the 1990s is often over the top with his faith in the organization, but even he sounded defeated with his recent statements.
While on First Take with Stephen A. Smith and Dan Orlovsky, Irvin said the Cowboys were easily the most disappointing team in the NFC East this weekend. That’s saying something since the Philadelphia Eagles gave up a lead with eight seconds to play and the Washington Commanders and New York Giants had a comedy of errors in their Week 5 tie.
For Irvin, however, it wasn’t so much about the play on the field - although he said that was bad. What really stood out to him was the sense of “hopelessness” he saw on the sidelines.
“I'm usually in a box up high, but I sat in a box down low, and I watched these guys. And I watched the sideline. Usually I'm up high watching like the all 22. I'm watching the sideline and not one point, not at one time did I ever see anybody going up and down that sideline saying, we're going to win this game. Don't give up. Let's keep going. We're going to win this game. I was sitting there saying, this is, this is ugly. And it looks hopeless. They played poorly,” Irvin said.
“This is ugly. It looks hopeless.” @michaelirvin88 sounds off on the Cowboys as the most disappointing team in the NFC East 📉 pic.twitter.com/rN0tH98fj5
Irvin also touched on a hot topic about a worker inside the stadium who called the loss “embarrassing” as Dak Prescott made his way to the locker room. Prescott seemed bothered by the statement and even tried to say the loss wasn’t embarrassing .
Irvin wasn’t having any of that, saying Prescott and the Cowboys don’t need to show fight against a fan and their opinion. Instead, he wants to see more fight on the field.
“The guy just spoke to Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. The gospel. It was embarrassing. So don't get mad at him. Don't fight him. Go back on that football field and fight those damn guys on that field. Not that poor guy that just shared his thoughts. And his thoughts were all of our thoughts. Everybody in Cowboys Nation. That was embarrassing.”
The Cowboys’ next game will be against the Green Bay Packers , who are coming off a big win against the Chicago Bears this past weekend. It will be another tough showdown for a team struggling to find its identity.

title: DaRon Bland Surprise Absence From Cowboys Practice Amid Individual Struggles
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have had their share of struggles on defense so far during the 2026 season, and that's putting it mildly.
While the defense has had its multitude of problems regardless of who's out there, there's no denying that the countless amount of injuries has likely contributed to these shortcomings.
The Cowboys appeared to be getting healthier ahead of last week's primetime matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers but that hardly mattered in an embarrassing 24-16 loss to a team that had entered the game winless.
Now, more potential injury questions are popping up as the Cowboys look to turn things around.
Cowboys cornerback DaRon Bland was not seen at the team's practice on Monday, per reports from Joseph Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News. Neither was cornerback Caelen Carson.
It wasn't all bad news though. The Cowboys saw Joey Porter Jr. return to practice on Monday after he missed last Thursday's game against the Bucs due to an unexpected illness.
Porter Jr. was joined by other cornerbacks like Reddy Steward, Alex Austin, Tyrek Funderburk and Derion Kendrick along with rookie defensive back Caleb Downs on the practice field.
The news of Porter Jr.'s absence broke right before kickoff, leaving the Cowboys without one of their best coverage cornerbacks despite the fact he is still adjusting to life with his new team.
Perhaps this last-minute change to the lineup put added pressure on Bland, and it's clear he wasn't able to answer the call.
Bland has faces some notable individual struggles the past two games for the Cowboys. He gave up multiple long receptions in the win over the Houston Texans before dropping a potential game-tying pick-six in the los to Tampa Bay. At the time, that miscue looked like it was going to be forgotten after Dallas got the ball back with a chance to tie the game, but instead, another Dak Prescott pass got tipped into the air and intercepted by the Tampa Bay defense.
This suddenly put a massive microscope on Bland's mistake. He has build a historical reputation for taking interceptions back for touchdowns but he was unable to come through when Dallas needed him most.
If he's healthy enough, Bland will need a bounce-back game in a major way on Sunday Night Football against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field, or the Cowboys risk falling to a dreadful 2-4 record.

title: Will Micah Parsons Play vs Cowboys? Injury Update Makes Dallas Revenge Game Unlikely
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys will hit the road in Week 6 to face off against the rival Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field, marking a potential showdown with former All-Pro pass rusher Micah Parsons.
Parsons' fallout with the Cowboys is well-documented , but any talk of "Round 2 of Revenge" is starting to taper off after the latest update from ESPN insider Adam Schefter, who shared some news regarding the pass rusher's return from a torn ACL .

title: Michael Irvin Supports 'Embarrassing' Heckler, Rips Dak Prescott & Cowboys For Bucs Loss
full_text:
Michael Irvin is not happy with the Dallas Cowboys and Dak Prescott, and nobody will blame him one bit.
The Cowboys have no grace from Irvin or their fans after the dreadful loss to a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team that was on the road and starting an undrafted rookie quarterback in primetime.
As if that wasn't bad enough, after the game someone in the tunnel was overheard saying "embarrassing" in regard to the loss while Prescott was walking through to the locker room, and the Cowboys quarterback shot back at him in the viral video.
"You say it once I look off, huh?" Prescott said .
Truth be told, whoever that was (it was reportedly a car service driver) echoed exactly how the Cowboys' fans feel right now. Heck, even though he didn't like hearing it, even Prescott admitted the guy wasn't wrong.
Michael Irvin went in on the Cowboys for their ugly loss while also backing the guy who made the "embarrassing" comment.
He also said Prescott should have worried more about fighting the Bucs than he did responding to the commenter.
"Go put some fire on them dudes that was in that damn uniform!" Irvin said on his podcast . "That's what I'm talking about, man."
"When that guy yelled 'embarrassing,' he was talking about you got everybody hoping and waiting that this is going to be different and it came out the same damn way it has always been over the last 30 years," Irvin added. "I had no issues with that man yelling 'embarrassing' because it was embarrassing."
"And I always say, you can have fight in you, make sure you know who and when to fight," Irvin said. "And fighting (the embarrassing guy) was not the damn fight. Fighting them boys on the football field was the fight. And you ran from that fight."
Irvin went on to say that "I was depressed, I was mad, I was hurt, I was in a grave, buried" after the loss, but seeing the Philadelphia Eagles botch their game against the Jacksonville Jaguars cheered him up.
There's nothing to really argue with when it comes to what Irvin is saying. The Cowboys just did not show up on Thursday night and Prescott even acknowledging whoever said "embarrassing" just looked petty and he should have just ignored it.
Irvin is all Cowboys fans right now, including his hilarious note about the Eagles' debacle on Sunday.
Cowboys fans were expecting much better than they've gotten this season, and that's especially true on defense, where the Cowboys made a ton of changes .
And, unfortunately for Irvin and Cowboys fans everywhere, this has been the norm for three decades now.

title: 4 Defensive Changes Dallas Cowboys Must Make To Try and Fix Putrid Unit in Week 6
full_text:
We are now more than a quarter of the way through the 2026 season and it's quite clear change is desperately needed on the defensive side of the ball for the Dallas Cowboys.
There are issues at every single level of the Cowboys' defense, but some of those issues will just have to work themselves out.
For example, the Cowboys aren't going to fire Christian Parker , so he just has to get better. Also, the Cowboys aren't going to bench disappointing players like Rashan Gary and Quinnen Williams, so they've got to fix themselves, too.
But there are clear changes the Cowboys can and should make for their Week 6 game against the Green Bay Packers. Here's four we'd suggest.
DaRon Bland is one of the worst cornerbacks in the NFL, full stop. Through five games this season, he's giving up completions on 72.4% of the passes thrown his way for 284 yards and two touchdowns, and he sports a passer rating of 126.2.
Pro Football Focus has him clocked with a 45.0 coverage grade and only 11 qualified cornerbacks in the league have a worse mark.
And even after all that, we're not sure those numbers do justice just how bad he has been . A total liability in every sense of the word. For a defense struggling as badly as this one is, the Cowboys cannot keep running him out there.
If Cobie Durant is back this week, he should be getting at least the vast majority of snaps opposite Joey Porter Jr. If Durant is not back, Ameer Speed and/or Shavon Revel will do just fine. The former has been playing good football in particular of late.
Whoever, the Cowboys utilize, they have to be better than what Bland has put on tape in 2026.
Malachi Lawrence did something in Week 5 that Von Miller apparently can't anymore: Lawrence recorded a sack.
Over five games, myself and Miller have the same number of sacks, although to give him credit, Miller does have six more pressures.
What's worse with Miller was that he routinely failed to set the edge against the run in Week 5, which only adds fuel to the fire that he shouldn't be playing much, or at all.
Miller saw a season-low 10 snaps on Thursday night. We would not mind giving those 10 snaps to the rookie, who has shown improvement as a run defender the past two weeks.
Downs has only played eight snaps in the slot combined the past two weeks, and it's understandable why given the injuries at safety .
But the Cowboys need to figure out that position another way and let Downs move back to the slot. Reddy Steward just has not been sufficient and Dallas needs someone better in the short-to-intermediate areas of the field.
Adding to that, Downs' skills as a blitzer and run defender are added benefits of having him playing closer to the line of scrimmage.
According to Sharp Football Analysis , the Cowboys have a blitz rate of 24.4% this season, the12th-lowest in the NFL. There is clearly room to dial up more blitzes moving forward.
The Cowboys have to figure out a way to account for their putrid coverage, and the best way to do that is to sack the quarterback, or at least get more pressure.
Dallas ranks 30th in pass-rush win rate (42%), according to ESPN, and we know they haven't been able to finish their pressures with sacks, so that's something that needs to change.
But Christian Parker can at least try and increase the chances of getting more pressures and sacks by sending more guys after the quarterback. At this point, he has nothing to lose because having more guys in coverage clearly isn't helping.

title: Ideal Cowboys 2027 Mock Draft Lands Prototypical DaRon Bland Replacement
full_text:
As the Dallas Cowboys aim to bounce back from last week's embarrassing effort at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , one thing remains clear: the defense is still in shambles despite all of the offseason efforts to improve the roster.
To be fair, the team has yet to field a healthy defense, and the secondary has been plagued by injuries, but former All-Pro cornerback DaRon Bland has been on the field and has been one of the team's biggest liabilities every week .
As the team searches for answers, there have been calls for the team to move on from Bland, who has been a perennial underperformer the past few years. That's why a new 2027 NFL mock draft from Pro Football Network will have everyone looking toward a brighter future.
In the latest mock, Dallas lands Clemson Tigers star cornerback Ashton Hampton , who is a "prototypical" cornerback who blends a perfect combination of size and ball skills.
The 2027 NFL Draft will be held from Thursday, April 29, through Saturday, May 1, at the National Mall outside of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C.
Let's take a closer look at what a player like Hampton could bring to the ailing Cowboys secondary.
Bland just hasn't been cutting it for the Cowboys since his blockbuster extension, and Cowboys Nation is desperate for the team to move on. Parting ways with Bland in favor of an exciting player like Hampton would be the kind of move to restore faith in the fan base.
"Bland has dealt with injuries and regression in play since his All-Pro campaign in 2023. Cobie Durant gives the Dallas Cowboys a new face in the secondary, but the cornerback room still has major question marks otherwise. The Cowboys had a lot of needs on defense, so you can’t fix them all in one year, but cornerback has remained a major weakness in 2026 ," Pro Football Network wrote.
"After a strong 2025 season, Ashton Hampton has arguably looked even better to begin 2026. He’s 6’-foot-2 and 200 pounds, using his prototypical build to jam receivers near the line of scrimmage and compete at the catch point. He’s a reliable form tackler who can hit hard as a downhill defender, and his mental trigger shows up well covering underneath."
A 6-foot-2 cornerback who can cover and play press coverage? One who excels physically and is not afraid to get dirty by helping against the run? You couldn't ask for a better player to plug into Christian Parker's scheme.
Last season, Hampton recorded 45 tackles, 9 passes defensed, three tackles for a loss, one sack, and one interception as a sophomore. This season, he has 15 tackles, an FBS-high 9 pass breakouts, one interception, and 0.5 tackles per loss in just five games.
His ability to make plays on the ball is only getting better, and he'd be a welcomed addition to the Dallas secondary. In the middle of Round 1, Hampton would be an incredible value pick.
Cowboys Nation can catch Hampton back in action on Saturday, October 17, at home against Charleston Southern. Kickoff is set for 12:00 p.m. ET on the ACC Network.

title: Cowboys & Jets Deemed Logical Trade Partners With Dallas' Need at Edge Rusher
full_text:
The more things change, the more they stay the same and the Dallas Cowboys are seeing that first hand.
After the total revamp of the defense this offseason, which included hiring a new defensive coordinator in Christian Parker and making several changes to personnel, the Cowboys are no better off than they were last season.
One of the issues in Dallas is the inability to get sacks . Dallas is getting some pressure, but nobody seems to know how to finish, and that is routinely exposing an inadequate secondary.
As a result, edge rusher is going to be a major priority as we inch closer to the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
With their need at edge rusher, the Cowboys are matched up as a possible fit for New York Jets edge rusher Will McDonald, who was dubbed a possible trade candidate by Pro Football Focus' Bradley Locker .
"Possible Fits: Bears, 49ers, Eagles, Cowboys," Locker wrote.
"The Jets seemed to make future investments in the edge rusher position with David Bailey and Joseph Ossai this offseason, while Kingsley Enagbare has also played more than McDonald," Locker added. "The 27-year-old on a one-year deal should draw eyes for teams looking to better pursue the quarterback."
McDonald was the subject of trade rumors last year, and this year, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler believes he could draw interest on the trade market.
McDonald still has one year left on his rookie contract after 2026, so it's conceivable the Jets will be open to parting ways with him, especially with the recent investments they've made at the position that Locker pointed to.
McDonald has posted two sacks and 12 pressures through five games, according to PFF. Unfortunately for the Cowboys, those marks would rank first and third on the team.
McDonald has shown he's capable of impact sack production in the past few years, as he tallied 18.5 sacks combined in 2024 and 2025, with 10.5 of those coming in 2024.
We would prefer the Cowboys swing for the fences for an elite edge rusher, but we also know those guys don't grow on trees because teams are rarely willing to part with them.
McDonald would be the next-best thing for Dallas, assuming he can reproduce what he has put on tape the last two seasons.
Trade compensation will be based on what McDonald does between now and the trade deadline, but the Cowboys will probably be looking at a third- or fourth-round pick.
That isn't too bad when you consider McDonald still has one more year left on his contract. The Cowboys do not have their third-rounder in 2027, but they do have a fourth-round pick. Dallas sports both of those selections in 2028, though.
If things keep going the way they're going and McDonald is out there as the best option for Dallas on the trade market, we could definitely see Jerry Jones swinging a trade.

title: Sean Payton's Best Decision vs. Chargers Could Have Lasting Impact
full_text:
Sean Payton's first game back as the Denver Broncos' play-caller didn't result in an offensive resurgence . In fact, one could argue that the passing offense looked even worse in Week 5, and the Broncos' inability to convert on third down was shocking (1-of-12).
The Broncos did win the game, though, defeating the Los Angeles Chargers 23-17 . It wasn't pretty offensively, but Payton did get at least one decision right in his first game back on the headset.
In this game, the Broncos finished with 29 planned runs and 28 passes. Bo Nix had another maddeningly inconsistent day, going 16-of-27 for 123 yards and a touchdown, while losing a fumble.
However, if Payton hadn't stayed committed to the ground attack — even in the face of frustrating early-game inefficiency — the Broncos wouldn't have scored 13 fourth-quarter points.
J.K. Dobbins's performance for most of the game was lackluster, but in the fourth quarter, as that stingy Chargers defensive front began to wilt, the veteran running back was able to break off some big gains that not only kept the chains moving but also led to those much-needed points after Justin Herbert got the lead back.
Dobbins finished with 20 touches: 18 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown, with two catches for six yards. It was his most productive game of the season, and Denver's win was no coincidence.
If Payton can continue to unlock Dobbins, and figure out how to get this offensive line run-blocking the way it's capable of, it would take an emormous amount of pressure off Nix. This is by design. Payton knows that a quarterback without a viable running game is vulnerable.
That's especially true for a slumping quarterback. On one hand, Nix has this team at 3-2 entering Week 6's tilt with the Seattle Seahawks; on the other, he's going through one of his worst periods as a pro.
"Obviously, the hardest thing to do in this league is play that position if you're not rushing the ball," Payton said from the post-game podium on Sunday.
So long as Dobbins can stay healthy, Payton will keep feeding him in hopes that he and this offensive line can heat up. Against the Seahawks, the Broncos are going to need a ground game.
Amid Dobbins's Week 5 rise, Harvey disappeared. He was seemingly excised from the game plan, finishing with just three touches after leading the Broncos with 10 receptions the week prior.
With Dobbins going against his former team, maybe Payton had a hunch that he'd play well, but Harvey is an impact player, and while his vision as a rusher isn't on Dobbins's level, his explosiveness makes him one of the Broncos' few weapons opponents actually fear.
The problem has been usage. When 90% of Harvey's touches are swing passes or check-downs, teams see it coming from a mile away and swarm to the ball. Then his presence on the field becomes a tell.
Nix's inability to work the middle of the field as a passer has allowed opponents to shade coverage toward the boundary with linebackers, cornerbacks, and safeties, and it has limited what Harvey can do with those check-downs. He's not getting one-on-one opportunities to make a guy miss; he's getting swarmed by three or four guys, which leads to short gains.
There are other ways to utilize Harvey's receiving skill set, including as an over-the-middle target, or even a guy who can run a shallow drag across the field and beat man coverage. But it takes a quarterback who can see that to find him and capitalize on Harvey's skill set, and right now, Nix isn't trusting his eyes.
Payton's message to Nix after Sunday's win at SoFi Stadium was to " let it rip ." Nix interpreted that to mean "trust what you're seeing."
Hopefully, he does start trusting his eyes because the Broncos have talent on offense. But it's been sacrificed at the altar of Nix's slump thus far. The hope is that the young quarterback will soon snap out of it.
It was great to see Payton lean on Dobbins this week, but it shouldn't ever come at the expense of a healthy Harvey not touching the ball.
One of the downfalls of Davis Webb's four-game audition as the Broncos' play-caller was a lack of run-pass balance. In one game back, Payton fixed that, and it made a difference in a tough divisional road matchup.
Against the Seahawks on Thursday night, Payton will need to stay patient with the run again, even if Darnold is able to put some early points on the board. If the Broncos' offense is rendered one-dimensional against a defense of this caliber, Nix is in for a long night.
Staying balanced offensively kept the Broncos in the game against L.A. If Nix was even just a little more effective as a passer, the were some big plays to be had. Alas, his penchant for bailing clean pockets way early led to Payton's best-laid plans going up in smoke, as the Broncos' passing offense devolved into a slapdash brand of backyard football.
Meanwhile, the Broncos have highly-paid pass-catchers, like Courtland Sutton, Jaylen Waddle, and Evan Engram, just dying for Nix to competently run the offense and execute Payton's passing plays. The opportunities were there in L.A., but as has been the case all season, minus two fourth quarters, Nix was almost blind to them.
He's not seeing the field because he's not trusting his eyes, his offensive line, or his receivers. And so, Payton has to continue to batten down the hatches and nurse Nix's confidence and presence of mind back to full bloom.
Why Nix seems so hestitant and unconfident is anyone's guess. But the best tonic for any struggling quarterback is a viable run game.
So, utilize Dobbins and Harvey and get through one more tough opponent because help is on the way. Rookie running back Jonah Coleman is eligible to return from injured reserve in Week 7, and the Broncos will have three extra days to prepare for the Arizona Cardinals after Thursday night's game against Seattle.
If Nix bounces back this week, and the Broncos manage to defeat a defending Super Bowl champion for the third straight year, the storylines will shift away from quarterback doomsday and the Bo pile-on we've seen over the past 48 hours.

title: Why Broncos Are Likely Preparing for Talanoa Hufanga to Miss Week 6
full_text:
Things are going from bad to worse for the beat-up Denver Broncos secondary, which was without starting cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs) for Sunday's victory over the Los Angeles Chargers.
Now, with a quick turnaround for Thursday Night Football against the visiting Seattle Seahawks, the Broncos could also be missing standout safety Talanoa Hufanga, who suffered an ankle injury versus Los Angeles and did not return.
Hufanga was listed as a "DNP" (Did Not Practice) on the team's initial Week 6 injury report. The report is an estimation as Denver didn't officially practice on Monday.
Surtain was also considered a "DNP," with his ankle expected to keep him out of action for at least another week. Moss was marked as a limited participant; he could have a chance to return this week.
Safety Brandon Jones (foot) and guard Ben Powers (biceps) were full goes in Monday's "practice."
Monday's #SEAvsDEN injury report: 📰 » https://t.co/l7MDqy4t8X pic.twitter.com/NXKLd2GiGm
One of the early stars of the young season, Hufanga recorded two solo tackles and a tackle-for-loss prior to going down in Week 5. He was replaced in the lineup by primary special-teamer Devon Key, who also made a pair of solo stops across 26 defensive snaps .
“I would say this, it’s time. There are two things, time and then the second thing is proper recovery from the last game," head coach Sean Payton said Monday when asked about the challenges of preparing on a short week. "For each player, getting their body ready for a short work week, so that the time and the recovery—those are the two things that hit me right away with that question.”
The entire Broncos defense — Hufanga included — deserved a game ball for their efforts against the Chargers, whom they held to just 237 total yards and turned over three times, as well as registering three sacks on slumping quarterback Justin Herbert.
However, their opponent this coming Thursday is on an entirely different level than the decimated Chargers. In addition to sporting the NFL's eighth-best scoring offense, the Seahawks feature arguably the sport's top wide receiver, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who leads the league in both receptions and touchdowns and is fresh off an eight-catch, 102-yard, one-TD performance in Week 5.
Smith-Njigba sustained an ankle injury during Sunday's loss to the 49ers, but he was listed as limited on Seattle's practice report and is anticipated to play on Thursday without any major restrictions.
Assuming he's on the field and Hufanga and Surtain aren't, the Broncos defense might have its collective hands full containing QB Sam Darnold's favorite target.
It's worth noting that Denver has three safeties currently on the practice squad — Taylor Rapp, Miles Scott, and Ugo Amadi — and may choose to promote one if Hufanga is ruled out.

title: Film Room: What's Really Behind Broncos' Alarming 3-and-Out Problem
full_text:
Sean Payton may have taken the play-calling away from Davis Webb this week, but the Denver Broncos still have many problems to solve on offense.
Forget the final score on Sunday. Denver beat the Los Angeles Chargers 23-17 , but that does not mean the offense played well, and it wasn’t called very differently to begin with.
For many reasons, Denver barely got any traction on Sunday. The Broncos' offensive line couldn’t execute in the running game.
To boot, the Broncos got little production out of the passing offense. They went 1-for-12 on third down and produced four three-and-outs in five possessions through the middle of the game. Denver had a fourth possession that only featured four plays thanks to a long defensive pass interference penalty.
When the Broncos were finally able to “generate” some scoring in the fourth quarter, every possession started in Chargers territory, with three of four possessions starting inside the 40-yard line.
Scoring 13 points on three consecutive fourth-quarter drives is awesome, but they all came on the heels of Denver's defensive takeaways and a turnover on downs. Those 13 points were achieved with just 79 yards of offense on 15 total plays, which is rather pathetic.
Denver's offensive inefficiency allowed the Chargers to stay in the game.
I dove into the Broncos' three-and-outs for this week’s film room to highlight issues in play-calling, personnel usage, and execution. It’s on everybody this week.
The first three and out of the game for the offense. Sean Payton in his bag with a pair of screens and a toss sweep to a WR. Great play calling.... pic.twitter.com/JgmX5JhH3Z
The first three-and-out possession featured some incredibly frustrating play-calling, combined with execution mishaps and infuriating personnel usage.
Payton tries to get running back Tyler Badie involved on the drive, opening up with a screen pass to get things started. Right tackle Mike McGlinchey whiffs on his block on defensive lineman Jamari Caldwell, who blows the play up in the backfield for a five-yard loss.
Caldwell uses a great swim move in open space to make the play, but McGlinchey needs to do a better job of walling this off and allowing Badie to make a play with the ball in his hands. If this play pops, Badie has blockers in front to open up a nice gain on first down.
On second down, Payton tries to get cute with a toss sweep to wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. This is an atrocious use of personnel and a horrible play call in this situation.
Mims manages to grind out three yards on the play, but there’s no reason to call this play in this situation. Denver paid $8 million to running back. J.K. Dobbins in the offseason. Let him run the football.
Following a McGlinchey false start, Payton has to dial up another screen play, this time to Mims on a receiver tunnel screen. Finding a quality play call for 3rd-and-17 while pinned deep in your own territory is an impossible task.
Getting quality execution is another thing. Tight end Nate Adkins and wideout Troy Franklin try to block the same defender on this play, but it wouldn’t matter anyways. This is folding your hand and trying to gain positive yards to help out the punting unit.
Bad execution on the next 3 and out. LAC was keyed into the run on 1st down, Bo vacates to the right and misses Trautman up the seam, then Badie runs into Powers and misses the cutback lane. I saw the safety crash down. Badie has to try to make a guy miss in the hole. pic.twitter.com/EnSES75bnh
Our next drive starts after Nik Bonitto sacked Justin Herbert to force a punt, and the Broncos' offense is pinned deep in their own territory again.
The Broncos try to get the running game going on first down with a pin-and-pull look to Dobbins. Adkins motions across the formation to kick out defensive end Ahkeem Mesidor, with left guard Ben Powers following behind him as a lead blocker.
McGlinchey doesn’t get any movement up front on the 3-technique defensive lineman, and the Chargers are keyed in on the run game, with the safety filling down from the second level when Adkins goes in motion. This is poor execution up front, and Dobbins has nowhere to go.
On 2nd-and-9, Payton calls a play-action pass with tight end Adam Trautman running a bender up the seam. The Chargers bring pressure from the left side, and Bo Nix panics in a fairly clean pocket, evading to his right rather than stepping up to find Trautman running wide open up the middle of the field. Nix has to start taking some chances with the football, especially when things aren’t as muddy as they seem.
With the Broncos now in another 3rd-and-long scenario, Payton calls up a draw to Badie to give the punt unit some breathing room. The offensive line does a great job opening up a large running lane to the right side, but Badie sees the safety crashing down to fill the gap from the third level of the defense and runs directly into the backside of Powers.
I understand trying to follow your blockers on this, but I would like to see Badie press this hole to the cutback and try to make a defender miss in the hole. You can’t block this play any better. Go make a play.
Nice drive starter to Engram. Dobbins doesn't have the speed on wide zone to get to the outside, and they can't execute Mesh on 3rd down due to pressure and WR timing. Another 3-and-out with bad execution. pic.twitter.com/HhWTRPYRsh
Following a long Chargers touchdown drive to open the third quarter, Denver goes three-and-out with some poor execution on second and third down.
They open the possession with a bootleg look and dump the ball down to tight end Evan Engram for a four-yard gain. This is a drive starter designed to get positive yards and set up a 2nd-and-manageable situation. Nice work.
On 2nd-and-6, Payton calls a toss sweep into wide zone with Dobbins carrying the ball, and Chargers linebacker Del’Shawn Phillips reads the play the whole way. It’s not always about the Xs and Os. Sometimes you need your Jimmies and Joes to make a play, and Phillips strings this out to the boundary.
This play highlights Dobbins's lack of explosiveness this season. He doesn’t look right as a runner, and he is too slow to bounce this outside.
Dobbins tries to cut back inside of wide receiver Lil’Jordan Humphrey at the point of attack, but it’s already too late. I’d like to see running back RJ Harvey tote the rock on this play, because his speed could have made a huge difference.
With 3rd-and-long upcoming, Payton draws a three-receiver set with the formation to the boundary, trying to open the middle of the field with a mesh concept. The timing of this play is messed up from the jump, with Mims and wideout Courtland Sutton bumping into eachother in their release package.
Nix gets instant pressure from a twist up front, and left tackle Garett Bolles gets called for holding while getting abused by Khalil Mack coming off the edge. The execution fails the offense, once again.
Run, Run, Pass. Solid work on 1st down. Powers gets beat by the swim on 2nd down. Bo and Sutton can't connect on the fade. This was after the Vidal TD. You HAVE TO have a better drive to stop the bleeding. pic.twitter.com/FEpxr1grAB
Denver only had the ball for one play on their next possession because Nix fumbled on first down, which led to a 42-yard Kimani Vidal touchdown run on the very next play. Down 17-10 and desperately needing an answer to stop the bleeding, the Broncos call a pair of runs to open the drive.
First down sees Dobbins pick up three yards on an outside zone. Dobbins reads this well, cutting back inside center Luke Wattenburg at the second level. Trautman does a nice job of walling off Mesidor at the point of attack, and the offense gets decent yardage to start the drive.
On second down, Wattenburg and Powers have a double team on inside zone, and Powers gets beat to the inside by a spectacular swim move as Wattenburg climbs to the second level. If Powers can sustain this block, Harvey has a great cutback lane to rip off a solid gain…

title: Broncos' Snap Counts Reveal Some Surprises in Chargers Victory
full_text:
It wasn't pretty offensively, but the Denver Broncos finally won at SoFi Stadium, defeating the Los Angeles Chargers 23-17 .
The win puts the Broncos at 3-2, tied with the Las Vegas Raiders for second place in the AFC West. The 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs were on bye this week, but they still lead the division.
The injury bug and Sean Payton's decision to take back the play-calling had a huge impact on the Broncos' Week 5 snap counts, with a few surprises. Let's examine how the Broncos relied in different players.
Keep in mind, on offense, Bo Nix and the Broncos' offensive line played 100% of snaps, with 62. Alex Palczewski garnered a season-high eight snaps in this one, too, as the Broncos deployed an extra O-lineman in some heavy looks.
After taking a back seat to Harvey last week, Dobbins led all Broncos running backs in snap share and  touches, finishing with 18 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown, while catching two passes for six yards. Harvey was a relative non-factor in Payton's first game back as the play-caller, carrying just three times for seven yards and garnering just one target, which he did not catch.
Badie carried once for six yards and caught one pass for minus five yards. Prentice received his first touch of the season, diving three yards to move the chains for Denver's offense.
Sutton again led the way in snap share, but only finished with two catches on three targets for 18 yards. But at least the Pro Bowler notched his first touchdown of the season.
Waddle posted his third game of the season with two catches or fewer, despite leading the Broncos with five targets. He dropped one that would have been a sizable gain.
Franklin continues to keep his head down and do the dirty work as a blocker, and when Nix looks his way, he answers the bell, finishing with two catches on two targets for 16 yards. Humphrey out-earned Mims in snap share, and caught his only target for eight yards; it was the Broncos' first first-down conversion on an opening drive of the season.
Still wondering what the heck is going on with Mims? Me too. He caught both targets for six yards and carried once for three yards.
Engram was one of the Broncos' few impact players on offense , leading the team with four receptions for 55 yards. He's staying on the field to block way more than last year.
Trautman is a blocker, and so is Adkins. Neither garnered a target in Nix's 27 attempts.
Allen once again had a monster game, finishing with several pressures and his fourth sack of the season. Roach was a force, too, notching three tackles and disrupting the Chargers' beleaguered offensive line.
Nose tackle D.J. Jones turned in one of the best performances of his career as a Bronco , while Sai'vion Jones saw a season-high snap share. The main rotation is a four-man show, though, with Uwazurike as the fourth leg.
Bonitto was a force, sacking Herbert twice. Robinson was disruptive, and Tillman led the group in pressures. Elliss is still looking a little... slow.
Denver might want to consider replacing Elliss with Robinson in the starting lineup until Jonathon Cooper returns.
This was one of the Broncos' linebacker duo's best games of the season. Both played well, with Strnad leading the team in tackles (eight), followed by Singleton's seven.
No other inside linebacker saw the field on defense this week.
A tip of the cap to Barron and Abrams-Draine for holding down the fort while Pat Surtain II and Riley Moss are injured. The two young corners played well, although it's worth mentioning that L.A. was without Quentin Johnston and Ladd McConkey.
McMillian was his usual solid self in the nickel.
Jones had a great game, notching an interception and a fumble recovery, but Hufanga exited with an ankle injury in the second half. That foisted Key onto the field, and he was... okay. Not great, but okay.
Amid the shock of losing Hufanga, Skinner and Anderson each garnered one snap. It was the first defensive snap of the season for Anderson, and only the second game of the campaign where Skinner saw time beyond special teams.

title: Broncos Player Grades: Bo Nix's Slump Continues in Ugly Chargers Win
full_text:
The Denver Broncos decided to make a big change on offense, with Sean Payton taking the play-calling duties back from first-year offensive coordinator Davis Webb ahead of Week 5's road game against the Los Angeles Chargers.
That was an indication that Payton felt the play-calling, and not the execution, was the biggest issue, though his feelings may have changed after the Broncos turned in their worst offensive showing of the season against the Chargers, when you factor in the quality of defense they are playing.
Denver won 23-17 , but it was ugly at times.
The Broncos scored four times off the takeaways their defense generated, including a turnover on downs, which is a credit to Vance Joseph's unit. The Broncos' defense put together a solid game, though they weren't without their faults, putting the win on their shoulders to move to 3-2 on the season.
This week's player grades reflect Denver's horrendous offensive showing and strong defensive display, minus a few miscues. Let’s get into the grades.
Tillman earned Defensive MVP after having the biggest impact on his snaps. He picked up three pressures on only 10 pass-rush snaps, and leading the team.
Several other Broncos tied with two pressures, all with nearly twice as many pass-rush snaps as Tillman. His run defense was stout as well, which helped him earn Defensive MVP in this one.
The Broncos' offensive line has had issues, but not Meinerz. Even against the Chargers, the offensive line struggled in both phases , but not the All-Pro right guard. A guard can only do so much to carry an offense, but that doesn't stop Meinerz from trying every week.
Sean Payton’s post-game comments were telling . Something is wrong with Nix mentally. Somehow, someway, he needs to get out of his own head; otherwise, it could be a long season.
This is Year 3, but Nix isn't playing like a quarterback with 39 regular-season starts under his belt. He looks like he's massively regressed.
D.J. Jones | DL | Grade: 79.4
This was one of the better games from Jones in his Broncos career, and it highlights when and how he can be a great run defender. The Broncos' run defense had issues, but not because of Jones in the middle, where he was stout and closed multiple running lanes.
Brandon Jones | S | Grade: 77.2
This was a 2024-level performance by Jones, back when he looked like an elite safety. Alas, this was his first game like that since 2024. He flew around the field, both in coverage and against the run, without getting caught out of position.
Garett Bolles | LT | Grade: 70.1
Bolles has been solid to good all season long, and against the Chargers, he put on an outstanding showing. Yes, the Chargers are beat up defensively, but Bolles looked great and held the fort down, minus one holding penalty.
Mike McGlinchey | RT | Grade: 67.9
McGlinchey was my matchup to watch against the Chargers' pass rush , and he answered the call. He stepped up and put on a good game for the first time this season. With no pressures allowed and a good run-blocking game, McGlinchey showed his value; now he just has to sustain that level of play.
RJ Harvey | RB | Grade: 31.7
If the Broncos want Harvey to improve, he has to do so as a pass protector first and foremost. The run game is lacking with him, too, but he can be a passing weapon. But if his pass protection doesn’t improve and it's as bad as it was against the Chargers, he will become too much of a tell for opposing defenses, if he isn’t already.
Devon Key | S | Grade: 34.8
When you play a position that isn’t rotated and have to come in for an injury, it can be difficult to come in and play well. Key has done that before, but this time, stepping in for an injured Talanoa Hufanga, he didn’t play well. Hopefully, Key can be ready for Thursday Night Football if Hufanga misses time.
J.K. Dobbins | RB | Grade: 37.6
It looks like the injuries have finally caught up with Dobbins. Even with a few solid runs, he averaged just 3.8 yards per carry and spent most of the game under a 3.0 average. He doesn’t look bursty or explosive, and that's been paired with some terrible vision of late.
Jonah Elliss | OLB | Grade: 39.7
Elliss is a technical player, but he isn’t overly explosive or athletic for an edge rusher. Denver should look to play Que Robinson over Elliss, and after this season, consider moving Elliss to an inside linebacker and defensive play-caller role, as his brothers do with their respective NFL teams.
