title: Sean Payton Had One Strong Message for Bo Nix After Broncos Beat Chargers
full_text:
Sean Payton's return to calling the plays didn't result in an offensive revival , but the Denver Broncos did beat the Los Angeles Chargers on the road, 23-17. It was Payton's first-ever win at SoFi Stadium as Broncos head coach.
“It was good enough to win, but there are still a number of things that we need to improve on," Payton said of his offense post-game.
It was barely good enough to win. Denver finished with 224 total yards but converted just 1-of-12 third-down attempts while going 2-of-5 in the red zone. Payton's return wasn't the quick fix to the biggest issue holding back the Broncos' offense: Bo Nix's Year-3 slump .
Despite having Payton in his ear and calling the plays, Nix still looked skittish and unsure in the pocket. With the exception of one 36-yard strike to tight end Evan Engram in the first quarter, Nix didn't push the ball downfield.
Nix seems like he doesn't trust his eyes. Everyone's got a theory on why the young quarterback suddenly looks so uncomfortable and unpoised, but it seems to be a between-the-ears issue.
Payton and his staff are trying to get to the bottom of it, but the veteran head coach had one parting message for Nix at the post-game podium: "Let it rip."
"I think, man, we as coaches, like I've said to him, I said, 'Man, you're the guy we wanted here. Let's go. You've done a ton of things well,'" Payton said of Nix. "But I think there's a lot that goes into that. It's important that, you know, in that old TV series The Bear , where they just said, 'Let her rip,' I want him to make sure that, hey, let her rip."
Payton isn't telling Nix to go be a fast-and-loose gunslinger. In fact, Nix believes his coach meant that he should trust his eyes.
“I think when a coach says ‘let it rip,’ it means trust what you see," Nix said post-game. "Right now, there’s just a little subtle piece of overall offensive execution that we’re still working towards, because at times, it’s there and we’re really good. At times, for whatever reason, the drive stalls."
Nix believes that a quarterback has to earn the right to "let it rip." It would seem that, by Payton calling on Bo to fire away, the Broncos' head coach believes he has earned the right — and, by extension, can be trusted to make the right decisions.
"I think there’s a lot of pieces that go into it, but... letting it rip is one of the best things that you can do as a quarterback," Nix said. "At the same time, you’ve got to sort of earn that right. When you do the preparation, you earn the right to react so that you can let it rip.”
Perhaps in his hesitancy as a passer, Nix is questioning himself and whether he's earned the right to "let it rip." Based on what we saw at SoFi Stadium, he's yet to fully embrace the let-it-rip mindset.
He went 16-of-27 for 123 yards and a touchdown. While Nix didn't throw an interception, he did fumble twice, losing one of them. That lost fumble came with the game tied and sparked an enormous momentum swing in the Chargers' direction.
The sudden change allowed L.A. to score immediately on the ensuing play with a Kimani Vidal 42-yard touchdown romp. The Chargers took a 17-10 lead at the bottom of the third quarter.
Thanks to some excellent clutch-time play by the Broncos' defense, Nix was given some additional opportunities in the fourth quarter, and while there were still some painful moments, the Broncos capitalized by punctuating their rather ugly offensive performance with 13 additional points.
Still, Broncos fans have gone from various stages of concern to — in some cases — outright panic over Nix's slump. That was clear enough from the comments on my X posts and the Mile High Huddle Podcast 's live chat after the game.
Although there's the distinct possibility that we could simply be seeing the ups and downs of a young quarterback still finding his way, it's hard to argue against the assertion that Nix has regressed. Myself, I wonder if Nix is truly over his broken ankle; the bone may be healed, but has his psyche caught up?
It sounds like Payton and his staff are trying to focus on the little things to get Nix rollling again in the bigger picture, starting with his feet.
"I would say this. I think the one area, obviously there's a lot been said about his feet. I think he's settling that down," Payton said of Nix. "I think it's important from a protection standpoint that early in games we provide that clean pocket so that clock doesn't get juiced up a little bit. I don't know what his dropback percentage was, but I think it was a little less tonight."
With Payton at the helm, the Broncos were more balanced offensively from a run-pass perspective, though it didn't lead to any big plays or obvious successes. Denver finished with 29 runs to 28 passes.
Nix's 27 attempts were a season-low, a reflection of Payton's drive to build a run game around his young quarterback, even if the returns on the ground weren't big. Fortunately, as is his way, Nix saved his best for when the chips were down, as the Broncos scored 13 fourth-quarter points on the back of three huge defensive stops.
When I say "his best," though, it's in relative terms. This was far from Nix's Week 3 fourth-quarter display.
"I think when we needed it down the stretch, there were some plays to be had. We got blitzed on [Courtland] Sutton's touchdown," Payton said. "We were hoping to get a certain coverage, but it was good because he's got a free rusher there."
We know one of the reasons Payton took back the play-calling was that he wasn't seeing a " championship " offense. Rome wasn't built in a day, but if Nix and the Broncos' offense took any steps forward in Week 5, they were extremely small.
You can point to Denver finally moving the chains for the first time this season on the opening drive as progress. The Broncos actually picked up two first downs on their opening possession, though it still ended with a punt.
The Broncos also led for most of the game, which has been another inconvenient and nagging storyline around this team through the first quarter of the season. That's progress, to be sure, but keeping it in context, it was by no means impressive.
Getting the run game over 100 yards on the day and staying balanced from a run-pass perspective was another step in the right direction, and the offense got points (13 to be exact) on each of the Broncos' takeaways. But I'm stretching to find the silver linings here, if you can't tell.
The Broncos took some small steps forward as a rushing offense in L.A., but they have a long way to go in terms of efficiency. Payton has been coaching in this league long enough to know that without a viable run game, a quarterback is often dead in the water.
That's especially true with a slumping Year-3 quarterback.
"I think after four weeks, there's a handful of things that collectively, and it starts with me, where it's like, all right, let's focus on these details," Payton said. "I think the byproduct helps the quarterback. Obviously, the hardest thing to do in this league is play that position if you're not rushing the ball."
The Broncos have a lot to work on with very little time to do it. The Seattle Seahawks are coming to Mile High for a Thursday night showdown, so once again, there's no rest for the weary.
After the Seahawks game, though, the Broncos will get three extra days — known colloquially as a 'mini-bye' — to prepare for their next opponent. That will be the Broncos' first and only chance to catch a breath before their actual Week 10 bye.
In the meantime, any improvement Nix shows will have to be done on the hoof.

title: Broncos' Biggest Winners & Losers in 23-17 Victory Over Chargers
full_text:
But the Denver Broncos' 23-17 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers was about as ugly as it gets . The Broncos' defense did the heavy lifting, while the offense stunk up the joint for most of the game.
Those Broncos fans hoping Sean Payton's return to calling the plays would be an immediate cure for whatever is ailing this offense were not only disappointed — they're likely even more alarmed.
However, the Broncos found a way to get it done. In his first game back at the play-calling controls, Payton was able to notch his first win over the Chargers at SoFi Stadium as Broncos head coach, as his team moves to 3-2 in the standings.
As we sift through the aftermath of Denver's divisional win, let's break down the Broncos' biggest winners and losers coming out of this game.
Payton put a mountain of pressure on his shoulders by taking back the play-calling from offensive coordinator Davis Webb . The decision also added more pressure on Nix amid his slump, but I digress. Payton asked for the pressure, and by virtue of the win, eased some of it.
However, the Broncos' offense didn't look markedly different with Payton calling the plays against the Chargers. But after Justin Herbert was able to battle back into this game and take the lead, it wouldn't have been a big surprise to see the Broncos wilt and lose this game.
That's not what happened, though. Thanks to some clutch-time play by the Broncos' defense, Payton was able to get his first win over Jim Harbaugh at SoFi Stadium, and preserve the appearance that his decision to take back the play sheet was the right one.
Alas, though, the Broncos finished with just 224 yards of total offense. They only converted one third down on 12 attempts — wrap your brain around that — and went 2-of-5 in the red zone. Nothing was working.
In terms of progress, there wasn't much to point to on Sunday. However, the Broncos did get move the chains on their opening drive for the first time this season and led for most of the game. I'll take that as a silver-lining development amid the upheaval of Payton taking back the play-calling.
Make no mistake, though: this game only hammered home the reality of Webb being the scapegoat for Denver's shockingly impotent offense. Payton has his work cut out for him to truly turn this ship around.
Something is wrong with Nix. What it could be is anyone's guess, but he continues to look far from the quarterback he was in his first two seasons.
In L.A., Nix started on solid footing, delivering an efficient if unspectacular performance early on. He had one really nice 36-yard throw to tight end Evan Engram to help set up the Broncos' first touchdown of the day.
It was all downhill from there, though. As has been the trend this season, Nix looked timid and completely unpoised against L.A. He's not trusting his eyes or his receivers, and it's leading to a multitude of missed opportunities and three-and-outs.
Nix finished the day 16-of-27 for 123 yards and a touchdown. He didn't throw any interceptions, but he fumbled twice, losing one of them. That lost fumble created a massive momentum swing that allowed the Chargers to take the lead late.
Nix entered the 2026 season with seven career fumbles. He has five already through the first five games of this season — another microcosm of the meta issues plaguing the third-year quarterback.
When it comes to what's eating at Nix, theories abound. It's not the play-calling, though. That, we know. The only thing that makes any sense to me, at this point, is that his ankle is still bothering him.
The Broncos need to get to the bottom of the Nix situation, fast.
Jones had one heck of a game. He totaled four tackles, and picked off Herbert late to help ice the game.
Brandon Jones in the right place at the right time 🗣️ @DENvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/iZZSY0BYw1
Earlier, Jones recovered a Charlie Kolar fumble forced by Talanoa Hufanga that led direcetly to the Broncos' first touchdown of the game. When Hufanga exited in the second half with an ankle injury, never to return, Jones did a lot of the heavy lifting on the back end of the secondary.
Lutz missed his third field-goal attempt of the season, a got-to-have-it 42-yarder with the Broncos' trailing 17-10 in the fourth quarter. He doesn't have the biggest leg, but inside of 45 yards, Lutz is usually reliable.
Not so this season. Special teams coordinator Darren Rizzi needs to get to the bottom of what's eating Lutz as quickly as Payton does with Nix.
I already mentioned him, but Engram was the Broncos' most effective pass-catcher on the day. He led the team with five receptions for 55 yards and came very close to scoring a touchdown.
Bo Nix drops it in the bucket to Evan Engram 🪣 @DENvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/AntTdNFDKs
Engram ran his routes well and when the ball went his way, he fought hard to pick up extra yardage. It was good to see the veteran tight end lead the team in receptions and yards.
Waddle posted his third game of the season with two or fewer receptions, finishing with two grabs on a team-high five targets for just 19 yards. He also had one rush for nine yards.
Despite showing his frustration on the sideline, Waddle's drop in the second half killed another dead-on-arrival drive. I was hoping that Payton's play-calling would lead to more consistent Waddle usage, but he and Nix continued to struggle getting on the dame page.
Given what Denver gave up to acquire Waddle from the Miami Dolphins, it's fair to consider him a big disappointment this season. Outside of his 138-yard Week 2 performance, he's been a dud thus far.
Bonitto entered this game with just one sack on the season, but he took down Justin Herbert twice. Bonitto gave L.A.'s depleted offensive line fits all game long.
Nik Bonitto breaks through and gets the sack 💪 @DENvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SapZ5OhaCU
The Pro Bowl rush linebacker continues to show modest progress as a run defender, too, finishing with a season-high four tackles. However, he missed two tackles against the Chargers, so there's still plenty of room for improvement.
Right tackle Mike McGlinchey was especially bad, but the Broncos' entire starting five turned in another concerning performance. They were unable to create any push in the run game until deep in the fourth quarter.
The lack of poise and discipline from this unit has become alarming. From pre-snap penalties to holding fouls, the Broncos' offensive line was a major reason for the Broncos' lack of success on Sunday.
The O-line only allowed one sack on Nix, but he was pressured five times. This unit is another quandry Payton needs to get to the bottom of fast, especially given the amount of salary-cap dollars the Broncos have allocated to the O-line.
Lastly, the Broncos need to strongly consider sitting McGlinchey down and rolling with Alex Palczewski at right tackle. McGlinchey is highly paid, but he's become a liability.
Dobbins ran hard in this game, but with only a few exceptions, he didn't get much help from his O-line. Finishing with 68 yards and a touchdown on 18 carries, the veteran back turned in his best performance of the season against his former team.
J.K. Dobbins scores the first TD of the game 👏 @DENvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2x4pE7u2qJ
It was great to see Dobbins notch his first touchdown of the season. His fourth-quarter running helped the Broncos battle back and win this game.
Like Dobbins, Sutton was able to score his first touchdown of the season, but he finished with just two receptions for 18 yards. He and Nix have not been able to get on the same page, which is another alarming symptom of just how bad this offense is, given the strong chemistry this duo forged over the preceding two seasons.
Sutton isn't fighting for the ball and coming down with it anymore. That used to be a hallmark of his game and why his quarterbacks — from Joe Flacco to Drew Lock to Teddy…

title: 3 Alarming Takeaways From Broncos' 23-17 Win Over Chargers
full_text:
It was frustrating, but the “Heart Attack Horsies” struck again, as the Denver Broncos managed to hold off the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium , 23-17.
Bolstered by an incredible defensive showing against a battered Chargers offense, Denver managed to sneak its way to a 3-2 start and keep pace in the AFC West. The Broncos' offense had several short fields to navigate and was in scoring position for the majority of the second half, but there were still a lot of issues.
We'll have film to watch tomorrow, but here are my three big instant takeaways from the Broncos' third win of the season.
Don't let the final score steer you wrong. Nix and the Broncos' offense were absolutely putrid against the Chargers.
Despite one long scoring drive in the second quarter that featured a fleeting look at a solid rushing attack, the Broncos couldn't execute in the passing game. Denver had five three-and-outs before the fourth-quarter scoring fest.
Outside of that long touchdown drive, Sean Payton's play-calling looked almost exactly the same as Davis Webb's in the first four games, with incredibly similar results. Webb was relieved of the play-calling duties last week, a scapegoat, it would seem.
Those fourth-quarter scores were all set up by Denver's incredible defensive play, including a strip-sack of Justin Herbert, a Brandon Jones interception, and a turnover on downs.
Denver had three fourth-quarter possessions starting inside the Chargers' 40-yard line and a fourth at their 41-yard line, so only coming away with 13 points is disappointing. Wil Lutz did miss a 42-yard field goal, but that drive started at the Chargers' 27-yard line, and the Broncos were only able to generate three yards.
That's not nearly good enough, especially with how poor and depleted the Chargers' defense was going into the game.
This was arguably the Broncos' worst offensive showing this year, and Payton called the plays. It's time for the offense to start executing on the field, and that's on the players.
But hey; at least Nix can now say he's defeated Justin Herbert head-to-head.
Even without all of the takeaways in the fourth quarter, Denver's defense played one heck of a football game. The Chargers had one long drive coming out of halftime and an explosive 42-yard touchdown run by Kimani Vidal in the third quarter, hot on the heels of a Nix lost fumble and a big momentum change, but that's pretty much it.
Denver has had tackling issues in the run game all year, and Vidal's touchdown was just another example to point to. But overall, Denver's run defense played well.
The Chargers may have finished the game with 155 yards on the ground, but outside of the Vidal touchdown, they only had 113 yards on 33 carries. That's 3.2 yards per carry.
54 of those yards came via Herbert scrambles. Omarion Hampton only had 33 yards on his 14 carries, and Keaton Mitchell finished with 11 yards on six attempts. You can't play it much better than that.
Even without Surtain, Denver's secondary was incredible. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine held it down on the boundary.
Abrams-Draine had an interception taken away due to his own pass-interference penalty, but otherwise went unnoticed for the majority of the game. He finished with three total tackles and broke up a pass.
Barron was awesome as a tackler in space and had a solid game in coverage as well. Having rarely seen the field to open the season, a lot of fans in Broncos Country were beginning to think that drafting him in the first round last year was a major mistake.
Barron gets to wave a finger in his doubter's direction.
The Broncos' secondary had a great day overall. Herbert only completed 14 passes on 24 attempts for 121 yards and a touchdown.
The veteran quarterback looked rattled at times and put his horrendous decision-making on full display, as best illustrated by his game-sealing interception thrown to Brandon Jones late in the fourth quarter. However, Herbert was playing behind a battered offensive line that played four rookies in place of starters, and he was without half of his receiving corps.
But good teams capitalize on such vulnerabilities. That's what the Broncos' defense did, sacking Herbert five times, taking the ball away thrice, and delivering Payton his first-ever win at SoFi Stadium as Denver's head coach.

title: 5 Dream Trades That Could Transform the Broncos
full_text:
NFL trade rumors usually don't heat up for another couple of weeks when we draw closer to the trade deadline on November 10.
And yet, this week alone, we've seen Philadelphia Eagles center offensive lineman Cam Jurgens traded and possibly Arizona Cardinals wideout Marvin Harrison Jr . Teams seem a bit more ready to get something done sooner rather than later if it means solving a roster problem.
Those selling might be more willing to admit they aren't quite ready to compete for a Super Bowl and need draft capital to get where they want to be. However, the Denver Broncos still have solid Super Bowl ambitions, so could they be in the market to make a big splash before the deadline — that one player to help them get over the hump?
The Broncos worked the phones ahead of last year's trade deadline and tried to make a deal with the Miami Dolphins for Jaylen Waddle. It didn't happen before the deadline, but the Broncos got their man in the offseason. Waddle is the most recent example of the Broncos' pre-deadline trade maneuvers.
If the Broncos really want to go big and find that one missing piece for the now and the future, there could be some opportunities to do just that, depending on whether they're willing to pay for the privilege.
Today, I'm breaking down five dream trade targets that would put the Broncos on much more solid Super Bowl footing. Keep in mind that these are dream trade scenarios. The likelihood of them happening is very low, so let's have some fun.
I can't think of a better player to add to this roster and really strike fear into the rest of the league than Simmons. Pairing Simmons with Zach Allen on the Broncos' interior, with Nik Bonitto and this edge-rushing group, would give this team the most feared defensive front in the NFL.
On top of his ability to get after the quarterback, Simmons is also an excellent run defender. He won’t fix all of Denver's problems on defense, but adding maybe the best interior defensive lineman in football would put the league on notice.
Simmons's contract is one of the biggest hurdles to making this a reality. The Titans just signed him to an extension, and they'd take on a big dead-money hit to trade him so soon. On top of that, the Titans would likely ask for something similar to Myles Garrett-type compensation.
That might not be in the Broncos' best interest for winning now and in the future.
Broncos Country has been pounding the table for a top-tier linebacker for years. The Broncos have made some attempts through the draft and free agency, but they either saw their target get drafted before their pick, or they got priced out of what they were willing to spend.
Maybe the Broncos' best option for an upgrade is through a trade. The Eagles seem willing to listen to trade inquiries right now. They're not fully committing to a rebuild yet, but if they lose another couple of games between now and November 10, I could see the Eagles taking more calls.
Sean Payton is very familiar with Baun, having drafted him in the third round back in 2020 with the New Orleans Saints. Baun didn’t have his breakout years under Payton, but I could see the Broncos head coach wanting to make up for lost time.
Baun has been a huge surprise for the Eagles and a big part of why they have been able to field a top-tier defense in recent years. He's 30 years old, but he doesn’t have a lot of wear and tear like so many linebackers of his age do.
Baun would also fit well into the Vane Joseph system as an aggressive downhill attacker who can also drop back into coverage. Baun might be the most realistic player to become a Bronco on this list, and I doubt it would cost an arm and a leg to get it done.
Perhaps an early Day 3 pick would close the deal.
Again, the Eagles seem like sellers at this time, and I could see Barkley added to the list of trade bait. He's heading into the back-nine of his career, which could mean the Eagles don't view him as part of their future plan.
Barkley is still playing at a very high level, averaging 5.5 yards per carry despite a shaky Eagles offensive line.
The Broncos' offensive struggles this season have been blamed on Davis Webb, but the poor execution is the biggest culprit. Running back is one position where an upgrade would do wonders for how everything else functions.
J.K. Dobbins doesn’t look healthy, RJ Harvey is more of a receiving option, and Jonah Coleman is on injured reserve until Week 7 at the soonest. Adding Barkley to this room would give the Broncos a back who can make something from nothing and force teams to respect the run game asa threat.
This is another situation where I don't think the trade would be too costly. With Barkley being 29 years old, I would guess a late Day 2/early Day 3 pick might be able to get a deal done.
Payne coming to Denver would probably not get people too excited. He had one great season a few years back and has been mostly average otherwise.
However, Payne would give the Broncos a very good run defender who could be added to the interior rotation. He can be streaky as a pass rusher, but there is no denying he is a force in the middle of a defense and does well holding his ground and locating the ball carrier.
Payne getting traded could also be a very realistic option. The Commanders are not looking great so far this season and he has an expiring contract.
Once again, the compensation would be overly pricey to acquire Payne — if the Broncos were of a mind to call Washington. He has a sizable cap hit, though, if he were to be traded, meaning the Broncos would likely want to rework his contract before making any kind of deal for him.
McBride might be the least likely trade of the five listed here. But the Broncos need some help on offense, and landing arguably the best tight end in football could elevate this offense.
McBride is one of the NFL's biggest matchup nightmares regardless of position. Throw in how he would instantly become a safety valve for Bo Nix and a weapon he could grow with over the next several years, and it's clear why McBride fits the dream scenario.
There would be hurdles to making such a trade possible. McBride just recently got paid, making it very difficult for Arizona to clear his contract.
Another big hurdle would be the compensation required to pry McBride off Arizona's hands. The tight end position is not usually considered high value, but he's such a game-changing player, I can't imagine he'd go for anything less than a first-round pick.
Are the Broncos willing to give up such premium draft capital for a non-premium position? The answer is likely no, but pairing McBride with Nix for the next several years would be a dream scenario.
The likelihood of any of these deals getting done is, again, very slim. Payton has never traded anything higher than a fourth-round pick at the deadline, and Broncos GM George Paton seems to be more inclined toward a seller's posture than a buyer's.
That said, the Broncos would be wise to make a move of some type ahead of the deadline. Maybe not Simmons, Barkley, or McBride big , but the Broncos have several positions that could use an in-season talent infusion.

title: Chargers' Strengths Are Clear, but Broncos Can Exploit These Flaws
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers may be winless, but they still have plenty of talent.
However, the Chargers also have glaring holes that should be easy to attack. That's exactly what the Denver Broncos will be aiming to do at SoFi Stadium.
The question is whether the Broncos can execute well enough to exploit the Chargers' biggest weaknesses, while doing what it takes to neutralize the biggest threats L.A. poses. If the Broncos struggle to do either, this game will be much closer that it should be.
Leading up to this game, I've laid out two key matchups , my bold predictions , and the Broncos' sleepers to watch . Now it's time to examine the biggest threats the Chargers pose to the Broncos on both sides of the ball, as well as the vulnerable spots Denver can attack.
Quentin Johnston would have been the guy here, but after he was ruled out on Friday, I had to make an audible. Gadsden is a talented receiving tight end who can create mismatches against linebackers and safeties.
His role in the Chargers' offense hasn't been clearly defined, which could be a needed break for the Broncos, given their recent issues with tight ends, especially tackling them (see the Travis Kelce and George Kittle touchdowns).
Even so, the Broncos will have to be wary of the threat Gadsden poses. Vance Joseph will need to have a plan to account for Gadsden, especially given some of the plays the tight end made against Denver a year ago when L.A.'s offense was performing at a significantly higher level.
Strange has been terrible since entering the NFL, and this year has been much the same. He has been the weak link in the Chargers' run game, has allowed nine pressures, and has been called for four penalties.
Strange has been one of the NFL's worst guards to start the season. Even with the Broncos' defensive line featuring Zach Allen and others, this should be a game where Malcolm Roach or Eyioma Uwazurike shines.
Even if that doesn't happen, Allen is poised for another monster game. With the Chargers' offensive line so beaten up and missing three starters, the Broncos have no excuse but to win in the trenches. The opportunities for the big negative plays will be there against Strange.
The Chargers have a very underrated corner in Still. He has size, length, and athleticism that help him match up with almost any type of receiver.
Still's versatility is a boost, and he can take the ball away anytime you target him. Now, he isn't immune to giving up big plays, as he is a risk-taker when attacking the ball, so the Broncos can still look to his side as long as they're calculated.
Despite Still's ball skills, he's yet to notch an interception this year, with only four in his career (all in 2024), and only two pass breakups, both in Week 4.
Phillips is playing a lot with Denzel Perryman out, leaving a void at the second level of L.A.'s defense. Daiyan Henley is a great linebacker, but he is struggling to put out the fires Phillips creates while Perryman has been sidelined.
Now, Phillips is a lighter downhill linebacker, which creates openings in the run game, and he really struggles in coverage. Denver should look to isolate matchups on Phillips, especially with running back RJ Harvey, tight end Evan Engram, or a receiver, and hunt for opportunities that come at the beleaguered linebacker's expense.

title: Detroit Lions 2026 First Quarter Grades: Defense
full_text:
The NFL regular season is over a quarter of the way done.
With five weeks in the books, the Detroit Lions have accomplished a 3-2 record entering their bye week. While there have been some struggles on defense, there have also been some encouraging moments that suggest signs of progress.
Ultimately, though the team has plenty of weapons on offense, it will likely be the performance of coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's defense that determines the team's ceiling. There are clear concerns, and using the bye week to find some answers will be pivotal for the team.
Here are grades for each defensive position group following the first five games of the 2026 season.
Getting some extra production in the pass-rush was a big point of emphasis across the fan base, as finding a reliable second option to work with Aidan Hutchinson is something fans have longed for. Ultimately, the Lions seem to have found that in veteran D.J. Wonnum.
Through five games, Wonnum leads the team with five sacks and is rapidly approaching his career high of eight in a season, which he has notched twice. He has sacked the opposing quarterback in each of the last two games, and has had two games with two sacks in that span.
Hutchinson, to his own credit, has been solid with four while Alim McNeill has posted three. Hutchinson is tied-for-first in pressures with 32, and has a league-best 91.1 pass-rush grade from Pro Football Focus.
Meanwhile, McNeill leads all interior defensive linemen with 23 pressures. This gives Detroit two of the top-performing defensive linemen.
The Lions have also been encouraged with the performance of a pair of young players in Tyleik Williams and Skyler Gill-Howard. The two players have worked as a tandem, with Williams serving as the run-stuffer while Gill-Howard offers athleticism in pass-rush situations.
Gill-Howard ranks first amongst rookie interior defensive linemen with 13 pressures, and is 16th in the entire league in that metric after five games.
Detroit's defense currently leads the league in sacks, and while there have been struggles as a unit against the run, this performance in pass-rush has given them a big boost at times where they've needed it most.
Signed to a contract extension after an All-Pro season last year, Jack Campbell has had an up-and-down start to the season. He was tasked in stepping up both on the field and as a leader with the departure of Alex Anzalone, and to this point hasn't quite been able to reach that level.
That said, there have been some encouraging moments for him. He had the game-winning strip sack against the Jets late in the fourth-quarter, and has improved in recent weeks.
Derrick Barnes has also played a big role, and shined in the team's season-opening win over the New Orleans Saints. Malcolm Rodriguez and Devin White have split duties as the third linebacker, though White is expected to miss some time after suffering a forearm injury Sunday.
White's injury could open up more opportunities for Jimmy Rolder, who has shown some flashes in a small role. His biggest moment to this point has been a tackle for loss against the Carolina Panthers in Week 4.
Trevor Nowaske has also flashed some ability, as his presence makes the unit faster. He has earned more opportunities, and is another candidate to fill the void left by White's injury.
The group that has faced the most scrutiny to this point for Detroit has been their secondary, with many questioning Brad Holmes' lack of activity amidst the Terrion Arnold saga that ended with the former first-round pick being released.
At cornerback, the Lions have leaned on D.J. Reed as the top corner, but the veteran has yet to show that he can be a shutdown corner in their man-coverage oriented offense. He has allowed an opposing passer rating of 124.2, which is the worst amongst Detroit's cornerbacks.
Opposite him, Rock Ya-Sin began the year as the starter but has been replaced by Roger McCreary. While McCreary has taken his lumps, he recorded six passes defensed in the win over Arizona which suggests that he could be an answer.
The safety position has also taken some lumps, with Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph both sidelined. Avonte Maddox, who began the year as a starter next to Chuck Clark, suffered a season-ending injury in Week 2.
That injury has forced Christian Izien into a bigger role, and the free agent acquisition has been serviceable. However, he did not log any defensive snaps Sunday as Keith Abney got a look at safety against Arizona, and that could be something the team explores as the season progresses.
Ultimately, the group is set to get a boost as soon as out of the bye with Brian Branch returning to practice next week. When he returns, he could be a much-needed spark for Sheppard's group.

title: 6 Lions Candidates Who Could Replace Tom Kennedy, Return Punts
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will be without wide receiver Tom Kennedy for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season.
Head coach Dan Campbell confirmed the news that the special teams ace and longest tenured member of the roster would need surgery to repair a significant MCL injury.
According to NFL media, "HC Dan Campbellw as hopeful Kennedy's absence would be shorter but further testing revealed the extent of the damage."
Speaking with local reporters, the former NFL tight end indicated he did not want wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown to return punts on a full-time basis, but would be in the mix on occasion.
The front office is currently looking across the league for potential replacements, but since the team is on a bye week, there is no real urgency this week.
Detroit next takes the field following their Week 6 bye next Sunday against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field.
Here are six Lions candidates who could fill in, while general manager Brad Holmes surveys the landscape to potentially add a new member to the roster.
While Saylors is not an elite touchdown threat, he has served admirably as the kick returner since last season.
According to the team, he ranked seventh in the NFL last season (27.2 yards/return).
He led the Lions and ranked ninth in the NFL with 897 kickoff return yards in 2025. He joined the Lions as an undrafted free agent after signing with the Bengals, following the 2023 NFL Draft.
The speedy wideout is always a threat to return a punt to the end zone due to his speed and elusiveness.
Similar to St. Brown, Detroit may not be comfortable with an offensive weapon serving in this role.
Campbell indicated Lovett was in the mix and could be an ideal first choice to replace the injured wideout. Lovett is currently on the practice squad.
In 12 games last season, he recorded one kickoff return for 22 yards.
Vaki has seen his role expanded in Detroit's offense as this season has progressed. He is considered among the top special teams players in the league.
"Ultimately in order to do well, you need good players," said special teams coach Dave Fipp. "And so we've been fortunate here since I've been here. We've had a lot of really good special teams players and a lot of guys embrace that role. And that really starts with (General manager Brad (Holmes) and those guys drafting good players and making sure that the bottom of the roster are guys that can help and contribute.
"Obviously (Lions Head Coach) Dan (Campbell) doing the same thing. So yeah, I mean we’ve still got our hands full and we got a long season to go, but yeah, a lot of the success starts at the very top and it really is the players.”
St. Brown did put the football on the ground a couple of time against the Cardinals. While he excels in many categories, it would be wise to only use the former first-round pick in spot duty to return punts.
Detroit can ill afford to lose St. Brown or any other key weapon for an extended period of time.
While lacking in return experience, he did serve as the kick returner after Kennedy departed the game in Week 5.
Dorsey has been a staple on special teams for the past few seasons. He could be used as the backup option, should the primary choice also go down with injury.

title: Detroit Lions Must Take Serious Look at Defense, Make Tough Decisions
full_text:
Dan Campbell and the Detroit Lions bounced back in a huge way Sunday, defeating the Arizona Cardinals, 45-21.
The Lions, which had lost two of their previous three games, seemingly heard the critics loud and clear. They played with an extra source of motivation and left no stone unturned in the Week 5 contest, notably scoring on seven straight drives from the second quarter on.
Detroit do-it-all back Jahmyr Gibbs spearheaded the dominant offensive effort, delivering a sensational performance. He notched big run after big run, evading defenders left and right on his way to 151 yards and two touchdowns on 25 carries.
Gibbs flashed big-play ability all afternoon, reminding Lions fans on multiple occasions of legendary back Barry Sanders. Gibbs finished the intraconference affair with a season-high 207 all-purpose yards .
With each passing week, Gibbs draws more and more comparisons to Sanders. And those won't stop anytime soon, especially now that the fourth-year back has surpassed the Lions all-time great for the most touchdowns in NFL history before the age of 25 (58).
Gibbs wasn't the only offensive standout for the Lions Sunday, either.
Detroit signal-caller Jared Goff produced yet another efficient performance to open up the 2026 campaign. The veteran quarterback played mistake-free ball, throwing for three touchdowns and zero interceptions in the blowout victory.
And through five weeks, Goff has compiled an impressive 1,485 passing yards and 12 passing touchdowns without tossing a single interception.
He's playing the definition of winning football, and is now just one of two quarterbacks in NFL history to throw for that many touchdowns without an interception through a season‘s first five games. The other QB: Russell Wilson.
"Goff is just Goff. He’s as good as they come,” Campbell said after the Week 5 win. “I’ve been so impressed with the way he’s played. He’s just gotten better every year, and here we are five in, he’s even better than last year. He’s the real deal.”
Goff is “the real deal” and has been all season long. And on Sunday, his teammates came through with their best collective performance of the 2026 campaign.
Yet, it doesn't mean the Lions have nothing to worry about headed into their bye week.
The Lions are still very much a flawed team, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. And while getting Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch will provide a much-needed boost, it won't cure all the team's defensive woes.
The Lions will notably remain thin at the cornerback position, a weakness which will likely continue to be the team's Achilles’ heel. Additionally, it's a sizable enough deficiency to where it could impede Detroit's efforts to win games in future weeks, just as it already has multiple times this season.
Along with that, Campbell & Co. need to take a critical look at defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's performance this season.
More often than not in 2026, Sheppard has been unable to put the defense in position to succeed. He's become known not only for devising faulty gameplans but also for failing to make the necessary in-game adjustments to get his unit off the field.
So, just because the Lions held the Cardinals to 21 points Sunday, it doesn't mean the second-year coordinator is off the hot seat all of a sudden. In fact, his fate is still very much in question, and I'm not yet convinced he's the right man to lead the defense moving forward.
Campbell & Co. could very well feel the same way. Subsequently, if they decide to keep him in charge of the defense, it doesn't mean he's guaranteed a job the remainder of the season. I think he deserves to be assessed on a weekly basis, and if his job performance regresses, there should be serious consideration for stripping him of his duties.
Sheppard still has much to prove in the weeks ahead, and so do the Lions.
Through the first five games of 2026, Campbell's squad has hardly looked the part of a Super Bowl contender. And beating the Cardinals doesn't move the needle for me (and it shouldn't for you, either).
Remember, Arizona was reeling coming into Sunday, and with the Week 5 loss, has now dropped four consecutive games. Consequently, you can't use the matchup with the Cardinals as a true measuring stick for where the Lions stand as a team.
The offense was undeniably explosive against Arizona, and has been the highest-scoring unit in the league so far this year.
However, it won't mean a thing if the defense reverts to its bad habits against Green Bay in Week 7. Sheppard, for his sake and the sake of Detroit's playoff hopes , can ill-afford for that to happen.
Without question, the Lions’ success the remainder of 2026 hinges upon Sheppard's ability to get the most out of the team's defensive personnel.

title: Everything Jared Goff Said After Detroit Lions Defeated Cardinals
full_text:
Here is everything Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff said, after the team earned their third victory of the 2026 NFL season by defeating the Arizona Cardinals 45-21.
The veteran signal-caller and Russell Wilson are now the only quarterbacks in NFL history to toss for 12 or more touchdowns and no interceptions, through the first five games of any season.
Against the Cardinals, Goff threw for 271 yards and three touchdowns. He added a rushing touchdown as well in the blowout victory.
On the aggressive approach to the game on both sides of the ball
“I think that’s kind of a part of our identity . It certainly has been in the success that we’ve had over the years. When we’re able to lean on teams and make them uncomfortable in situations that we’re comfortable with in some of these fourth downs and some of the stuff they’re doing defensively on third downs, it is the way we want to play. It is the way we want to be dominant and in control.”
Whether he felt the aggressive approach was necessary today
“I'm sure Dan (Campbell) may have, I think it worked so I would say I’m glad we did a lot of it. I don’t think it had anything to do with them. I think it's just we wanted to kind of get back to who we are and early on there, certainly we were sputtering. You've got to give kudos to our defense for holding us down there those first three drives and keeping us in it and not allowing that game to get out of hand. Then I think we scored seven drives in a row. We had a good day.”
Significance of the fourth-down conversion by TE Sam LaPorta
“I thought Sam was the catalyst today for everything. He really was. He had the fourth-down conversion on the in-cut which wasn’t a great throw and he made a great catch . Then he had the fourth down, fourth-and-one touchdown. Then he had a number of other catches — the third down and long that I checked down to him that he went and I think he got us into fourth and one, which we then scored on. Those three plays alone changed the entire landscape of the game and he's a hell of a player and I'm happy he's on our side. ”
On the play of running back Jahmyr Gibbs
“There are a lot of comparisons there, but he’s unbelievable. He really is. We did a good job in the run game, and still probably didn’t do as well as we could and he made a lot of guys miss in the backfield. and got a lot after the first touch. Obviously, he caught the ball well in the backfield. I think he had what, 50 or 60 yards through the air. Gosh, he’s electric. I think you saw the full scope of what we’re capable of.”
The importance of taking care of the ball after having five turnovers for gain so far this season
“I mean, some of them bounced our way. I think I had a sack-fumble today that we landed on, but I’ve been very conscious of that and through the last handful of years of my career tried to really focus on that. I have been doing a good job of that up to this point. Again, a lot of this stuff is the way the ball bounces, but I’m proud of that right now and want to keep that going.”
What the performance can do for the team going into the bye week?
“You almost wish you could play tomorrow after a game like today, but it’s good. It really is. It is better than the alternative and to win in the way we did — I think the way we were feeding off each other today and the energy the defense was giving us — that’s the way the game goes. It is a complementary football game and you could certainly feel it. I felt all day of (the fact that) they were playing with energy and swagger and then we were feeding off that, getting short field, scoring and then they would multiply that. It feels good to win in that way for sure.”
On the seven straight scoring drives
“It felt like (Offensive coordinator) Drew (Petzing) could call whatever he wanted and we were going to make it work. I think today was a good example of, like I've said, where we can go and what we are capable of. I think I said it earlier last week (but) we’ve been good, right? Today we were great ,and there are still some things to be better at certainly, but today we were like ‘OK, that’s what we were capable of.” It’s good to know that’s our standard now and we can hold guys accountable to what we just did today.”
On whether the win was meaningful for offensive coordinator Drew Petzing:
“I think it’s cool. I really think it is not as meaningful as it may seem outside to us, but yeah I think it’s cool anytime that happens against your former team. It's cool.”

title: Detroit Lions Grades: Offense Shakes Off Struggles, Mows Down Cardinals
full_text:
The Detroit Lions got off to a sluggish start in Week 5 against the Arizona Cardinals.
They went three-and-out on their first series, then gave up a touchdown to the Cardinals on their first defensive series. However, when the second quarter rolled around, their fortunes changed dramatically.
Pushed forward by some aggression offensively, the Lions scored on seven consecutive drives including 31 unanswered points at one time and wound up with an emphatic 45-21 win to move to 3-2 on the season.
Here are grades for each position group following the Lions' dismantling of the Cardinals.
Jared Goff was once again excellent for the majority of Sunday's game. He was sacked on his first two drop-backs, including on a safety blitz from Budda Baker that wasn't picked up, but was clean and efficient after that.
Goff made some tight window throws to Sam LaPorta and Jameson Williams to convert fourth downs, with the throw to Williams going for a touchdown. His first touchdown pass came on a well-designed concept that left LaPorta running uncovered up the right sideline.
The veteran finished 19-of-30 for 271 yards and three touchdowns, and now has 12 passing touchdowns and zero interceptions through five games. He became the second quarterback to have thrown 12 touchdowns and no interceptions through that time frame.
Jahmyr Gibbs helped spark the Lions' offense. After the initial fourth-down conversion to LaPorta, Gibbs rushed for 16 yards on the next play fueled by a push from several of his teammates. He'd punch it in two plays later, giving him the first of his two scores on the afternoon.
The Alabama product broke Barry Sanders' record for most touchdowns by any player under the age of 25, and will likely create some serious separation given that he doesn't turn 25 until next March.
Gibbs also had some valuable reps in pass-protection and had an overall thorough performance. He tallied 151 rushing yards and two scores on the ground, along with five catches for 56 yards as a receiver.
The Lions had some unique looks for their wide receivers in Sunday's game. There was a double reverse involving Amon-Ra St. Brown that turned into a screen, as well as multiple slot-screen looks for St. Brown.
Ultimately, the group was highly efficient throughout the game. Jameson Williams made his two catches count, as both went for touchdowns including a 39-yard scoring grab in the third quarter after he beat his defender deep.
St. Brown had 69 yards on six catches, while Isaac TeSlaa did not have a catch on two targets. In an unfortunate development, Tom Kennedy went down with a knee injury on a punt return and did not re-enter the game.
LaPorta was a huge spark for the offense in Sunday's game. After the team went three drives without a first-down, they finally broke through when LaPorta snagged a 12-yard reception on a fourth-down to move the chains and set up their first touchdown.
He'd reach the end zone on the next drive, as some clever play-designing from Drew Petzing left him all alone for a 38-yard touchdown on a fourth-and-1. LaPorta would finish with a game-high 88 receiving yards on five catches.
It was a tough start for Detroit's offensive line, as their first two pass plays ended in sacks. Budda Baker's blitz was well-timed and simply overpowered the outnumbered line, while center Juice Scruggs was to blame for the second sack as he was beat by former Lion Roy Lopez.
After that tough start, however, everything clicked for the group. They finished averaging over five yards per carry on the ground, and would allow just one more sack.
Rookie Blake Miller took some lumps, as he was whistled for two penalties, but delivered another reliable performance.
The Lions notched five sacks on Sunday, giving them 20 as a team which is the most in franchise history through five games. D.J. Wonnum led the charge with two sacks, both of which came at key points in the first half.
Aidan Hutchinson teamed up with linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez on a sack that forced a fourth-quarter turnover on downs, while rookie Skyler Gill-Howard and Alim McNeill teamed up for one to force a long field goal that was ultimately missed.
Detroit did some shuffling with their linebacking corps ahead of kickoff, with Devin White returning to the starting lineup. However, White suffered a forearm injury in the first half and is expected to miss significant time.
As a result, the Lions leaned on their depth. Jack Campbell had a team-high 11 tackles, and had good coverage on Trey McBride's touchdown where the tight end made an incredible juggling catch.
Elsewhere, Derrick Barnes had a sack and five tackles while Rodriguez was credited with a half-sack when he teamed up with Hutchinson.
Sunday was Detroit's best defensive game to date, and one of their top performers was cornerback Roger McCreary. The Cardinals went after McCreary early and often Sunday, and he finished the game with a team-high six passes defensed.
D.J. Reed had three tackles for loss amidst his seven solo tackles in Sunday's game. Rookie Keith Abney logged some snaps at the safety position, and recorded his first-career interception on the final play of the first half.
Detroit had some early miscues on special teams, as they were called for illegal formation on kick return and nearly had a punt blocked. However, they were outstanding in the return game with Tom Kennedy and Jacob Saylors notching some big returns.
Kennedy was replaced by Amon-Ra St. Brown as the punt returner when he exited, and St. Brown nearly had a disaster as he coughed up the ball on his first return. However, Tay Martin avoided the damage by recovering the fumble.
Jake Bates remained perfect on the year, connecting on a 46-yard field goal before the half and knocking through all of his extra points.
While the slow start took away the potential for a perfect showing for the coaching staff, it was their best schematic game through the first five weeks. Offensive coordinator Drew Petzing had a number of well-designed plays go for big gains, and defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard worked around a tough start to dial up a nice showing.
At one point, the defense had forced five-straight three-and-outs, which was a big development from weeks past. Sheppard seemed to be pulling the right strings throughout the game, which led to the success.
Now, the Lions get a week to recover and bounce back before two-straight divisional games that will be pivotal to Detroit's hopes of winning the division.

title: Everything Dan Campbell Said After Detroit Lions Defeated Cardinals
full_text:
Here is everything Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell said to reporters, after defeating the Arizona Cardinals, 45-21, at State Farm Stadium.
The former NFL tight end took the opportunity to immediately give play-by-play voice Dan Miller a game ball.
Miller's wife, Cindy Miller, passed away, significantly impacting the organization and the roster.
“We'll start with this. This ball goes to Dan Miller and his family. It was hard to hear what they went through. It's been a tough road for Dan. This is for him. Salt of the earth, Dan is salt of the earth, and I know this has been hard. But now I know Cindy's (Miller) at peace, and we love you, Dan. So appreciate you. I'll open with that. The guys really responded in a big way. I thought our defense really got everything started; we attacked the run. I thought we were sticking in coverage. Very disciplined, minus a couple of plays there. I thought ‘Shep’ (Defensive Coordinator Kelvin Sheppard) and the staff did an outstanding job. The players really responded. They took it to heart. Tried to do all the little things right and we played with aggressiveness, and just really set the tone for the day. The offense fed off of that and once we found our rhythm, then the defense fed off of them and special teams, and I just thought it was a great team effort. We cleaned up a lot of the little stuff. It's not good enough; it's not. We're going to have to be a hell of a lot better when we play Green Bay coming out of the bye. But that was a step in the right direction. It got us to win number three going into the bye. I was proud of them.”
Sam LaPorta’s success on fourth down calls
“Yes, that was big, that was really big. Took it in the back of the head on a critical catch; that was a contested catch. That was a great job by (Lions QB Jared) Goff progressing through, we're going to  'Saint' (Amon-Ra St. Brown). I mean, he worked his way through it. The O-line gave him time and he found it, gave him a ball to make a play on and he went and made a play and then took a shot, held on to it. It was huge. That was really big. I thought the guys answered the bell and I thought we played pretty fearless today. That’s what we have to be able to do. That's our offense. I thought our guys really fed off each other. The O-line got going, and opened some holes, and then 'Jah' (Jahmyr Gibbs) started to come to life. He obviously made some of his own plays there once we got him started. (Sam) LaPorta was huge for us today. Jamo (Jameson Williams) was huge for us today. Those guys really stepped up and obviously 'Jah', in the run and pass game. Goff is just Goff. He's as good as they come. I’ve just been so impressed with the way he's played these five games here. I thought he's just gotten better every year, and here we are five in, and he's even better than last year. He's the real deal. Proud of these guys. I thought special teams played with some enthusiasm, some energy, which we were looking for. Our specialists did a heck of a job (Jack) Fox and (Jake) Bates. It was a good team effort; good team win.”
How important it was to play this game with a sense of urgency?
“I think the important thing is that you go all in no matter what you're going to do. Either it crumbles or they rise up, but you're going all in. You have to push your chips all the way in and you have to believe in it. We did, we applied a little pressure. Players really responded, did a great job, and they brought it to life here on Sunday. It's a good win. It'll be nice to be able to enjoy this on this flight home and for a couple of days here going into the bye.”
On getting their sense of aggression back
“Yes, it felt good. When you believe in your players, you believe in the matchups, and you feel your young players are growing. That's a lot of it. We have a young (team). Our right tackle is young, our right guard is young, our left guard is young. So when your O-line has some youth in it, they have to continue to grow and you have to be able to trust if we get certain looks, or we get a curveball, (or) it's 4th down. There's a lot that goes into it, and I really feel like they're growing. They did a heck of a job today. We picked up the protection really well. ‘Jah’ had a couple of critical pro protection reps that helped us on some of those downs. It helped, and as I said, once we get in a rhythm , we are hard to stop, and we were hard today to stop.”
On what impressed him most about the defense
“I just love the pass defense. ‘PDs’ (passes defensed), man. We got our hands on some footballs (and) we knocked some footballs down. I didn't feel like we were stressed. That's good to see. Roger (McCreary) wasn't perfect, but I thought Roger really played some sticky coverage today and I thought (D.J.) Reed played some sticky coverage. That was good to see us challenge some footballs on the back end and work in unison. We played sticky and then we got a sack. We closed the pocket in and made some huge plays there. Just to get that many 3-and-outs back-to-back-to-back, and then you answer offensively — that's the white squall. Here comes the massive wave that's coming at you, and it felt that way a little bit so that's good. We just have to get better there. We have to continue to do those things, play off of each other and be on top of the little stuff. Honestly, the couple of things we did get hit on — those are ‘mentals’ (mental mistakes). Those are ‘mentals’ and they can't happen. You can't play that good for that long and all of a sudden we get dirty eyes or we mess something up and we give up a 30-yard (play) and now they're in field goal range. It was better and I thought those guys answered the bell .”
Thoughts on playing more man-to-man coverage this week
“It helped today. You have to go by what opponent it is. We knew ‘85’ (Cardinals tight end Trey McBride), they were going to get him the football and he's a factor. They're going to target him and they're going to go to him. And then ‘14’ (Cardinals wideout Michael Wilson) is their other bell cow. He's a good receiver and he does it the hard way. He'll muscle you and wrestle you — that's what ‘85’ does too. They're pretty crafty guys so we knew we had to try to eliminate those two and it just felt like the right thing to do today. That was good. For what we did, the game plan, ‘Shep’ (Kelvin Sheppard) did a good job, players executed, and it was a ‘W.’"
On whether he felt like the team's back was against the wall this week which led to them being more aggressive on fourth downs and playing more man coverage?
“No I just felt like it was what was right for this opponent. Every week's a little bit different — we play man-to-man. We play man every game, it's just how much do you play it? Most teams play some man-to-man on third down no matter what you believe in. We opened it up a little bit today — a little bit more and reduced the variables of other things that can happen in zone (coverage) for this opponent and knowing what they had. When you do that and you do some of the things we did — there are guys who have one-on-ones in man coverage so you have to win. You have to win. You can take away guys — their best players or a best player — but somebody's still single and that player has to win. We won today.”
Update on the injuries to Lions LB Devin White and WR Tom Kennedy
“It doesn’t look good. I think Devin’s probably going to need surgery. It’s a broken forearm; it’s unfortunate. I hate it because he was doing some good things for us in this game. Then for T.K., it doesn’t look good. As far as anything short-term, we’ll know a lot more tomorrow. I think it could be a sprain somewhere in there, a pretty good sprain. title: 8 Winners, 3 Losers From Lions’ Win Over Cardinals
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions looked to get back to their winning ways in Arizona. The Lions looked to rebound following a loss to Carolina in Week 4, squaring off against a 1-3 Cardinals team.
The Cardinals started with a strong defensive effort , sacking Goff on each of his first two dropbacks and scoring on their opening drive. However, it was all Motown after that, with the Lions up, 24-7, at half. The Lions kept their foot on the pedal after the break, and a garbage-time touchdown by Arizona gave the 45-21 final an ounce of respectability.
Here are the winners and losers from the contest.
Kennedy provided a spark during an underwhelming first quarter for the Lions, with a 22-yard punt return setting up the offense in Cardinal territory. His next return was not as far on the yardage, but also set the Lions up with the ball at midfield. Unfortunately, he was injured on the play. Kennedy did not return to the game.
LaPorta was the first player on the offense to wake up after an extremely slow first quarter, with the tight end recording 61 yards and a touchdown in the first half. His first catch of the game was on fourth down, giving the Lions their initial first down of the game.
The Iowa product would add a 38-yard scoring strike after the Cardinals got caught looking at a play action to Gibbs.
LaPorta was not done on the day, either, adding two more catches for 27 yards to finish as the leading receiver on the day with 88 yards.
Wonnum was part of the stout defensive unit that gave Jacoby Brissett and the Arizona offense fits. The first-year Lions defender had his second multi-sack game, taking down Brissett twice. On his second sack, it was a pure effort play. Wonnum got into the backfield for pressure, but was evaded.
The defensive end refused to call it a play and chased down Brissett for the sack.
Williams has had a solid start to the 2026 season, but was held out of the end zone in the receiving game. The former Lions first-round pick took that as a challenge, scoring in each half.
Both touchdowns were displays of Williams’ pure speed, with the wide receiver flying past his corner on a slant for the first and reeling in a deep shot on the latter.
Abney II has been in and out of the Lions lineup this season. This week, with Rock Ya-Sin out and Chrisitan Izien getting back to health, it was time for the Lions fifth-round draft selection to be in the lineup. Abney responded with a strong starting effort, and hauled in his first career interception on a desperation heave by Brissett to end the first half.
Gibbs had a lesser role than expected against Carolina, and that was not the case against Arizona. Sonic had 30 touches on the day, and topped 200 yards from scrimmage. The back was all over the field, showcasing his patience on multiple runs and cuts.
Gibbs saved his best play for last, cutting back across the entire defense on the goal line and out accelerating a corner for his second touchdown. That score also pushed him over 150 rushing yards for the day.
Goff had a highly efficient outing for Motown. After an extremely slow start, with the former top overall selection being sacked twice on his first two dropbacks, Goff responded with a four-touchdown game.
The Lions signal-caller threw for 271 yards and three scores, and added a sneak where Goff extended in the air for the score.
McNeill continued his strong start to the season with a half-sack on Sunday. The N.C. State product entered among the top 10 in the league in sacks, and it is clear that his dominant 2023 and 2024 form has returned.
McNeill was a difference-maker until his injury in 2024, and the 2025 season is a distant memory. With the half sack, McNeill has tied his 2024 total, which was achieved in 14 games.
On the second pass play of the game, Scruggs was completely blown off the ball by former Lions DT Roy Lopez. The former Texans offensive lineman stood no chance, and it was a bad rep that was part of a first quarter that saw Detroit finish in the negative for total yardage.
Reed found himself targeted more as the game wore on, with Roger McCreary putting in a strong effort of his own to dissuade Arizona from targeting him. The veteran was picked on, and it did not go well for Reed.
He allowed multiple first downs and catches to continue drives for the Cardinals.
Clark did not meet his standard on Sunday. In the second half, two of the big plays for the Cardinals offense, including a touchdown, came with Clark out of position. In both instances, the veteran defensive back threw his hands up in frustration. Perhaps it was a missed assignment by a teammate, but regardless, it was a bad look for a team leader .

title: Lions Provide Unfortunate Injury Updates on White, Kennedy
full_text:
While the Detroit Lions handled the Arizona Cardinals with ease Sunday afternoon, it was not all positive for Dan Campbell's squad in the desert.
It's because the Lions lost not just one but two players to game-ending injuries in their Week 5 tilt with the Cardinals.
Reports after the game indicated that Devin White left the locker room with his arm in a sling, while Tom Kennedy left on crutches with his right knee in a brace. Campbell provided grim updates on both players as far as their short-term status goes, with White expected to miss significant time.
"Doesn't look good. I think Devin's probably gonna need surgery, broken forearm," Campbell said. "It's unfortunate, I hate it because he was doing some good things for us this game. And then, TK, it doesn't look good as far as anything short-term. We'll know a lot more tomorrow. I think it could be a sprain, somewhere in there, a pretty good sprain. But neither one of them are gonna be around for a bit here, I hate that. Both players have done a really good job here."
White, who was active for the first time since Week 2, suffered a forearm injury in the final seconds of the first quarter. The game broadcast, televised on FOX, showed the veteran defender leaving the field on a cart, and he was later ruled out for the rest of the game.
Reserve linebackers Trevor Nowaske and Malcolm Rodriguez logged the majority of the snaps in place of White.
White, who was signed by the Lions less than a week into training camp this summer, has recorded 10 total tackles in three games with Detroit.
Then later in the first half, Kennedy suffered a knee ailment. It came on a 22-yard return in which his foot got caught in the State Farm Stadium turf and his right knee bent awkwardly.
"TK, I really thought hit it. We kind of challenged him on getting some of these returns. His first was outstanding," Campbell said. "His second one, he caught it and put his foot in the ground. He took it to heart, and I hate it for him that that happened. But, I don't think it's long, long-term. I think this is something that, we're gonna miss him for a little bit."
Initially, Kennedy was able to walk off the field on his own. However, after being examined in the blue tent, he was carted off to the locker room, and was eventually ruled out for the second half of the Week 5 matchup . He finished the contest with two punt returns for 33 yards.
The Lions are light on receiver depth, with only Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa and Tay Martin as the other options on the active roster. Detroit does have three receivers on the practice squad in Lawrence Keys, Lucky Jackson and Dominic Lovett.
St. Brown proceeded to replace Kennedy on punt return duties. He logged two punt returns in Kennedy's absence, amassing 36 yards, including 31 yards on his first return of the day.
Altogether, St. Brown compiled 105 all-purpose yards in the road victory for Detroit.
Next up for the Lions is their bye week, which will be followed by a pivotal NFC North matchup with the Green Bay Packers in Week 7.

title: Key Takeaways From Detroit Lions 45-21 Victory Over Arizona Cardinals
full_text:
The Detroit Lions entered Week 5 looking to get some much-needed momentum moving in their direction.
After a crushing loss to the Carolina Panthers evened their record at 2-2, the Lions traveled to State Farm Stadium looking to jump over the .500 mark ahead of their Week 6 bye.
Moving into their Week 5 matchup with Arizona, the Lions emphasized consistency after their performance fluctuated throughout the first four weeks.
"Yeah, any time you have a loss, you can't wait to get back to work and get back to the next game to get that taste out of your mouth," head coach Dan Campbell said in a pregame interview with Lions flagship radio. "At the end of the day, you've got to keep in mind that everything is about improvement, man. As much as you'd like to take these giant leaps, that's not how it works. The most important thing is the steady climb, and that's what we haven't done. We've done this teeter, this kind of roller-coaster. We've got to get out of that and begin to slowly climb every week and get better and better. It starts with Arizona."
Though they started slow, an emphatic second quarter resulted in a dominant 45-21 win for the Lions heading into the bye week. Here are takeaways from the team's win over Arizona.
The Lions elected to take the ball to start the game, but it was a non-ideal start. They went three-and-out, with the drive ending after Budda Baker blitzed untouched and sacked Goff on third-down.
Detroit's defense looked to have the Cardinals neutralized on their opening drive, forcing them into a third-and-11. However, Jacoby Brissett hit Kendrick Bourne for 22 yards to kickstart the drive.
Again, the Lions would force the Cardinals into a crucial situation as Brissett and company would face a fourth-and-1 from Detroit's 9-yard line. Rather than kick a field goal, Arizona dialed up some trickery as wide receiver Michael Wilson tossed the ball to Brissett after a reverse to pick up seven and a first-down.
Arizona would score on the next play, with Brissett hitting Teagan Quitoriano for a 2-yard touchdown to cap off the 14-play, 73-yard drive.
Detroit would go three-and-out on its ensuing drive, with former Lion Roy Lopez putting Detroit behind the sticks immediately with a sack of Jared Goff. They finished the first quarter with three three-and-outs, totaling negative-nine yards of offense in that timeframe.
While the Lions' offense struggled, the defense picked them up by forcing two straight punts to preserve the deficit at 7-0 through the end of the first quarter. After the second, the offense started to pick up steam.
Their momentum was sparked by a fourth-down conversion, as Goff hit Sam LaPorta for 12 yards and an additional 15 was tacked on thanks to a personal foul. After Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 15 yards with the help of his blockers, the Lions would call his number two more times and he reached paydirt to tie the game at 7-7 with 12:22 to go in the first half.
After stopping the Cardinals once again, the Lions caught a break when they were able to fall on a fumbled punt return by Amon-Ra St. Brown. Once again, they found themselves in a fourth-and-short after an unsuccessful challenge by Dan Campbell.
Once again, the Lions converted as Goff hit Sam LaPorta for a 38-yard touchdown. After a play-action fake, LaPorta snuck out wide open up the right sideline and strolled into the end zone to give the Lions the lead.
The defense came up big once again, forcing a three-and-out, and the Lions took advantage offensively. Once again, the Lions converted a pivotal fourth-down as they capped off their third scoring drive with a touchdown from Goff to Jameson Williams on fourth-and-4 from Arizona's 8-yard line.
Defensively, the Lions forced five-straight three-and-outs with D.J. Wonnum putting the exclamation point on the stretch with a third-down sack of Brissett. The Lions would tack on a 46-yard field goal from Jake Bates to take a 24-7 lead late in the first half.
Arizona was able to record a first-down on its final drive of the half, but another sack from Wonnum and the first career interception for Keith Abney II ended the half.
Wonnum with the third-down SACK pic.twitter.com/buiBiRTf7z
The Cardinals moved the ball quickly into Lions territory on their first drive of the second half, with Brissett connecting with Elijah Higgins for a 38-yard gain. However, Alim McNeill and Skyler Gill-Howard teamed up for a sack, and Chad Ryland's 53-yard field goal was no good.
Detroit's offense picked up right where they left off on the ensuing drive. Gibbs had a 10-yard run for a first-down, and then Tate Ratledge made a clutch fumble recovery after St. Brown lost the ball on a reception.
Facing a third-down, Goff dialed up a shot and connected with Jameson Williams on a 39-yard touchdown.
Jameson Williams TD! Second of day pic.twitter.com/lM0yP26n2E
Arizona would rally for their first points since their opening drive. Brissett rolled right and found Quitoriano for a 13-yard score, his second of the day, to make it 31-14 with 4:22 remaining in the third quarter.
However, the Lions snuffed out any momentum the Cardinals may have had by driving 74 yards in eight plays. They finished the drive out with yet another fourth-down conversion, this time a Jared Goff 1-yard quarterback sneak for a score. It was Goff's first rushing touchdown since the 2023 season.
The Lions have several players who logged significant accomplishments on Sunday. Most notably, running back Jahmyr Gibbs set an NFL record for the most touchdowns by a player under the age of 25 with his second rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter.
On a second-and-goal, Gibbs bounced off a tackle and reversed field, racing three yards into the end zone for the record-setting score. It capped off a 13-play, 79-yard drive and gave the Lions a 45-14 lead with five minutes remaining.
The Cardinals would punch in a late touchdown as Brissett hit Trey McBride, who made a terriffic juggling catch.
1.) Detroit Tigers play-by-play broadcaster Jason Benetti filled in as the Lions' play-by-play voice on the radio for Sunday's game. Dan Miller did not call the game after the passing of his wife, Cynthia .
"Our thoughts are with Dan right now, all weekend, and for the future, with the loss of his wife of 33 years, Cindy, a couple of days ago," Benetti said on Sunday's broadcast. "Dan is one of the most remarkable people I have met in my time in Detroit. One of the most sincere human beings you can possibly dream of. A fantastic voice of the Lions for more than two decades."
2.) Linebacker Devin White and wide receiver Tom Kennedy both suffered injuries in the first half. Both players did not return to the game. Amon-Ra St. Brown filled in for Tom Kennedy on punt return duties.
3.) Amon-Ra St. Brown made history on Sunday, passing Minnesota's Justin Jefferson for the most receiving yards in the first six seasons of a career.
4.) The 24 points the Lions scored in the second quarter were the most they've scored in a quarter since 2013.
5.) Wonnum set a new personal best with at least one sack in three-straight games.
