title: 3 Matchups That Could Make or Break the Colts in Pittsburgh
full_text:
For whatever reason, the Indianapolis Colts just do not play well when they travel to Pittsburgh.
The Colts haven't won in Pittsburgh since 2008, including a 27-20 loss at Acrisure Stadium last season. But this time around, Indianapolis has a pretty clean path to finally ending that drought.
Both teams enter Sunday at 2-2, with Indianapolis sitting as a 2.5-point underdog ahead of the 1 p.m. ET kickoff on CBS.
This game should come down to creating pressure and forcing the other quarterback to make mistakes.
Here are three matchups that could decide it.
This one is pretty simple: Make Aaron Rodgers move.
Indianapolis enters Sunday with a 35% pass-rush win rate, which ranks dead last in the entire NFL, via ESPN. They are lined up against Pittsburgh's 10th-ranked pass-blocking unit, and generating pressure has to be the priority.
Rodgers has completed 88 of 153 passes for 999 yards, seven touchdowns and four interceptions, but he has already been sacked 13 times.
And at 42 years old, he isn't exactly escaping the pocket and turning broken plays into 20-yard gains anymore. Rodgers has just seven rushing attempts for 12 yards this season.
If the Colts can consistently win up front and force Rodgers to extend plays with his legs, Pittsburgh's offense becomes significantly more uncomfortable.
The formula isn't complicated. Get Rodgers off his spot, make him move and force him into poor decisions.
Gardner has himself a prove-it game after what happened in London.
He allowed four catches on five targets for 117 yards and a touchdown against Washington, including completions of 47 and 48 yards. Gardner later called his performance "unacceptable," and Sunday gives him an immediate opportunity to respond.
His job is usually pretty simple: Take away the opponent's No. 1 receiver.
This week, that means DK Metcalf.
Metcalf has 16 catches for 213 yards and a touchdown through four games, and he is coming off a 115-yard performance against Cleveland.
Indianapolis absolutely cannot allow Rodgers and Metcalf to get comfortable, especially on the deep ball. Gardner gave up a couple big shots in London, and I would imagine he is itching to pitch a shutout this time around.
This might be the most important matchup of the afternoon.
Jones has been far too careless with the football through four weeks, throwing four interceptions while also putting the ball on the ground multiple times.
Watt already has 4.5 sacks, a forced fumble, a fumble recovery and even a pick-six this season. If Jones gets careless with the football again Sunday, Watt is exactly the kind of player who will make him pay for it.
Jones has to know where No. 90 is at all times.
Get the ball out quickly or roll out to Watt's opposite side. Just don't give him the opportunity to completely wreck the game.
Indianapolis does not need to complicate its game plan this Sunday. Pressure Rodgers, don't let Metcalf beat you deep and keep Watt away from the football.
The formula is right in front of Indianapolis. Now it's a matter of executing it in a stadium that has given this franchise problems for nearly two decades.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: Colts-Steelers Final Injury Report: Who’s In and Who’s Out for Week 5?
full_text:
The final injury reports are in ahead of the Colts and Steelers’ Week 5 clash on Sunday. Both teams go into the weekend with different questions they each need answered before kickoff as they each look to improve to 3-2 on the year.
Let’s take a look at both teams’ reports, determine who’s likely to play, who’s likely to sit out and what each injury means going into an important early-season bout between two conference foes.
Indianapolis Colts Final Injury Report
Indianapolis rules out four players, with no true surprises. That said, the Colts will be down two starters on defense. Defensive end Arden Key is expected to miss multiple games with his hamstring injury, with this week being the first. Linebacker Jaylon Carlies, who had an interception for the Colts last week, also suffered a rib injury that will keep him out of this Sunday’s contest.
Expect plenty of rookie action on Sunday as a result of these knocks. CJ Allen and Bryce Boettcher to both take snaps at linebacker while the edge duo of Caden Curry and George Gumbs Jr. should see some playing time as well. Gumbs is yet to suit up for an NFL game, so his professional debut could be on the horizon.
Ashton Dulin will miss his third game of the season already, so the Colts will have to make things work on special teams without their top gunner. Tight end Will Mallory just had his 21-day practice window opened on Wednesday after starting the season on injured reserve, but him being ruled out against Pittsburgh proves the Colts are using an abundance of caution with him moving forward.
Center Tanor Bortolini went from limited on Wednesday to a full participant Thursday, and now logged another full practice Friday. He enters the weekend without an injury designation and will start. That’s an underrated development, as Indy’s offensive line has been stellar through the first month and losing continuity would be a big hit to the unit’s current positive momentum.
There’s three Colts listed as questionable this week, with two wide receivers. Keenan Allen is questionable for the second week in a row, but completed a full practice on Friday, which is a significant step towards suiting up this weekend. Darius Slayton is a new addition to the injury report late in the week having been limited on Friday with a knee injury. Given the issue appears to have just popped up, Slayton may have to wait yet another week to make his Colts debut.
Cornerback Charvarius Ward is trending towards playing. After two straight days being limited, Ward was a full participant in the week’s final session. The questionable tag does add a little uncertainty, but a week of progress indicates Ward should be good to go.
Finally, it’s worth noting that defensive tackle DeForest Buckner did not practice Friday due to rest. No reason to worry about the veteran, though, as he doesn’t have any injury designation.
Overall, the final report for Indianapolis could’ve been much longer. Twelve different names showed up on the practice report this week, but only seven enter Week 5 with a designation. The possibility of being down three wide receivers is far from ideal, making that group the main on to monitor ahead of Sunday. On the practice squad, the Colts could turn to Nick Westbrook-Ikhine like they did last week should they need extra bodies.
For defensive practice squad elevations, Carl Lawson is likely to get the nod. WIthout Key, the Colts defensive end room lacks significant experience, so getting the 31-year-old into the mix could prove beneficial.
Pittsburgh Steelers Final Injury Report
Not as long a final list for the Steelers, but a top-heavy report. Worst case scenario, Pittsburgh could be without four starters. Michael Pittman Jr.’s foot injury got worse throughout the week, so he won’t be playing his former team. No Jamel Dean hurts the secondary, especially with Jalen Ramsey also carrying a questionable tag. If both can’t go, the Steelers will have to turn to their backup cornerbacks Daylen Everette and Sean Murphy-Bunting, who was signed off the Buccaneers’ practice squad earlier in the week.
Safety DeShon Elliott’s 21-day practice window was opened this week but he’s yet to be activated off injured reserve, so he’s unavailable to dress until that transaction occurs.
Rico Dowdle was limited all week and is officially questionable with the toe injury that’s kept him out of Pittsburgh’s last two contests as well.
Comparing the two reports, I’d give the Steelers a slight advantage, although Pittsburgh’s secondary concerns and Indy’s injuries at wide receiver make for an interesting storyline entering the game. Those matchups on the outside could have a major influence on the eventual outcome, so how effectively each team takes advantage of the other’s personnel concerns could be a deciding factor.

title: Colts Are Keeping Themselves Alive By Dominating In These Key Areas
full_text:
Despite having as many wins as they have losses, the Indianapolis Colts have gotten off to a rocky start to the 2026 regular season.
The 2-2 Colts struggled immensely on defense to start the year, specifically during the team's first two matchups against the Baltimore Ravens and Kansas City Chiefs, but have since found their footing with back-to-back wins over the Houston Texans and Washington Commanders.
However, both the Texans and Commanders sported subpar offensive units, with injuries giving the Colts advantages defensively, so there's reason to believe they'll go back to struggling against more respectable offenses.
Furthermore, the Colts' offense has largely kept them in each of their four games so far in 2026, though inconsistency sprouting from turnovers and a revolving door of pass-catching options has kept them from putting together an efficient operation.
With that said, the Colts have managed to, for the most part, stay competitive through one month of regular-season play thanks to their top-tier execution in a few areas of the game that are typically overlooked.
Without further ado, let's break down the three areas in question where the Colts are raising their overall floor.
The Indianapolis Colts have struggled to replicate their efficient output from a season ago through four weeks of the 2026 regular season, but when they've gotten into the red zone, it's almost a guarantee that they're scoring.
According to Sumer Sports via Locked On Colts' Zach Hicks, the Colts' offense ranks in the following red zone categories entering Week 5:
3rd in total EPA (Expected Points Added) 4th in EPA/play 5th in overall success rate 5th in EPA/pass 4th in pass success rate 3rd in EPA/rush
According to Team Rankings, the Colts rank 6th in the NFL in red zone touchdown rate. Indianapolis is scoring a touchdown on 75% of its red zone trips.
Head coach Shane Steichen's Colts offense doesn't have an issue with scoring in the red zone; they have a problem getting into red zone territory altogether.
They are tied for the 17th-most red zone scoring attempts (3.0 per game) with several teams, which shows that they have untapped potential offensively.
If starting quarterback Daniel Jones can limit his turnovers, and if pass protection gets sorted out, the Colts' offense can begin to unlock its potential.
Fourth-year special teams coordinator Brian Mason has only improved his unit with each year in Indianapolis.
So far in 2026, the Colts' special teams unit looks like one of the best in the entire NFL - and that's without having longtime special teams ace Ashton Dulin available for half of their games.
Mason made the impossible decision of choosing between Spencer Shrader and Blake Grupe to become the team's starting kicker before the regular season arrived, and his choice has aged flawlessly.
Spencer Shrader was named the Colts' starting kicker ahead of the season after dominating the team's preseason slate, and he's gotten off to a tremendous start in 2026.
Shrader missed his first kick of the new year, an extra point attempt in the team's season opener, but has been perfect since going 11-for-11 on field goal attempts.
The Colts' kicker has nailed each of his four 50+ yard attempts so far this season, including a 53-yard game-winner against the Houston Texans in Week 3, and the special teams unit as a whole (kickoff, punt, etc.) has been just as effective.
Indianapolis's rookie class has been a strong injection of talent to the special teams unit, with running back Seth McGowan flashing as a kick returner, and defenders Caden Curry and Bryce Boettcher showing up on kickoffs.
The Indianapolis Colts still have some things to clean up if they want to be treated as legitimate playoff contenders, but their special teams operation is not one of them.
The Indianapolis Colts have been the most disciplined team in the NFL through one month of regular-season play.
According to Tru Media analytics via Rotowire's Ian Hartitz, the Colts have been flagged for the fewest penalties on both sides of the ball through four weeks.
Colts have been flagged for the fewest penalties on offense *and* defense this season pic.twitter.com/1FyN2lIPmo
There's been plenty to critique so far this season, but playing disciplined football has not been one of them.
If anything, the Colts' disciplined play has been one of the main reasons they're sitting with a 2-2 record entering Week 5.
Football is a game of inches and margins, and the Colts' success in these three areas has allowed them to stay afloat as they iron out their deficiencies on both sides of the ball.

title: 3 Takeaways on Jaguars Signing Long Snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer and What it Means
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are reportedly set to make a big addition before Week 6.
According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, the Jaguars are set to sign veteran long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer ahead of their next battle in London against the Houston Texans. This, of course, comes after the Jaguars had to deploy nose tackle Davon Hamilton at long snapper due to an injury to Ross Matiscik in Week 5.
So, what does the Bobenmoyer signing mean for the Jaguars after their big 19-17 win over the Philadelphia Eagles? We break it down below.
Long snapper news: The #Jaguars are signing NFL veteran LS Jacob Bobenmoyer as their new long snapper, which means DT DaVon Hamilton can return to his day job. He’s already flown to London. Hamilton filled in admirably for injured Ross Matiscik, which won’t be placed on IR. pic.twitter.com/kFLoTpFqkf
The good news for the Jaguars when it comes to this report is that Matiscik is not expected to be placed on injured reserve. That makes sense considering the Jaguars bye week is next week, which means could sit this week and get two games of rest before the Jaguars start the second-half of the season. If the Jaguars had placed him on injured reserve today, he would miss Sunday, which is already expected, along with the first three games of the bye week since the bye week does not count as one of his four weeks missed on injured reserve.
By playing this form of roster gymnastics, the Jaguars have given themselves some flexibility with the long snapper spot. Matiscik is a legit weapon for the Jaguars at the long snapper spot thanks both to his consistency as a smaller and his tackling ability on coverage teams. The less time the Jaguars are without him, the better for Heath Farwell’s unit. He is a big piece of what they do, so you can certainly count this as positive news for the Jaguars and their special teams moving forward.
There is obviously not a lot of room to breakdown long-snapper tape, but we can go off numbers. Bobenmoyer has been an active long snapper on coverage teams just based off how many tackles he has record. He has recorded at least three tackles in every season, recording 22 tackles in 97 games over the last six years. By comparison, Matiscik also had 22 tackles in six season before entering the 2026 season.
In short, he will likely not be Matiscik on coverage teams because, well, nobody is. But he should at least give the Jaguars something on coverage teams, which makes sense consider the Jaguars likely wanted to target a long-snapper who could give them similar things to Matiscik. Nobody is going to ask him to be a star tackler like the Jaguars' All-Pro long snapper, but he can help them.
Is there anything more we can say about Davon Hamilton? Not only has he been one of the best defensive tackles in football this season, but he stepped up for the Jaguars at a moment's notice and held down the fort at the long snapper position in a key one-score game. Hamilton was at his best when the moment demanded it against the Eagles, and he is a key reason the Jaguars won the game.
While the Jaguars won't need Hamilton to step up again this week, he got them through a touchy situation. He deserves all the credit he is getting for his performance against the Eagles, but it was also smart of the Jaguars to move quickly to secure a full-time long-snapper ahead of a key game against the Houston Texans on Sunday.

title: 3 Options the Jaguars Must Consider if Anton Harrison Misses Significant Time
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars might have a serious injury question facing them.
The Jaguars left Week 5 with a much-needed last-second victory over the Philadelphia Eagles , but it didn't come without its costs. Left tackle Anton Harrisonwas carted off the field in the third-quarter and did not return, and now his status is up in the air.
“Yeah, I mean, we'll have to see. He just got an MRI, just now, so we don't have the results back yet. We're kind of at the mercy of that and to see what that looks like and how he feels. He's a little stiff," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Monday.
"I have a lot of belief in [Jeff Ferguson, Vice President of Player Health and Performance] and our group downstairs to be able to…If anybody's going to get him ready to play, it'll be them, and we'll have to be patient with, obviously, if he's not able to, you know, practice what that looks like and go from there. But, you know, it was a weird play. He was trying to block on the turnback, and it just tweaked on him a little bit. We'll have to see what the MRI looks like. We're at the mercy of it right now.”
So if the Jaguars are set to be without Harrison for an extended period of time, what are their options moving forward? We break it down below.
This is the most obvious, and most likely, scenario. Walker Little is a legit starting offensive tackle talent in the NFL, and there are not a ton of teams who he would have opened 2025 as a backup for. That is why the Jaguars have valued their offensive line depth the way they have over the years, and they have the rare luxury of having another starting offensive tackle ready to play if the scenario ever came up where they needed one.
Little played well for the Jaguars during his half of football against the Eagles, and there is plenty of reason to think he can hold his own moving forward. In this scenario, the Jaguars would likely have Wyatt Milum as their swing tackle option, with Daniel Faalele also joining the mix. Eventually, the Jaguars will be set to get Patrick Mekari back from injured reserve as well, giving the Jaguars another potential depth option for offensive tackle.
Little has started a lot of games at left tackle before, and the Jaguars are in a better spot than many teams would be if their starting tackle was injured. This is what makes the most sense for the Jaguars and their offensive line moving forward.
Another option could be to do some musical chairs at the offensive tackle position. Cole Van Lanen did some great things at left tackle last season when he earned his big-time contract extension, and Little has experience at right tackle as well. Daniel Faalele and Wyatt Milum are also better depth options as right tackles as opposed to at left tackle, which could make this the best way for the Jaguars to get their best five on the field.
That is not to say this option would be without its faults, of course. Van Lanen has spent every single snap of this season at right tackle, and the Jaguars even noted before Week 1 that Van Lanen's most comfortable spot is at the right tackle spot. He played great at left tackle a year ago, but he is still just five games into his season after a serious knee injury in January. Putting a position switch on top of that could be asking quite a lot.
This feels like the least likely option, but it is worth considering. There are not many teams that would be willing to part with starting-caliber offensive tackles, but I think James Gladstone is the general manager who could find a deal if there was one to be made. The Jaguars have a decent amount of draft picks to work with as well, which means Gladstone could get aggressive if it appears the Jaguars will be without Harrison for the long-term.
Again, the lack of options would be an issue, which is what makes this more of an extreme option than anything else. But the Jaguars have quickly put together trades to fill holes on the roster in the past, and it would not make much sense to count out Gladstone and the Jaguars from doing it again if the situation demands it.

title: Jaguars Week 5 Snap Count Analysis: Liam Coen's Staff Must Make One Big Shift
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- With the Jacksonville Jaguars facing their fair of injuries both before and during Sunday's Week 5 win, this week's snap count report looks quite a bit different.
The Jaguars had several players play their largest roles of the season in Week 5's win over the Philadelphia Eagles, but what do this week's snaps really tell us about how the Jaguars approached their latest win? We break it down below.
The Jaguars had rookie safety Jalen Huskey active for the first time in his rookie season on Sunday, but it did not result in him seeing the field very much. Huskey ended up playing zero offensive snaps and just three special teams snaps, making it clear that the Jaguars see him way down the pecking order at safety. While that even may be a fair argument for them to make since they know him best and see him practice every day, it is hard to imagine the Jaguars should let him continue to watch at safety if Eric Murray misses any more time.
The Jaguars had Rayuan Lane play 100% of the snaps and practice squad safety Kaevon Merriweather serve as the No. 3 safety with 34% of the defensive snaps. The Jaguars did not get great production out of the safety room outside of Antonio Johnson, however, and the Jaguars should consider a shift to Huskey as at least the No. 3 safety if Murray continues to miss time. Lane fills his depth role well, but he just looked a bit out of his element as a starter on Sunday.
If the Jaguars had not already made it clear, there is a lead back in Duval: Bhayshul Tuten, who had one of his highest rates of usage in his career. Tuten played a career high in snaps with 49 (68.1%), while his 22 carries were also an easy career high. When the Jaguars needed an important play on the ground, it was Tuten who they leaned into. The Tuten usage has never been higher, but that does mean it has to go backward for someone else.
That player is clearly Chris Rodriguez Jr., who has seen his role diminish significantly since even Week 1. Rodriguez played a season-low snaps with nine (12.5%) and only had two carries, making it clear that he is, above all else, Tuten's backup. He did get red-zone short-yardage work, but he is clearly just a role player right now, as opposed to Tuten being the Jaguars' clear No. 1 running back by really every single definition.
Tuten has seen his role take a massive leap, first compared to a year ago and now compared to Week 1. It feels like by the end of the season we will start to see Tuten get 20+ carries almost weekly considering how balanced the Jaguars' offense is.
The Jaguars' pair of rookie skill players combined for five catches on six targets for 63 yards (12.6 yards per catch). Josh Cameron caught three passes for 43 yards and Nate Boerkircher caught two passes for 20 yards, while playing nearly 50% of the snaps in a 12-personnel happy game plan against the Eagles. As a whole, the duo combined for 63 yards on 29 routes, which comes out to 2.17 yards per route run. For context, that would rank top-25 amongst all NFL wide recievers in yards per route run.
Boerkircher got plenty of run with 35 snaps (49%), while Cameron played 22 snaps (31%), with each player having a significant impact despite not playing full-time snaps. The Jaguars are getting instant production from each non-first round draft pick, which is an ideal outcome for any team like the Jaguars coming off a playoff season. The Jaguars' offensive rookies have already become true hits.

title: Jaguars Stock Report: 3 Players Rising, Falling After Eagles Win ... Starting With Walker Little
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. --  The Jacksonville Jaguars' roster has taken some significant strides over the last two seasons, and those strides helped the Jaguars improve to 4-1 in Week 5.
It took a full team effort, of course, for the Jaguars to get past the Philadelpia Eagles on Sunday. but in the NFL, a win is a win. Thanks to the performances from the roster in the 19-17 win, several Jaguars saw their stocks rise -- while a few others saw theirs slip. We break it all down in this week's Jaguars Stock Report.
At times like these, it makes it clear why the Jaguars have put such an emphasis on their offensive line depth. The Jaguars faced a serious injury question in the third-quarter with Anton Harrison getting carted off the field with a knee injury. The Jaguars have one of the best backup offensive linemen in all of the NFL with former starting left tackle Walker Little, and he quickly proved his worth against a tough Eagles front.
Little allowed zero pressures on 18 pass blocking snaps according to Pro Football Focus, making it clear that the Jaguars' plans for the offensive line and preparing for the worst-case scenarios have paid off. Little has played good football before for the Jaguars, and they are lucky to have him in the event Harrison now misses time, starting with Week 6 against the Houston Texans and the Will Anderson/Danielle Hunter duo.
It just continues to feel like this season is slipping away for Brian Thomas Jr., who now ranks fourth in catches (9) and fith in yards (105) this season. He has fewer yards (105) than sixth-round rookie Josh Cameron (117). The connection just has not been there for him and Trevor Lawrence, with Thomas having the lowest catch rate of any of the Jaguars' primary skill players. Right now, he is on pace for 30 catches and 357 yards.
I still think this has much less to do with Thomas and his talent than it does with his role in the style of Coen's offense. Thomas did have Quinyon Mitchell beat on a deep route that Lawrence underthrew after being hit on the throw, but it just hasn't worked out in the offense. On Sunday, he was out-paced in the passing game by Nate Boerkircher, Travis Hunter, and Chris Rodriguez Jr. I do not know where they go from here.
Brenton Strange was once again a significant factor for the Jaguars' offense on Sunday. Over the last three weeks, Strange ranks sixth amongst all tight ends in catches and third in yards, as well as ranking only behind Brock Bowers in yards per route run. Strange has had some miscues, such as a drop on Sunday, but he has elevated his role in the passing game in a big way over the last several weeks.
Part of this could be due to matchups, with the Jaguars playing three teams in a row who struggle against tight ends in coverage. But there are more teams who struggle to slow down tight ends than there are teams who struggle to slow down receivers, and Strange could be an X-Factor of the offense moving forward.
It felt like some of the Jaguars' failed red-zone trips on Sunday featured Chris Rodriguez Jr. for one way or another. The sequence where he had a near fumble (after Jalen Carter wrecked the play) and then missed the block on Zack Baun on the failed fourth-down sweep to Bhayshul Tuten was a tough one, and it just felt too often like the thought of "why isn't Bhayshul Tuten in the game here?" crept up over the course of the game.
Overall, Rodriguez only got two carries for the Jaguars as they leaned on Bhayshul Tuten more and more. Part of this might have to do with the fact that the Jaguars knew they would need a running back to create before the line of scrimmage, but Rodriguez's role has just yet to be overly significant in any game.
It feels like Antonio Johnson has been all over the place for the Jaguars over the last few weeks. He continued this on Sunday with some quality reps both against the run and in coverage, while also splitting a sack with Travon Walker. This was the first game in Johnson's career where he was the sole veteran voice at safety, and he certainly played his role well against the Eagles.
Antonio Johnson with a lot of big plays for the #Jaguars last few weeks: pic.twitter.com/vA5r8JO5VI
Johnson has stepped up for the Jaguars, and his game has improved even from his breakout season a year ago. Johnson is a key cog of this unit every week, but he is even more important now that the Jaguars are facing some injuries and having to play some backups at the safety spot next to him over the next few weeks.
Sunday marked the first start of Rayuan Lane's career, and he did do some good things. He was an effective blitzer and made some nice run fits playing downhill, but he did have some issues when the Eagles were able to isolate him in space. Lane plays hard and competes on every snap, but Sunday made it hard to see him having much success as a full-time starter at safety. Maybe more and more reps help, but this did not feel like a great step in the right direction.

title: 3 Things We Learned About the Jaguars vs. the Eagles: Trevor Lawrence's Fire
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars had to pull out all of the stops for their fourth win of the season, but they made it happen in Week 5.
The Jaguars survived an upset attempt from the Philadelphia Eagles thanks to Cam Little hitting a walkoff 57-yard field goal in a 19-17 win. But what did we learn from the Jaguars' narrow win, and what could it all mean moving forward?
Trevor Lawrence did a lot of good things on Sunday sans his second-half interception. He was faced with plenty of unfavorable 2nd- and 3rd-and-long situations due to the penalties for the second week in a row, but he made so many plays in and out of structure that helped the Jaguars move the ball. Had the Jaguars figured things out in the red-zone, the score would have more so reflected the performance that Lawrence had. But among all other things, Lawrence also showed some of the maturation as the general of the offense when he, well, was irate after yet another red-zone penalty.
Trevor Lawrence CRASHED OUT on his center 😭 pic.twitter.com/bUC2oV1z3Y
It was a sign of Lawrence's fire that, frankly, needed to be shown considering the situation. I have covered every single game of Lawrence's NFL career, and I never once saw him quite so frustrated and then let the rest of the offense know about it. Lawrence is a cool, calm and collected type of leader, and this isn't something he would have done a few years ago at least not in my eyes. Call it the Liam Coen impact, call it the natural growth of a franchise quarterback, but Lawrence showed the fire that many thought he was missing entering the NFL.
"I do like seeing him have that fire and that, you know, competitive edge. You know, he wants it to be good. He wants the operation to be clean. I think there was a lot of frustrations throughout that game that probably built up to be more emotional in that moment," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Monday
I thought Parker Washington had the best game of any Jaguars skill player, which is easy to say with two touchdowns and over 120 receiving yards. Washington is far and away the clear Jaguars' No. 1 receiver, even with his one-catch game in Week 4 in the rear view window. But after Washington, I think we are starting to see a second player establish himself on the Jaguars' pecking order in the passing game: Brenton Strange.
Over the last three weeks, Strange leads the Jaguars with 21 targets, 17 receptions and 195 yards despite ranking third on the team in routes in that span with 75. Strange has been effective for the Jaguars aside from a few uncharacteristic drops in that span. His increase in volumn does not seem like an accident, though, especially considering most teams are better at defending passes out wide than they are in the middle of the field.
Washington is the clear No. 1. Brian Thomas Jr. clearly is a small part of the offense. Jakobi Meyers has, so far, felt more like an auxilary option other than in Week 3. I think Strange is the No. 2 pass-catcher in the offense right now.
The Jaguars simply have to sort out their penalty issues. Some flags have certainly been silly calls by the officials, but some have been purely the Jaguars' fault. It is not the fault of the officials if the Jaguars are getting false starts and delay of games, which has happened far too often over the last two weeks especially. "The penalties are concerning when you start the season off in the first three weeks as the second-least penalized team in the NFL, and now over the last two weeks, we're arguably one of the most penalized teams in the NFL," Coen said.
The Jaguars have won each of their last 2 games despite 26 total penalties. They are the first team since the Seahawks in Weeks 10 and 11 of the 2011 season to win consecutive games with 13+ penalties in each game. Penalties are the major reason why the last two wins have had to come in one-score games, and the Jaguars simply have to figure out how to play cleaner football in all three phases. Penalties alone have wiped out three touchdowns and an interception for the Jaguars in the last two weeks. What happens when this happens against a good team and not just the Bengals or Eagles?

title: Shipley's Dozen: 12 Takes on Jaguars' Wacky Win Over Eagles, Parker Washington and More
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are no strangers to wacky games with heart-stopping ends, but Week 5 was something else.
The Jaguars managed to simply find a way to win against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 5 in a thrilling 19-17 walkoff , but there was, well, a lot that happened between the first snap and the last one. We break down one of the craziest Jaguars games in recent memory in this week's Shipley's Dozen column.
I can say with confidence that I do not believe Parker Washington is going anywhere. That is not due to some insight or knowledge of his pending contract negotiations with the Jaguars. Instead, it is due to the fact that it becomes clearer and clearer with each passing game that the Jaguars' offense would likely be in big trouble without Washington. He is the Jaguars' top pass-catcher for so many reasons, but the most important one might be trust. Just look at the play he makes on his second touchdown, and look at the trust it took between him and Trevor Lawrence to make that play happen.
Washington is going to be a key piece of the Jaguars for a long time because, simply because it is not really possible to envision a Jaguars offense without him. Those are the kinds of players this regime does not let leave the building.
An unbelievably clutch play from Parker Washington. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/C7Y6hQ0Coc
I thought the first half of football from the Jaguars' defense had some good things, but the two touchdowns they allowed were simply drives that should not happen considering the state of the Eagles' offense. The depleted Eagles put together a first-half scoring drive that ended with a two-yard Will Shipley touchdown, and the real issues for the Jaguars were on third-down. The Jaguars allowed conversions on 3rd-and-8, 3rd-and-10, and then 3rd-and-17 in the red-zone due to a Travis Hunter pass interference call. Add in a 62-yard touchdown allowed to Darius Cooper shortly thereafter, and the Jaguars had work to do.
But the second half went much differently. The Eagles gained just three first downs on their first six drives of the second-half, with five of those drives ending in punts and one ending in a turnover on downs. The Jaguars were especially effective in the fourth quarter, forcing three three-and-outs and allowing just three net yards on the first three drives of the game. The Jaguars did see the Eagles have a short drive for a field goal, but it was a nine-play drive that barely averaged four yards per play. The defense was perhaps the biggest reason the Jaguars won this game.
This has to be the biggest present concern for the Jaguars. They do have some offensive tackle depth, as evidenced by Walker Little stepping in and playing well during the second-half of the game. But Anton Harrison was carted off with a knee injury, and there was not much of an update for the Jaguars' blindside protector on Monday other than Liam Coen noting that he got an MRI but no results yet. Harrison missing extended time while Cole Van Lanen also goes through some of his own struggles would be bad timing with the Houston Texans coming up, and it would also mean the Jaguars would have to lean into offensive line depth like Daniel Faalele and, eventually, Patrick Mekari to help fill-in.
Jalen Huskey did not play a single defensive snap on Sunday, which seems ... odd. The Jaguars had Rayuan Lane fill in for Eric Murray and the second-year safety played 100% of the defensive snaps, while Kaevon Merriweather served as the third safety and played 21% of the snaps. Even with two safeties out with Murray and Ransaw, Huskey still didn't see the field. The Jaguars can get better production out of safety than they did on Sunday, and moving toward Huskey as at least the third safety could go a long way toward making that happen.
The Jaguars have long had a strong red-zone offense under head coach Liam Coen, but it was simply all over the place on Sunday. I think penalties were the biggest issue on the day, such as the false starts and delay of games. But I also think those are self-inflicted mistakes that the Jaguars can fix with improved execution. To me, the real concern in the red-zone was the fact that the Jaguars let Jalen Carter completely wreck the game. Carter is one of the highest-paid defenders in all of football for a reason, after all, but it felt like the Jaguars' inability to run the ball at Carter is what led to the ill-fated Bhayshul Tuten fly sweep. If the Jaguars can't block elite defensive linemen when they need just a few yards, that will be an issue that doesn't just go away or work itself out.
I have long considered the London games to be road games for the Jaguars, no matter how they are classified on the schedule. The Jaguars have to make their longest trip of the year to play the game, disrupting entire weeks of work in the process, and then they do not have a homefield advantage in any shape or form come game time. This was truer than ever against the Eagles, with the game feeling like an Eagles home came considering the crowd noise, especially when the Jaguars were inside the red-zone. Despite the Jaguars upheaving their travel plans for London each year, it is still a tough road test. That is an odd sense of irony that could come into play again next week against the Texans.
The Jaguars do not win this game without Heath Farwell's unit. The Jaguars did miss one extra point, but the Jaguars made all of their other kicks despite punter/holder Logan Cooke having to adjust to some high snaps from backup long-snapper Davon Hamilton and he was just one of several impressive special teamers. The Jaguars also saw Josh Cameron return a kick for a nullified touchdown, Cam Little make a 57-yard walk-off, and Ameer Abdullah and the kickoff return team producing one of the most important special teams plays of the last few years with his fourht-quarter kick return. Heath Farwell should wear this game proudly.
I was surprised the Jaguars went with man coverage as often as they did. They went away from it a bit after the first-half, but it was a big reason the Jaguars allowed a 62-yard touchdown to Darius Cooper. The way to beat Jalen Hurts is by using zone coverage to muddy the picture in the secondary, while man coverage provides him with the ready-made answers he needs. The Jaguars adjusted well, but they paid for it a bit at the start of the game. Man coverage allowed some of the biggest plays of the day, which is a stark contrast from other weeks in the season.
The Jaguars' defensive line playing well. They completely shut down the Eagles' rushing attack, while Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker combined for 10 pressures and four quarterback hits. The Jaguars had an easier matchup this week considering the state of the Eagles' offensive line, but they also did what they needed to when it came to taking advantage of the matchup. I thought this might have been the best game the Jaguars' front has had this year, and this comes a week after I thought the same thing.
Davon Hamilton. That's the tweet.
Jaguars walk off win in improbable fashion with game-winning Cam Little 57-yard field goal + backup long snapper Davon Hamilton: pic.twitter.com/BXhZmb9aSG
It says a lot about the AFC South that a 1-4 team is pretty easily still the second-best team in the division, but that is the case through five weeks. The Indianapolis Colts dropped to 2-3 after a loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, and even with their win over Houston a week ago I do not think anyone can confidently say the Colts pose a larger threat to the Jaguars than the Texans do after Week 5. Perhaps that is because the Texans are next up on the Jaguars' schedule , but it very much so feels like the Texans are a better team as a whole than the Colts are.
8️⃣0️⃣ YARDS TO THE HOUSE @Nunless2 pic.twitter.com/veiSAV9F4M
The Texans still have their fair share of flaws, of course. Their win over the Tennessee Titans was expected in every…

title: 5 Winners, 5 Losers From Jaguars' Close Win Over Eagles: Cam Little Wasn't the Only Game-Changer
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars just won one of the wackiest football games you will see in 2026, if not longer than that.
"One of the craziest games, maybe the craziest games I've ever been a part of, and I've been in some pretty wild ones," Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence said after the 19-17 last-second win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
"Just how cool is this sport? The game's never over, and I think the belief from our team, man, obviously didn't look great there at the end, but just the belief of our kickoff return unit, Ameer [Abdullah] being smart, breaking through, and still getting down at the second. So many things had to happen, right? I felt like we finally got a break at the end of the game, and that play went our way. Obviously, we had some bad stuff we've got to clean up. But just keep playing. It's not always going to be pretty. That's this league. It's tough to win. So, when you can win them, especially like that, you've got to enjoy it.
So, which players had the biggest hand in the Jaguars' dramatic win over the Eagles? And which players saw their stock maybe go down as a result of the game? We break it all down below.
Parker Washington had one of the best games in his entire career on Sunday, catching two touchdowns and hitting 124 yards in the process. Washington won on contested catches in the red-zone, after the catch in space, tough coordination catches near the sidelines, and seemingly everything in between. It has become clear that Washington is the alpha male of the Jaguars' passing attack, and he took it a step further on Sunday considering the stakes that came with both of his touchdowns.
Cam Little was terrific for the Jaguars on Sunday. He did miss an extra point that I think you can likely chalk up to the fact that the Jaguars had some errant snaps from backup long-snapper Davon Hamilton. But Little having the ice in his veins to make the 57-yard game-winner was everything the Jaguars have always needed from him. He has hit some big kicks before, but this one ensured the Jaguars enter Week 6 with a three-game lead over the Texans instead of a two-game lead.
Davon Hamilton was once again one of the Jaguars' most important players. Yes, he stepped in for the Jaguars im some big moments when thrust into the action as the long-snapper. But Hamilton once again had a terrific outing as the Jaguars' nose tackle that really set the tone. Hamilton manhandled the Eagles' offensive line on several reps in both the run and pass game, and it is fair to say the Jaguars do not win without his contributions on both defense and special teams.
Take away his interception, and I think Sunday was another good performance from Trevor Lawrence. He was under siege all day by a talented Eagles' defensive line and one of the best defensive coordinators in the NFL, but he managed to make big throws for the Jaguars on each of the game's most important drives. His second touchdown pass to Parker Washington is one of the best passes he has thrown all season long, and Lawrence was the biggest reason the Jaguars were in a position to win this game. Had the Jaguars not goofed on two red-zone trips, the score would have looked better to reflect the kind of performance that Lawrence had.
You can't talk about this win and not mention Ameer Abdullah , who is on his seventh team in 12 seasons. Abdullah has found a home in Jacksonville, though, and has been active in every single game despite the Jaguars having the No. 1 through No. 3 running back spots locked up. The Jaguars do not win this game without Abdullah's stellar kick return on the second-to-last play of the game, and he has earned the full-time kick returner role next to Josh Cameron.
Brian Thomas Jr. did not catch a pass for the first time in his entire career on Sunday. He was targeted three times, but one resulted in an interception after Trevor Lawrence underthrew the ball while getting hit. The other two targets came in the end-zone, and Thomas was not able to come up with either pass for a touchdown. He was out-produced in the passing game on Sunday by Travis Hunter, Nate Boerkircher, and Chris Rodriguez Jr. Things have just not panned out for him this season.
The Jaguars turned to Rayuan Lane to replace an injured Eric Murray on Sunday, and he certainly did not have the kind of game that will bring much confidence from those outside of the Jaguars' building. Lane had a good game against the run and as a blitzer, but it felt like he was getting picked on at times in coverage, and he also took a few angles that expose some of his flaws as a defender in space.
Anton Harrison lands here this week after being carted off the field with a knee injury in the third-quarter. The Jaguars' offensive line had its own share of issues in Week 5, but Harrison had appeared to be playing the best of any of the Jaguars' offensive linemen. If Harrison misses any extended time for the Jaguars, this is a very significant loss in both the run and the passing game. Harrison is the Jaguars' most talented offensive lineman, and his injury will be a big storyline to watch before they face the Texans' pass-rush next week.
The Jaguars saw Montaric Brown return for Sunday's game after missing last week's contest against the Bengals with an injury. It did not turn out to be the return anyone likely hoped, though, with Brown losing on the 62-yard touchdown allowed to Darius Cooper. Brown did not play another snap in the game, either, with the veteran cornerback getting re-added to the Jaguars' growing injury list in the secondary. It has become a season to forget so far for Brown.
There just was not much out there for Chris Rodriguez Jr. on Sunday. He did have a key block on Ameer Abdullah's kick return before Cam Little's game-winning kick, but he also had a few not-so-great reps on offense. He very nearly fumbled the ball at the goal line before the end of the half, though I think he gets a semi-pass considering the Jaguars never scored on that drive anyway. But the offense just looked out of sorts each time the Jaguars had him as the focus over Bhayshul Tuten, and his missed block on fourth-down at the end of the first half is the main reason Tuten didn't score.

title: Ameer Abdullah's Signature Moment Becomes Latest Example of Jaguars' Maturation
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are 4-1, and it took every single member of the active roster to make it happen in Week 5.
That included veteran running back Ameer Abdullah, who quietly made one of the biggest plays of the season with his fourth-quarter 53-yard kick return to set up a game-winning field goal in the Jaguars' 19-17 win over the Eagles. In the process, he became the latest example of the Jaguars' maturation as a franchise.
Abdullah's kick return set the Jaguars and kicker Cam Little up to win the game with a 57-yard field goal , and it showed all of the things that have made Abdullah valuable since the Jaguars signed him as a free agent late in the offseason: toughness, smarts, experience, and an ability to still make explosive plays. The fact that Abdullah had the burst to get the ball where he did is impressive. The fact he knew to get down with one second left is even more impressive.
JAGS HUGE KICK RETURN. They're in range for one more shot at a field goal! @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XSWbKBTvW2
Abdullah was seen as an afterthought perhaps externally when the Jaguars signed him, but he had stellar performances in training camp and the preseason to put himself in a position to make the Jaguars' roster. He is amongst the oldest and most experienced players on the roster, and he has clearly made his impact felt.
"He's that dude. He's one of the first in the building every single day, him and Parker. Ameer, to get in our building this spring, Ameer had four votes -- four or five votes to be a captain. He made such an impression on this team right away, right from the beginning," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said after the game.
"He takes care of his body, takes care of his mind. He prepares to be a starter. He's been one of the best teammates. He's just such a great human being and a guy that I cannot say enough about, has gone through so much in this last six months actually. I pray for him. I love him to death. I'm so happy that he's a Jaguar, and I'm very proud of him today."
This Jaguars regime has mastered finding edges by uncovering diamonds in the rough, something that the best franchises do every single year. Their scouting shows up not just in the win-loss column, but in the fact that players like Abdullah have continued to help the Jaguars pick up wins during the Liam Coen era, which has seen the Jaguars go 17-5 in 22 regular-season games.
The Jaguars have been one of the NFL's best franchises since Coen, general manager James Gladstone, and executive vice president of football operations Tony Boselli took over, and Abdullah has become the latest example of why they have thrived. Abdullah had touched the ball 18 times (12 on offense, six kick returns) before Sunday, but he was always ready. Despite having a marginal role, he proved to be a difference-maker between the Jaguars being 4-1 and the Jaguars being 3-2.
Abdullah is far from the only diamond in the rough the Jaguars have mined. Sixth-round receiver Josh Cameron is another one. LeQuint Allen, Quintin Morris, Dennis Gardeck, Danny Striggow, BJ Green, and Matt Dickerson a year ago, too. The Jaguars have proven that they can fill the back-end of their active roster with talented players who can help them win games, which is what allows them to make moves like contract extensions and the Travis Hunter trade.
The Jaguars have matured into a real-deal football team. They are doing the things that the best franchises have always done, and Abdullah is a shining example of why it is working.

title: Game Balls from Jaguars' Nailbiter vs. Eagles: Unlikely Hero Emerges
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- There are team wins, and then there is whatever the heck just happened between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Philadelphia Eagles in London.
The Jaguars had their entire active roster step in and make an impact in Sunday's 19-17 last-second win over the Eagles , making it the kind of performance where every single player on the roster can confidently say they left their fingerprints on it.
"Mental toughness. It's kind of what we talked about all week, staying the course. One second left on the clock, guys competing to the end when things weren't really going your way," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said after the game. "It wasn't clean, a lot of penalties, didn't execute in the red zone. Let them off the hook a lot on third and long. It just was a weird kind of vibe game, weird. Guys stayed the course and made plays, we had D-Ham [DaVon Hamilton] snapping again. It was just kind of wild we were in that position. Nobody flinched. Nobody blinked. Nobody blamed. Guys stayed the course and ended up squeaking away with a win."
So, which Jaguars deserve game balls for their performances against the Eagles? We break it down below.
This one was relatively easy. An argument could be made for Trevor Lawrence, of course, but Parker Washington was a one-man wrecking crew against the Eagles. Washington led the Jaguars in receiving for the third time in five games, catching six passes for 124 yards and both of the Jaguars' touchdowns. Washington created the plays for the Jaguars in both instances, with Washington scoring a 51-yard touchdown that was almost all yards after the catch. His second touchdown was then a spectacular one-handed catch in the end-zone on a fourth-quarter 27-yard touchdown that was also on fourth down.
51-YARD TOUCHDOWN FOR PARKER WASHINGTON @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Gf38EGe1Qr
Washington has been the Jaguars' go-to receiving in big-time situations, and he had ice water in his veins in the game's biggest moment on Sunday. Games like this one are exactly why the Jaguars will make him a big-money reeiver much sooner rather than later.
It's a big time moment and big time play. We needed a play right there. First, I'm looking, I was looking in the air. I was like, ‘where is the football?’ I'm like, I know I'm supposed to be getting it," Washington said after the game. "Then as soon as I saw it, I was like, okay, there we go. Just being able to make that play, that's what it's all about. That's what the off-season is for. That's what all the training, that's what the training camps, OTAs, that's what it's all about. So, just making that play and being a guy that your team leans on in a big time moment, that was special for me.
The Jaguars' defensive line needed to take over this game, and I think you can certainly make the argument that Josh Hines-Allen did exactly that. While the Jaguars may have only sacked Jalen Hurts once, there is zero question what kind of impact Hines-Allen had. The Jaguars' veteran pass-rusher had one of his most disruptive games of the year, recording two quarterback hits to lead the team while also recording a team-leading two tackles for loss against the run.
Other defenders like Ventrell Miller, Davon Hamilton, Travon Walker, and Antonio Johnson deserve some consideration as well, but this was a vintage Hines-Allen game. As long as you do not hyperfixiate on sacks, then it is hard to not appreciate the kind of physical and dominating performance Hines-Allen had on Sunday.
There are a few different ways to go with this one. Cam Little made a stellar 57-yard field goal, Ameer Abdullah had a massive kick return, Josh Cameron got jobbed on a kickoff return touchdown, and Davon Hamilton stepped up at long-snapper. With all of that in mind, I think this one has to go to Logan Cooke. The fact the Jaguars did not have an errant snap was 100% due to Cooke, who stepped up on every single Hamilton snap to mostly positive results. A lesser performance as a holder, and the Jaguars could have been in trouble.
"It's not like a ton of live reps by any means. It's mostly in a walk-through setting. Whether as a defense on the other side, but without a true live rush all the time. And I don't know if Logan handles that many snaps like that throughout the course of a week," Coen said. "I think those guys do a nice job of mixing it up in practice and being able to give him some of that kind of hot potato drill if you will. Logan's one of the best athletes on our team in terms of hand-eye coordination. He's one of the better golfers. He can throw it. He's just such a good hand-eye coordinated athlete that he was huge today. He was massive."

title: Good, Not So Good From Jaguars' Late Win Over Eagles: OL Concerns Have Set In
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars somehow found a Week 5 win against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday.
The "somehow" label, of course, is a result of the Jaguars putting together their worst performance of the season in their 19-17 win over the Eagles. So, what were the ups and downs of the Week 5 victory? We break it down below in this week's Good and Not So Good.
I thought this would be a good game from Trevor Lawrence , and it was outside of his interception to Quinyon Mitchell. But you can't talk about Lawrence's performance against the Eagles and not mention his connection with Parker Washington on two of the game's most important plays. Washington has become more and more invaluable to the offense every week outside of his career-low day against the Bengals last week, and this duo is what really got the Jaguars over the hump.
Lawrence connected with Washington on both of his touchdown passes, with Washington leading the Jaguars in receiving for the third time in five games. You can just tell that Washington and Lawrence have a different connection than the rest of the pass-catchers in the room, and that connection is what helped the Jaguars improve to 4-1 for the second year in a row. Washington is going to be a very rich man sooner than later.
PARKER WASHINGTON, WOW. JAGS TAKE THE LEAD. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ubE4xivDcD
We have never seen a Jaguars run defense like this one. The Jaguars once again completely shut down the opposing rushing attack, but they might have been at their season-best with their domination of the Eagles up front. The Eagles' running backs combined for 16 carries for 20 yards, though Will Shipley did score on a two-yard run. But when the Jaguars needed to make a stop, they made it.
The run defense is a big reason the Jaguars' defense was so much better in the second-half. They consistently forced negative runs on early downs to put prressure on the Eagles' passing game, and it led to a number of failed Eagles' drives. This is an even better run defense than it was a year ago, which says quite a bit.
I know the Jaguars missed an extra point, and also had a few short punts and a few too many long returns allowed. With that said, the Jaguars do not win this game without the special teams. Heath Farwell's unit was needed to ensure the Jaguars left with a win, and they made several impact players to go along with a few that might have gone a bit unseen.
DaVon Hamilton stepping up at long-snapper was huge. So was Logan Cooke getting some of his high snaps down. Cam Little kicked a bomb on the game-winning 57-yard field goal, but that was only made possible thanks to a stellar Ameer Abdullah return that was set up by blocks from Quintin Morris, Josh Cameron, Chris Rodriguez Jr., Tanner Koziol, and Jahlani Tavai.
JAGS HUGE KICK RETURN. They're in range for one more shot at a field goal! @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XSWbKBTvW2
Josh Cameron has been one of the Jaguars' best rookie performers all season long, and he took it another step in Week 5. He had a stellar kick return touchdown called back on a questionable call, while he also had a few big plays for the Jaguars as a pass-catcher, run-blocker, and as a blocker on special teams. Cameron has gotten better and better for the Jaguars with every performance this season, and Week 5 was another big step forward.
Josh Cameron Takes It To The House To Start The Kickoff, OMG. That’s A Statement. 🔥 pic.twitter.com/PhXI3oACqv
The numbers might not be pretty for Bhayshul Tuten's day, with the Jaguars' lead back rushing 22 times for just 72 yards with a season-worst 3.3 yard per carry average. But when watching the game live, it was clear that those numbers could have been much, much worse if Tuten was not creating yards on his own and surviving his fair share of negative runs and contact being made behind the line of scrimmage.
Tuten had several zero-yard or one-yard runs that looked like they were about to be stopped a few yards in the backfield, and I would venture to guess a big chunk of his yards came after contact. Tuten played very, very well on Sunday, even if the numbers might not have reflected that on the box score at the end of the day.
The Jaguars' offensive line had some big questions to answer this week, and it is hard to say they passed the test. It felt like it was a rough game for all five linemen at different points, with Ezra Cleveland and Cole Van Lanen giving up sacks, Robert Hainsey having issues with delay of games, and with Emmanuel Pregnon getting three holding calls. Add in Anton Harrison getting carted off with a knee injury, and it is a hard day for the Jaguars' offensive line.
Jalen Carter has been dominant in the first half of this game. 4 tackles, 2 sacks, 2 forced fumbles @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/oJIA9Heufp
I do not think I have ever seen a worse Jaguars game in terms of offensive performance in the red-zone. The Jaguars turned the ball over twice despite getting the ball to the Eagles' one-yard line, and there were numerous reasons why: penalties, missed blocks, drops, odd play-calls. The Jaguars did everything wrong that they could do in the red-zone on Sunday, and it almost cost them a game they had no business losing.
"We need to make some of those plays that we had opportunities to make in the red zone that we didn't," Liam Coen said after the game. "So I think [Trevor Lawrence] was frustrated, but man, I never felt him waver. I never felt him get nerved up or anxious. He was frustrated, but he kept coming off the sideline like we're just shooting ourselves in the foot. Statistically, when you felt the flow of it, it never felt like it wasn't we couldn't get going. We were getting going. It was like positive, negative, positive, negative. So as frustrating as it is, it still leaves you hope because you're moving the ball. It just wasn't really pretty.
Eagles deny the Jaguars at the goal line! Eagles head into the half with a 14-7 lead. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/K1f1ZnsWCj
The Jaguars allowed over 25% of their allowed yardage on one play: a 62-yard touchdown to Darius Cooper that made up pretty much the entire value of the Eagles' passing game. The pass defense deserves credit for forcing Jalen Hurts to be 20-of-39 for 158 yards (4.05 yards per attempt), but the long bomb given up to Cooper was a mess from a few areas: there was no point to show Hurts man since he is much worse against zone; Montaric Brown got beaten badly on the rep; Backup safety Rayuan Lane completely whiffed with his angle and missed tackle.
DARIUS COOPER, 62-YARD TOUCHDOWN EAGLES TAKE THE LEAD. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/eKpCwhW8QZ
This was the 36th game of Brian Thomas' career, and it was the first one that he ever got completely shut out in. That is saying something considering he had just three catches in his last two games combined, but his role and production somehow got diminished even more this week. The unfortunate part of this game, though, is that it isn't like Thomas wasn't given the chances to succeed.
Thomas should not get dinged for the Trevor Lawrence interception; Thomas actually had Quinyon Mitchell beat deep. Thomas also had a block that helped spring Parker Washington on his first touchdown. With that said, Thomas led the Jaguars in end-zone targets Sunday but failed to come down with either. One got broken up and went off his hands in the first-half, while a second one was caught but saw Thomas fail to get two feet down. We are not trying to bang the Thomas Jr. Trade Drum , but this one was rough.

title: Here’s Why Chiefs Rookie Cyrus Allen Could Finally Be Featured in Kansas City’s Offense
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs' bleak wide receiver circumstances worsened before the bye when Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton went down in the same game. While Rice's hamstring issue is minor and shouldn't keep him out long, Thornton will miss most, if not all , of the regular season with a dislocated ankle. Between rumors about a reunion with Tyreek Hill and bringing another proven wideout on board before the trade deadline, KC fans are starved for help in the receiving corps. However, a viable option may be waiting in the wings of the Chiefs' offensive unit.
Remember Cyrus Allen, who quickly transformed into a fan favorite with his strong training camp? There was a time when he looked like he'd be facing an uphill battle for playing time, but a scenario where he assumes a significant role in this offense looks a lot more realistic with the current injury situation.
Allen was selected No. 176 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft and brings plenty of versatility, as he's capable of lining up in the slot or on the outside. He led the Big 12 with 13 touchdowns as a senior, which helped his draft stock skyrocket. A shin bruise during camp slowed Allen's progress and has been cited as a reason why the coaching staff has been hesitant to use him. Before that, though, reporters viewed Allen as perhaps the team's best pass catcher not named Rice or Xavier Worthy.
During the Chiefs' Week 4 win over the Raiders, when the two aforementioned receivers got hurt, Allen only saw the field for five snaps and recorded his first NFL target. That could change now that the coaching staff has a week of preparation to get him more involved.
What Kansas City is truly missing in the receiver room is a playmaker who can make things happen with the ball in his hands. Rice is great in the intermediate game, but he isn't necessarily someone defenses are going to key in on to open things up downfield. And despite Worthy's tremendous straight-line speed, he's been largely ineffective in all areas of the offense in 2026.
Allen generated a lot of buzz in limited preseason action, with the biggest highlight coming on an impressive snag in the exhibition opener. Insiders and other observers have made it clear that he has as much burst and is shiftier than anyone in the short passing game.
When speaking to the media on Monday , head coach Andy Reid mentioned the possibility of Allen seeing increased snaps with Thornton heading to the IR. Those opportunities would only grow if Rice is unable to suit up this week versus the Chargers. "Yeah, I think he would probably work into the mix there a little bit more," Reid said. "He's a good football player, and even though he's young, he's got good ability."
Andy Reid on if rookie WR Cyrus Allen will receive more playing time moving forward: “Yeah, I think he would probably work into the mix there a little bit more. He's a good football player, and even though he's young, he's got good ability.” pic.twitter.com/mMeGf7WVX1
Those words don't necessarily mean Allen is going to see a dozen targets on Sunday, so his biggest supporters should take Reid's comments with a grain of salt. Reid tends to have a level of comfort with the players he trusts to catch passes from Patrick Mahomes, which helps explain why the front office brought two-time Chiefs Super Bowl winner Justin Watson back to the practice squad during the bye.
Depending on Rice's injury status before the upcoming matchup, this could be Allen's biggest chance to earn a consistent role in Eric Bieniemy's offense. If he makes the most of his snaps, even in a limited role, he could earn a bigger place in the game plan moving forward.

title: The Chiefs' Highest-Paid Linebacker Hasn't Been Their Best, and That's Alright
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs rolled into the year with plenty of questions on the defensive side of the ball, especially after an offseason filled with change. That applied to the linebacker position as well, with Leo Chenal departing for the Washington Commanders in free agency and leaving someone else to fill his spot.
With that said, the starting duo of Nick Bolton and Drue Tranquill remained. The former is regarded as the on-field coach and leader of the defense — essentially an extension of coordinator Steve Spagnuolo. The latter, meanwhile, was coming off a couple of down years and took a pay cut to return for what could be one last dance in Kansas City.
Four games into the season, the expectations of many haven't aligned with reality. Bolton and his $19.25 million cap hit have been outplayed by Tranquill and his $5M mark , although that isn't necessarily the end of the world. It's less of an indictment on Bolton and more a praise of Tranquill's performance thus far.
Coverage numbers tend to vary by site, so it's better to paint a picture of a player's output by coming up with an average. After sorting through Pro Football Reference , Pro Football Focus and NFL Pro 's data, the stat line matches the eye test.
Both players combined for an average of 12 targets in the passing game in Weeks 1-4. Bolton surrendered 10.3 completions, 7.0 yards per target and a 103.0 passer rating. Tranquill, on the other hand, ceded 5.3 completions, 5.3 yards per yarget and a passer rating of 60.0. Add in that Bolton's facing the lowest average depth of target of his career (3.1 yards) and Tranquill's is his highest since 2022 (4.8), and you get a pretty clear read.
Tranquill is also faring better as a disruptor in all phases despite Bolton having 22 "stops" to his 18. The 31-year-old maintains an 11.8% pressure rate to his peer's 9.1% figure, along with a 3.3% missed tackle clip to Bolton's 9.8%. There wasn't a much better game to sum up Tranquill's efforts than him terrorizing the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4.
Spagnuolo is using Tranquill in a variety of ways, including lining him up along the defensive line on 36 occasions. The 'backer owns a 27.9% blitz rate, which clears 2025 (24.4%) as his most significant usage in that role as a Chief. Bolton himself admitted back in August that there would "never" be a true replacement for Chenal, but Spagnuolo throwing multiple things at the wall and hoping something sticks seems to be the plan. Tranquill is a part of that attempted solution.
The same can't really be said for Jack Cochrane or Jeffrey Bassa. Neither player is making much of an impact on defense, but Bassa did notch a forced fumble on special teams in Las Vegas. The signing of Cam Jones to the 53-man roster signals that Cooper McDonald isn't ready to return, and Cole Christiansen's game-day elevations from the practice squad are capped. This is a depth chart that's extremely top-heavy entering Week 6.
Bolton enjoyed plenty of plus moments before the bye, but it's Tranquill who's been the plus player at that position to this point. The blend of better-than-expected coverage, relentless attacking in run defense and quality fundamentals as both a tackler and blitzer is tough to argue against. The Chiefs can't ask for much more and should instead simply hope this level of play can be sustained.
If the rest of the linebacker room ascends as well, the Kansas City defense will continue to jell post-bye and down the stretch of the regular season.

title: Why Didn't the Chiefs Trade for Marvin Harrison Jr.?
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs need wide receivers.
After Tyquan Thornton suffered a gruesome ankle injury , the Chiefs made a patchwork move, reuniting with Justin Watson . The Chiefs still need wide receivers, both short-term and long.
Many of my pre-draft opinions revolved around my desire for the Chiefs to use one of their premium picks on a pass catcher. They didn't. Much of this summer's training camp hype cycles belonged to fifth-round rookie Cyrus Allen . So far, he's played fewer offensive snaps than defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga.
Looking to the future, there's just as much uncertainty. The Chiefs' No. 1 receiver, Rashee Rice, is in a contract year. Former first-round pick Xavier Worthy is under contract through 2027, but the Chiefs will need to make a decision regarding his fifth-year option after this season. Thornton is under contract for 2027 with a $7.5 million cap hit.
I would make the argument that the Chiefs' biggest need for the rest of the 2026 season and their biggest need for the next several seasons all revolve around the wide receiver position. Why am I rehashing this opinion in mid-October?
Because even I don't think the Chiefs should have beaten the Houston Texans' bid to trade for Marvin Harrison Jr.
To be clear, I was at least somewhat interested in the Chiefs being the "change of scenery" destination for the embattled former No. 4 overall pick, but those delusions were shattered by the reports of what Houston gave up in the deal.
In exchange for Harrison and a 2027 seventh-round pick, the Texans gave up a 2027 second-rounder and a '27 sixth. Essentially, a second-rounder for Harrison and a largely cosmetic late-round pick-swap. Here's the even wilder part: the Texans are 1-4! Right now, that pick would fall at No. 39 overall according to Tankathon . The Texans certainly hope to make a playoff push, but even if they go 8-4 the rest of the way, ending at 9-8 and just outside of the postseason, they'd ultimately be sending a top-50 pick to Arizona in the deal.
From the Cardinals' perspective, that's a worthwhile return. For the 4-0 Chiefs, the apparent only realistic path to Harrison would have included Kansas City's 2027 first-round pick. Even if KC would've gained a mid-round pick from Arizona in this hypothetical, I wouldn't have blamed general manager Brett Veach for hanging up the phone before Arizona finished their pitch.
Should the Chiefs be willing to offer their most precious pick, the 2027 first-rounder, for some wide receivers? Possibly! Do the Philadelphia Eagles want to move DeVonta Smith to jumpstart their rebuild? I'd listen! But for a player in the midst of as disastrous of a season as Harrison? Not even I am receiver-starved enough to make that call.
WR Separation Score vs TPRR 📊 -- Carnell Tate building chemistry with Ward -- Downs, Doubs, Odunze, Pickens prime targets for positive regression -- MHJ in a league of his own pic.twitter.com/kDtxG8H22T
For further context, Bill Barnwell of ESPN took a longer look at just how bad things have been for Harrison in Arizona.
"He hasn't been getting much separation, hasn't hit high-end speed, and isn't winning on contested catches very often," Barnwell wrote. "He needs to be a different player altogether in Houston."
Brutal, right? ...Well, that was just Barnwell's summary on Twitter ! The deep-dive brings some of the stats that underscore the disappointments that have come with Harrison's career so far.
"During his time with the Cardinals, Harrison ranked last in the NFL among all wide receivers (with 50 targets or more over the past three years) in separation, averaging just 2.1 yards of separation when targeted, per NFL Next Gen Stats," Barnwell continued on ESPN.com . "Great receivers—even ones who get plenty of attention from opposing defenses—are typically able to create more space for themselves. The likes of Ja'Marr Chase and Justin Jefferso n average over 3 yards of separation on their routes. In Arizona, McBride averaged 3.3 yards of separation on his targets during that time, while Wilson was at 2.5 yards."
Barnwell's assessment continues at length, with unflattering statistics couched by a few fair criticisms of the Cardinals' offense throughout the dissection.
There's certainly a chance that Harrison does become "a different player altogether" with the Texans, but looking at the deal from the Chiefs' standpoint, there's no way I would have beaten that price for a receiver who needs to be nearly unrecognizable on his new team.

title: Chiefs Injury Report: Kingsley Suamataia Is Back, Updates on Josh Simmons and Rashee Rice
full_text:
The Chiefs received an extended period of rest with their bye week. It was a much-deserved break for a Kansas City squad that started the year with an impressive 4-0 record.
Now, Andy Reid's team will have to play 13 consecutive games without a break, which should make for a brutal stretch down the road. The head coach spoke to the media for the first time in a week to provide a few updates on his team.
Kansas City has already been hit by the injury bug, but left guard Kingsley Suamataia was benched in Week 4 against the Raiders due to a "coaching decision." It appears that no further disciplinary action will be taken against the third-year offensive lineman, who was replaced by Mike Caliendo in the victory. "Yeah, he'll be back," Reid confirmed with the media this afternoon.
When Reid was asked about Suamataia's benching last Sunday, he stated that he didn't want to disclose any further information about the reasoning and that Suamataia would "be better for it." However, that one-game absence seems to be the extent of his punishment.
In addition to Suamataia's situation, the Chiefs have been without starting left tackle Josh Simmons for the entirety of the regular season because of a bulging disc in his back. Despite all the speculation surrounding his status, Reid provided a more positive update on Simmons today.
"I'll know more soon. They [Josh Simmons and Rashee Rice] were in last week," Reid said. "Josh was here all week doing his rehab and stuff. So, we'll see. They'll be back tomorrow, and I'll have a better idea of what's going on."
Although a return doesn't sound imminent, this is a lot more encouraging than Reid's typically vague answers about Simmons' back. It's an excellent sign that he was rehabbing with the training staff during the bye.
Andy Reid, following the Chiefs' bye, said the team signed Justin Watson to the practice squad. Tyquan Thornton (left ankle) is expected to be placed on IR. Reid on Josh Simmons: "Josh was here all [last] week doing his rehab. They'll be back tomorrow & I'll have a better idea."
Getting Suamataia back already bolsters KC's unit in the trenches, but having Simmons back would be an even bigger development. If he's ready to go in Week 6 versus the Chargers, the Chiefs could move acting left tackle Kahlil Benson to the right side and send Jaylon Moore to a swing tackle role.
In the receiver room, Rashee Rice remains day-to-day with the hamstring injury he suffered in the first quarter last game, while Reid confirmed that Tyquan Thornton will likely be placed on Injured Reserve. The breakout speedster dislocated his ankle late in the fourth quarter during a career day in the victory over Las Vegas. To help offset those losses, Kansas City has signed Justin Watson to its practice squad , who won a pair of championships with the team in 2023 and 2024. The Chiefs could elevate him as early as this weekend given his familiarity with the scheme.
