title: Chiefs Adding Justin Watson to Insulate WR Room Amid Flurry of Roster Moves
full_text:
Coming out of their Week 5 bye, the Kansas City Chiefs have the chance to take down yet another divisional foe when they square off against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. As a new week of practice soon begins, though, there will be a new face entering the fold.
New to the 2026 Chiefs, at least, as it's a familiar friend signing with the team. Reported by Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network , Kansas City is signing wide receiver Justin Watson to the practice squad.
Head coach Andy Reid confirmed the move during his Monday media availability, adding that wideout Tyquan Thornton ( ankle ) will likely be placed on the injured reserve list. Linebacker Cam Jones is expected to take his place on the 53-man roster.
"I will tell you that Tyquan is most likely going on IR here," Reid began. "We'd elevate Cam Jones. We also signed Justin Watson to the practice squad, so those are the immediate updates."
Watson, who turned 30 in April, was originally a member of the Chiefs from 2022-2024. That span saw him appear in 50 regular-season games, starting 20 of them. He won a pair of championships in the club's back-to-back run, finishing his initial tenure with 64 receptions on 119 targets for 1,064 yards and seven touchdowns.
The former fifth-round pick was a trusted vertical passing target for quarterback Patrick Mahomes, evidenced by his 17.2-yard average depth of target in KC. He netted 16.6 yards per reception as a Chief in the first go-round.
When asked about the reunion with Watson, Reid praised his versatility and understanding of what's requested of him within the offense.
"He was a good player for us when he was here," Reid said. "He obviously can run fast, and he's got great size. He's willing to do everything, he knows the offense. He's a smart kid. We felt like he could come back in as needed and contribute, step in and go. With just a slight review, he should be fine and good to go."
On Friday, Chiefs On SI covered Kansas City's reported interest in Watson. Here's some of the conclusion after weighing the pros and cons of a potential signing:
"At the end of the day, Watson might just be a more appropriate Thornton replacement than multiple internal options or free agent avenues. Even if he isn't a clear-cut needle-mover, it may not hurt to bring him in and see what he's got as a part-time player. An emphasis should be placed on the part, though, coming with the understanding that the double champion with the Chiefs wouldn't be saving the receiver room."
As a member of the practice squad, Watson can only be elevated to the game-day roster three times. After No. 3, he'd be required to sit on the practice squad for the rest of the regular season or be signed to the 53 directly. With Thornton expected to miss 12-16 weeks following his gruesome ankle injury , adding depth here makes plenty of sense.
The Jones signing stems from linebacker Cole Christiansen reaching his activation limit for the year. Cooper McDonald remains on IR for the time being, so bringing up Jones was a no-brainer. The 26-year-old has played 161 defensive snaps for the Chiefs in 34 regular-season contests, on top of another 567 reps on special teams.
With just six days remaining until a new challenge versus Los Angeles, the Chiefs' roster shuffle continues.

title: While the Chiefs Enjoy a Bye Week, the Rest of the AFC West Has Plenty to Prove
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs are 4-0 and the only undefeated team still standing in the AFC . That, of course, means the Chiefs are in command of the AFC West while the Las Vegas Raiders try to hold on to their second-place standing and the Denver Broncos look to improve on their .500 start.
Oh, and the Los Angeles Chargers would probably like to win a game sooner rather than later, too.
With the Chiefs enjoying their bye week, let's take a look at Sunday's pair of games containing AFC West squads, plus two primetime matchups with other AFC contenders.
The Raiders acquited themselves admirably against the Chiefs last week, taking their first loss of the season in decidedly un-Raider-y fashion. (Un-Raider-y isn't a word, but you know what it means!) In some ways, I'm more convinced that the Raiders are a legitimate playoff-adjacent team now than I was before their loss to the Chiefs. However, they're not getting a break from their upcoming schedule anytime soon.
Las Vegas gets the New England Patriots in Foxborough this week before hosting the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams in the next two weeks. The Raiders don't need to win all of those games to retain their new semi-contender status, but they can't lose four consecutive games and still be taken seriously in the second half of the year.
New England, on the other hand, is coming off an impressive win over the Bills in Buffalo last weekend, stabilizing the team after a blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 3.
The Raiders may still be a year of progress away from true contention, but Chiefs fans should obviously be pulling for the Patriots in this one.
these posts came a week apart life comes at you fast and all that pic.twitter.com/pVD2tc26og
Even with impressive home victories over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3, the vibes around quarterback Bo Nix and the Broncos' offense seem to have taken a considerable shift after last week's loss at the San Francisco 49ers. For what it's worth, I still think the Broncos are the second-best squad in the division and should be expected to return to the playoffs again this season, but that confidence would be severely shaken if the winless Chargers can pull off the upset in LA.
The Chargers have been one of the biggest disappointments in all of football this season, and they're running out of time to do something about it. After hosting the Broncos, the Chargers will head to Kansas City in Week 6 before "visiting" the Rams after their Week 7 bye. If there's any life left in the Chargers at all, they'll need to prove it against Denver.
Not that Chiefs fans need my guidance here, but a Chargers win would be good for both the Chiefs' lead over the Broncos and for a week of NFL comedy.
Beyond the AFC West, two of the Chiefs' top AFC rivals will go up against a pair of 2-2 NFC teams in primetime. The Baltimore Ravens (3-1) will face the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday Night Football, while the Bills (3-1) will travel to Los Angeles to take on the Rams for a Monday night showdown.
It's far too early in the year to be seriously considering playoff seeding, but any extra wiggle room for the Chiefs' hunt for the No. 1 seed would be beneficial, especially with Kansas City's Thanksgiving showdown with the Bills looming large.
Chiefs fans should enjoy the experience of rooting for Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson in their new homes on Monday Night Football while pulling for the Falcons to take a game from Baltimore on Sunday night.

title: Chiefs’ Pass-Rush Unit Could Return a Sneaky Weapon From Injury Soon
full_text:
Much has been made of the Kansas City Chiefs' defensive line failing to record a sack in each of the past three games. However, Steve Spagnuolo's unit could be getting a huge boost in the upcoming weeks.
Following Kansas City's bye, the Chiefs will finally be eligible to get 2025 second-round pick Omarr Norman-Lott back on the field. He's been on the PUP (Physically Unable to Perform) list since training camp and was required to miss the opening four contests of the year, but Week 6 marks the first point at which he can return to game action. The University of Tennessee product tore his ACL in Week 7 of last season and has been rehabbing ever since. There was hope he'd progress to full health and participate in offseason sessions, but the front office elected to place him on the PUP list to allow him extra time to recover.
It's been almost a full year since Norman-Lott suffered the injury. Barring any setbacks, it shouldn't be too long before we see him active again. Of course, every ACL tear is different, and not everyone can make a nine-month return like Patrick Mahomes did.
Head coach Andy Reid alluded to Norman-Lott "potentially" returning after the bye in late September. It was the first positive injury update the Chiefs had received on him in quite some time.
Andy Reid also says Chiefs DT Omarr Norman-Lott is a possibility to return from IR after the bye week. Reid says he’s doing more and getting closer to a return.
The Chiefs certainly won't be in any rush to bring Norman-Lott back from a serious knee injury at 4-0. Once they open his 21-day practice window, KC must either activate him during that span or transfer him to the IR for the remainder of the season.
As a rookie, Norman-Lott played sparingly but was an effective interior lineman. Across five contests, he finished with one sack, four solo tackles, and one tackle for loss, earning a 54.2 Pro Football Focus (PFF) grade. While Norman-Lott plays on the inside, his profile is more as a pass rusher than a run defender. He's extremely explosive for his size and has a relentless motor when getting after the quarterback, boasting an impressive 18.9% pass-rush win rate as a senior in college.
As we've noted in recent days on Chiefs at SI, the pass rush hasn't really been as invisible as it seems. It especially started to come alive in the second half of the victory over the Las Vegas Raiders. However, Norman-Lott's return to the squad could open up a plethora of possibilities for the defensive line rotation.
The Chiefs drafted another defensive tackle early in this year's draft, selecting former Clemson standout Peter Woods with the No. 29 overall pick . He and Khyiris Tonga have split snaps throughout the season, with both playing a little under 50% of the defense's reps. Norman-Lott could slot in during passing downs to rush the quarterback alongside Chris Jones on the inside.
When Coach Reid speaks to the media on Monday, we could get more clarity on Norman-Lott's status. It's been quiet on the injury front for ONR lately, but the Chiefs could have a secret weapon in the pass rush ready to deploy when he's healthy.

title: Mansoor Delane and Nohl Williams Star in a Bright Future for the Chiefs' Cornerback Room
full_text:
It was a bit of a surprise when the Kansas City Chiefs traded up to obtain the No. 6 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, then even more of a surprise when they used that selection on LSU cornerback Mansoor Delane . Immediately, Delane rightfully had sky-high expectations as the new face of the Chiefs' secondary.
Delane was limited throughout the majority of training camp due to a shoulder injury and then played just three snaps (including an interception of Bo Nix) in Weeks 1 and 2 due to an issue with the same shoulder. Even with just two full games under his belt, Delane looks to be worth that draft selection, and he's not alone as a rising star in Kansas City's overhauled cornerback room.
As any Chiefs or Los Angeles Rams fan knows by now, the Chiefs traded away cornerback Trent McDuffie to the Rams this offseason, and Jaylen Watson reunited with McDuffie after leaving for LA in free agency. That left a significant void for the Chiefs to fill at corner.
To begin 2026, veteran cornerback Kristian Fulton was entering the second year of his two-year deal with the Chiefs after a disappointing 2025, and '25 third-round draft pick Nohl Williams was looking to follow his promising rookie campaign with a more consistent workload in his sophomore season.
Delane, Williams and Fulton all hit the ground running .
Highest graded CBs in man coverage this season Mansoor Delane         93.8 Kristian Fulton             92.8 Nohl Williams               91.8 Trent McDuffie            90.9 Travis Hunter               90.3 pic.twitter.com/4Tv5R4kLLU
Delane has been excellent , even when asked to take on difficult coverage responsibilities, as he was asked to do at times against Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. He's also been a missile in run defense, playing with speed and physicality that fits Steve Spagnuolo's defense perfectly.
Mansoor Delane with one of the GREATEST two-play sequences you’ll see from a rook. Registers a TFL on Ashton Jeanty, and follows it up with CLAMPING Brock Bowers. The Chiefs rookie CB NEUTRALIZING some of the NFL’s top weapons 😳🔒 pic.twitter.com/oHzd3YU6qM
Delane has the fifth-highest overall cornerback grade from Pro Football Focus through the first four weeks of the 2026 season, while Fulton lands at No. 11. Williams appears at No. 41 in overall PFF grading but lands at No. 23 with his coverage grade alone.
good player this Mansoor Delane https://t.co/HNmzmM6Pbj pic.twitter.com/XPGheGgX3M
The one area of concern in the Chiefs' cornerback room comes in the slot, where veteran L'Jarius Sneed has provided some value and some tough snaps in his second act with the team. Sneed has the second-worst PFF grade among qualifying cornerbacks (No. 102 of 103), but he's been a positive force against the run and as a blitzer.
Sneed began the season in excellent fashion against the Denver Broncos in Week 1 before being routinely bested by Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs in Week 2. I'll argue that it's a bit too early (and a bit unnecessary) to rush to end the Sneed-reclaimation experiment, but he's certainly struggled more than the team's trio of outside corners to begin the year.
I'd be interested to see Delane get a bit of work in the slot if that would enable Williams and Fulton to hold the outside corner roles in nickel packages, but I'd also understand some hesitance, as Delane's potential value is probably highest as a shutdown outside corner, and he's still acclimating to the NFL game (though you wouldn't know that if you only watched him play).
What other options could the Chiefs have?
Rookie defensive back Jadon Canady was a healthy scratch in Week 4 as safety Chamarri Conner returned to the lineup, while slot corner Kader Kohou remains on the practice squad, so neither Canady nor Kohou seem particularly close to challenging Sneed for those slot corner reps. Versatile DB Chris Roland-Wallace took a season-high 29 defensive snaps against the Raiders, but Sneed has taken more than 72% of the defensive snaps in every game so far this season.
Ultimately, the Chiefs' slot corner position will require more monitoring (and, ideally, better play) in the weeks to come, but the Delane/Williams outside duo—with room for cameos from Fulton this season—appears to be one of the NFL's most promising young pairings.

title: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker Welcomes Potential Tyreek Hill Reunion in Kansas City
full_text:
While the Kansas City Chiefs are off to a 4-0 start heading into the bye, the front office is actively looking to bolster the roster. Kansas City will likely be without wide receiver Tyquan Thornton for the remainder of the regular season and could miss wide receiver Rashee Rice for some time as well.
KC has been linked to several wideouts, but the most obvious addition could come in the form of a reunion with Tyreek Hill . The speedster is coming off a dislocated knee last season and could make his return to the NFL with the team he started his career with. Rumors have been swirling between Hill and the Chiefs for quite some time. It's the worst-kept secret that Kansas City is showing interest in the 32-year-old. Recently, one of the AFC's biggest stars revealed his thoughts on Hill potentially returning to play for Andy Reid.
In an interview with Yahoo Sports on behalf of Orgain, running back Kenneth Walker III was asked what he thought about Hill potentially rejoining the Chiefs. The NFL's leading rusher is all for bringing "Cheetah" back.
"I've seen his speed. Everybody knows Tyreek Hill is just straight speed, and he's just an athlete in general," Walker said. "And just watching him over the years, I'm like, 'He's one of the best players that really played.' So, it's cool to see that. I think it's cool and it would be a great addition to our team."
Through the first four games of his Chiefs tenure, Walker has truly been an MVP candidate . He's currently sitting at 537 rushing yards with six total touchdowns. Chiefs fans knew he was talented when he signed with the franchise in March, but no one could have expected this level of production.
Part of the reason why Walker believes a reunion with Hill would work, as he later explained in the interview, is that it would make the Chiefs' offense more versatile. Between Patrick Mahomes' arm talent, Walker's dynamic running style , and Hill as a downfield threat, opposing defenses would have a difficult time containing those three players at once. While the backfield is set in Kansas City, the wide receiving corps is far less certain. The aforementioned injuries to Rice and Thornton will hinder KC, leaving the team with Xavier Worthy, Jalen Royals, Cyrus Allen, Nikko Remigio, and a potential practice squad elevation for next week's group of wideouts.
There's more at play than Brett Veach simply signing him to a cheap one-year contract, though. Hill is currently battling a civil assault and battery trial in court and has a pending Personal Conduct Policy investigation from the NFL. The Chiefs are already starting to look at other options, including former Chief champion Justin Watson .
Hill is coming off a devastating injury himself and hasn't played in an NFL game in over a year, but he's only two seasons removed from leading the league in receiving yards. If he's even 80% of his old self, he'd be a tremendous help to this offense, and Walker's comments reflect that.

title: Reported Chiefs Interest in WR Reunion Underscores a Harsh Reality
full_text:
Although the Kansas City Chiefs are on a bye week, many folks are still talking about the lone undefeated team left in the AFC. Some of that is for good reason, but there's also a glaring hole on the roster that needs to be addressed at some point.
With wide receiver Tyquan Thornton suffering a dislocated ankle in Week 4's win over the Las Vegas Raiders, it'd likely behoove general manager Brett Veach to add another pass catcher. The only issue is that the in-season talent pool doesn't contain many quality options, leaving the franchise in a tough spot.
The most recent bit of Chiefs-related wideout news sums that up pretty perfectly. According to Pete Sweeney of the Kansas City Star , Veach and Co. are "among several teams" interested in free agent Justin Watson.
The Chiefs are among several teams interested in WR Justin Watson, per source. Watson played for Kansas City from 2022-24 and is a three-time Super Bowl champion, having beaten the Chiefs with the Bucs before being part of their back-to-back title teams.
Watson being the latest name tied to KC emphasizes just how dried up the market is. Barring a trade that would almost surely cost NFL Draft capital, he's right in the thick of the tier of players the team could be vying for. Does a reunion with the three-time Super Bowl champ make any sense? Let's break it down.
They oftentimes come off as buzz phrases in Chiefs circles, but they do matter to the organization and come in handy given the timing of any potential signing once the season's rolling. Veteran experience, familiarity with the scheme, attention to detail, alignment versatility and more all carry significance. Watson checks each and every box there.
Now in his age-30 campaign, Watson has 1,716 regular-season offensive snaps under his belt as a member of the Chiefs and over 500 spanning five other years with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Houston Texans. Thinking from a Thornton-esque perspective regarding the operation of the offense, the former fifth-round pick also possesses proven chemistry with quarterback Patrick Mahomes on vertical passing concepts.
Watson carried a 17.2-yard average depth of target in Kansas City from 2022-2024. He averaged 13.9 yards before the catch per reception and owned an 89.8 passer rating when targeted. According to Pro Football Focus , Watson spent between 63.9% and 68.8% of his time lined up out wide over his three Chiefs seasons. Thornton was at 62.5% in 2025 and is at 70.9% in 2026.
It also doesn't hurt that Watson is a bigger-bodied player than most of the current Chiefs receiver room (6-foot-2, 215 pounds), is a willing and (mostly) capable blocker and can play special teams. Things like that stand out to the coaching staff and front office, for better or worse.
Simply put, Watson just wasn't a very good player during his time with the Chiefs. According to SumerSports , his 50.94% catch rate ranked sixth among all Kansas City wideouts in 2023. The following year, he owned an 0.72 yards per route run figure that was dead last in the group and trailed sixth-place Marquez Valdes-Scantling (0.89) by a decent margin.
The advanced data not being in Watson's favor doesn't stop there. NFL Pro pegs him as posting a -9.8% catch rate over expected in 2022, then a -1.3% mark in 2023 before it spiked to +6.0% in his final Kansas City season. He was worth 17.2 EPA in the latter campaign, but that can't be a reliable expectation baseline for the current year.
Other factors must also be considered, even with Thornton set to miss most or all of this season . What's the latest with Tyreek Hill? The Chiefs have been linked to him at every step over the last few weeks, although his ongoing legal situation muddies those waters quite a bit. Would a Watson addition put that potential acquisition on ice?
What about costing players like second-year man Jalen Royals and rookie Cyrus Allen developmental reps? Is Watson that much better than either option at this stage in his career? So many moving pieces make this far from a no-brainer of a decision.
Now on the wrong side of the aging curve, it's fair to question what Watson has left in the tank. His Texans tenure was virtually silent, but it's also not like he forgot how to function in a Kansas City-style offense after the end of the 2024-25 campaign. As long as there's still some speed, he can execute the same type of role he used to have.
If the Chiefs did sign Watson, this writer doesn't believe head coach Andy Reid and company would be quite as compelled to put him on the field as often as a JuJu Smith-Schuster. Additionally, Watson doesn't carry any off-the-field baggage and isn't recovering from a major injury, so he'd be a more immediate plug-and-play (and keep in the lineup) fit than someone like Hill.
At the end of the day, Watson might just be a more appropriate Thornton replacement than multiple internal options or free agent avenues. Even if he isn't a clear-cut needle-mover, it may not hurt to bring him in and see what he's got as a part-time player. An emphasis should be placed on the part, though, coming with the understanding that the double champion with the Chiefs wouldn't be saving the receiver room.
Again, that's an unfortunate reminder of where things are at. Help could be on the way while still not solving the current problem to the optimal degree.

title: Chargers Are Cheap and It Could Cost Them Jim Harbaugh and Justin Herbert
full_text:
Nothing says more about the Los Angeles Chargers right now than Jim Harbaugh finally being speechless after the latest loss.
The Chargers sit at 0-5 and it’s easy to throw out blame. Sure, blame Harbaugh for some bad in-game decisions. Blame Justin Herbert for the sandwich-themed turnovers. Blame Mike McDaniel. Blame Joe Hortiz for the state of the roster.
But Harbaugh didn’t forget how to coach. Herbert knows how to quarterback. McDaniels is trying to run an offense with players who wouldn’t crack a 53 for other teams. And Hortiz probably has his hands tied by Chargers ownership.
Because it starts at the top: The Chargers are cheap.
The Chargers bought the expensive car but won’t put the nice fuel in it. They paid for Jim Harbaugh and Mike McDaniel.
But they’re also 31st in cash spending . The Chargers’ cap-to-cash ratio (0.9711, no other team is below 1) is dead last.
Onlookers can argue until they’re blue in the face that this doesn't matter. But there’s a fine line between being “smart” with money and just being “cheap.”
Being “cheap” is what creates a five-man competition at left guard all summer in front of the franchise quarterback. Cheap is signing the bargain free-agent center before the market opens to get a deal. Cheap is still rocking with Quentin Johnston because it’s a deal. Or trading for Odafe Oweh, seeing his production in the defense, then not paying to keep him. Cheap is pretending to overvalue the comp pick process in the name of strong depth, when it’s really about budget.
And cheap is still sitting on $26 million in cap space while this all unfolds.
There's perplexing stuff to the cheap factor too. Best example is drafting a first-round running back instead of a premium position, when running back is the one position where "cheap" can be a really good, productive idea. Kimani Vidal says hello.
Not that Chargers fans expected anything different from this ownership group. But it’s going to cost them Harbaugh, and it might just cost them Herbert, who appears to be in a funk only a change of scenery will solve.
And if the time to move on from Herbert comes, Chargers ownership hasn’t exactly instilled confidence that it will use the bounty of assets gained in a way that does anything other than carefully balancing the checkbook before anything else.

title: Chargers Snap Count Analysis: Biggest Winners, Losers and Role Changes From Week 5
full_text:
Now that the Los Angeles Chargers are 0-5, the chances of making the playoffs are near zero, with no team ever making the playoffs after such a start. The team will need to look into rebuilding their roster and focusing on their future.
This can start with making role changes week by week by getting younger/players of the future reps now, rather than having them sit. Who are some of those winners and losers that they could use to build upon?
Logan Taylor was surprisingly slotted in at guard during the Chargers Week 5 matchup, with many believing he would play offensive tackle, as he did last week filling in for Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater. At guard, Taylor had a solid game against a strong Denver Broncos defensive unit, giving fans hope that he can continue this ascension and become an NFL-caliber offensive lineman for the Bolts.
Snap Changes Since Last Week: 28 -> 67
Derius Davis is once again on the losers list, this time not for a single major mistake he made during a game, but for a continued lack of opportunity. This is inherently a good thing as he has been making the aforementioned major mistakes, but his lack of a role is an obvious sign of him falling down the depth chart.
Practice squad wide receivers Marquez Valdes-Scantling and Theo Wease Jr. saw snaps over the former fourth-round pick Davis.
Snap Changes Since Last Week: 3 -> 10
Tuli Tuipulotu has been one of the biggest bright spots of the Chargers' defense, playing with major tenacity and effort every play. He recorded a forced fumble and created more opportunities for the poor Chargers offense all day long. He is well deserving of a contract extension .

title: 3 Winners and 3 Losers After Chargers Drop Yet Another Heartbreaking Game
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers had an opportunity to finally get their season moving in the right direction Sunday, but another late collapse left them searching for answers.
The loss dropped the Chargers to 0-5, making the start to the 2026 season increasingly difficult to ignore. Although several players delivered encouraging performances, costly mistakes ultimately overshadowed the positives.
Here are three winners and three losers from the Chargers’ latest defeat.
Vidal provided one of the game’s most exciting moments. The running back finished with 57 rushing yards on eight carries, including a spectacular 42-yard touchdown that gave the Chargers their first lead of the afternoon. His scoring run demonstrated the explosiveness and determination the offense desperately needed. Vidal broke multiple tackles and found a way into the end zone when the Chargers needed a spark.
Although his performance wasn’t enough to secure a victory, Vidal gave the coaching staff another reason to get him involved moving forward.
The Chargers’ defense needed a game changing play, and Tuipulotu delivered one late in the third quarter.
With Denver threatening to regain the lead, the defensive lineman forced a fumble from quarterback Bo Nix and recovered the ball himself. The turnover immediately put Los Angeles in excellent field position, setting up Vidal’s go-ahead touchdown on the following play.
While the defense couldn’t finish the job, his ability to create a takeaway was one of the afternoon’s biggest positives.
Rucci made his first NFL touchdown catch count. The tight end hauled in a seven-yard scoring pass from Justin Herbert in the third quarter.
The touchdown capped a productive drive that showed what the Chargers’ offense could accomplish when it sustained possession and converted important third downs. Rucci wasn’t the biggest name on the field, but his contribution mattered in a game where offensive production was difficult to find. His performance offered a small bright spot in an otherwise frustrating afternoon.
Herbert’s fourth-quarter mistakes proved decisive. The Chargers quarterback finished 14-of-24 for 121 passing yards and a touchdown, but his late-game struggles overshadowed the earlier scoring drive.
Herbert has previously demonstrated the ability to carry an offense through difficult situations. However, the Chargers need better execution from their franchise quarterback when games reach their most important moments.
Kolar’s early fumble helped put the Chargers in a difficult position from the opening quarter. The turnover gave Denver possession in favorable territory, allowing the Broncos to capitalize with a short touchdown run.
In a game decided by six points, surrendering possession so close to the end zone was an expensive mistake.
Herbert was sacked five times, and the offense struggled to maintain momentum throughout the afternoon.
The failed fourth-and-one attempt early in the fourth quarter was particularly damaging, preventing the Chargers from extending their lead and giving Denver a chance to tie the game.
With the offense already dealing with significant personnel challenges, the offensive line must find ways to provide Herbert with more time and create dependable running lanes.
The race to No. 1. pic.twitter.com/9dyLTbGqHh

title: Chargers Could Be Buyers and Sellers in the Coming Weeks
full_text:
The head coach was Marty Schottenheimer and the team finished 4-12 and in last place in the AFC West. The year was 2003, and the then-San Diego Chargers lost their first five games that season. Thanks to Sunday’s 23-17 setback to the visiting Denver Broncos, the Chargers are in that same boat in 2026.
Now keep in mind that that Schottenheimer and company righted that ship a year later, winning the AFC West with a 12-4 record. Is that in the cards for Jim Harbaugh and company?
In any case, it’s that time of the year when teams that find themselves in dire straits may be willing to part ways with some proven performers. At the same time, they may also be looking for some help on an area of the team that is not performing well for any number of reasons.
Last Wednesday, Bradley Locker of Pro Football Focus assembled a list of 15 players that could be dealt for. The deadline is Tuesday, November 10 at 4:00 pm ET. The first name listed is wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. and this weekend, the Arizona Cardinals sent the fourth overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft to the Houston Texans.
1st and 10 · Denver Broncos Bo Nix ( @BoNix10 ) runs up the middle for 1 yard to DEN 41, fumbles, recovered by Tuli Tuipulotu ( @TuipulotuTuli ) at DEN 42 https://t.co/B3495YSvR2 pic.twitter.com/7zdiKxkD6F
Also listed by Locker are Chargers’ pass-rusher Tuli Tuipulotu and wide receiver Quentin Johnston. The former is in the final year of his rookie contract, and he and the team didn’t agree to an extension this offseason. Johnston is also in the last season of his original deal after the franchise picked up the fifth-year option on the 6’2”, 208-pound wideout.
Tuipulotu has been a player on the rise, and a year ago he not only led the team with 13.0 sacks, the former USC standout was named to his first Pro Bowl. He’s been a bright spot on a club that hasn’t had much to cheer about. He’s tied for third on Chris O’Leary’s defense with 22 tackles, third on the team with a pair of sacks, and leads the Chargers with eight quarterback hits. He also had a pair of takeaways, and two forced fumbles.
Meanwhile, there may not be a big market for Johnston. He’s played in all four games, been targeted 19 times and caught just seven passes for 108 yards and no touchdowns. In his first three NFL seasons, Johnston totaled 144 receptions for 1,877 yards and 18 scores. But his 59.5 catch percentage over that span also left a lot to be desired.
On the other hand, a Chargers’ offensive line that may be in worse shape than last year’s unit needs help at tackle once again with Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt ailing. Locker suggested that Pittsburgh Steelers’ right tackle Dylan Cook may be a player available now that he’s lost his starting job to 2026 first-round pick Max Iheanachor.
Next up for Harbaugh’s team are the first-place Kansas City Chiefs, who were off last week. The same could be said for the 2026 Chargers in terms of every game this season to date.

title: The Morning-After Thunder: Chargers, Harbaugh Make Dumb Mistakes, Season Slips Away
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers welcomed the Denver Broncos to SoFi Stadium in Week 5 crushed by injuries. Los Angeles started four rookie offensive linemen and were down nearly every wide receiver on the roster. Despite the terrible circumstances , the Chargers had a chance to win this game and boneheaded mishaps handed the Broncos the keys to victory.
At 0-5, the Chargers season is over. Mathematically they have not been eliminated yet but the writing is on the wall. The Chargers must now face tough questions and the demons that haunt organization. How did the team, with Super Bowl aspirations essentially fall off a cliff and forget how to play football on the way down.
The front office will be heavily criticized for how the team has performed and rightfully so. The franchise faces organizational questions that must be answered moving forward.
The game actually went almost exactly as I expected and key matchups proved to be just that. The Chargers defense owned the line of scrimmage for the majority of the game. The Chargers young and inexperienced offensive line attacked the Broncos smaller edge rushers in the run game and opened up the play-action game.
The biggest mistakes were made by Jim Harbaugh and Justin Herbert. Harbaugh made a complete error in judgement when using his first challenge to challenge the spot of a Bo Nix quarterback sneak. The odds of that being overturned are minimal and is was a waste of a timeout and challenge.
That wasted challenge came back to haunt the Chargers as they lost their second challenge later and faced a situation late in the game where that challenge would have helped them win. With just over ten minutes remaining and the Chargers up 17-10, Justin Herbert scrambled for what appeared to be a critical first down. The referees had an awful time with spotting the ball in this game and did not give Herbert the spot. If the Chargers could have challenged it, they would have won.
Harbaugh then made the fatal mistake. He irrationally sent out the Chargers offense to try to secure the first down via quarterback sneak and failed. To that point, the Broncos offense had only managed to score three points on their own, they scored a touchdown only on a short field prior to that. Instead of punting the ball and letting the defense continue on the warpath, Justin Herbert was stuffed and pushed back.
The field position and momentum that immediately went to the Broncos was a killer. Justin Hebert, sensing the lack of offense with nearly no receivers left, became reckless in this game as well and after that momentum swing, he started pressing and trying to do too much leading to turnovers. Herbert's fumbles and interception were squarely on him but so was the entire offense.
The Spanos family and Chargers ownership must be scratching their heads with how this season has gone. The investment in facilities, coaching staff and the big play to bring in Mike McDaniel were never considered risky, they were all considered home run moves.
Are coaching changes on deck? Mike McDaniel called a relatively good game and had a good game plan to attack Denver, especially with the lack of available players. Jim Harbaugh clearly is lost and does not understand how the team is here. Joe Hortiz has been a good drafting general manager but a catastrophic failure on the free agent market and with the offensive line.
My attention as it will be for many Chargers fans will pivot to 2027 draft preparation. But will the Chargers make a move with any of the coaches or the front office. Much of the data and analytics staff left the Chargers shortly after Jim Harbaugh's arrival , he could have used some extra advanced data against the Broncos and at the very least the organization may have to look to reinforce the department.

title: Chargers Trade Deadline Big Board:  Realistic Targets and Trade Assets
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers season has been an absolute disappointment given the expectations heading into the season. The Chargers have shot themselves in the foot nearly every week with questionable in-game decisions, poor preparation and injuries have mounted.
Los Angeles dropped their fifth straight game to hand the 2026 Chargers the worst start for the franchise since the 2000 season. They took on the Denver Broncos in week five with a severely depleted roster and ended up starting four rookie offensive linemen.
The Chargers roster had several questionable holes and depth entering the season and most of those questions have become problems to one degree or another. Looking forward to the trade deadline, is it realistic that a team staring down the barrel of potentially the worst season in franchise history would be buyers? No, they definitely wont be looking for mega deals or franchise-altering additions. However, simple trades for players on expiring contracts that could be potential free agent targets in the offseason may be worth lat-round considerations.
The Chargers are poised to be sellers at the trade deadline. Despite mounting injuries, the Chargers do have several strong position groups and may be able to get draft compensation for certain players. Most NFL trade deadlines come and go quietly, the Chargers likely wont conduct a fire sale but a handful of players could finish their 2026 seasons elsewhere.
The Chargers are likely to deal Khalil Mack to his destination of choice. Los Angeles will still have Tuli Tuipulotu and rookie Akheem Mesidor but behind them is veteran Bud Dupree and practice squad edge rushers. For the rest of this season and for the future, edge depth will be needed.
Former UDFA from the Kansas City Chiefs Malik Herring started the season with the Titans and made his way to the Dolphins where he has been playing significant rotational snaps. More importantly, Herring's pass rush productivity rate is higher than Bud Dupree and has graded out significantly higher as a run defender.
The Chargers could use him if Khalil Mack is gone and potentially get an early look at a potential long-term depth piece. Herring likely would not cost more than a late-round pick swap.
The Chargers already have one weapons grade ginger in Scott Matlock, why not add another? Ko Kieft is listed as a tight end but operates much more as a fullback. He can be trusted to handle defensive ends and edge rushers one-on-one and will clear holes for running backs.
Kieft missed most of 2025 with a broken leg and returned to Tampa Bay this past offseason but has not been getting snaps when healthy. Kieft is a savage blocker and could immediately help in many formations and uses.
TE Ko Kieft (41) is here to kick ass and chew bubble bum...and he's all out of gum. https://t.co/Okw3he3x3N pic.twitter.com/YEf7z6CF8b
Kieft may be redundant with Matlock and  Alec Ingold on the roster but Matlock is on an expiring contract and Ingold has not been playing particularly well and the Chargers have been cycling through tight ends so far this year. If the Chargers plan to deploy a fullback in 2027, it would be great to get a look at another option before free agency. Kieft would likely not cost more than a late Day 3 pick.
It is no secret at this point that there are trade rumors around Khalil Mack. He deserves to go wherever he wants to go to compete for a contender. He can still provide leadership and be a productive edge for a team in need. The Chargers will likely net an early to mid day three pick for Mack.
It would be hard to see homegrown local linebacker Daiyan Henley leave the franchise but he is on an expiring deal and the Chargers have young linebackers ready for playing time alongside several veterans. Henley still boasts speed and coverage skills who could help a team in need. He would also likely net a mid day three pick.

title: Jim Harbaugh’s Damning Quote After Chargers Fall to 0-5 Signals Total Crisis in LA
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have now fallen to 0-5 to begin the 2026 NFL season, a season where they were supposed to be one of the Super Bowl frontrunners. A season where the exciting hiring of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel was supposed to finally give Justin Herbert an environment conducive to success. A season where new hire Chris O'Leary was supposed to continue the elite defensive ecosystem left by now-Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter.
The fact of the matter is that this team is in complete shambles and their leader, Jim Harbaugh, is now running out of answers to be able to help this team fight for competency in the National Football League.
Harbaugh, known for quirky catchphrases and toughness that is infectious through football locker rooms, is seemingly out of, to quote one of those aforementioned catchphrases, "an enthusiasm unknown to mankind."
In the most recent post-game press conference after the Denver Broncos took a 23-17 victory over the Bolts in Week 5, Harbaugh was asked about the message for the team after now being 0-5. He responded with: "Yeah, I don't know what that message is."
Chargers HC Jim Harbaugh on message to the team at 0-5: "Yeah, I don't know what that message is.
An obviously damning statement from the "CEO" head coach who is supposed to be known for his leadership and mentality. He does follow up that statement with a generic motivational comment: " It's just in the players to just fight their hearts out, to play, give it everything they have. That's the only way. That's the best way."
The entire press conference exchange is another shake to what is the Chargers' crumbling foundation. While it was shut down, there have already been talks of Mike McDaniel being fired , with that hot seat seemingly spreading to Jim Harbaugh. Simply put, the team is desperate for answers, and their leader has none.
Even with the hot seat beginning to heat up, it should be noted that Harbaugh's ability to motivate is highly respected throughout league circles, with former Chargers general manager Tom Telesco recently commenting on Daniel Jeremiah's podcast, Move the Sticks , "If you didn't have a head coach right now and you're like, 'We need someone to help us get out of this [the 0-4 start],' it'd probably be Jim Harbaugh." This belief is likely shared within the Chargers front office, making the Harbaugh exit as the Bolts' head coach a much longer wait than if he were someone else.

title: Chargers Stock Report: Three Players Rising and Two Falling After Week 5
full_text:
While the entire Los Angeles Chargers team is lacking any sort of excitement or hope for the team's chances of doing damage later in the season, it is still reasonable to look at some guys on the roster who may be impactful in the future or guys who will not stick around as they are not performing up to expectations.
Kimani Vidal was arguably the lone bright spot of the Chargers offense in Week 5. The team was down their top five wide receivers and was down to nearly an entire backup offensive line. Vidal, as the team's third RB, had an electric run that gave the Chargers one of their only highlights of the entire season.
Vidal had eight carries for 57 yards and a touchdown, coupled with a few nice blocks on Herbert scrambles, continuing to grow his trust in this offense.
Oronde Gadsden II is a talented tight end who has shown plenty of promise in his rookie season, but in Year 2, he has looked like a completely different player. He is not featured in the offense and is not someone who is seemingly making the same plays as before.
He is falling on this team, as he had one target for this entire game, even with the Chargers missing the majority of their receiver room.
Charlie Kolar returned in Week 5 after missing a few games with a forearm injury, making his impact known early. He made an impressive catch-and-run...that ended in a fumble. Which is obviously not a great look, but outside of this error, he helped the Chargers' running attack, making key blocks on the first and second levels of the defense. Kolar was the team's leading receiver with three catches for 37 yards.
Keaton Mitchell is still featured heavily in this Bolts' offense, garnering six carries for 11 yards and three receptions for 18 yards. While Mitchell has shown promise as a receiver, he has yet to have an elite chunk-run play, showing why the Chargers went out specifically to add him to their roster. His 1.8 yards per carry is simply not enough.
The final name on this list is Akheem Mesidor , the Chargers first-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. Mesidor has played well in his role as the team's EDGE3. He has shown immense effort and skill, collecting another sack and forced fumble in Week 5. He also led the team in tackles with eight. Look for Mesidor to continue rising, giving the team at least one player to build around for the 2027 NFL season.

title: Rams Are Running Out of Excuses as Special Teams Disaster Strikes Again in Overtime Loss to Bills
full_text:
It may as well have just been another day that ends in “y” for the Los Angeles Rams in their 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football. Last season, the Rams lined up for a 44-yard field goal to beat the Philadelphia Eagles. The kick was blocked and the Rams lost. On Monday night, Harrison Mevis lined up for a 48-yard field goal to beat the Bills from the same hash. The kick was blocked and five plays later the Bills kicked a game-winning field goal of their own.
The Rams put up 454 yards of total offense. Matthew Stafford threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns. While the defense didn’t play well, they got a timely turnover in overtime to give the Rams a chance to win. Once again, it was the special teams unit letting them down when it mattered most.
It’s been the common theme for the Rams going back to last season. Three losses can be pinned on special teams in 2025. Every week this year, the Rams have had some sort of special teams mistake. On Monday night, the game ended the same way it started. To open the game, the Rams allowed a 70-yard kickoff return. As it ended, it was the special teams failing to rise to the occasion.
Entering Week 5, the Rams needed a win to keep pace in the NFC West. With the San Francisco 49ers beating the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, they improved to 5-0. A loss to the Bills now puts the Rams 3.5 games behind the 49ers and below .500 for the third time this season.
Coming off of last week’s win against the Philadelphia Eagles, it felt like the Rams had turned a corner. When they drove 98 yards to start their 10-point comeback, it seemed like the offense had found something.
Some of that carried over into Monday night. While the Rams scored just seven first-half points, the offense was moving the ball. Mevis missed a 50-yard field goal, and a penalty stalled another promising drive. The Rams’ first two possessions combined for 28 plays and lasted 14:58. Stafford and Adams also connected in the red zone, displaying how difficult that duo is to defend in that area of the field.
Defensively, the Rams limited Allen and the Bills’ passing game for much of the night, with most of the big plays coming on screens and in the run game. However, the Bills’ 26th-ranked pass defense also managed to limit Stafford's explosiveness early. Stafford completed 16 of 23 passes for just 99 yards in the first half, with his longest completion going for only 12 yards. He was just 2-for-7 on passes beyond 10 yards as the Rams trailed, 13-7.
The Rams wasted little time getting going in the second half, scoring a touchdown on their opening possession and re-taking the lead. It was the first time all season that the Rams had scored on their opening drive of either half.
What started as a defensive battle ended in an offensive shootout. Despite previous inconsistency , Stafford came to life. To end regulation, the Rams and Bills traded six straight touchdown drives. When the Bills took a 19-14 lead, the Rams answered with a six-play, 83-yard touchdown drive of their own. The Rams’ offense struggled to find explosive plays in the first half, but it was a 28-yard pass to Tyler Higbee and then a Corum catch-and-run for 34 yards to set up a Stafford pass to Nacua in the end zone.
Nacua finished with a career-high 17 catches on 24 targets for 138 yards. Other Rams wide receivers combined for six catches for 55 yards. Nacua was the centerpiece of the offense.
After the Bills went 80 yards in five plays and converted a two-point conversion to take a 27-20 lead, the Rams answered again. On a day when the defense struggled to get a stop, the offense kept stepping up to the plate. Stafford hit Tyler Higbee on a no-look pass for 30 yards and then found Davante Adams in the end zone for his second touchdown of the day.
The Bills responded with another touchdown, scoring with 1:39 left to play and leaving the Rams with just one timeout. As Stafford has throughout his career, he rose to the occasion when the pressure was at its highest in the fourth quarter.
Stafford hit a 14-yard pass to Adams before hitting Nacua for 16. With another 15-yard completion to Adams, the Rams were already in the red zone with 47 seconds still left on the clock. On 3rd-and-7 from the nine-yard line, Stafford lasered a pass to Kyren Williams at the one-yard line before the Rams’ running back finished it on the next play with a run up the middle to tie the game at 34 with four seconds remaining.
While the Rams won the toss in overtime, they opted to kick to the Bills. Earlier in the game, linebacker Nate Landman forced a fumble on running back James Cook, but the Bills came out of the pile with the ball. After a 57-yard catch-and-run by Khalil Shakir, the Bills looked in position to score a seventh consecutive touchdown.
However, on the next play, Landman forced a second fumble, and this time it was the Rams’ defense that came away with the ball. It was Landman’s first forced fumble that resulted in a turnover since Week 11 of last season.
Given how the offense had moved the ball in the fourth quarter, the Rams looked to be in prime position to win. Stafford navigated the pocket to find Davis Allen for 21 yards and then hit Nacua for 21 two plays later.
Had McVay continued to call the offense as he had for the previous quarter, it’s hard to say that the Rams wouldn’t have eventually ended up with the ball in the end zone.However, from the 35-yard line, McVay called an under-center pass that went incomplete. On the next play, McVay called a screen to Nacua that went five yards. Facing 3rd-and-5 from the 30, McVay called a run play that gained zero yards.
Despite having a kicker who was 1-for-3 from 48 yards in his career and 4-for-7 beyond 45 yards, McVay got conservative and seemed content with a long field goal. Mevis had missed from 50 yards earlier in the game and from 48 yards last week against the Eagles.
For as aggressive as McVay has been at times over the last year, this was his former self taking over with the game on the line. Earlier in the game, the Rams went for it twice on fourth down, including a 4th-and-6. In large part because of the inconsistent field goal unit, McVay’s fourth-down decision-making has become more aggressive. Yet, while going for the win against the Bills on Monday, McVay’s conservative side took over and it was costly.
Greg Rousseau, who had been quiet most of the game, split through the line and blocked Mevis’ kick. After runs of 19 and 13 yards by Allen, the Bills were in field goal range. While Tyler Bass missed a long extra point earlier in the game, there was no doubt about his game-winner from 45.
With the loss to the Bills, the Rams now fall to 2-3. The Rams can certainly bounce back from this loss and could realistically sit at 7-3 at their bye week. At the same time, the Rams will undoubtedly feel a sense of major disappointment after letting this game slip away.
Until this team proves otherwise, it’s hard not to compare them to the 2010 Chargers, who had a top offense and defense but were plagued by special teams. We’re five weeks into the season and talking about special teams every single week. How many more games do the Rams have to lose because of special teams?
Do the Rams fire Bubba Ventrone five games into the season after hiring him? At this point, do the Rams make a change at kicker? One thing is certain and that’s that the Rams can’t continue going into games with this special teams unit and call it good. Simply saying “It needs to be better” is no longer good enough.
Coming into the season, very few would have expected the Rams to be sitting at 2-3 after five games. At this point, they are no different than the 2011 Philadelphia Eagles who entered the season as a “dream team” only to be a major disappointment.
Again, that’s not to say that this Rams team can’t turn it around. Myles Garrett will return to action and it’s possible that they find their stride. However, is this a hole that the Rams can get…

title: Rams Get Major Boost on Defense as Quentin Lake Officially Active vs. Bills
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to have safety Quentin Lake available on Monday night against the Buffalo Bills. Lake didn’t practice on Thursday and Friday and was a limited participant on Saturday before officially being listed as questionable for Monday’s game on the final injury report . However, despite questions about his availability, Lake is active for Monday night's game against the Buffalo Bills.
Lake missed Thursday and Friday’s practice with a hip injury. However, Rams head coach Sean McVay described it as a minor injury. When McVay spoke to the media on Saturday, he seemed optimistic about the possibility of Lake playing.
“I feel like he's turning in the right direction and feels good so that's a positive for us.”
Having Lake available will provide a huge boost for the Rams’ defense. Lake activates a lot of what the Rams want to do defensively because of his versatility. He is the only player on the Rams’ defense who has played 100 percent of the defensive snaps.
“We're just being smart with him,” said McVay this week as Lake missed practice. “He's played so many snaps. We just wanted to be smart.”
Through four weeks, Lake ranked second among safeties in impact plays with 12 according to Sumer Sports and led all safeties with seven pass breakups. He’s allowed 4.2 yards per target in coverage, which ranks 10th.
Heading into Week 4, Lake was the highest-graded safety according to Pro Football Focus with an overall defensive grade of 91.1. His 92.7 coverage grade was also the highest among all safeties.
Lake's versatility is what makes him such a valuable piece in the Rams’ defense. Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula calls a lot of multiple-safety looks and Lake allows them to do that. According to PFF, Lake has 67 snaps in the box, along with 71 snaps at free safety and 41 snaps in the slot. His versatility allows Shula to get Kam Curl, Kam Kinchens, and Lake all on the field at the same time.
The Rams will certainly appreciate having Lake in the secondary as they prepare to face one of the NFL's best quarterbacks in Josh Allen . Also expected back on Monday night is cornerback Jaylen Watson, who missed last week’s game with a dislocated shoulder.
While Lake is active, the Rams have listed CJ Daniels, tight end Max Klare, offensive lineman Bill Murray, and defensive lineman Larrell Murchison as inactive. Additionally, quarterback Ty Simpson is inactive, but will be the emergency third quarterback.
The Rams will need their defense at its best to slow down Allen and the Bills on Monday night. Having Lake available gives Shula more flexibility with his personnel and allows the Rams to deploy the multiple-safety looks that have been an important part of their defensive success this season.

title: Rams vs. Bills Position-by-Position Comparison: Where Each Team Has the Edge
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills are set to play in a highly anticipated matchup on Monday Night Football in Week 5. Both teams have had some inconsistencies through four weeks and will be looking to find some rhythm. Monday night presents an opportunity to make a statement against another Super Bowl contender. Here's how the Rams and Bills compare at every position and which team has the edge.
When Matthew Stafford and Josh Allen are playing their best, they are both top-five quarterbacks in the NFL. These are the 2024 and 2025 NFL MVPs. However, that has not been the case this season, especially for Stafford, who is off to a slow start . From a pure talent standpoint, these two players are pretty even. Based on the first four games, Allen has clearly been the better quarterback. Allen is fifth in EPA per play while Stafford is 18th. Advantage: Bills
Both Kyren Williams and James Cook have been two of the more underrated running backs in the NFL over the last few seasons. With that said, when both teams’ offenses are at their best, it’s usually because Williams and Cook are also getting involved. Williams and Cook are in the same running back tier, with Cook bringing a little more explosiveness. Still this is pretty even. Advantage: Even
The Bills have worked to get better at wide receiver, drafting Keon Coleman in the first round and trading for DJ Moore. However, Coleman hasn’t lived up to expectations and Moore has been hurt. The Rams will have the clear advantage here with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, especially going up against the Bills’ cornerbacks. Advantage: Rams
Over the past few seasons, the Bills have built their entire offense around their tight ends. Over half of their offense is run out of 12 and 13 personnel. The Rams lead the NFL in 13 personnel usage, but the Bills are right behind them. This might be closer if Terrance Ferguson were healthy, but Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox are a good tight end duo. It wouldn’t be surprising to see the Bills try to exploit the matchup with those two players against the Rams’ tight ends. Advantage: Bills
Neither of these units are necessarily elite, but they are both good enough to get the job done. Dion Dawkins has struggled at left tackle this season and the Rams have gotten by with Warren McClendon and Alaric Jackson. At the very least, these two units are even. Advantage: Even
The defensive line is arguably the biggest strength of both defenses. Deone Walker is having a great year for the Bills and could provide some problems on the interior for the Rams. Ed Oliver has been solid and Greg Rousseau led the NFL in sacks heading into Week 4. The Rams are getting Aaron Donald back , while Kobie Turner and Byron Young have played well this year. With Myles Garrett, the Rams would have the advantage. Right now, this is pretty even. Advantage: Even
The Rams likely won’t have an advantage at linebacker all season. It wouldn’t be surprising to see the Bills try to exploit the Rams’ linebackers and safeties in coverage with Kincaid and Knox. Advantage: Bills
The Rams will have a clear advantage in the secondary, especially if Quentin Lake plays. The Bills have had some injuries at cornerback, and that’s affected their pass defense significantly. Jaylen Watson should be back for the Rams as well. If the Rams can shut down the Bills’ wide receivers, McDuffie and Watson could make it very difficult for Allen. Advantage: Rams
The Rams continue to have special teams mistakes in every game . Meanwhile, the Bills rank seventh in special teams DVOA. Greg Dortch has some upside as a kick returner and Tyler Bass is one of the more consistent kickers in the NFL. Advantage: Bills
It’s very possible that Joe Brady becomes a good head coach. However, he’s still in his first season. Jim Leonhard has upside as a defensive coordinator, but his defense has been up-and-down through four weeks. This is where the Rams should have a clear edge. Advantage: Rams

title: Rams Monday Morning Rambling: The NFC West Is Already Slipping Away
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams enter Week 5, they sit at 2-2 and 2.5 games back in the NFC West after the San Francisco 49ers beat the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. It’s only Week 5, but it feels like unless the Rams can get a win on Monday night against the Bills , the division may already be slipping away from them.
Through four weeks, the Rams have yet to find any consistency. They already have a Week 1 loss to the now 5-0 49ers. Additionally, the 49ers have another leg up on the Rams after closing out their Week 4 game and getting a win against the Denver Broncos.
It’s true that the Rams will get healthier as Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson eventually return to the lineup.The Rams also play the 49ers again later in the season and will have an opportunity to avenge their loss.
At the same time, heading into the season, this isn’t necessarily where the Rams saw themselves. The Rams are no longer favored to win the NFC West. They are clearly behind the 49ers in that aspect. According to ESPN, the Rams have just a seven percent chance to win the division. The Athletic gives them a 20 percent chance, but that’s still well below the 49ers at 68 percent.
If the Rams beat the Bills on Monday night, that jumps to 24 percent, but those still aren't great odds. A loss would drop them to a 14 percent chance of winning the NFC West.
This isn’t to have a negative outlook on the Rams’ season, but it’s simply where they are. It’s Week 5, and if the Rams want to win the division, it’s going to be an uphill battle at this point. In the NFL, things can change rapidly.
Look no further than the NFC West last year. The Rams led most of the way and won an important Week 11 game against the Seahawks. Still, after Week 5, both teams were 3-2 and the Seahawks never fell out of reach. That’s the danger that the Rams are in right now with the 49ers at 5-0.
That’s not to say that the Rams can’t win the Super Bowl without winning the division, but it would make their path a lot more difficult. Yes, the Rams added Garrett and Trent McDuffie to help in December and January. However, it was also to help make their path to the Super Bowl easier.
Since the NFL expanded to seven playoff teams in each conference, only three non-division winners have made the conference championship game and none of them have gone to the Super Bowl.
It happened fewer than a handful of times under the six-team format and hasn't happened since the most recent playoff expansion. No matter the format, winning three road playoff games is hard. Had last year’s NFC Championship game been played at SoFi Stadium, the result may have been different.
Again, the Rams made the moves that they did this offseason to help make the path easier. Stafford hasn’t lost a home playoff game. Stafford won his first road playoff games of his career last year and is 2-6. That’s not necessarily a bad record. Peyton Manning was 2-5 in the playoffs on the road. In all three Super Bowls he made, his teams had home-field advantage.
Winning one road playoff game is difficult. Doing that three times in a row is extremely difficult and that was evident last year when that was the path that the Rams would have had to take. Yes, they got very close to doing it. At the same time, it’s not a path that’s necessarily viable. When the Rams won the Super Bowl in 2021, they had to win just one road playoff game.
Again, this isn’t to say that the Rams don’t have a chance or their season is already over. Still, it shows the importance of needing to win on Monday night against the Bills to keep pace with the 49ers. They can’t continue to fall behind.
Coming into the season, the Rams and Bills were a popular Super Bowl matchup and that might still be the case for some after four weeks. Neither team has truly found its rhythm yet, but it feels like only a matter of time. When the Rams and Bills have played over the last few years, it has typically come with a dramatic finish. In 2024, the Rams narrowly escaped 44-42 after leading 38-21 entering the fourth quarter. Not many would be disappointed if these two teams played again in February.
This will be a matchup between the last two MVPs. With many recent MVPs coming from one conference, this isn’t as rare as some might think. In fact, it happened just last year in Week 1 as Josh Allen and the Bills beat Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens 41-40. This isn’t as common between AFC and NFC MVPs.
It should have happened in 2023, but Aaron Rodgers left the Green Bay Packers for the New York Jets and then got hurt in Week 1 before he would have played Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. This should have happened again in 2021, but Lamar Jackson was hurt when the Ravens played the Packers.The last time it happened was in 2015 when Peyton Manning and the Broncos played Rodgers and the Packers. Manning and the Broncos won that game, 29-10.
There has been a lot of talk in 2026 about NFL offenses transitioning to more 13 personnel and heavier tight end sets. No two teams have leaned into this more than the Rams and Bills. The Rams lead the NFL with a 13 personnel usage rate of 31 percent. Behind them are the Bills at 26 percent. Whichever team has more success with multiple tight ends will likely win Monday night’s game.
This isn’t to say that Kyren Williams has been underrated, but the step he’s taken toward becoming a more complete running back this season hasn’t been discussed enough. Williams became the first Rams running back last week since Todd Gurley to have at least 10 rushing attempts and 10 receptions in the same game. Williams has been one of the best all-around running backs this season and without Stafford playing well and Puka Nacua missing some time, he’s been the engine of the offense.
Through most of the first four weeks, the Rams’ passing game has lacked some consistency. It hasn’t necessarily struggled as the Rams rank second in passing yards per game. However, the EPA and success rate tell a different story.
With Matthew Stafford’s turnovers , the Rams rank 18th in EPA per pass. Their 48.5 percent passing success rate ranks ninth and is behind the New York Jets. They should have a chance on Monday night to find something. The Bills have some injuries at cornerback and rank 26th in EPA per pass allowed and 28th in pass defense success rate.
The NFC West had a busy weekend. On Saturday morning, it was reported that the Arizona Cardinals were trading away wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. It wasn’t confirmed which team until Sunday afternoon when it was announced that the team he was being traded to was the Houston Texans. That’s notable as the Rams play the Cardinals next week.
Additionally, the 49ers and Seahawks played one of the better games of the season.The Seahawks turned the ball over three times in the first half, leading to 21 first-half points for the 49ers. While they clawed back, they came up just short on a controversial call on 4th-and-10. The Seahawks went to the Super Bowl last season, despite having a -3 turnover differential. They were 6-3 in games in which they turned the ball over two or more times. Both games that the Seahawks have lost this season, they’ve struggled with turnovers.
A Seahawks win would have been good for the Rams as the 49ers now sit at 5-0 and are in complete control of the NFC West. They are 3-0 in division games and have looked like the best team in the NFL. If the Rams aren’t careful, the 49ers could start to pull away.

title: Sunday Morning Rams Notebook: Sean McVay Linked to Amazon, Myles Garrett Update, and More
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams enter Week 5 looking to build some momentum after their comeback victory over the Philadelphia Eagles. At 2-2, the Rams have an opportunity to get above .500 for the first time this season when they host the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football.
Several stories have emerged this week that are worth exploring further, including Myles Garrett’s return timeline and whether the Rams will be a team to watch ahead of the trade deadline. Let’s get into this week’s Sunday Morning Rams Notebook
It seems as if almost every year there is some speculation around Sean McVay leaving coaching and going into broadcasting. The door opened once again recently when details emerged from the new contract that Kirk Herbstreit signed with Amazon Prime.
According to Andrew Marchand from The Athletic , there is a clause in Herbstreit’s contract that would allow the network to move on from him if Sean McVay were to become available.
“The terms give Amazon flexibility to move on if one of its top targets, like Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay, becomes available, according to sources briefed on the decision who were not authorized to speak publicly,” wrote Marchand.
There is some history with McVay and Amazon Prime. Back in 2022, Prime tried to recruit McVay after the Rams went 5-12 and had a disastrous season. According to Marchand, Al Michaels preferred McVay over Herbstreit. However, McVay signed a new contract with the Rams and has remained with the team for the last four seasons.
With that said, McVay was close to leaving coaching for media after the 2022 season.McVay said this himself last year when he went on “Bussin’ With the Boys .”
"I almost quit coaching," McVay said. "And you can use the narrative that I was gonna go to media or whatever. But the truth would have been, I was quitting. I couldn't handle the losing. It was almost like a scarlet letter. I mean, there was moments…I was like counting down the days for that season to be over. Like, what a fraud."
There is some speculation that McVay won’t coach forever. He’s only 40 years old and has been coaching for 10 years. McVay has two kids with his wife Veronika Khomyn, and it’s possible that he leaves coaching at some point to get a better work-life balance.
Still, that doesn’t seem imminent, and the clause in Herbstreit’s contract appears to be more about the network protecting itself and maintaining flexibility. It’s possible that McVay leaves at some point. He could potentially tie himself to Matthew Stafford and leave once the Rams’ quarterback retires.
Mike Sando from The Athletic noted that some who know McVay suspect from afar that something has been bothering him this season. At the same time, with McVay’s input, the Rams just drafted a rookie quarterback in April to take over for Stafford. All of the McVay in the media rumors remain speculation at this point.
McVay was supposed to have an update for the media on Myles Garrett on Thursday, but didn’t. The result was some panic that the Rams were hiding more information than they were letting on when it came to Garrett. It was an understandable conclusion given how the Rams have handled the injury since July.
This trade has been a disaster for the Rams. https://t.co/VdXC1OzpJQ
However, McVay’s tone on Thursday when it was brought up was that he genuinely forgot. There were three days between McVay’s first media availability this week on Monday and when he spoke again on Thursday. The Rams’ head coach came ready with an update during Saturday’s media availability .
“He’s making good progress, but what I will say is he's not ready to say whether we'll open that window or not,” said McVay. “It's week to week in terms of how he feels, but I would say it's more likely that we do not start his clock next week.”
McVay stressed the importance of not just putting Garrett in a position to play, but in a position to return to performance. In Week 1, Garrett was in a position to play, but after the game he told the media that he didn’t feel like himself. The Rams will continue playing it safe with Garrett, which is how they’ve generally handled the situation since July.
While Garrett is eligible to return to practice next week ahead of the Rams’ game against the Arizona Cardinals, it doesn’t appear that he will. If you’ve followed our coverage here on Rams On SI, that shouldn’t come as a surprise.
A few weeks ago, it was reported by NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport that Garrett was given a six-week timeline following his arthroscopic knee surgery. However, last week, Jonathan Jones of The Athletic r eported that Garrett could return for Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders.
Since the beginning, Garrett has been determined to beat the timeline, but that doesn’t mean the Rams aren’t going to continue erring on the side of caution. Four weeks always seemed optimistic, with five weeks being more realistic, and six weeks being a worst-case scenario.
We’ll have to wait and see what happens with Garrett, but waiting another week to open his practice window provides the Rams with more flexibility. It wouldn’t be surprising to see the Rams open his practice window ahead of the game against the Raiders, see how his knee responds, and then decide whether to activate him to the roster. Much like with Aaron Donald on the Commissioner’s Exempt List to begin the season, the Rams have some flexibility.
The NFL trade deadline is about a month away, but don’t expect the Rams to make any big splashes. Unless the situation drastically changes, it would be a surprise if they made a significant move. There are two main reasons for this, along with how the Rams’ front office and coaching staff may view their situation.
After signing Eric Kendricks to the practice squad this week, the Rams only have around $981k. That’s almost half as much as the next closest team. That little cap space makes it very difficult for the Rams to do anything via trade. It might not even be possible for the Rams to make it through the rest of the season on that number. At some point, they may have to rework a contract to open up some cap space, but their current financial situation makes a trade unlikely.
Additionally, the Rams don’t have the draft capital available to make a big trade. While the Rams have a second-round pick in 2027, if they were to move that, they wouldn’t pick until the fourth round. It’s possible they could look to move picks in 2028 like the Baltimore Ravens did when they acquired Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles last week. However, the Rams don’t have a second-round pick, and moving their first would put them in a difficult spot.
It’s possible the Rams don’t see their roster in a spot where they need to make a trade to get over the top. The front office and coaching staff will likely see Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson returning from injured reserve as in-season additions.
An argument can be made that the Rams need a third wide receiver, but they will see Ferguson as a player to fill that role in the offense. This isn’t to say that a trade won’t happen or that the Rams won’t explore anything. However, it does remain unlikely.
Earlier this week, Mike Ditka passed away at the age of 86. While I never got the pleasure of meeting Ditka, he was a big part of my NFL Sundays growing up. I remember watching Mike Ditka on ESPN’s Sunday NFL Countdown, which was a must-watch for me on Sunday mornings. I’ll always remember Ditka as a no-nonsense personality who wasn’t afraid to speak what was on his mind.

title: Rams Week 5 Injury Report: Aaron Donald Among Three Starters Set to Return vs. Bills
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to get multiple starters back as they head into Week 5 to take on the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football. After missing last week, tight end Colby Parkinson, cornerback Jaylen Watson, and defensive lineman Aaron Donald all look to be ready to go for Monday’s game. The only player with a game designation on Saturday’s injury report was safety Quentin Lake, who is listed as questionable.
Lake didn’t practice on Thursday or Friday with a hip injury, but was upgraded to limited on Saturday. There wasn’t too much concern with Lake this week with the Rams just being smart with him given his workload this season.
“He got it when he fell backwards on something so it's a weird deal, but he's doing good,” said McVay this week. “We're just being smart with him. He's played so many snaps. We just wanted to be smart.”
Edge rusher Josaiah Stewart also didn’t practice earlier in the week, but was limited on Saturday. Stewart wasn’t given a game designation and presumably will be good to play. The same can be said about linebacker Nate Landman, who has been banged up over the last couple of weeks. Landman was a full participant on Saturday.
While Donald didn’t practice on Saturday, that has been his routine this season. All indications are that Donald will play. Speaking to the media this week, Donald said, “I'm planning to play this week.”
The Rams missed Colby Parkinson last week, as they were unable to utilize their usual 13 personnel packages with three tight ends. Without Parkinson, the Rams utilized 11 personnel at an 88 percent rate , which was their highest since Week 5 of last season. Cornerback Jaylen Watson is also set to make his return. Josh Wallace played well in his absence, but getting Watson back will provide a big boost to the Rams’ secondary.
“They're good to go," McVay said.
On the Bills’ side, defensive lineman Ed Oliver and wide receiver Joshua Palmer have already been ruled out. The Rams will certainly be watching the status of wide receiver DJ Moore before Monday’s game. Moore is officially listed as questionable along with defensive lineman Landman Jackson and cornerback Dee Alford.
The Rams have struggled to find consistency through the first four weeks of the season, but getting healthier should help as they look to build on last week's win over the Eagles. With Donald, Parkinson, and Watson expected to return, the Rams will have several key pieces back in place for one of their toughest matchups of the season.
