title: Rams Coaches Detail Biggest Challenges of Facing Josh Allen and Bills
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams a re set to take on the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 5. Heading into the season, both teams were seen as Super Bowl contenders. It wouldn’t be surprising if this ended up being the Super Bowl matchup when all is said and done.
However, heading into Week 5, both teams are still trying to find their rhythm. The Bills are 3-1, but haven’t played well the last two weeks. They turned the ball over five times and somehow still managed to beat the Los Angeles Chargers. Meanwhile, the Rams have been up and down and have yet to get above .500. A win on Monday night could propel either team into a winning streak.
Throughout the week, the Rams’ coaching staff and players have spoken about some of the challenges that the Bills will present.
When the Rams and Bills played in 2024, Josh Allen threw for 342 yards and three touchdowns as he went on to win MVP. Allen not only has one of the best arms in the NFL, but he’s also a great athlete with the ability to make plays with his legs.
Allen has 1,039 yards passing this season to go with six touchdowns and three interceptions. His 0.18 EPA per play ranks fifth in the NFL. While the Rams have the No. 2 overall pass defense, Allen will provide a good test. Over the last three weeks, the Rams have faced Jameis Winston, Bo Nix, and Jalen Hurts. Allen will give the Rams their biggest test since playing Brock Purdy in Week 1.
“You can see he's obviously one of the ultimate competitors in this league,” said defensive coordinator Chris Shula. “He's a great quarterback standing there playing in the pocket. Then, you can see all the off-schedule plays that he makes. He's one of the best players, if not the best player, in the NFL right now.”
The Rams are set to get Aaron Donald back against the Bills as well, which should help against Allen.. Donald missed last week with a sore back, but is set to return for Monday night’s game against the Bills.
Donald has played against the Bills three times, but only twice has he faced Josh Allen. In 2022, the Rams lost to the Bills 31-10 in the season opener. Donald had one sack in that game. In 2020, Donald had a vintage performance, recording two sacks with a forced fumble and fumble recovery.
“He's a playmaker,” said Donald. “He's a different type of player. I call him a futuristic ‘Big Ben’, more athletic, harder to tackle, a lot faster, able to move a lot differently. He can hurt you in a lot of different ways. He's not easy to take down. He's a playmaker. That's all you can say. You have to find ways to keep him in the box, make sure when you get your hands on him, make sure you get him down to the ground. Don’t let him stiff arm you and be able to look downfield and throw a touchdown. He’s a guy that you have to worry about and have to try to find a way to affect [him].”
Back in 2020, the Rams previously had interest in Jim Leonhard, but ended up hiring Brandon Staley instead. Leonhard spent the last two years on the Denver Broncos’ coaching staff before he was brought in as the defensive coordinator for the Bills this offseason under Joe Brady.
The Bills currently rank 29th in defensive EPA and have especially struggled against the pass. They’ve allowed 0.11 EPA per pass, which ranks 26th in the NFL. Over the first four weeks of the season, the Rams have struggled to find some consistency in the passing game . Playing the Bills could provide them with an opportunity to get things back on track.
“I have a lot of respect for him, his career, his background, type of mentality that he has in general,” said Rams offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase. “You can see that all over their defense with their ability to challenge you with different looks, their ability to move guys into different spots and honestly have an attacking style. They do a great job up front. Their front makes their squad go. If you don't take care of those guys both in the run game and in the pass game, you can end up in some tough spots. As much as you can, you want to stay on track and not let those guys be able to set a rush and be able to pin their ears back.”
If the Rams are going to win this game, they’ll need their top two wide receivers in Davante Adams and Puka Nacua to step up and play well. With Nacua out of the lineup in Weeks 2 and 3, Adams played like he was in his prime, recording back-to-back 100 yard games. The Rams have yet to get both players going in the same game this season.
Last week, Romeo Doubs had success with the New England Patriots when facing off against Maxwell Hairston.Doubs scored two touchdowns on Hairston, and the Rams may try to get a similar matchup with Adams. However, this will be Adams’ first time facing a defense coordinated by Leonhard, and he spoke about that challenge on Friday.
“Watching as much tape as possible, whether that's stuff that they've done against us, this season, or things that they've done in the past,” said Adams. “Also, not getting too wrapped up in that because come gametime, you have to react to the coverages or whatever they decide to throw at you. You can get immersed in everything and think you have it figured out, but you still have to react once the call is made and once the play starts. I like to have a decent idea of what they like to do. Then go and roll with the punches from there during the game.”

title: Rams Midweek Report: Searching for Consistency, Myles Garrett Update, Trade Deadline Outlook
full_text:
A big theme this week for the Los Angeles Rams has been whether they can find some consistency . The Rams have the No. 2 offense and No. 2 defense, but the 32nd-ranked special teams unit. They have a top-five offense but are just 19th in points per game. They have a top-5 offense, but are just 19th in points per game.
If the Rams are going to become the team that many expected coming into the season, they need to find consistency. This is a team that’s been penalized 21 times over the last two weeks, the most in a two-game stretch under head coach Sean McVay. They have a -5 turnover differential through four games, which is tied for 28th in the NFL. Untimely turnovers, penalties, and special teams gaffes have been a recurring problem for this team.
“I'm interested to see how we can play cleaner football,” said McVay on Monday. “We have to play better. We have to consistently do it in all three phases and we have to earn the right to play better quality football. We have to all coach better too.”
The Rams are doing things that we aren’t accustomed to seeing from a McVay-coached team. That’s what makes the penalties and untimely mistakes so baffling at times . McVay can become pass-happy at times, but over 100 pass attempts in a two-game stretch is unheard of even for him. Sunday marked the first time since 2012 that Stafford had 50 or more attempts in back-to-back games.
Through four weeks, Matthew Stafford has an EPA per pass of -0.01. At this time last year, it was 0.15. Stafford starting the season slowly is nothing unusual, but his mistakes have cost the Rams in big moments or put them in difficult positions.
“Definitely room for improvement. There have been some really bright moments and some stuff I'm really proud of and stuff that I definitely wish I could take back to help us be in a better position to win games,” said Stafford. “I want to do everything I can to put our team in the best position to succeed. I've done that sometimes this year and other times I have not. I want to make sure that I do that at a more consistent clip moving forward.”
Given that teams no longer play their starters in the preseason, there is some belief that it can take those first three or four weeks for starters to get up to speed. The Rams have now played four games. There are no more excuses.
Coming into the season, this was a team with high expectations, and they have yet to really play up to that level. A lot of that is because of the lack of consistency. After coming back from 10 points in the fourth quarter against the Philadelphia Eagles, the Rams seemed to find something. They’ll have a chance on Monday night to show whether they can carry that over or if it was just another flash in the pan.
"It's that time of the year where you're establishing your identity both schematically and the mentality that you play with," said offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase. "There are things that we can do to take care of stuff that we can control so that's been an area of emphasis for us, especially this week."
Prior to the season, the Rams placed a pair of offensive linemen in Keagen Trost and Justin Dedich on injured reserve. Trost injured his hamstring in the first preseason game and Dedich managed a hand injury all summer. With the Rams having played four games, both players are eligible to come off of injured reserve . However, it doesn’t appear as if the Rams are in any rush to do so.
“Those guys, they could,” said McVay. “We could open that up, but that's not a conversation that we've had at this point.”
It makes sense for the Rams to hold off for now, as both players are depth pieces and not immediate starters. The Rams only have eight injured reserve return designations to use and they are already set to use two on Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson. There’s a chance one or both are activated at some point, but given the current health of the offensive line, the Rams are waiting.
McVay was asked on Thursday whether Garrett will return to practice after his four-week injured reserve window. Monday night will mark Garrett’s fourth game that he’s missed and he’ll be eligible to return.
“I'm not sure yet,” said McVay. “I know that the rehab is progressing well. He's looked good in the meetings.”
The Rams’ head coach had previously mentioned that he would have more of an update, but that was not the case on Thursday. With that said, based on reports that exist , the Rams remain hopeful that Garrett will return next week, but Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders is more realistic. Garrett had a six-week timeline, which would have put him on track to return in Week 8 against the Los Angeles Chargers, but that was more of a worst-case scenario. Garrett has been progressing ahead of that.
Prior to Sunday’s game against the Eagles, the Rams placed Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve . Just when Ferguson was starting to have a positive impact on the offense and become a featured piece, a medial ankle sprain has forced him to miss time.
Ferguson will have to miss four games, which would put his return in Week 8 against the Chargers. Based on what McVay said on the Coach McVay Show this week with JB Long, it doesn’t seem like Ferguson will miss any more time beyond that.
“He’ll be back. He’ll be ready to go after those four weeks,” McVay said.
I wouldn’t expect the Rams to be active at the trade deadline. That doesn’t mean they won’t make a move, but it would be very difficult for them to do anything significant. It’s possible the Rams will see Myles Garrett’s return and getting Terrance Ferguson back as in-season additions.
There are a few things to note here. The Rams currently only have around $981,000 in cap space. That’s by far the lowest in the NFL. It would be nearly impossible for them to take on another contract at that number. TThe Rams also don’t have a lot of draft capital to send away. They don’t have a first- or third-round pick next year. If they moved that second-round pick, they wouldn’t select until the fourth round. Additionally, they don’t have a second-round pick in 2028. While the Rams could use a third wide receiver, it just isn’t something that will be in the cards.
It’s certainly possible that the Rams will beat the Bills on Monday night . The Bills are dealing with injuries in the secondary, which will provide the Rams an opportunity to get something going in the passing game. However, the Bills are coming off of a loss last week and will be ready to play a clean game.
A loss to the Bills isn’t the worst thing. That would put the Rams at 2-3 with two of their three losses against AFC opponents. The Rams can ‘get right’ against the Cardinals in Week 6 and then the schedule lightens up. It’s possible the Rams could rattle off six straight wins before playing the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 13. A Week 14 matchup against the 49ers will then provide an opportunity to avenge their loss in Week 1.
The Rams signed Eric Kendricks this week, which came as a bit of a surprise. While some have speculated that Kendricks is a special teams addition, it may have been more than that. Some of Kendricks’ early role may come on special teams. The Rams have already used two of Eli Neal’s three roster elevations. Grant Stuard is also dealing with an injury this week.
However, at 34, Kendricks likely wouldn’t have signed on simply to play special teams. He’s beyond that point of his career. His addition will give the Rams some flexibility to manage Nate Landman’s injury if needed, while also allowing Kendricks to rotate in alongside Omar Speights. He may have a bigger role once he settles in.

title: 5 Keys to Victory for the Rams Against the Bills in Week 5
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to host the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium on Monday Night Football in Week 5. With a win, the Rams could get above .500 for the first time this season . Over the first month, the Rams have been scrapping to get by, and Monday night will provide a good test against a team many consider to be a Super Bowl contender. Here are five keys to victory for the Rams to beat the Bills.
Under Joe Brady, the Buffalo Bills have had their most successful run game under Josh Allen. James Cook has a 52.9 percent rushing success rate. Cook’s 11.4 percent explosive run rate is also the highest in the NFL.
For the Rams defense to operate the way it wants to, stopping the run is key. It’s something that they didn’t do in Week 1. However, over the last three weeks, they’ve been much better. Their -0.2 EPA per rush allowed in that span ranks sixth in the NFL. The Rams need to be able to contain James Cook and limit the explosive runs. That will also limit what the Bills can do in the passing game with their tight ends in heavy personnel.
Last week, Kyren Williams became the first Rams running back since Todd Gurley to have at least 10 carries and 10 receptions in a game. The Rams have struggled to find a third wide receiver in the offense with Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve. It’s possible that Williams can be that third option in the passing game.
The Bills could provide another opportunity to get Williams involved. Defensively, the Bills have allowed the third-most targets to running backs with 21 receptions. Their 162 receiving yards allowed to running backs are the seventh-most and they’ve allowed three receiving touchdowns. This is an area where Williams showed last week that he can be a threat in this area, and the Rams may need him to contribute again.
For as solid as the Bills have been at tackle in the past, that hasn’t been the case this year. Dion Dawkins allowed a seven percent pressure rate last year and that’s up to 12 percent in 2026. For the most part, Dawkins has struggled this season.
#Patriots rookie Gabe Jacas's bull-rush puts five-time Pro Bowl LT Dion Dawkins on the ground. pic.twitter.com/8Wu10Z0Tle
This is a matchup that the Rams will have to win if they’re going to have a chance in this game. Byron Young has one of the highest pressure rates at 18.8 percent among edge rushers. That ranks 10th in the NFL. He also ranks eighth with 18 pressures. Without Myles Garrett, the Rams need Young to continue taking over games as he did last week.
The Bills have struggled at cornerback this season as they’ve dealt with some injuries. However, it’s also just not a position group that’s played well. The Rams should have the advantage here throughout the game. Puka Nacua returned from injury last week, but the Rams will also need Davante Adams to play like he did in Weeks 2 and 3.
If the Rams can get Adams isolated against Maxwell Hairston a few times, that’s a matchup they can take advantage of and find success with. Romeo Doubs scored two touchdowns against Hairston last week. The Rams haven’t gotten the connection between Stafford and Adams going in the red zone yet this season. Monday night could provide an opportunity.
When in doubt, attack Maxwell Hairston. He’s been horrible Bench him. Put in Kani Walker pic.twitter.com/MW1ELJHLKq
For as much as fans will want the Rams to play man coverage, that’s simply not something they can do against Josh Allen. Allen has the ability to scramble for large gains, which are effective against man. Against man coverage, Allen has a 0.36 EPA per play, which is the sixth-best in the NFL. Against zone coverage, that drops by more than half to 0.17.
This isn’t to say that the Rams should stay away from man coverage altogether. However, Chris Shula will need to mix up his coverages and do so selectively. He’ll need to pick his spots and do the same when he opts to blitz. This will be a good test for Shula and the defense, who haven’t faced a true challenge since playing the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1.

title: Matchups the Rams Must Win to Beat the Bills on Monday Night Football
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams play the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in what should be one of the best games of the week. When these two teams have gotten together in the past, it usually comes down to a dramatic finish. Two of the last three games have been decided by three points or less. Here are three matchups that could decide the game between the Rams and Bills.
This season, the Rams have averaged 1.5 yards before contact in the run game, which is the sixth-most in the NFL. However, when Deone Walker is on the field for the Bills, teams have averaged 0.1 yards before contact compared to 1.8 when he’s not on the field. Walker has been a key piece on the Bills’ defense, and they are much better when he’s on the field. On all plays, the Bills average 5.2 yards per play compared to 6.2 when he’s off it.
Deone Walker lol I'm not fully convinced he knows what he's doing on a down-to-down basis... but this dude is massive and athletic lol some straight freakazoid reps pic.twitter.com/WM4b45MrHY
If the Rams are going to get the most out of Matthew Stafford on Monday, they need to be able to remain balanced in the run game. They also need to protect the pocket. That starts with Coleman Shelton, Steve Avila, and Kevin Dotson against Walker. Walker’s 20 impact plays rank third in the NFL among interior defensive linemen.
It’s no secret that the weakness of the Rams’ defense is at linebacker. The Bills utilize heavy tight end sets more than any other team in the NFL. This season, the Bills have utilized 12 personnel on 20 percent of their offensive snaps and 13 personnel on 26 percent of their offensive snaps. Out of 12 personnel, the Bills rank third with 0.31 offensive EPA per play.
While Dalton Kincaid may not be a featured piece of the Bills’ offense, when he gets involved, he can be successful in the pass game. The Bills could have a huge matchup advantage here with Kincaid against Omar Speights, who can struggle in coverage. Speights has allowed 1.51 yards per coverage snap this season, which ranks as the eighth-most in the NFL. Both of the Rams’ linebackers are better in the run game.
The Rams will need to be ready on the offensive line as the Bills have the personnel up front to take over a game. Despite having to throw more than 100 times over the last two weeks, the Rams have done well from a protection standpoint. The Rams held one of the better pass rushes in the NFL in check two weeks ago against the Denver Broncos. The Bills will provide another challenge.
NFL sack leaders through Week 4 Greg Rousseau        6.0 Dallas Turner            5.5 T.J. Watt                      4.5 Will Anderson Jr.     4.5 Mason Graham       4.0 pic.twitter.com/IcCI3R05IF
This season, the Bills have a 45.8 percent pressure rate, which is the fourth-highest in the NFL. It’s a group led by Greg Rousseau. His 24 pressures rank fourth in the NFL, despite him facing the sixth-most double teams. He also leads the NFL with six sacks. Warren McClendon has been good, but he certainly has his deficiencies.

title: One Raider Shined in Patriots Loss: Find Out Who Stood Out
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (3-2) looked terrible in a 45-17 blowout loss to the New England Patriots (3-2) on Sunday.
To say that nearly nothing went right would be correct. While some players did perform well, and I will discuss that in my weekly report card, to call it anything other than a bludgeoning would be disingenuous to the reader and simply journalistic malfeasance. I detailed that in my winners and losers article.
Early this morning, a Raiders player contacted me. They had seen the video I posted of Klint Kubiak’s postgame press conference, and it moved them.
“Thanks for KK [Klint Kubiak’s] press conference after the game. That guy is the real deal man. We let him down, but he owned it in that, I love playing for him.”
After years of Raiders coaching fanning accountability and quietly throwing shade at everyone but themselves, the overachieving first-year head coach didn’t do so.
I have told you for months that as a reporter I appreciate Kubiak’s honesty.
He has been marvelous as the leader of the Silver and Black; the only shocking thing about Sunday was how long it took this team to perform that badly. The fact that we were even considering that they might have flipped the script to talking about the NFL Playoffs is nothing short of amazing.
Missing players at key positions, thin at others, and young nearly everywhere, the Raiders' head man stepped to the microphone and pulled no punches.
“It's on me to get us ready to go, and we weren't ready to go.”
The NFL was watching, and they paid close attention.
One highly successful NFL executive called me shortly after I got off the plane this morning. I called him on my way to the facility, and he told me, “You could see Klint was livid, embarrassed, and he was mad at himself.”
I told him about the player’s comments. He wasn’t shocked.
“Just like his dad man. That is integrity, those guys [Raiders Players] will run through a wall for him when you do that. High class move by him.”
I asked Kubiak today about the message he sent to his locker room. The steely-jawed leader of the Silver Black answered resolutely to a locker room that hangs on his every word.
"Well, I just think that if guys know what to expect from you that you're the same guy, whether you win or you lose, at least that's what I try to be; I'm not saying that I'm successful at that, but that's what I want from others to be consistent."
"Some of that you can count on, hold someone to a standard, and if it's not there, tell you the truth. If it is there, tell you, 'Good job'. But however you handle something, win or loss, the goal is to win the game. And we did not win yesterday, and we have a long season ahead of us, and we have big goals."
After the butt-kicking the Raiders took on Sunday, many people might be shocked to see Kubiak emerge as a shining example of the Raiders' promising future. But here is what you have to understand.
Every player in that locker room who failed on Sunday, and it was many of them, and every coach who failed, and it was many of them, knew coming into the season that this was a rebuild.
To use the proverbial Vegas term, they were playing with house money for one reason: Kubiak.
Kubiak had willed this team to 3-1. They trust him. They believe in him.
They saw him celebrate some terrific wins, and on Sunday they saw the same reaction to getting humiliated. They saw him step to the microphone, and while technically speaking to millions across the NFL pantheon, he was really talking to his players and coaches.
He took the blame. He should have. But several men here should have, in the past, and didn’t. He took the heat; took the blame, and he led from the front.
Anyone who knows anything about football knew what this season was from the start. If you didn’t know, you either haven’t followed my reporting since last December, or you were caught up in the ether of overachieving. Tom Brady, John Spytek, and Kubiak are cutting no corners. This was and is a rebuild.
Coaching the Raiders isn’t easy. Arguably the biggest name in NFL history, Al Davis, looms over this storied franchise. Icons like John Madden and Tom Flores coached here. To say that Kubiak is one of them would be ludicrous and insulting to both Kubiak and those men.
They are the standard that he has set for himself, but he is off to a great start.
After only eight months, to say he has the same character and mentality as those men is not hyperbole, and it is promising. More promising and realistic than the Raiders have had in a long time.
The Raiders are so much better than last year, but they still have a long way to go before they hoist their next Lombardi Trophy. But they know they have their leader.
No off-the-record finger-pointing, no quiet excuses; like a general, the Raiders' young coach stepped up and led.
The Raiders aren’t winning a Super Bowl in 2026. That should surprise no one. But they have found their leader. They have found the anchor of their foundation.
Klint Kubiak is a lot of things, but as one Raiders player put it, “That guy is 100% for f---ing real. That’s my motherf---ing coach.”
He’s your coach, Raider Nation.
He emerged from a terrible loss, leading the Silver and Black out of the smoke and the haze from the front.
I do not know his father, but I do know what he stood for and did. He raised his son in his image. Kubiak lived up to his father’s stellar reputation as a leader of men.
Make no mistake, he is his own man, a Raider man. He’s your man, Raider Nation.
The loss stunk for Raider Nation, but it gave all of us, fan or not, a glimpse of your future.
There will be more tough losses this year, but the balm is that there will be much bigger wins in the future, and more of those than these.
Future free agents love to play for winners, and Kubiak proved that in his worst loss.
If steel is forged in fire, then count Sunday as an inferno.
But out of that inferno, Kubiak showed something tangible, real, and valuable. He has what it takes to lead this rebuild and to take this franchise where it needs to go.
Players won’t magically appear on the roster tomorrow; they'll arrive as these young players develop and mature, and as free agents and future NFL Draft picks are added.
But you have your coach. Finally, and he is a good one. There will be more fires, but the fire he just led his team through should have burned away the doubts. Now, back to the Raiders rebuild.

title: Grading Every Raiders Position Group After Week 5 Loss
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders had a forgettable Week 5 road performance against the New England Patriots. Essentially, everything that could go wrong did, from the very start. Still, the Raiders are in the early stages of a rebuild, which has been clear and will remain so.
Las Vegas' Week 5 matchup against the Patriots was the second game in a handful of games against some of the best teams in the league. Las Vegas will follow up losses against the Kansas City Chiefs and New England Patriots with games against the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams.
Las Vegas is about where most expected them to be at this point in its first season under Klint Kubiak. If anything, they are still ahead of schedule after two consecutive games against top teams. Few expected Las Vegas to be this far along yet.
Below are the grades for each Raiders position group based on their respective Week 5 performances.
What you see is what you are going to get from Kirk Cousins for the rest of the season. The first three games of the season were the ceiling with Cousins under center, which is more than they have had in the last three seasons.
The Raiders' two most recent games are what they will be against top teams with Cousins under center, and likely if Fernando Mendoza takes over. The roster has issues that need both experience and mobility from their play caller.
Cousins has experience; Mendoza has mobility; neither has both. The veteran will continue to start for at least the foreseeable future. However, Mendoza's lone drive against the Patriots, albeit in a blowout and against a much less aggressive defense than Cousins faced, is a glimpse into the future.
Mendoza had the same supporting cast Cousins did, and the offense looked much smoother during his few plays. With Mendoza in, it seemed that even if the pocket broke down, he had the chance to make a play.
His passes were crisper and got to the receivers sooner. Mendoza also showed a pocket awareness that seemed delayed with Cousins under center. There is no magic bullet. Mendoza will struggle too. Yet his struggles are more productive for the organization long-term.
Mendoza may give them their best chance to win right now with the players they have. A few positive Mendoza scrambles can help get eight players out of the box and help open up the run game. Mendoza could be a part of the answer to the Raiders' struggles through the air and on the ground.
It was another dismal day for the ground game. However, defenses having zero respect for the Raiders' passing game could play a part in the struggles Las Vegas is having running the ball.
Connor Heyward does his job.
The Raiders entered Week 5 without two of their starting receivers. It was bound to be a tough day for the group .
The unit could have performed better, but elite defenses have little to worry about when facing the Raiders' offense. Defenses are not scared of Cousins' arm, his ability to move in the pocket, or the Raiders' group of receivers. Defenses can stack the box and bring consistent pressure.
Eventually, that pressure gets to Cousins, and he has nowhere to go. The offensive line can be better, but they could use some help from Cousins, like when he moved the pocket late against the Kansas City Chiefs. Cousins threw the ball 52 times against the Chiefs and wasn't sacked once because he did a solid job of moving in and around the pocket.
If he cannot do that consistently, the Raiders are in trouble. An offensive line can only block for so long with no receivers getting open on passes and eight players in the box on runs because the Raiders' passing game is pedestrian. Las Vegas' offensive problems are circular.
One of the few bright spots for the Raiders on Sunday and likely their most consistent position group overall.
The unit sustained several injuries but still have room for improvement.
We are seeing what the Raiders' defensive backfield is like without a consistent pass rush. Elite teams are exposing what some may have overlooked during the first three weeks of the season. The Raiders likely need another offseason or two to fully rebuild this group.
The Raiders' linebackers are better than what they showed against the Patriots. However, it does not matter what the linebackers do if receivers run wide open downfield and running backs aren't getting touched until they reach the second level of the defense.
Cole punted the ball four times, and averaged nearly 50 yards per punt.
Matt Gay missed his first field goal of the game. His miss shortly before halftime gave the Patriots the ball in scoring position.
Might have been the best outing for the group this season.
Deven Thompkins deserves more action on special teams and potentially even as a wide receiver. He registered one of the Raiders' best punt returns of the season on Sunday.

title: Raiders Stock Report: 3 Players Rising, Falling After Week 5
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders had a rough day on the road against the New England Patriots. Few things went Las Vegas' way. Las Vegas has followed up its 3-0 start with two consecutive losses to two of the league's best teams.
This was always going to be Las Vegas' toughest stretch of games, facing the Kansas City Chiefs, New England Patriots, Buffalo Bills, and Los Angeles Rams back-to-back. While the season's first three games showed growth, the last two showed where it still needs to improve.
The Raiders suffered an ugly loss on Sunday. It would be easy to say there were no positives from the performance, but that would be inaccurate. Just as there are negatives during wins, there are positives during losses, especially for a team in the early stages of a rebuild.
Las Vegas' loss to New England was their worst game of the season. The Patriots' offense posted one of the best offensive outputs in franchise history, yardage-wise. Las Vegas now has a clear idea of where they stand and how far they are from the league's best.
Below are a few players on the rise and some whose stocks are falling following the Raiders' Week 5 road loss to the Patriots.
Bowers continues to look like the league's best tight end after another impressive performance. Every team in the league knows the Raiders want to get the ball to Bowers, yet he still dominates when they need him. Bowers was again the team's leading receiver.
Bowers registered 110 yards on eight catches and gave the Raiders a puncher's chance on a day when they were clearly outmatched, outcoached, and outplayed. Bowers was one of the few bright spots from an all-around bad outing for the Raiders.
Tucker did not fill the stat sheet like he did in Week 2. However, his chances of doing so on an offense with Cody White as its next-best wide receiver are slim. Tucker caught two passes for 21 yards in the first half, both of which were significant for the struggling unit.
Porter had several big plays, including a fumble recovery. He also played solid coverage on several plays, showing the speed that helped him rise up the depth chart. It was a rough day for the Raiders as a whole, but it was encouraging to see Porter have some success.
The Raiders' defensive line is the deepest position group on the roster. Las Vegas needed that depth, losing multiple interior defensive linemen throughout the game. During that time, Butler, one of the Raiders' most experienced defensive linemen, quietly gave the unit solid play.
Shortly before halftime, Butler forced a fumble that was recovered by Porter. It did not result in points for the Raiders' offense, but it helped keep points off the board for the Patriots.
Las Vegas' questionable defensive backfield needed protection from the Raiders' defensive line. Last Sunday against the Kansas City Chiefs and today against the Patriots showed what will likely happen throughout the season if the unit cannot generate a consistent pass rush.
The Raiders' defense has been aggressive all season. On Sunday, the unit seemed unable to generate a pass rush or stop quarterback Drake Maye, who was playing with several of his backup wide receivers.
Many of the struggles Cousins and the Raiders' offense are having are innate. Looking at the depth chart and the team's training camp and preseason, it was evident that the roster still had things to fix, especially on offense. Some of those things can't be fixed until next offseason.
It was well known that Cousins' health and age could affect things. The Raiders would not be 3-2 without Cousins' experience. However, the deficiencies Las Vegas' offense has do not match well with the deficiencies in Cousins' game at this point in his career. Defenses have figured that out.
The Patriots had backup wide receivers wide open downfield multiple times. It was not a talent issue; it was a schematic and roster issue. Las Vegas' defensive backfield and wide receivers are their Achilles' heel.

title: NFL World Goes Crazy As Raiders’ Fernando Mendoza Takes Field
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders suffered a disheartening loss on Sunday, falling to the New England Patriots 45-17.
Losing by that margin let head coach Klint Kubiak give Fernando Mendoza worthwhile snaps. It goes without saying this wasn't the result Las Vegas wanted, but it let the team see Mendoza in a regular-season game. Here's how the NFL world reacted to Mendoza's debut.
With just over six minutes left in the game, Las Vegas waved the white flag and took out most of their starters . The rookie quarterback took the field, with an opportunity to gain invaluable experience early in his career.
Fernando Mendoza hace su debut en la NFL sustituyendo a Kirk Cousins en el último cuarto con los Raiders perdiendo por 28 puntos. pic.twitter.com/xKg9YQnpow
Seeing Fernando Mendoza march out today had me like pic.twitter.com/xwrVqYP72L
The No. 1 overall pick looked the part, and his arm strength was on full display. More importantly, Mendoza looked completely comfortable, completing 6-of-8 passes for 48 yards. Mendoza connected with five different pass catchers, navigating the pocket and going through his reads swiftly.
Fernando Mendoza with a strike in his NFL debut today. Finished 6/8 in one drive down the stretch. pic.twitter.com/LaBCy5JFOx
Fernando Mendoza, first play with the Raiders pic.twitter.com/9TmBNGfaf3
Mendoza certainly looked sharp, but fans wasted no time suggesting the Raiders consider making a quarterback change. Obviously, it was an ugly performance in a 28-point loss, but it's not as if Kirk Cousins was the culprit for the defeat. The 38-year-old quarterback completed 19-of-28 passes for 243 yards and one touchdown.
I could see the Raiders eventually trading Kirk Cousins and rolling with Fernando Mendoza https://t.co/QK44lewPfA
Fernando Mendoza looked better on his first NFL drive than Kirk Cousins did today. Just saying.
After starting the season 3-0 and now losing two straight games, it's easy for fans to panic, especially with the upcoming stretch. However, there are two reasons not to panic. One, Las Vegas is still above .500 and is the No. 6 seed in the AFC playoff picture. Second, the Raiders' future is bright with their long-term franchise quarterback in the building. It's a quick snapshot, but Mendoza illustrated what he's capable of.
This is what Raider Nation should be excited about. Starting 3-0 was fun but don’t let it blind you. The goal is, and always will be, to build a team around Fernando Mendoza. https://t.co/cRcKM95Gv8
🚨 Preview of A New Era in Las Vegas.  Fernando Mendoza Throws His First Pass. Despite the loss the Raiders have a lot to be excited about.  A 3-2 start and they get their first taste of their long-term future. Kirk Cousins leads the team for now.  But here is who has next 👇.… pic.twitter.com/1YnybjLscQ
Cousins has been excellent this season, throwing three touchdowns in each of the first three games. The 15-year veteran has fit seamlessly into Kubiak's system. That said, Mendoza's mobility was apparent on Sunday. The rookie quarterback extended and made plays with his legs.
With all due respect to Cousins, he doesn't provide that element, so it limits what Kubiak and the coaching staff can call. While Kubiak wants Cousins to keep the offense on schedule and ahead of the sticks, it's nice to have a quarterback who can create plays outside the constructs of the scheme.
Mendoza needs to start. Kirk can’t maneuver this o-line. Fernando can extend drives with his legs
Fernando Mendoza got the ball quick to receivers benson had a drop on 3rd down Dozer damn near picked it up on his legs 4th & 5 almost rook 💪
The NFL world was certainly excited to see Mendoza take the field.

title: 3 Overreactions to Raiders Blowout Loss vs. Patriots
full_text:
Two weeks ago, the Las Vegas Raiders were the talk of the NFL with a 3-0 start. Fast forward to the present day, they are now 3-2 with two consecutive losses, including Sunday's beatdown by the New England Patriots, 45-17.
This was as bad a game as you could've imagined for the Raiders, who entered the matchup hoping to repeat last year's results with another victory in Foxborough, Massachusetts. Instead, Las Vegas and head coach Klint Kubiak were humbled by Drake Maye and the Patriots. Here are three of my overreactions to Sunday's disappointing results.
It's like we're reliving last year's run game where nothing went right for the Raiders. Ashton Jeanty continues to struggle after rushing for roughly 100 yards in the season opener, tallying only 2.7 yards on 10 attempts, with the team getting just over two yards per carry. Not great.
Jeanty hasn't done himself any favors by struggling to be deliberate and seeing blocks form in front of him, and the offensive line has to do a better job of creating displacement at the line of scrimmage. Something must change for this unit to improve, and it may take patience and growth within Kubiak's wide-zone system.
I think it's fair to say this is who we thought the Raiders were supposed to be in some form. The only two positives from this game were Brock Bowers and the debut of first-overall rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza (6-of-8, 48 yards). The defense spiraled against Maye and the Patriots' skill players while struggling to stop the run.
This is a young team with some combination of veteran talent that was just humbled on the road against a resurgent Patriots team, and Maye has completely flipped the script with five total touchdowns. Las Vegas has a lot of work to do, and it won't get any easier when the Buffalo Bills and the league's best quarterback, Josh Allen.
Turning to the Raiders' defense, it was a disappointing display, as defensive coordinator Rob Leonard played with an aggressive approach against the Patriots' pass-catchers and got burned. Wide receiver Kyle Williams was as good as anyone at winning against press alignments, and both Darien Porter and Hezekiah Masses had rough days, as did the linebackers against tight ends Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon.
Teams like the Bills, Los Angeles Rams, San Francisco 49ers, and Seattle Seahawks will all pose similar challenges. This may not be the last low-level performance for the Raiders' defense. This is where Leonard will have to create some magic with the talent he has.

title: Raiders vs. Patriots: Winners & Losers From New England
full_text:
FOXBOROUGH, MASS.—The Las Vegas Raiders (3-2) came into New England today to play the Patriots (3-2) and looked terrible from the start.
Riding a wave of optimism and excitement, with a chance to flip the script from a Raiders rebuild to the NFL Playoffs, today's letdown can possibly be credited to the “Rat Poison” of positive press Nick Saban so famously called out. Perhaps it was traveling across the country and playing a game at 10 AM PT; whatever the reason, at no time since Klint Kubiak arrived has this team looked so bad.
I asked Klint Kubiak about Saban's "Rat Poison" analogy, and he was blunt with his assessment: "Well, I think it's going to show a lot about who we are, how mature we are, how good our leadership is with myself, for our players. It's an opportunity for us to move forward. We have our whole season ahead of us, and we can't let this game beat us twice."
The Patriots, decimated by injuries all over the field, eventually triumphed 45-17. The Raiders looked totally discombobulated in every phase from start to finish.
The Las Vegas Raiders, in every phase from coaching, defense, offense, and special teams, looked completely discombobulated today.
Prompting one Super Bowl-winning and well-respected NFL OC to text me, “Such a disappointment with today's performances after last week's game.”
Klint Kubiak minced no words, saying to the media before he could even be asked, "Very disappointing performance today from everyone, players and coaches. Obviously give a lot of credit to the Patriots. They did a great job. We had eight penalties today; far too many. It's a game that we have to move forward from very quickly. We have everything ahead of us as a team. We're not happy with what happened today, and we have to go do something about it. We have to fix it and move on."
Before this game, I said the Raiders were not good enough to come here and beat themselves and the Patriots. Unfortunately for Raider Nation, I was right.
The Raiders were not ready. The second offensive play (First Pass) was nearly picked off, as the Patriots read the play and jumped the route. That is on coaching; to self-scout tells for plays.
In every phase of this game, the Patriots staff had their number. It was clear that on this day, the Raiders coaching staff didn’t have their team ready or a game plan that should have punished a New England team that resembled a M*A*S*H* unit more than a Patriots team.
Kubiak again went blunt in his assessment: "Well, defensively, offensively, special teams, I don't think any of us played well enough to win today."
We knew coming into this season that this would be a Raiders rebuild. Credit this staff for an amazing job that even gave this team the opportunity to flip the script.
But the reality is that before today’s game I told you, “If the Raiders play on Sunday as they did against the Kansas City Chiefs, they will win." I didn’t think I needed to add a caveat about the coaching staff.
The aforementioned NFL OC texted about the staff, “This is first game where I don't like either offensive or defensive strategies. Mental letdown after last Sunday by coaches.”
This is not the end of the world, but it was a total disaster. I have lost zero faith in Kubiak, his staff, or this roster. None of them have been perfect this year; it's just that none of them have been collectively this bad on the same day.
We anticipated and discussed all week that Mike Vrabel would sell out to stop the run, and he did. What we didn’t expect was that down four cornerbacks, FOUR, the Raiders couldn’t get any traction at all. Drives stalled, unforced penalties, and a complete lack of a schematic attack plan that Vrabel couldn’t answer.
Failing to convert on opportunity is not how you win in the NFL, and we have seen the Raiders perform at a much higher level in the first four weeks of this early season. Just not today.
So, reverting to this level of performance is not acceptable when they have proven their ceiling is much higher.
If the Raiders had performed like this all season, it would have made more sense; they haven’t.
The Raiders' offense looked stale, uncreative, and as if it were on autopilot.
Kubiak said of his offense today, “I think just overall today, we were playing from behind all day, so it became a passing game, and it didn't need to be that way. I abandoned the run game too early and didn't give it a chance to get going."
He went further when talking about the relentless pass rush on QB Kirk Cousins: "Well, they did a great job in their blitz package. When you pass it that many times, there's going to be those. But overall, I think they did a great job of pressuring us today."
Despite numerous key injuries, the Raiders' defense finally looked like the young, thin unit we've seen all year. Former Raiders HC Josh McDaniels put on a masterful performance calling the Patriots' offense
The Patriots took it to the Raiders and went right after them.
The Raiders' attacking style looked tentative, almost as if they expected the beat-up Patriots to surrender. The Patriots went on the attack, and the Raiders' D looked like Mike Tyson when he took a surprise punch from James “Buster” Douglas, who went on to win the fight.
No one told Douglas Tyson was invincible, and no one told the Patriots they were too depleted to win. The Raiders' coverages were beaten by backups, and the Silver and Black failed to adjust to what the Patriots continued to do, with no success.
The Raiders D gave up 45 points, 165 rushing yards, 371 passing yards, and ruled the day on the field.
The Patriots were not perfect; the Raiders D was worse.
Kubiak said of his defense, "They kept going after us and they made big plays. Credit to them."
Matt Gay missed a field goal he should have made, and Darrell Luter Jr. made a brutal mistake by not downing a perfect AJ Cole punt. They weren't the sole reason the Raiders lost, but as professionals, they certainly didn’t do enough to do their part to win.
Kubiak said of his special teams, when I asked him if it surprised him with their mistakes, “Yeah, it did. That's been a strength of our team. I see it as a strength moving forward. We have to go to work to get it fixed."
Always present, Raider Nation showed up today. Adam Vinatieri went off on Raider Nation during a halftime ceremony, essentially saying, "I always thought we owned the Raiders, and now, thanks to Tom Brady, I guess we do."
Adam Vinatieri goes off on the Raiders.  Basically,  said, I always thought we owned the Raiders, and now, thanks to Tom Brady, I guess we do. He then thanks Raider fans for always being there for so many of his biggest moments.
The Raiders fans roared with boos. Despite Vinatieri's verbal whipping, Raider Nation did their part; sadly, the team didn’t.
I will get into the details later this week when I give my report card and review the film.
This was a bad day, the first in five games for a rebuilding team. Raider fans are disappointed because this staff and team have overachieved this year.
The fact that it took us five weeks into the year to finally write this story is perhaps the even bigger story.
This is still a rebuilding season; the Raiders are still thin, young, and void of talent at certain positions. The staff had a bad day, and so did the players.
It was just the first day; they all came together on one day.
Today was a hard smack in the face to a team that had overachieved.
Back to the drawing board, the Buffalo Bills, a true Super Bowl contender like the Kansas City Chiefs, are coming back to Allegiant next week.
Their “Mafia” of fans will be loud, and the Raiders will quickly return to getting better.
That was the plan all along. The joys of two weeks ago in New Orleans are offset by today's doldrums. That is all part of rebuilding the Raiders.
Sometimes, reality hurts. It hurts for the Silver and Black today.
Kubiak said of how he told the team to take this loss, "Well, I think it's going to show a lot about who we are, how mature…

title: What Stood Out in Fernando Mendoza's First Raiders Regular Season Action
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders delivered a forgettable road performance against the New England Patriots in Week 5. Las Vegas' offense failed to get anything going for a second consecutive week, leaving their defense on the field for extended periods. It was the opposite of complementary football.
There were not many positives to take from Las Vegas' worst game of the season. Week 5 was an avalanche for the Raiders, as they could not get out of their own way long enough to threaten the Patriots in any meaningful way. It was the first time all season the Raiders were not competitive.
The Raiders fell behind early and never recovered. That deficit grew into a massive, double-digit gap that their offense couldn't overcome. Eventually, it became evident there was no need to continue putting Kirk Cousins in harm's way, given his inability to escape the Patriots' pass rush.
With the Raiders down by nearly 30 points, Klint Kubiak and the Raiders' coaching staff made a quarterback change, thrusting No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza into action. Given the situation, not much was expected from the rookie, but it was the right time to get him in.
When Mendoza will actually start a game is still a mystery, but Las Vegas got an idea of what Mendoza could do in a meaningful game.
Mendoza's outing on Sunday was a small sample size, as he only played one drive. The Raiders were also down by so many points that Mendoza saw a different version of New England's defense than Cousins did for most of the game. Yet there were still noticeable aspects of Mendoza's drive.
Las Vegas likely did not have much of a game plan specific to Mendoza at that point in the game. So, the play calling may not have been all that extensive. Still, Mendoza's ability to get the ball out quickly was on display. His mobility and willingness to use his legs seemed to open things up for Las Vegas.
Mendoza finished with six completions on eight pass attempts. Mendoza finished with three rushing yards. Mike Washington finished with five rushing yards, and Dylan Laube finished with nine. You have to use your imagination with the handful of plays Mendoza was in.
Through five games, it is pretty clear what the ceiling is for the Raiders' offense, with Cousins leading the way. Mendoza has a lot of work to do, but it may be time to consider letting him learn by playing in the regular season.
Las Vegas has two more challenging games remaining before a road trip against the New York Jets. If the Raiders' coaching staff is serious about winning this season, they must be honest about the things holding their offense back.
The Raiders' coaching staff must realize that one of their quarterbacks is better equipped to succeed with the players that are on the field. Teams are starting to figure out the Raiders' offense. Mendoza needs more regular-season action.

title: Raider Nation Reacts to Lopsided Road Loss to Patriots
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders have now dropped two straight games after beginning the season 3-0.
The Raiders are still in the beginning stages of a rebuild, but are clearly ahead of schedule. However, the franchise now faces an early roadblock after a 45-17 defeat in New England to the Patriots.
Teams have been selling out to stop the Raiders' run attack, and that continued today. Las Vegas rushed for just 38 yards on 18 carries, an average of 2.1 yards per attempt. Ashton Jeanty was increasingly limited in practice this week leading up to the game, and he ended with 27 yards on 10 carries. Dylan Laube scored the Raiders' lone rushing touchdown of the afternoon, totaling four carries for nine yards and that score.
Well, so much for the Raiders being a thing. Cute 3-0 start that will soon turn into 3-4. Their next two games are against the Bills and Rams. Back to reality.
4 penalties for 70 yards in the 1st Quarter for Raiders. Have to clean that up quickly.
Mike Washington Jr. only had one carry for five yards in the outing.
Out coached and dominated on both sides of the ball…. that’s all…. #raiders
Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers continues to cement himself as arguably the best tight end in the National Football League, as he is the driving force of this Las Vegas offense. The former Georgia Bulldog went for eight catches for 110 yards and a touchdown to lead the team. The Raiders' next leading receiver was Jeanty, who finished with three receptions for 50 yards. Las Vegas' top wide receiver in Boston was Cody White, who notched two catches for 44 yards.
Even when Brock Bowers is covered, he’s still open. Hell of a grab
Brock Bowers the best TE in the league
As the final score will show, the Raiders struggled to find any offensive consistency, never scoring more than seven points in any quarter and being completely shut out in the second frame. Kirk Cousins finished 19-of-28 passing for 243 yards and one touchdown.
Thank God for Brock Bowers… jeeze
Overall, the Raiders had their positives and negatives, but they have come back down to earth over the last two weeks after a scorching hot start to the season. Especially after a tight loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, a game that the Raiders had a legitimate chance to win, this was a tough outing for the franchise as they suffered their second straight loss.
Fernando Mendoza looked comfortable in his first few snaps… 👀
omg Fernando Mendoza just did a quick prayer on the sideline we are about to watch his debut on a rainy day in New England

Here we go welcome Fernando Mendoza
Mendoza is the hopeful future for Las Vegas, and fans got to see their cornerstone on the field for the first time in the regular season.

title: Key Takeaways From Raiders' Rough Week 5 Loss to Patriots
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders traveled to the East Coast looking to bounce back from their Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Instead, a questionable early call set off a downward spiral the Raiders could not work their way out of.
Las Vegas entered Week 5 as one of the least-penalized teams. That changed quickly, as the Raiders' defense was flagged for multiple penalties that helped the Patriots' offense get going. It was a sloppy day on both sides, as both teams were heavily penalized.
Still, several penalties called against the Raiders were questionable at best. The number of penalties and yards were relatively equal, but everyone knows that not all penalties are the same, and their timing isn't either. The penalties were equal; their magnitude was not.
Although the penalties undoubtedly affected the flow, the referees and the penalties they called are not why the Raiders were thoroughly outplayed in every facet of the game. Plenty of blame could be placed on the whole team, as Sunday was a disappointing performance.
Below are some of the biggest takeaways from the Raiders' blowout loss to the Patriots.
It took some time, but as the game went on, Las Vegas' defense began playing the physical brand of football that helped them jump out to a 3-0 start to the season. It was far from pretty, but it was effective. New England entered Week 5 missing several players due to injury.
Before the first half ended, New England lost several more players. However, Las Vegas also lost players. Defensive linemen Tonka Hemingway and Folorunso Fatukasi sustained injuries. The Kansas City Chiefs and the Los Angeles Chargers also lost multiple players against the Raiders.
Bowers seems to make big plays every week, and that continued in Week 5. With the Raiders down by seven points early and struggling to move the ball, Las Vegas began getting the ball to Bowers. Las Vegas completed two big passes to their star tight end, including a touchdown.
Both completions were big catches that many others on Las Vegas' roster likely would not have made. Bowers is special. There really are no words. Yes, Bowers had lost a fumble late in the game. It was the first time he has lost a fumble as a professional, and the Raiders were already down by 25.
In their first three games, Las Vegas played an unbelievable amount of complementary football. It could be argued they played more complementary football than is realistically sustainable given where they are in their rebuild and the remaining deficiencies on offense.
For the past two weeks, the Raiders' offense has been somewhat exposed . They are dealing with injuries to their receiving corps and starting running back, Ashton Jeanty. Still, the Raiders' defense has done enough to keep them in games, even with the mental lapses they have had.
Las Vegas' offense still has debilitating issues. Those issues are roster-related and have affected their ability to call plays. Running back Ashton Jeanty is clearly hurt. Blocking issues are also making it hard to run the ball. Both factors are hindering the offense. They must figure it out soon.
It doesn't matter what Las Vegas' defense does if the offense cannot score points. The Raiders' offense isn't only struggling to score points; it has failed to sustain long drives to give its struggling defense a rest. Las Vegas has to change something with two tough games coming up.
Entering the season, it was well known that the Raiders needed additional help at the wide receiver position. When healthy, their group of receivers is serviceable. However, their group of receivers has been the most impacted by injuries so far this season, making that need even worse.
Las Vegas entered Week 5 missing two of their starting wide receivers, but the Patriots were missing multiple wide receivers too. New England's offense did not struggle as much as the Raiders' receivers did. The Raiders' lack of receiving options is reaching the point where it can derail the season.
Raiders franchise cornerstone and No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Fernando Mendoza, made his regular-season NFL debut today against the Patriots. Mendoza checked in with about six minutes to go in the fourth quarter, and the Raiders already down 45-17. As many would expect, the NFL world was excited to see the highly-touted rookie take the field for the first time in the regular season.
Mendoza finished 6-of-8 passing for 48 yards and a QBR of 89.6. It isn't so much about the performance itself, but about Raider Nation seeing their future on the field for the first time in the regular season.
The former Indiana Hoosier has a long road to go, but this is a huge deal for Raider Nation and the future of the franchise.

title: Raiders vs. Patriots: Week 5 Live Game Thread
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' Week 5 matchup against the New England Patriots will be the team's third road game in four weeks. Las Vegas has handled its early success and road trips well, jumping out to a 3-1 start on the season. New England will be another tough test for Klint Kubiak's Raiders.
Las Vegas looks to stay ahead of the curve, with matchups against the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams on the horizon. The Raiders had a strong week of practice heading into their road game against the Patriots, knowing the Patriots are a formidable team despite their slew of injuries.
Las Vegas has its own depth chart issues to work through heading into Sunday, as running back Ashton Jeanty is questionable heading into Sunday. The Raiders are also without wide receivers Jack Bech and Jalen Nailor.
So far, the Raiders have started the season with three impressive wins that required them to pull out late-game victories. Regardless of Sunday's outcome, Week 5 will likely come down to the wire, too. Veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins noted how well the team has responded in such situations.
“I think it's been a resilient group. I think our defense has played very well. I think guys are making plays. I think it's probably less learning and more confirming what I learned about them back in the spring or even in training camp," Cousins said earlier this week.
"These guys, they want to do it the right way. Football means something to them. They're hardworking, listen well, and it makes it a joy to be the quarterback for a group of guys like that. But you got to go prove it again every week."
The Raiders have a chance to secure a solid 4-1 start after winning only seven games in the past two seasons combined. Las Vegas will have its work cut out for it against a well-coached Patriots team in a road game where the weather could affect play.
Las Vegas must limit the mistakes that cost them last week against the Kansas City Chiefs, many of which stemmed from poor execution. The Patriots, while talented, are a team the Raiders can beat, but that will only happen if the Raiders take care of their end of things for all four quarters.

title: Why Dolphins Coach Is Right in Squashing Idea of Benching Willis
full_text:
The question truly was ridiculous, except it needed to be asked because it's fans are talking about it and would want to ask the question themselves, and journalists are conduits between fans and coaches.
So it was that the first question in Miami Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley's regular day-after-the-game media session Monday was this: "Are you giving any thought to starting Kyle McCord against the Jets after the bye?"
That would be quarterback Kyle McCord and the suggestion was whether Malik Willis' performance and stats through five games and maybe even in the Week 5 loss against the Cincinnati Bengals was enough to considering making a change.
But Hafley quickly, and absolutely correctly, shot down that notion.
And the thinking in saying so?
"We've played five games, and Malik is our quarterback."
During the remainder of his 20-minute session, Hafley was asked other questions about Willis and he made it clear that he expects better from his starting quarterback while also indicating that several factors are involved in the success — or lack thereof — of the passing game, such as pass protection and receivers running the correct routes and getting open.
All of it is off right now, up to and including Willis.
Before the Week 5 Monday night game, Willis was last among 29 qualifying quarterbacks in passer rating and completion percentage with only two touchdown passes against four interceptions.
There is nobody who should be happy with Willis' work so far this season or think it's anywhere near good enough for him to even begin being considered as a long-term answer.
And it's five games with a young and sub-par supporting cast, one that's been without it's best player (De'Von Achane) for almost three games and without its most dynamic wide receiver at the moment (Caleb Douglas) for three-plus games.
Remember when some folks were calling the Dolphins wide receiver corps about as bad a group as there's been in the NFL in a long time? Well, that group always was about long-term potential and that potential has not been reached yet.
And let's also not pretend that Willis has benefited from great pass protection, either, because pressure is getting there in a hurry on a pretty regular basis.
This isn't to excuse everything that Willis has struggled with, but it absolutely does explain some of the poor numbers.
"I think you guys are going to get tired of my answers however the questions are phrased, it's everything," Hafley said. "It's a detail of the route running. It starts with the protection. It's going through the progression. It's everybody being on the same page, and everybody being more efficient in their 1/11."
But, of course, the quarterback is the one who's going to be in the spotlight and Willis also is the one outside free agent the Dolphins signed all year for something beyond the minimum or almost-minimum salary.
Hafley and GM Jon-Eric Sullivan talked about Willis in terms of handing him the keys to the offense and building around him, and so far that construction project is not looking very good.
But would it make any sense whatsoever to give up after five games?
Or even go with this idea of having Willis sit for a bit and give Kyle McCord a shot to see what he can do?
Sure, the idea of McCord might be intriguing for those who liked him at Syracuse, but do we need to remind everyone that after the Philadelphia Eagles selected him in the sixth round of the 2025 draft, they waived him and then let him leave off their practice squad for Green Bay this year, only to have the Packers trade him to the Dolphins for a 2028 sixth-round pick?
Again, let's repeat that: 2028 sixth-round pick. Using the gauge of dropping a pick for every year down the road, that's the equivalent of a 2026 eighth-round pick.
Yes, the Packers don't believe in keeping three QBs on their roster, but if they valued McCord, would they have basically just given him away like that, much the same way the Dolphins gave away Quinn Ewers?
Maybe McCord will become a good NFL quarterback at some point, but the reality is it's probably a long shot.
And maybe the same holds true for Willis.
Except that Willis actually has appeared in an NFL regular season game and he actually looked very good doing it during his time with the Packers, where Hafley and Sullivan also got to watch him first-hand on a daily basis.
What's happened so far in the 2026 season probably isn't what they had in mind or hoped, but suggesting for even a millisecond they would give up on Willis this quickly bordered on ridiculous.
The Dolphins have 12 games remaining in the 2026 regular season and that's plenty of time for things to change, to get better with Willis, the passing game and the entire offense.
None of it is good enough right now. But the Dolphins don't have to make any decisions right now as it applies to 2027 and they owe it to Willis and more importantly to themselves to give him a chance to show what he can do.

title: Miami Dolphins 2026 Week 5 Snap Counts Stories: Injuries Cause Shuffling
full_text:
What stood out regarding play counts in the Miami Dolphins' 31-24 loss against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday:
We'll start with the list of inactives, which was highlighted by four players missing the game with injuries, including wide receiver Caleb Douglas out for a third consecutive game with an ankle injury.
The only Dolphins player who was active but did not play was backup quarterback Kyle McCord.
Since we've been keeping track every game, the starting lineup was back to six rookies Will Kacmarek at tight end, Chris Bell at wide receiver, guard Kadyn Proctor, linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, cornerback Chris Johnson and safety Michael Taaffe.
-- The Dolphins opened with two tight ends and two wide receivers, which was why rookie fullback DJ Herman didn't get a start.
-- After the Dolphins had only 39 offensive snaps against Minnesota, that number jumped to a lot more respectable 66 against the Bengals.
-- After playing fewer snaps than Kacmarek against Minnesota, Greg Dulcich got a very heavy work load in Week 5 with 49 offensive snaps. That was his second-highest total of the season behind the 51 he played against the Kansas City Chiefs in the Week 3 home opener.
-- Besides QB Malik Wilis and the offensive linemen, the player with the most offensive snaps was wide receiver Malik Washington with 53, yet another indication of his value.
-- At running back, practice squad elevation Carlos Washington Jr. got as many offensive snaps at Jaylen Wright, who continues to struggle to find his footing in his third season with the Dolphins. Ollie Gordon II got 43 snaps firmly established as the No. 1 back in the absence of De'Von Achane.
-- Jonah Savaiinaea ended up playing 18 snaps before leaving the game with an ankle injury and being replaced by Jarrett Kingston for the final 48 snaps at right guard.
-- Rookie tight end Seydou Traore got his first offensive snap against the Bengals after being used exclusively on special teams in the first four games — but it was only one.
-- With Jordyn Brooks, JuJu Brents and Michael Taaffe all temporarily leaving the game with injuries, Jacob Rodriguez and Dante Trader Jr. became the only players who played every snap on defense.
-- 2025 first-round pick Kenneth Grant made his return to action but played a very modest 16 defensive snaps, which probably made sense in helping him work his way back into the action. That number better increase once the Dolphins return from their bye, though.
-- The Dolphins opened the game in the nickel and played a good portion of the game with that five-DB alignment, with Chris Johnson Jr. playing 64 of the 65 snaps and Jason Marshall also played 57 snaps.
-- Josh Uche, who's become the most effective edge defender on the team, got the snap count to reflect that, with 45 snaps compared to 36 for Chop Robinson. Practice squad elevation Rodney McGraw played 14 snaps, not far behind Malik Herring.
-- With Brooks leaving the game temporarily, Willie Gay Jr. got extra work at linebacker and finished with 37 snaps, his highest total since the opener against the Las Vegas Raiders when the Dolphins used a lot more three-linebacker looks.
-- With Brents missing some snaps when he was banged up, newcomer Jaylin Simpson got five snaps on defense and had a nice third-down pass breakup against Ja'Marr Chase.
-- Because of the injuries, only four non-specialists saw action only on special teams, down from eight against Minnesota. This time it was Andre Jones Jr., Julius Wood, Marcellus Dial Jr. and Andrew Meyer.
-- Speaking of special teams, Traore again led the way with 21 snaps, followed by 17 for Jones and 15 for McGraw.

title: Four Losers And Four Winners From the Week 5 Dolphins Loss
full_text:
Don't let the 31-24 final score deceive you; this was not a close game between the Miami Dolphins and Cincinnati Bengals. In an important game for Cincy regarding the standings in the AFC North, they took care of business and handed the Fins their fifth straight loss.
At the minimum, if you're looking for player and team progression in the same vain as the Minnesota game, you won't find it here. The offense was stonewalled for three quarters, only finding rhythm when it was too late, and the defense gave up over 300 total yards and four touchdowns.
The Dolphins head into the bye week battered and bruised, figuratively and literally, and worst of all, still searching for answers. Only three teams remain winless in the NFL: Miami, Tennessee, and the Los Angeles Chargers. Based on their performances against the Bengals, it's difficult to predict when they'll finally shower Jeff Hafley with Gatorade.
Yes, Willis doesn't have a star-studded list of weapons to throw to. But Willis flat-out held the offense back, was unable to deal with Cincinnati's commanding front seven, and was more of a liability in the passing game than ever before.
Regardless of how you felt about the comments that Bengals DB Jordan Battle made about Willis's ball-tapping and how it's a tell that he's going to throw the ball, is it purely a coincidence that the DB who caught both interceptions that Willis threw was Battle?
Willis also lost a fumble pretty much by himself near his own goal line and was sacked three times. One of those sacks came on second-and-goal in the third quarter — a case of holding onto the ball for too long, trying to make an impossible play happen instead of throwing the ball away — a consistent mistake he's made this season.
To his credit, he looked decent as a scrambler with 74 yards and a touchdown, but this was by far his worst game of the season purely from a mistake standpoint. His game looks extremely limited, and because the weapons at his disposal are also limited, you get an offensive performance like the Dolphins got against the Bengals — simply not good enough.
Johnson and Miami's secondary had a tough task against Cincinnati since two of their wide receivers, who were questionable — Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins — ended up playing. But Johnson held his own with six total tackles, a low number because he locked down most receivers he was matched up against.
Like the other rookies on defense, Johnson also achieved his first major highlight of the season, a Peanut punch on Chase Brown in the red zone, forcing a fumble that was picked up by Chop Robinson — ignore that Robinson also had the ball punched out, only for JuJu Brents to corral it in the end.
There were only a handful of receptions that Johnson gave up, but nothing major. He may have had a slow start to the season in terms of effectiveness, but he's heating up for the Dolphins at a solid pace.
After being stuffed by the Minnesota defense, Wright needed a bounce-back game to genuinely help out this offense whenever he was on the field, but once again, he was made a non-factor — six carries for 11 yards.
The offensive line has been able (for the most part) to create gaps for Miami's running backs, but Wright's running can be predictable, purely horizontal, and he's been unable to either evade or shake off tacklers in the same way that Ollie Gordon has been able to do.
Both wide receivers Chris Bell and Malik Washington  were both used in the running game for one play each and recorded more rushing yards than Wright (26 & 18). Miami's duo in the backfield was once De'Von Achane and Gordon, and now it's forced to be Gordon and Willis because Wright isn't doing enough to justify remaining the backup running back.
It might not look like much, but Coleman had a breakout game for the Dolphins that was well-needed — three receptions for 30 yards off seven targets, including his first touchdown in the NFL that came in the fourth quarter, beginning a way-too-late rally for Miami that obviously fell short.
Miami's fifth-round pick showcased the ability to create separation even with limited space, headlined by the aforementioned touchdown. He also showcased his athleticism when he dove for a catch at the six-yard line with a minute to go, leading to Willis sneaking into the end zone right after.
Caleb Douglas is still injured and, spoiler alert, Chris Bell had a disappointing game. So, seeing Coleman have the performance he did is reassuring, and maybe Miami's offense could turn to him more often as the season progresses.
The aforementioned "rush" for Bell was an end-around play that he made the most of, assisted by solid blocking from both Kadyn Proctor and Will Kacmarek. As a receiver, Bell was targeted twice but did not record a single reception.
It feels like a combination of the Dolphins not utilizing him as much as they could, along with Bell being unable to create distance between himself and the defensive backs he's matched up against. It's a problem that reared its ugly head against Minnesota and continued into this game.
All in all, it's clear the Dolphins are looking elsewhere in terms of who they want Willis to throw to, and when Douglas is once again available, it wouldn't be shocking to see Bell's already small snap count be erased.
Things got scary for Brooks when he suffered a foot injury in the first half. He would return later on in the game and still come away with eight tackles, tied for the second-most in this game.
Aside from showing the toughness and grit that's to be expected from a veteran like Brooks, he made good on his responsibility to limit tight ends following what TJ Hockenson was able to do for the Vikings. Erick All Jr. was held to 25 yards on three targets. Mike Gesiscki scored a touchdown on Cincinnati's opening drive, but didn't record a single reception the rest of the way.
We have our first coach on one of these lists, and it's been a long time coming for special teams coordinator Chris Tabor. Between the punting, kicking, returning, and especially fielding, this has been a horrific start to the season for the Dolphins, and the blame needs to fall on someone.
Miami, which hasn't had a lead all season, was denied one out of the gate when the Dolphins gave up an 81-yard return on the opening kickoff. Not long after, one of their kickoffs missed the landing zone, which would have placed the ball on the 40-yard line if not for a Cincinnati personal foul that set them back 15 yards.
Riley Patterson cashed in on a 29-yard field goal, but missed an extra point following the final touchdown with a minute to go. It ultimately didn't mean anything because the Dolphins didn't recover the ensuing onside kick, but what if they had? Since he missed the PAT, seven points would have forced overtime instead of winning the game outright.
Bradley Pinion, at the least, had a decent game with a pair of 57- and 59-yard punts, but this was another overall messy performance by the special teams. Miami's offense and defense have enough on their plates to worry about without the special teams putting them in awful situations.
Miami's safety net in the offense, Gordon had another quality game with 88 yards on 18 carries and a touchdown in the first half. Thankfully, his visit to the blue medical tent was brief, and he immediately returned to the game.
The only "negative" you could say about Gordon was that his emotions spilled out on the sidelines, which was caught on video from multiple angles. It occurred following Miami's field goal in the third quarter, despite the offense having a first-and-goal on the 1-yard line.
But honestly, Miami's offense has played and looked so stale up to this point that the outburst from Gordon was genuinely a welcome sign. It shows he cares and wants to see the offense improve more than any other player or even coach for the Dolphins.
