title: Five Instant Overreactions to Dolphins-Bengals Matchup
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins recorded their fifth straight loss to begin the Jeff Hafley era, as they fell to the Cincinnati Bengals by a score of 31-24. Let’s overreact to this game:
This is, without question, the worst special teams unit I have ever seen. Even their best play, a kickoff that landed the Bengals inside the 5-yard line, wasn’t even a smart kick by Riley Patterson, but rather a very poor one that would have been an out-of-bounds penalty if the returner simply placed one foot on the sideline as he caught it.
The opening kickoff return went 81 yards for the Bengals, setting them up for a quick touchdown. Later in the first half, they attempted a knuckling kick that wound up short of the landing zone, but only placed the Bengals at the 25-yard line because of a personal foul by Cincinnati. Riley Patterson also missed a PAT late.
Somehow, the Bengals found a way to match the Dolphins’ ineptitude multiple times, but it doesn’t excuse the fact that this unit has consistently failed to execute. Blown assignments have drawn the blame of the staff, but it’s worth estimating when this becomes a coaching problem. Either way, this needs to be addressed, because it’s bordering on embarrassing.
The Dolphins’ passing game is broken on every level right now. Their receivers don’t consistently create separation, their play-calling is stale and rarely uses all five eligibles, and Malik Willis just had his worst game of 2026.
The quickest way to fix this would be to simplify things for Willis. Less drawn-out play-action looks, and the understanding from the quarterback that if he doesn’t see anything on the front side, he can use his world-class speed to create something.
Miami has shown legitimate flashes on the ground, and if their passing game can take even a half-step up, they might be able to grab their first win. To achieve that, though, Caleb Douglas needs to come back, Bobby Slowik needs to find rhythm in his play-calling, and Willis’ decision-making needs an overhaul.
Joe Burrow dinked and dunked the Dolphins to death this week, finishing with 23 completions on 32 attempts for 190 yards and four touchdowns. Cincinnati was able to stay ahead of the sticks, primarily by attacking underneath, where they were left with little resistance.
Part of this is simply the Dolphins’ game plan. Their defensive backs play deep to limit explosives and keep possessions to a minimum. However, as their record shows, this may not be conducive to winning games.
It might be time to force the issue. The offense doesn’t have the level of ball control necessary to maximize the few possessions they get, and the defense has, at the very least, shown an ability to create turnovers. A more pressing defensive scheme may actually be more effective as Jeff Hafley searches for his first win.
The loss of De’Von Achane in Week 3 was seen as a death knell to an already struggling run game, but with Ollie Gordon leading the charge, they’ve been explosive over the last two weeks.
In Weeks 4 and 5, Gordon has accumulated 27 carries for 188 yards and two touchdowns. Credit is certainly in order for the offensive line, who have opened up holes consistently, but Gordon’s power and (perhaps more impressively) footwork at 6-2 and 226 pounds has been enough to take advantage of them.
Achane is, obviously, still the No. 1 back on this team when he returns next season, but the potential of spelling him with a skill set that foils his own is exciting. Gordon looks like a gem so far in year two.
As the Dolphins hope to remedy their aforementioned struggling passing game, one key should be third-year receiver Malik Washington, who has really impressed as of late. His start-and-stop ability makes him dangerous in the open field, where he has consistently made the first defender miss. That level of dynamism is seemingly unmatched among Miami’s weaponry.
Washington looks improved in the technical elements of his game. His route-running has looked refined this season, and he’s made a couple nice catches against tight coverage. The chemistry between he and Malik Willis is something the Dolphins should rely on more by getting him in space early and often.

title: Dolphins Week 5 Instant Takeaways: Miserable Day for Malik, Pass Defense
full_text:
A mere look at the final score might suggest some progress for the Miami Dolphins in their Week 5 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals, but it actually was the opposite.
The Dolphins did set a new season high with their 24 points, almost doubling their previous high of 13, but the final score of 31-24 didn't do justice to what we saw at Hard Rock Stadium.
The biggest disappointment of all was the play of quarterback Malik Willis, who turned the ball over three times on a day when the margin for error against Joe Burrow and the Bengals.
Willis is in a tough spot with a young wide receiver corps that could be good in time but certainly isn't there yet and with consistent pressure, but it never justified all the miscues and it certainly wasn't the case on this day. And Willis repeated a mistake he had made earlier this season when on a second-and-goal from the 3 he took an unnecessary and ridiculous 8-yard sack when he rolled out of the pocket and just didn't chuck the ball out of bounds for an incompletion before he was taken down.
Pressure or not, regardless of wide receiver play, that's the kind of mistake that Willis has got to stop making.
The Dolphins don't have to make any determination about their quarterback situation until the next offseason, but all the folks calling for the team to spend their first-round pick on that position sure got some good arguments for their case on this day.
-- If we're discussing the wide receiver corps, it was great to see Chris Bell gain 26 yards on an end-around (props to good blocks by Aaron Brewer and Kadyn Proctor), but it's disappointing to not see him be more of a factor in the passing game. Bell still should become a productive NFL wide receiver, but he's not creating a ton of separation at this time.
-- And we've said it before and we'll say it again, Malik Washington easily is the best and most dependable wide receiver at this time, and it's not ideal when he's really like he should be a third wide receiver on a contending team.
-- For his troubles in the passing game, Willis showed again what he can do as a scrambler with 74 yards, including a long of 39. Willis has been reluctant to take off too early so far this season, but for the best results in 2026 maybe that's the way he needs to start operating.
-- Ollie Gordon II had another solid performance with 88 yards on 18 carries, and he's very obviously established himself as the top running back with De'Von Achane gone.
-- The kick coverage units set a bad tone with that long kickoff return allowed on the first play of the game, and this is where maybe the bottom of the roster needs to be churned some more if those players can't get the job done in the kicking game.
-- It didn't matter in the end, but at some point there'll need to be a conversation about Riley Patterson, who just can't be missing extra-point attempts.
-- Bradley Pinion, on the other hand, had a big game punting the ball and his floppy drop of the punt against San Francisco probably has been forgotten by now.
-- By yards alone, the defense did a good job of holding Cincinnati to only 307 total yards, but allowed a 9-for-13 third-down rate was a killer.
-- The pass defense didn't give up the big play, with one exception, but again gave up way too many easy completions underneath.
-- Even on that long touchdown pass from Joe Burrow to Ja'Marr Chase, Jason Marshall Jr. had great coverage but Chase made a great catch on the 50-50 ball and was victimized by bad luck as the ball hit Chase's shoulder pad first but bounded softly enough to allow him to still make what became an incredible catch.
-- After being a factor against Minnesota, Chop Robinson again was a complete non-factor, though it's not like Burrow was holding the ball very long. And then there was that bad offside penalty in the fourth quarter.
-- Jacob Rodriguez again piled up the tackle numbers in this game, but the reality is this wasn't a great game for the rookie linebacker. He was beaten in coverage for Cincinnati's first two touchdowns, though he did take a really accurate throw by Burrow on the TD pass to Samaje Perine.
-- So now the Dolphins are 0-5 heading into their bye with the New York Jets next in Week 7, and if it wasn't early obvious, the wins are going to be difficult to come by.

title: Five Dolphins Players Who Have To Deliver in Week 5
full_text:
If the Miami Dolphins take down the Cincinnati Bengals, a lot would need to go their way, including a complete team effort from top to bottom.
The losses that the Dolphins have piled up are slowly improving in terms of the margin of victory for the opponent. They went from an undefeated Minnesota team to a 2-2 Bengals squad that was expected to compete for the AFC North but has had a rough start to the season.
Regardless of which side of the ball the Dolphins are on, there are a few players who need to step up for Miami. Some of them are still looking for a breakout performance, while others already have impressed this season, but Cincinnati will provide some of their most difficult matchups thus far.
After getting removed from the injury report Friday without a status designation, Wright needs to have a breakout game. Ollie Gordon II did well with 100 rushing yards and the team's lone touchdown against the Vikings, but Miami's offense regressed whenever Wright (Who started for this game) took the field, being shut down for 7 yards.
Wright has been thrust into a serious role in the run game and has underperformed. The Dolphins will have their hands full against a stout Cincinnati run defense. Gordon will give everything he has to move the ball, but he can't be the only running back contributing in this game.
So far, Brewer has played well enough to justify his three-year contract extension back in June. He hasn't given up a single sack and has only committed three penalties in 226 snaps. Against Minnesota, he was near-perfect with no QB hits, penalties, and only one pressure.
However, Brewer will be matched up against his toughest assignment so far — nose tackle Dexter Lawrence. Cincinnati acquired Lawrence from the New York Giants ahead of the 2026 NFL draft in exchange for their first-round pick, and he's helped turn their defense into a reliable unit, coordinated by former Miami Hurricanes head coach Al Golden.
Lawrence is having a great start to the season with 10 tackles, a team-leading three sacks, and five tackles for a loss. He and Cincinnati's front seven are doing a great job against the run, allowing just under 100 rushing yards per game (99.5), which doesn't bode well for a Miami offense that'll want to, once again, rely on the run game.
There's no secret when it comes to beating the Bengals since Joe Burrow was drafted in 2020: defenses need to apply pressure on the Pro Bowl quarterback. He's an excellent passer who will make opponents pay if they give him time in the pocket, having thrown for 1,171 yards and seven touchdowns through the air so far this season.
However, he's also been sacked nine times. Both Pittsburgh and Jacksonville applied heavy pressure on Burrow over the course of their contests in the past two weeks, sacking him twice in each game, and the Steelers and Jaguars came out on top.
It just so happens that Miami's pass rush is coming off its most successful game of the season against the Vikings, spearheaded by Sieler who registered two sacks on Kyler Murray. He'll need to bring the momentum of that game to Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday.
Usually, Burrow has a plethora of talented wide receivers to throw to, but that might not be the case on Sunday as Ja'Marr Chase (concussion), Tee Higgins (groin/neck), and Colbie Young (knee) are questionable for this game.
After not having to deal with Justin Jefferson last week, the Dolphins could find themselves facing yet another battered and bruised receiver corps. However, their Achilles' heel against the Vikings was their inability to limit the tight end, TJ Hockenson, who put the offense on his back for 119 yards.
Brooks, who claimed responsibility for Miami's struggles against Hockenson, will need to do a better job maintaining Cincinnati's tight end and former member of the Dolphins, Mike Gesicki. If Chase, Higgins, or Young are out, that could mean an expanded role for Gesicki, who caught Cincinnati's only receiving touchdown of the game against Jacksonville.
Except for their two-score win over Houston, the Bengals have been in close games all season, defeating Tampa Bay by six points but losing to Pittsburgh and Jacksonville by three and five points, respectively.
This is to say that Cincinnati is no stranger to one-score games. The Dolphins could be in a position where they'll need to turn to Patterson to keep this game within reach, or maybe even take the lead. If that were to happen, Patterson better not miss.
Patterson has been perfect when it comes to mid-range kicks between 20 and 40 yards, but missed a 41-yard field goal against Las Vegas, then a 51-yarder against San Francisco. These are distances that are slowly becoming more automatic for the next generation of NFL kickers.
Granted, Patterson has been perfect in his last two games, but hasn't been tested at the aforementioned long-range distances. While almost no major media outlet is expecting a Dolphins upset, there are a fair share of predictions for a one-score win for the Bengals. In a situation like this, the difference between a win or loss could simply come down to a kick.

title: Breaking Down the Grant Transaction and the other Week 5 Dolphins Saturday Moves
full_text:
Kenneth Grant indeed will make his 2026 debut for the Miami Dolphins in their Week 5 game against the Cincinnati Bengals.
The Dolphins activated Grant off IR on Saturday after he practiced all week with no setbacks after missing the first four games of the regular season because of a toe injury.
To make room on the 53-man roster for Grant, the Dolphins waived Brady Cook, who had served as the emergency third quarterback for each of the first four games.
His release means the Dolphins will have only two quarterback available for the game against the Bengals, starter Malik Willis and Kyle McCord, though it's likely that Cook will be re-signed to the practice squad at some point after he clears waivers, as one would suspect he will.
Additionally, the Dolphins elevated running back Carlos Washington Jr. and edge defender Rodney McGraw from the practice squad for the Cincinnati game.
Washington will serve as the third running back behind Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon II because newcomer Kaytron Allen, claimed off waivers from the Washington Commanders on Friday, is too new to the team to be able to contribute right away.
Washington was on the 53-man roster for the game against the Minnesota Vikings last weekend and was active, but he did not play in the 15-10 loss.
McGraw is getting an elevation for a second consecutive game, a reward for making himself noticeable against the Vikings. This move indicates he's currently ahead of rookie seventh-round pick Max Llewellyn in the pecking order.
The one move the Dolphins didn't make was activating cornerback Storm Duck from Reserve/PUP after he was a full participant in practice all week.
Duck, who has been out recovering from his 2025 knee injury, was downgraded to OUT on a Saturday injury report.
He's got another full week of practice left before the Dolphins have to activate him or keep him on PUP for the rest of the 2026 season.
Grant clearly is a more significant player as the team's first-round pick in the 2025 NFL draft.
Grant will join the expected Dolphins rotation at defensive tackle alongside Zach Sieler, Jordan Philips and Zeek Biggers.
Without mentioning names, head coach Jeff Hafley indicated this week that Grant's presence provides more flexibility on the defensive line in terms of being able to use one of his interior defensive linemen outside, though Biggers logically is the player involved here.

full_text:

The Bengals are off to a 2-2 start, which is if anything a bit disappointing considering the lofty expectations some media members put on them after they beefed up their defense in the offseason with moves highlighted by the trade acquisition of former New York Giants DT Dexter Lawrence. Cincinnati has lost its last two games after Joe Burrow turned the ball over on a potential game-winning drive, a fumble against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3 and an interception against the Jacksonville Jaguars last Sunday. Burrow, though, remains the driving force for Cincinnati along with his star wide receiver tandem of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
-------------------------------------------------------------------
The Dolphins had chances to win in the fourth quarter of each of their last two games against Kansas City and Minnesota, and at some point they'll break through and make the plays down the stretch. The heat and humidity factor always should be considered for an early-season game at Hard Rock Stadium, but perhaps more significant is the fact that Chase and Higgins both missed practice time during the week.
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Chase and Higgins both practiced Friday, and both of them playing changes the outlook of this game quite considerably. With both in the lineup, Burrow passed for 309 yards and four touchdowns at Hard Rock Stadium last December, and this Dolphins defense probably isn't as good as the one Burrow torched 10 months ago. Unless the Dolphins can control that Cincinnati offense, it's hard to envision them being able to keep up considering they haven't scored more than 13 points in any game this season.
The Dolphins defense is stepping up in weight class big time in this matchup if Chase and Higgins both play, even if it's only Chase, and stopping the tight end will become a minor problem for Miami as opposed to a major talking point. With Caleb Douglas likely out for a third consecutive game, it's just very difficult to envision the Dolphins scoring enough to get that elusive first victory. At this point, merely scoring two touchdowns would represent progress. Final Prediction: Bengals 27, Dolphins 17

title: What to Know About New Dolphins RB Kaytron Allen
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins filled their one vacancy on their 53-man roster Friday by claiming another rookie draft pick, this time running back Kaytron Allen from the Washington Commanders.
Allen was a sixth-round pick out of Penn State who was waived this week after the Commanders brought back veteran Austin Ekeler.
Allen played in each of Washington's first four games and had 12 rushing attempts for 41 yards (3.4 average). He played 25 snaps on offense in those four games and another 29 on special teams.
The Dolphins had a roster opening since they waived fellow running back Carlos Washington Jr., who since has been re-signed to the practice squad.
Allen joins Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon II as running backs on the active roster, with De'Von Achane on IR and out for the season and Washington and Jarquez Hunter on the practice squad.
Heading into the draft, Allen was compared by NFL.com draft analyst Lance Zierlein to current Arizona Cardinals running back Tyler Allgeier and projected to go in the fifth round.
"Allen is productive with good size and vision but below-average explosiveness," Zierlein wrote before the draft. "He’s a fluid runner with ideal patience and a natural feel for when to cut off his blocks. He runs low to the ground with the strength to run through arm tackles and fall forward after contact. A feel for lane development allows him to fit any run scheme, but his lack of burst is likely to constrict the field and limit his ability to find explosive runs. Allen appears to lack third-down and special-teams value, but he could earn a spot as a solid backup."
In four seasons at Penn State, Allen averaged 1,045 yards a season, with a high of 1,303 yards in 2025 when he averaged 6.2 yards a carry and scored 15 touchdowns.
Allen was the ninth of 12 running backs selected in the 2026 draft.
Allen became the 13th player the Dolphins have claimed off waivers in 2026, a string that started in May when they landed defensive lineman James Ester from the Green Bay Packers and moved him to guard.
The Dolphins picked up seven players off waivers on August 31 after the roster cuts to the NFL limit of 53: QB Brady Cook (N.Y. Jets), CB Marcellas Dial Jr. (Dallas), T Chukwuebuka Godrick (Kansas City), TE Justin Joly (Denver), OL Jarrett Kingston (Houston), CB Reese Taylor (Denver) and S Julius Wood (Dallas).
Earlier in the summer (and at different times), the Dolphins got on waivers WR Ryan Miller from the New York Giants, CB Jai'Onte McMillan from the Indianapolis Colts, CB Ahmari Harvey from the Pittsburgh Steelers and TE Jeremiah Franklin from the New England Patriots.
Every player the Dolphins have claimed this year currently is on their 53-man roster except for Ester, who is on the practice squad; and McMillan, Harvey and Franklin, who were waived.

title: Vikings' Snap Count vs. Saints: Biggest Winners, Losers & Role Changes in Week 5
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings defeated the New Orleans Saints in Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season despite injuries piling up for the Purple and Gold and some important mistakes being made on the field.
The 23-13 victory keeps the Vikings undefeated heading into their bye week at a time when the rest should help multiple key players get healthy in time for the next game in two weeks against the Indianapolis Colts.
One key reason that Minnesota was able to keep its winning ways alive was how head coach Kevin O'Connell used the players he had available and how those players were able to contribute to Sunday's contest.
Here are five observations from the Vikings' snap counts against the Saints.
Starting tight end T.J. Hockenson was coming off a huge game against the Miami Dolphins where he caught 13 passes for 119 yards. Sadly, he only played two snaps before having to leave the game with a concussion.
Gavin Bartholomew stepped into his role and played 44 offensive snaps along with eight special teams snaps. He finished second on the team in receptions (5) and receiving yards (33) while earning a 71.3 Pro Football Focus grade for the game.
Typically, it is a great thing if a player is on the field for every possible snap. Even though Josh Metellus was one of only two players who were in the game for all 45 defensive snaps, he struggled mightily against New Orleans.
Metellus had the lowest PFF grade of all Minnesota defenders on Sunday (46.7). The problem is that the Vikings are trying to limit Harrison Smith's snaps but still maximize his efficiency. Meanwhile, Theo Jackson is getting 31 defensive snaps, and Jacob Thomas only got three.
Blake Cashman was the other defensive player to participate in all 45 defensive snaps. He turned that into a team-high nine tackles, one for a loss, and one quarterback hit, on his way to a 79.2 PFF grade for the game.
Defensive coordinator Brian Flores can't afford to take Cashman off the field this season. He is a stabilizing presence in the middle of the defense and deserves to play every possible snap if he is able to.
Jauan Jennings played 49 offensive snaps against the Saints. He was held without a catch and was only targeted once in the game. There is absolutely no chance that giving him that many reps is the most efficient thing for the offense.
He was outplayed by Jeshaun Jones and Tai Felton, both of whom had fewer offensive opportunities. After the bye, it wouldn't be shocking if Jones starts cutting into Jennings' snaps more significantly to get more value out of the routes.
When Hockenson left the game and didn't return, Bartholomew stepped into the receiving role at tight end, and Yurosek became the blocker. However, he showed that he could do a lot more than just block because he caught a pass on Sunday.
Yurosek can block to keep offensive tackle Caleb Tiernan from trying to do what Josh Oliver was doing before his season-ending injury. The fact that he was on the field for 39 offensive snaps and 14 special teams snaps shows how much the coaching staff believes in him.

title: Vikings Stock Report: Who's Rising (and Falling) After Impressive Week 5 Win
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings enter the bye at 5-0 after a dominating showing against the New Orleans Saints, and now have a week to get healthy before taking on the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7.
The Vikings' offense has finally started to inch closer to the defense after several weeks of mediocrity, and Minnesota is playing some of the best complementary football in the league. But while some players are on the rise, not everyone is pulling their weight through the perfect start.
So who is seeing their stock soar, and who is seeing their's tank in this week's stock report?
Murray's ascension continued again this week , culminating in his best performance to date with 283 total yards and a score. It's hard to imagine that it was just a few weeks ago that some fans were calling for Carson Wentz to start, but now Murray has this offense rolling. Plus, all it took was the low, low price of four weeks of absolute misery to get there.
He's 36-for-43 since the fourth quarter of the Miami Dolphins game, and the now-functional offense will be getting much healthier after the break, too. Have the Vikings found their quarterback for 2027 and beyond?
It was hard to find many weak spots in the Vikings' dominant win, but after another goose egg from Jennings, it's getting harder and harder to see what his future in Minnesota is. With just two catches on the season despite injuries to Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, Jennings is starting to look like a very expensive WR3 who doesn't add any value on special teams.
Now, that's not to say a trade is imminent, and the Vikings still seem to value his run-blocking. But Jennings is giving other pass catchers, including Odell Beckham Jr., every opportunity to steal his job. Maybe a week off will give the coaches some time to evaluate his role in the offense.
After losing T.J. Hockenson on the second play of the game, Bartholomew stepped up, notching five catches for 33 yards. He was inches shy of reeling in a long touchdown from Murray as well and finished second in receptions and yards, behind only Jefferson.
Bartholomew had some training camp hype, but had to wait his turn behind Hockenson and Josh Oliver. With both out on Sunday, he certainly made the most of his opportunity. While Hockenson will regain his starting status upon his return, Minnesota may look to work Bartholomew in more and more after proving he can handle the load.
Dallas saw just five offensive snaps in a game where Aaron Jones once again carried the load. Dallas' value has primarily been on special teams, but with Jordan Mason set to return after the bye, the Vikings likely won't keep four backs. Keeping a 27-year-old running back who doesn't contribute on offense is a tough sell to Vikings GM Nolan Teasley.
If Demond Claiborne remains a part of the Vikings' future plans, Dallas will surely be the odd man out. If he is released, he'll finish his time with Minnesota with three carries for 10 yards, four catches, and one incredible kick return block.
After a relatively quiet season, Murphy came alive against New Orleans with two interceptions. He was the highest-graded Viking in the win, notching an 86.7 overall grade from Pro Football Focus . With his productive day, Murphy is now tied for the league lead in picks.
The Vikings held Tyler Shough to just 96 passing yards and allowed 85 to Malik Willis the week prior. While Murphy and the secondary have allowed their fair share of big plays, they've remained a steady and redemptive bunch.

title: Harmon's Longship Week 5: Key Takeaways as Vikings Sail South to Defeat Saints for a 5-0 Start
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings are docking their ships and returning to shore for a bye-week rest after a decisive 23-13 victory against the struggling New Orleans Saints at the Caesars Superdome. While the scoreboard shows a ten-point game, it never felt that close.
The day's most encouraging moments came from the passing game and quarterback Kyler Murray, who's been fighting desperately to prove he fits in this offense. Here’s how the Vikings got it done in New Orleans and what it means for their pursuit of the ultimate prize.
Sunday’s game proved that Kyler Murray could and should thrive in Minnesota, even with five key offensive starters out with injury. Murray was decisive, patient, and strategic all afternoon. While all-22 footage from his first full game in Tampa Bay showed an internal clock that would send him scrambling before his receivers broke open, yesterday showcased a level of trust and patience in his weapons and line that we had yet to see.
Murray used his legs effectively to gain 51 yards on 10 scrambles, but on multiple plays, a conscious decision to stay in the pocket was evident. Good news: it worked.
Murray ended the best day of his short Viking tenure, completing 24-of-30 for 229 yards and a touchdown through the air. It's even more impressive considering the team lost T.J. Hockenson early after Jordan Addison was ruled out pregame. His gutsy, precise throw to Justin Jefferson over three defenders in the back of the end zone was a jaw-dropper, allowing the Louisiana native receiver to hit 'The Griddy' in front of his hometown crowd (h/t Vikings).
Speechless. @k1 @JJettas2 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/FOHP5Fh7oG
Murray still has room to grow, and head coach Kevin O’Connell still has much to learn about scheming for his specific skill set. But Sunday's passing performance is a reason for optimism, especially since Murray and his weapons have played 18 snaps together this season due to injury, per my count.
Brian Flores and his defense had another stellar day despite totaling only one sack. Saints QB Tyler Shough never caught his breath, as Flores’ unit attacked him all afternoon. At one point near the halfway mark, the Vikings blitzed on an astounding 90.9% of snaps per the FOX broadcast. Minnesota’s defensive backs also had a big day, with Byron Murphy Jr. coming away with two interceptions. Shough, who entered the game with the third-most passing yards in the league, was held to just 96 passing yards and no TDs. The Vikings defense just finds ways to dominate, even when they’re not stacking sacks.
Then there’s Will Reichard, who needs no introduction at this point. The Vikings’ elite kicker went a perfect 3-of-3 on field goals and 2-of-2 on extra points. Even with a positive day from the offense, Reichard’s 53 total points this season are higher than the offense's 50 total points through five weeks (h/t VikingzFanPage). Reichard is also on pace for the second-most points scored by a single player in a season (180). This would fall just six points shy of LaDainian Tomlinson’s 2006 record. His 34 straight field goals dating back to last season are only 10 shy of the NFL record set by Adam Vinatieri in 2016.
#Vikings K Will Reichard has more points (53) than the Vikings offense (50) this season. (Via @JasonHarmonNFL ) pic.twitter.com/Z8HzjBQ63l
The biggest takeaway from yesterday’s game is simple: let Kyler cook. When O’Connell leans into Murray’s skill set and doesn’t try to mold him into Sam Darnold, good things happen. While Murray's passing chart (h/t Will Ragatz) may have given 2024 KOC a jump scare, it's leading to winning football. Avoiding turnovers and dominating time of possession are the best ways to take advantage of the team’s stellar defense, and Murray looks poised to do just that.
If O’Connell can limit the procedural penalties and poorly timed trick-play calls, this offense could do exactly what it needs to for the Vikings to contend… especially once they’re back at full health.
I can’t believe I’m saying this, but thank goodness the Green Bay Packers won yesterday. The Pack’s 31-7 victory over the Tyson Bagent/Case Keenum-led Bears widened Minnesota’s division lead. Detroit, Chicago, and Green Bay are now 3-2, while Minnesota holds a comfortable 5-0 record, including 2-0 in divisional games. The Vikings can build an even larger division lead if they defeat the Lions in Week 8.
The rest of the NFC looks wide open, with San Francisco looking like the Vikings’ biggest threat in the conference. The two teams will meet in Mexico City on November 22 in what could be the game of the year. At this point in the season, I’m feeling confident that the eventual NFC champion will come from the NFC North or West.
I can’t wait for November 22. pic.twitter.com/GsEBzHXm6v
The Vikings now enter the bye week in desperate need of recovery. While I typically dislike an early bye, Minnesota’s list of injuries on offense is too long to be sustainable. O’Connell hopes to have Christian Darrisaw, T.J. Hockenson, Jordan Addison, and Jordan Mason all back as the Vikings host the Colts after the bye , per Will Ragatz.
Listening to Kevin O’Connell, it sounds like Jordan Addison, Jordan Mason, Christian Darrisaw, and T.J. Hockenson all have a realistic shot to return after the Vikings' bye.
The reinforcements would be crucial for an offense that will face a much harder schedule starting in November. For now, the Vikings rest, and fans can celebrate a hard-fought and often ugly 5-0 start.

title: 3 Studs & 3 Duds From Vikings' Week 5 Win Against the Saints
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings got the job done on the road against the New Orleans Saints in Week 5. With the 23-13 win , the Purple and Gold remain undefeated heading into the team's much-needed bye week.
This was not an easy game for the Vikings. Two turnovers kept the Saints within striking distance for most of the game, but Minnesota's defense and solid special teams performance kept the door closed on any hope for New Orleans to escape with a win.
Needless to say, several great performances from multiple players helped Minnesota stay undefeated on Sunday afternoon. Here are the studs and duds from Minnesota's Week 5 contest against the Saints.
The Vikings had two interceptions against Saints quarterback Tyler Shough, and both of them were hauled in by veteran cornerback Byron Murphy Jr. Minnesota needed those takeaways after losing two fumbles of their own in this game.
Murphy added three tackles, including one for a loss. His awareness and ability to track the ball in the air were major factors in determining Sunday's game, considering Shough was held to under 100 passing yards for the first time this season.
Aaron Jones Sr. had a good day, rushing 25 times for 113 yards and a touchdown. He also added three receptions for four yards. However, Jones' second-half fumble inside the red zone led to New Orleans' only offensive touchdown of the day.
That said, Jones shouldn't be the only running back carrying the workload. At the same time, DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne didn't have a single carry against the Saints and combined for two catches for 17 yards, while the veteran Jones had to do all the work on the ground.
For a player who was questionable on the injury report, Jefferson looked ready to go against the Saints. The superstar wide receiver was targeted seven times by Kyler Murray and caught six of those for 79 yards and a touchdown.
OH MY JETTAS ✈️ @MINvsNO on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/9JQWo9ugMo
Seeing Minnesota get into the end zone on Sunday was a thing of beauty, especially with how much the Vikings have struggled offensively lately. Seeing Murray trust Jefferson in a crowd of New Orleans defenders in the back corner of the end zone was both surprising and welcome.
Another week, another dud from Jennings. At this point, it is hard to know what is holding the former 49ers receiver back from contributing in Minnesota. Also, Jennings is being outplayed by Tai Felton and Jeshaun Jones, which is not good.
Jennings was the only Vikings player to be targeted by Murray and not catch a pass. He now has two catches on four targets for nine yards this season, which likely has general manager Nolan Teasley wondering why he signed the free-agent pass catcher in the first place.
If the season ended today, kicker Will Reichard would be the team's MVP. He remained perfect this season, connecting on two extra points and three field goals on Sunday, including a great kick from 55 yards out as the clock expired at the end of the first half.
The FOX broadcast said that Reichard has made 57 consecutive kicks, including field goals and extra points. Vikings fans should be extremely happy to hear that, but longtime fans might also feel uneasy hearing that statistic.

title: Vikings Take Down Saints to Stay Undefeated (Here Are 3 Things That Mattered Most in Week 5)
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings traveled south to battle the Saints in New Orleans on Sunday in what quickly turned into a chaotic matchup. Star receiver Justin Jefferson returned after hurting his ankle in Week 3 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, while Jordan Addison was inactive with a hamstring injury . The newly signed Odell Beckham Jr. was elevated from the practice squad on Saturday but was ultimately ruled inactive shortly before the game.
In an odd twist, the Vikings offense dominated the day with 364 yards of total offense. But Brian Flores’ unit still had its moments. Outside linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel had the team’s one sack, and corner Byron Murphy Jr. came away with two interceptions.
Here’s what else mattered as the Vikings remain undefeated at the bye.
Despite a plethora of miscues, including multiple timeouts to avoid delay-of-game penalties, two red zone fumbles, some questionable play calls, and a few mistimed throws that could have been touchdowns, the Vikings’ offense looked pretty cohesive.
Kyler Murray had the best game of his Vikings career, totaling 229 yards through the air, 51 on the ground, and a gutsy touchdown throw to Jefferson between three Saints defenders in the back of the end zone. Jefferson’s three TDs in 2026 have already exceeded his total from last season (2).
Justin Jefferson, in triple coverage —HOW DID HE CATCH THIS?! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/jaBttL0Apb
Aaron Jones powered through an aggravated knee injury to find the end zone and rushed for 113 yards on the ground. Jones is the workhorse for a Minnesota RB room that desperately needs depth. Hopefully, Jordan Mason is cleared to return from the thumb injury that landed him on the IR after the bye week.
Once again, Will Reichard was the most trustworthy force on the entire Vikings’ roster, nailing another three field goals, including a 55-yarder. Reichard has now hit 34 straight field goals to start the 2026 season, accounting for 53 total points this year.
Myles Price also showed his skills as a returner, making it easier to forgive his brutal fumble on offense. Price continued to flash his patterned evasiveness on returns, including an impressive 43-yard punt return.
Rookie linebacker Jake Golday punched the ball out on the Saints’ kickoff return to start the second half, with wideout Jeshaun Jones recovering the fumble, setting up the Vikings' first offensive touchdown since the second quarter of Week 3.
Special teams coordinator Matt Daniels has put together quite the group, and the multiple awards the unit has won so far this season continue to speak to the unit’s impact.
Tight end T.J. Hockenson looked primed for a big day after building a strong connection with Kyler Murray against Miami last week. Unfortunately, his day would not last long, as he left the game on the first drive to be evaluated for a concussion. Jones aggravated a knee injury on a fumble near the goal line but returned.
The Vikings head into the bye hoping to recover and reload before hosting the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7. Christian Darrisaw is working through a concussion ; Mason will be eligible to return from IR; Addison seems likely to return from a hamstring injury, and Hockenson will hope to be out of concussion protocol.
If the Vikings are 5-0 with significant injury issues, we can only hope to see what they can do at full strength.

title: Why Odell Beckham Jr. Might Have an Even Bigger Vikings Role Than Expected on Sunday
full_text:
UPDATE: The Vikings announced on Sunday morning that Beckham Jr. and Addison will both be inactive for today's game.
Vikings WR Justin Jefferson is ACTIVE for today's game against the Saints. WR Jordan Addison INACTIVE. WR Odell Beckham Jr. INACTIVE.
The Minnesota Vikings are in a sticky situation at wide receiver heading into Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season. Although the team signed Odell Beckham Jr. to the practice squad earlier this week, there is a good chance he could see the field on Sunday.
On Saturday afternoon, the Vikings elevated Beckham Jr. and Jeshaun Jones from the practice squad to the 53-man roster.
An ankle injury limited superstar pass catcher Justin Jefferson during practice this week, and he is listed as questionable for the game against the New Orleans Saints. Vikings WR2 Jordan Addison is on the injury report with a hamstring injury and is also questionable for the game.
If Jefferson and Addison are unable to play this week, Minnesota can't trust Jauan Jennings and Tai Felton to pick up the slack. Those two receivers have been non-factors this season despite getting offensive opportunities in previous games.
Beckham's recent history isn't very impressive. He hasn't caught a pass since Week 14 of the 2024 season and hasn't scored a touchdown since Week 14 of the 2023 season. However, he is a three-time Pro Bowl receiver who won Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2014, opening the door for him to contribute.
Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell needs to do whatever he can to spark this offense. The Vikings are ranked last in the league in passing yards per game (156) and have four passing touchdowns and two interceptions.
Giving quarterback Kyler Murray a veteran target with Beckham's accolades could create mismatches and assist other pass catchers in getting open. Even though he turns 34 years old later this year, this could be a great opportunity for the Super Bowl LVI champion to prove he still has gas left in his tank.
Even if Jefferson and Addison can suit up and play against the Saints, having them on the field for every offensive snap isn't wise. Therefore, having a capable player to take some of the weight off their shoulders will help.
If a player has to play while not being fully healthy, there's a calculated risk of aggravating the injury and forcing him to be out longer. Since Minnesota has a bye week in Week 6, it would make a lot of sense to play Jefferson and Addison as little as possible against New Orleans to give them the maximum amount of time to recover before returning from the bye.
That said, with Beckham being elevated to the 53-man roster, let's hope he can turn those opportunities into positive plays for Minnesota on Sunday afternoon.

title: Vikings at Saints: Who Wins and Why in Week 5
full_text:
It's Week 5, and the Minnesota Vikings have a few concerning injuries to monitor ahead of Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints. Christian Darrisaw has already been ruled out, and both Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison are questionable. Not ideal.
Still, the Saints' defense hasn't exactly been a model of consistency, and the Vikings will have opportunities to move the ball in New Orleans. So let's get into who wins and why in Minnesota's attempt to go 5-0 before the bye.
The Vikings offense is certainly getting plenty of chances to break out of their funk, getting the disastrous Miami Dolphins in Week 4 and now the 1-3 Saints in Week 5.
Outside of a Week 2 win against Baltimore, the Saints defense has been torched for 37 points per game in their other three contests, earning them the 32nd-ranked scoring defense in the NFL. That's welcome news for a Vikings team that is averaging just 21 points per game themselves.
Kyler Murray and the Minnesota offense looked respectable in the fourth quarter last week, going 13-for-14 for 120 yards against Miami. Bringing that momentum into New Orleans should be doable, but Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison's health could be a hindrance if one or both are limited. Newcomer Odell Beckham Jr. may see his first action of the season, which could be entertaining if nothing else.
The deciding factor in this game, though, could be how backup tackle Ryan Van Demark protects Murray's blindside. The Saints brought down Lamar Jackson three times, and without Christian Darrisaw, Murray may be sent on a running tour of the Superdome.
Tyler Shough is top-five in the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns, and without starting running back Travis Etienne, he will be asked to carry the load again. He's thrown fewer than 40 times just once this year, so the Saints will almost surely be looking to air things out again. That's potentially a blessing for a blitz-happy Brian Flores, who could add to the 12 sacks Shough has already taken this year.
As for the run game, the six-touchdown Alvin Kamara of 2020 (not one of our better days) is far removed from the 2026 version, who has averaged just three yards per carry this season. Instead, the Vikings' secondary will get its first real test since Jordan Love in Week 1.
Even though Isaiah Rodgers and James Pierre have been extremely reliable this season, the same can't be said for the Vikings' safeties, who have allowed plenty of big plays on the back end.
Harrison Smith and Joshua Metellus are considered bottom-five safeties in the league by Pro Football Focus , but it doesn't take much more than a quick eye test to see they've been burned far too many times.
Saints receiver Chris Olave leads the NFL in receiving yards, and it's not unfathomable to think he has another big day against Minnesota's secondary.
Still, the Saints are probably too one-dimensional on offense to keep Dallas Turner and the rest of the pass rushers at bay. Without a running game threat, there's no reason Flores won't continue his 70% blitz rate in Week 5.

title: Vikings Have 3 Clear Advantages Over Saints in Week 5
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings hope to keep their winning ways alive on Sunday when they take on the New Orleans Saints. There is not much love between these two organizations, since they have caused each other heartbreak for many years.
One team will be leaving the Caesars Superdome with a loss on Sunday and it would be devastating if the team to hand Minnesota its first loss of the season was a team like the hated Saints.
Minnesota has some clear advantages over New Orleans that should make the difference in this weekend's game. If the Vikings can make the most of those opportunities , they should get a big road win to take them into the bye week with an undefeated record.
The Saints are tied for giving up the fourth-most sacks in the league through four games. They will need to do a great job protecting Tyler Shough against the aggressive pursuit of Brian Flores' defense.
New Orleans is going to struggle to keep pass rushers out of the backfield on Sunday. The Pro Football Focus grades for their offensive linemen tell a story of a team that is going to need to keep extra blockers to protect their quarterback.
The pass blocking of the tackles should play right into the hands of Minnesota edge rushers Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel. The tackles on the offensive line for the Saints are Taliese Fuaga and Asim Richards, both of whom have a PFF pass-blocking grade of under 50 for the season.
If the offensive line holds up for New Orleans on Sunday, it could be a long day for Minnesota's defensive secondary. The Saints are not only tied for the fourth-most passing touchdowns in the league (9), but they also have the fifth-most passing plays of 20 yards or more (15) and are tied for the seventh-most passing plays of 40 yards or more (3).
The bad thing for New Orleans is that Minnesota is allowing the lowest completion percentage to opposing quarterbacks (51.2) while being tied for the fewest passing touchdowns allowed (3) and racking up a league-high 16 sacks.
It is going to be interesting to watch the Saints try to pass against the Vikings in Week 5 and see which side wins this battle of strengths.
Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson had a huge game against the Dolphins last week. His 13 catches for 119 yards isn't likely to happen again, but he will create a tough matchup for New Orleans, particularly for the linebackers who try to take him down after catching the ball.
On the injury report , starting Saints linebacker Kaden Elliss is listed as out with a calf injury, while edge rusher Anfernee Jennings is also out with a knee injury. Not only that, but Jaylan Ford is questionable, and Carl Granderson was limited in practice earlier this week with an ankle injury.
New Orleans is all banged up in the middle of their defense, and Hockenson should be licking his chops at the opportunity to have another great day with Kyler Murray throwing him the football.

title: Vikings' WR Depth Will Be Tested If Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison Can't Play vs. Saints
full_text:
The Vikings released their final Week 5 injury report on Friday , and it could significantly impact Sunday’s game against the Saints in New Orleans (h/t: Vikings). Star left tackle Christian Darrisaw was confirmed to be out as he works through a concussion . Rookie corner and fan favorite Charles “Chuck” Demmings will also miss the game with a hamstring injury.
While confirmation of their status was disappointing, neither player being ruled out was a surprise.
Final #Vikings Week 5 injury report OUT: Christian Darrisaw and Chuck Demmings QUESTIONABLE: Jordan Addison, Justin Jefferson, Michael Jurgens*, Brian O’Neill and Ben Yurosek* *Currently in 21-day return to practice window pic.twitter.com/TLCCJUfUFF
The real intrigue came from the list of questionable players. Starting right tackle Brian O’Neill’s status is uncertain due to a knee injury, adding to concerns about an already depleted offensive line. Most significantly, the inclusion of wide receivers Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison suggests the team may be without both of its top receiving options.
Unfortunately for Vikings fans, the current depth at the position means Sunday’s game could get very interesting.
Let’s do what we can only assume head coach Kevin O’Connell is doing and mentally prepare for what Sunday could look like without Jefferson and Addison.
If neither can play, the WR room will likely include Jauan Jennings, Tai Felton, Myles Price, and practice-squad elevations for Jeshaun Jones and the newly signed Odell Beckham Jr. Based on the group’s production so far this season , they’ll need to hope someone in the room has a breakout performance.
Possible Vikings WR group for Sunday in New Orleans and their 2026 stats: *Jefferson and Addison listed as Questionable* - Jauan Jennings: 2 receptions for 9 yards. - OBJ: 0 receptions for 0 yards. -Tai Felton: 1 reception for 14 yards. - Myles Price: 2 receptions for 6…
Jennings would, in theory, be the team’s WR1 if Jefferson and Addison were to be ruled out. While his 2026 season has been a disappointment, the film tells a different story. Jennings is getting open , but he’s often too far down the list of progressions for Kyler Murray to find him while he works to figure out the timing of the offense (h/t: JClyyde)
WR Separation Score vs TPRR 📊 -- Carnell Tate building chemistry with Ward -- Downs, Doubs, Odunze, Pickens prime targets for positive regression -- MHJ in a league of his own pic.twitter.com/kDtxG8H22T
Felton, a 2025 third-rounder, looked to be coming into his own during this summer’s training camp, but has yet to make an impact so far this season. His inconsistent route-running makes him hard to count on in the passing game , but the team may not have a choice on Sunday.
Price is another interesting name to watch, as the special teams star flashed skills at the WR position during the preseason. But one name would naturally get all of the attention…
The Vikings signed the 33-year-old Beckham to the practice squad earlier this week. O’Connell’s comments to the press after his signing indicate he’s likely to be elevated regardless of Jefferson or Addison’s availability.
Beckham has largely been a non-factor in the league since totaling 565 receiving yards with the Ravens in 2023, before not even playing in the 2025 season. But his relationship with O’Connell from their Super Bowl run with the Rams, and the team's desperation in the passing game, could create opportunities on Sunday.
Luckily, I don't think anything short of an apocalyptic event will keep Justin Jefferson off the field on Sunday. His mid-week comments to the media made it clear he intends to play in what would be his first professional game in front of a crowd in his home state (h/t: ESPN' s Kevin Seifert).
Justin Jefferson on playing Sunday in New Orleans: "Hopefully so. That's definitely the plan. Being back at home, being in Louisiana, is definitely something that I want to do. So the plan is for me to play, but who knows? We going to take it day by day."
Addison’s status seems to be more of a mystery, but having one or both available on Sunday could help the offense find a desperately needed stride before the bye.

title: One Thought on All 11 Vikings Defensive Starters One Month Into the 2026 Season
full_text:
On Thursday, I broke down my thoughts on each of the Vikings' offensive starters now that the first month of the 2026 regular season is behind us. Today, let's dive into the defense and give one thought on each of the starters there.
The unit led by Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores is playing among the best in the NFL, and it's no secret they've propelled the team to a 4-0 record.
Here are some quick hits about each Vikings defender's start to the season.
The Year 3 breakout is officially underway as Turner ranks second in the NFL in sacks with 5.5. He's also got a whopping 29 pressures through four games, but many have been quick to point out that 16 of those 29 were either unblocked or against a running back or tight end.
Still, Turner is a beast off the edge, and should never apologize for having a mad, scheming defensive coordinator getting him into favorable one-on-ones.
One of, if not the most underrated defenders in the league, Van Ginkel is once again playing at an All-Pro level this season.
With one of the most impressive stat lines in the NFL, with three sacks, three tackles for loss, an interception, and a forced fumble, 'Gink' truly does it all. In a contract year at 31 years old, his situation heading into next season will be something to monitor.
The sacks haven't been there in 2026 after a breakout season with six last year, but don't be fooled. Redmond is still playing really good football. His 90.1 Pro Football Focus run grade ranks first among all interior defensive linemen, and he has nine pressures to boot.
Redmond will be another big payday candidate in 2027.
A former seventh-round pick now starting is a success story in itself, but it isn't because the Vikings have no other options. Despite investing heavily up front in this year's draft, Rodriguez has been playing at a high level, notching six tackles and a sack at nose. The future is probably with Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange, but Rodriguez's relentless motor and ferocity will still be valued on this defense for a long time.
Yet another Kwesi Adofo-Mensah pick getting some run after the former general manager's departure, Ingram-Dawkins has been a nice stopgap in 2026. Like Rodriguez, he likely isn't the Vikings' long-term plans as a starter, but he's flashed at times, especially in the run game with two stuffs. Ingram-Dawkins came back in Year 2 leaner and potentially meaner, and is a key part of one of the best (and least expensive) defensive lines in the league.
If Van Ginkel is the most underrated defender in the league, Cashman may be a close second. The veteran has 15 straight games with at least seven tackles, the longest in franchise history, and has added 2.5 sacks so far this year for good measure.
Unfortunately, he's missed at least three games in each of his seasons with Minnesota, so here's to hoping he stays healthy in 2026.
Wilson had one elite game against Tampa Bay (10 tackles, 1.5 sacks) and three average ones beside it (14 tackles, no sacks). The 32-year-old was rewarded with a new deal after a breakout in 2025, and so far the results have clearly been mixed. He's definitely a player Flores loves, though, and as long as he can avoid accidental contact with officials this year, he'll remain a valuable piece.
The Vikings CB1 may actually be playing worse than CB2/3 this year. Murphy had a huge pick against Chicago, but otherwise has 15 catches allowed to just two breakups. The constant pressure Flores sends at opposing quarterbacks is also doing a pretty good job of keeping it off of Murphy.
Murphy is a solid corner, but he's yet to play up to his $54 million contract signed last March.
Rodgers has been playing some lights-out football in 2026 after a modest 2025 season outside of the wild Cincinnati game. He's allowing just 37% of passes thrown his way to be completed, combined with a 36.1 quarterback rating when targeted. Rodgers and James Pierre have been two bright spots in an otherwise troubling secondary.
If you look up from your bowl of guac and see an opposing receiver walking into the endzone, there's a decent chance Metellus was the closest defender. It's been a rough year on the back end for Metellus, who has been best deep on multiple occasions.
Metellus has allowed nearly 25 yards per reception when targeted, although part of that can be attributed to Flores constantly sending the other 10 guys at the quarterback. He's a team captain and leader, but there's no question he's been more of a liability than not.
It hurts to type, but Smith is playing like his age. His return was celebrated, as it should have been, but the play on the field has been rough. Still, his value at this stage is more about his brain than his brawn, and the Vikings are likely benefiting in ways not super apparent to the average viewer. He is graded as the third-worst safety in the NFL by PFF, for what it's worth.

title: Ventola: Patriots Rookie Class Criminally Underrated in Recent Rankings
full_text:
In a recent ranking of all 32 teams' rookie classes by On SI's Justin Melo , the New England Patriots' 2026 draftees were placed 24th, a criminally underrated ranking for a group which has already made substantial contributions just five weeks into their careers.
Here's how New England's rookie class has proven itself to be far better than the subpar ranking it earned.
Lomu has had a limited role early this season for the Patriots, but has impressed in the opportunities he has gotten.
New England drafted the former Utah lineman in the first round as the long-term replacement to veteran right tackle Morgan Moses. Through the Patriots' first four games of the season, Lomu had solely been used on a limited snap count in relief of Moses and as a jumbo tight end.
However, on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders, Lomu had his first opportunity for extended playing time. When starting left tackle Will Campbell went down with an injury early in the matchup, Lomu stepped up.
All of Caleb Lomu's snaps at Left Tackle yesterday in his Rookie Debut for the Patriots Thought he was pretty solid in pass pro, lost a few reps to the outside, but overall pretty good showing pic.twitter.com/E9GUBWslr2
The 21-year-old allowed just one pressure on his 25 pass blocking snaps. The 4% pressure rate allowed was second-best among New England linemen, behind just Alijah Vera Tucker (0 pressures on 38 pass blocks).
"I don't think it was too big for him," head coach Mike Vrabel said regarding Lomu's performance. "I think he was able to settle down. You didn't really notice him a lot, so I think that's probably a good thing. He was able to anchor at times on some power and allowed Drake (Maye) to be able transfer up into the pocket. I thought it worked together well with (Alijah Vera-Tucker) when he got in there."
While Lomu hasn't quite contributed on a game-by-game, play-by-play basis, he has thrived in his role as a sixth lineman and emergency fill-in.
The start to Jacas' tenure in New England was filled with its fair share of turmoil. However, since then, the second-round pick has helped revitalize the Patriots' edge rusher room. The 22-year-old's top-tier strength has shown up through the first five weeks of his career.
Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas are DUDES pic.twitter.com/Hbj8saXg75
"He cares an extreme amount," Vrabel said on Sept. 20. "He comes in early; he stays late; he's with (outside linebackers coach) Mike Smith; he works with me; he works with all the coaches; he cares about his teammates. He goes hard, makes mistakes. The thing about Gabe is that he can work through mistakes, and I think that's really critical for any young player trying to improve."
Through his first five career games, Jacas has tallied 1.5 sacks, 17 total tackles and an interception.
When Raridon was first drafted, it seemed uncertain he would have an opportunity to carve out a substantial role in the Patriots' offense. However, after veteran Julian Hill suffered a season-ending injury in the summer, Raridon was quickly thrown into the fire as the Patriots' second tight end.
The rookie has taken full advantage of his opportunities thus far. Raridon has shown flashes of being a true multi-tool player for New England's offense. Against the Raiders, the 22-year-old caught all five of his targets for 57 yards.
Rookie TE Eli Raridon's 5 targets against the Raiders this week You can really see the athleticism and speed when they get him on crossers. Also love how he slightly sold his route being in the flat, before getting upfield on the wheel route. He finished with 5 catches for… pic.twitter.com/jQ2HtrC7yk
"I think it was good to see Eli work at the line of scrimmage, block a little bit, but then also be able to get out and do some things in the pass game and things that he'll have to improve on," Vrabel said on Monday about Raridon's performance in Week 5. "If you're targeted five times as a tight end, you want five catches."
While the Patriots' first few draft picks have gotten extended looks early on, New England has also gotten plenty of contributions on the back-end of its roster from a handful of rookies. Five of the team's six picks on the final day of the NFL Draft made the 53-man roster. The team also currently carries a trio of undrafted free agents, with another two currently on injured reserve.
Operating with a roster fresh off a Super Bowl appearance, which has since made signifcant upgrades through trades and free agency, the Patriots still getting valuable play out of late-round and undrafted rookies is a positive sign for what the group can do in the future.
From the significant contributions by early-round pick to the work being done by the rest of the Patriots' rookies, ranking New England's draft class 24th is simply blasphemous.

title: Patriots Don't Have Clear Update on TreVeyon Henderson's Ankle Injury Just Yet
full_text:
FOBXORO — TreVeyon Henderson missed the New England Patriots' first game of the year with an ankle injury he suffered in practice. Another ankle injury forced him out of their Week 5 game as well, and now he might miss some more time.
The Patriots, in the midst of their 45-17 drubbing of the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday , were forced to go the entire second half without Henderson and offensive tackle Will Campbell — who both got banged up on the same drive in the second quarter.
The second-year running back had four carries for 22 yards, and one reception for 16 yards on a lateral play from wide receiver Efton Chism III . He was slow to get up on the sideline, and then after a few snaps, would depart to the sideline. Henderson wouldn't go into the blue medical tent, and would walk to the locker room ahead of halftime.
Henderson would be spotted walking in the locker room after the game once reporters entered.
Speaking on Monday, head coach Mike Vrabel shared an update on Henderson's ankle — and how he's in a similar boat to Campbell this close to the game ending.
"We'll evaluate here and see how it looks," Vrabel said. "Wasn't able to finish the game, and you know, if we see that on Wednesday he's going to be limited, then we'll let you know he'll be limited. And I know that those two players will do everything that they can to get back, but unfortunately, they weren't able to finish the game.
"So I don't know where their availability will be just less than 24 hours after the game."
The Patriots would have to go the rest of the way with just Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner in the backfield. Vrabel calling the running game "inconsistent" postgame, as Stevenson (13 carries, 64 yards, one touchdown) had some productive runs, but nothing was able to be stretched out for all four quarters.
On Kiner's first carry of the game, he had the ball punched out by former Patriots defensive tackle Adam Butler.
"There was some good ones in there, and then we got too many for, you know, no yardage," Vrabel said Sunday. "We just wanna be able to stay consistent with that. But there was some good ones there at the end, and I thought it was just enough, and Drake made some good decisions with his legs."
Both Henderson and Campbell underwent tests Monday, and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that Campbell is believed to have suffered a knee bruise on the same knee that he tore his MCL in a season ago. That injury could force him to the sidelines for a little bit, putting some more stress on an already-banged up offensive line unit.
"It'll get looked at and (Campbell will) continue to rehab," Vrabel confirmed. "(He) wasn't able to finish the game."
Rookie Caleb Lomu would likely step up at left tackle if Campbell isn't able to go next week.
Edge rusher Dre'Mont Jones and cornerback Charles Woods also left the game with shoulder injuries. Defensive tackle Cory Durden also got rolled up on late.
We'll get another update on Henderson and his status on Wednesday when the Patriots take the field for their first practice of Week 6. If Henderson isn't able to go, the Patriots could potentially elevate second-year back Lan Larison from the practice squad. He made his NFL debut in Week 1 in Seattle .

title: Drake Maye's Confidence Never Wavered — And It Showed in Patriots Win
full_text:
Drake Maye, ladies and gentlemen. Just a few weeks after the sky was falling ( and I said it's time for concern ), the New England Patriots quarterback rebounded back to his normal self.
He was surgical, mistake-free and operated with conviction as the Patriots trounced the Las Vegas Raiders, 45-17, at Gillette Stadium. Maye had five total touchdowns, one of them with his legs, and just took full control of an offense down several starters.
A.J. Brown. Mack Hollins. Mike Onwenu. TreVeyon Henderson. Will Campbell .
It didn't matter for Maye, who returned to his usual confident poise under center. He says his confidence remains sky-high for every game, but he just looked like a totally different player than he did in losses to Seattle and Jacksonville.
"I'm gonna be confident going into every game," Maye said postgame. "I'm confident in the guys around me, confident in myself, and I think it's just really just an example of practice execution showing up in the game."
With no Brown and Hollins recently placed on IR with a calf injury, it was a slim wide receivers room for the Patriots. They entered the game with just four on the active roster, and only two of them had really made dents to this point.
All of them contributed in the win , with DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams both finding the end zone for the first time this season. Romeo Doubs helped move the chains by drawing two defensive pass interference calls, and Efton Chism III caught five balls.
But their play was elevated by their quarterback, who gave them catchable balls and put them in positions to succeed.
"It's just awesome for me to see guys like Caleb (Lomu) getting in there and playing his butt off and different guys and Pop (Douglas) have been playing and running routes well all year and finally getting rewarded," Maye said. "I just love to see guys that do the right things over and over and finally get rewarded in the game, and I think that's one of the best things about my position is able to spread the wealth and see other guys succeed and it's beautiful to watch."
After a few weeks where a bad turnover (or two, or three) felt like a given, there was no worry about if Maye might throw a costly interception this week . He delivered the ball with speed and accuracy, and had the footwork to move in and out of the pocket with ease. Maye completed 26 passes on 34 attempts and finished with a quarterback rating of 150.9 (the highest it can be is 158.3).
He's now sitting at 3-2 and could end up being back in first place if the Buffalo Bills lose . But more important, the Patriots feel like they can lean on the 24-year-old Maye. His confidence remains even-keeled, and now the results are starting to show.
"I'm gonna come into every game and every week and attack it, and I'm confident in myself and my abilities and the guys around me," Maye said.

title: 5 Winners, 2 Losers in Patriots' Blowout Win Over Raiders
full_text:
The New England Patriots are back to a winning record for the first time this season. The team dominated the Las Vegas Raiders in Gillette Stadium on Sunday, 45-17.
From domination in the trenches to depth pieces stepping up in their increased roles, here are the biggest winners, and losers, from Sunday's victory.
Another week, another step up for Maye. The third-year signal caller tossed just one touchdown and seven interceptions through the Patriots' first three games of the season. A week ago against the Buffalo Bills, he tossed for three scores and combined for a pair of turnovers.
But against the Raiders, Maye was near-perfect. The 24-year-old scored five touchdowns (four passing, one rushing), completed over 76% of his passes and had his first turnover-free game of the year.
"It was beautiful to be a part of today," Maye said after the win. "(Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels) was clicking on all cylinders, making us look good, and we were executing. I think that's what it's like when we put some things together and, and we still have some. I mean, it's crazy to say we still got some, some left to to squeeze."
The Patriots traded for Kiner prior to roster cuts to be the team's third running back. Prior to Sunday's battle with the Raiders, the former Arizona Cardinal had fit that role perfectly.
However, against Las Vegas, Kiner was responsible for New England's sole turnover of the day. On his first rush attempt of the day, with the Patriots up by just one possession, the 24-year-old had the ball punched away from him to give the Raiders possession in field-goal range.
Heading into Sunday, Douglas had a very tame stat-line on the season: just nine receptions for 82 yards and no touchdowns. Against the Raiders, however, he had one of his best performances of his career.  The 25-year-old caught four passes for 65 yards and a pair of scores, marking his first-ever multi-touchdown day.
"It's just awesome for me to see guys like Caleb getting in there and playing his butt off and different guys and (Douglas) have been playing and running routes well all year and finally getting rewarded," Maye said on Sunday. "I just love to see guys that do the right things over and over and finally get rewarded in the game, and I think that's one of the best things about my position is able to spread the wealth and see other guys succeed and it's beautiful to watch."
When the Patriots drafted Lomu in April, the plan seemed for him to be an "in case of emergency" option at tackle as he developed to be the long-term replacement to Morgan Moses. On Sunday, however, that emergency situation arose. New England's first-round pick played 49 snaps after left-side starter Will Campbell suffered an injury.
In Lomu's action, he allowed just one pressure. Plus, the 21-year-old wasn't called for any penalties.
"Just proud of our offensive line, and I wanna recognize them," Vrabel said after the win. "I thought that they understood what the protection was and how to keep the middle of the pocket clean...And so that's a testament to them for understanding what they have to be able to do, and guys stepped up. You know, Caleb [Lomu] had to go in there, and, you know, everybody, we had all hands on deck."
While Campbell and Lomu held their own at left tackle, Moses had his struggles on the right side. The veteran allowed three pressures and a quarterback hit in his 38 pass block snaps. Even worse, however, were the penalties.
Moses was flagged twice on Sunday, each in detrimental situations. The 35-year-old was called for holding on a third-and-2. Later on that same drive, he was penalized for a false start on first-and-goal from the 1-yard line. While New England fought through both calls, those easily could have wiped points off the board.
Heading into the afternoon, the Patriots were incredibly thin at cornerback. New England was without starters Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis III, plus depth pieces Karon Prunty and Channing Canada. One of only three players active at the position on Sunday, Vildor stepped up.
The 28-year-old allowed just two receptions and broke up a pass in the five targets he saw. He also forced a fumble on Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers.
"Just exactly what we would expect," Vrabel said regarding Vildor's performance. "You know, that's why we had him in that position and had ability for him to be elevated or get signed and step in there and compete. And nothing was perfect. Nothing is ever gonna be perfect, but, you know, for him to understand what he has to do and, you know, great opportunistic hammer and turnover and punch out there, it's, you know, the competitive spirit of some of these guys is, is really truly special."
Ponder has been a force to be reckoned with this season for the Patriots. He has already surpassed his sack total from last season with 4.5 (team-high). Two of those came on Sunday, including a forced fumble at the end of the first half which could have led to another score had New England recovered.
The former undrafted free agent also notched a pair of run stops and pressured the quarterback on four of his pass rushes. Although the Patriots' edge rusher group was looked upon as one of the worst in the NFL heading into 2026, Ponder has played a substantial role in bringing the pass rush's production up to par.

title: Patriots Don't Get Positive Initial Update on OT Will Campbell's Knee Injury
full_text:
The New England Patriots lost a pair of offensive linemen earlier in the season, forcing them to make changes at the right guard position. Now they might need to make a change at left tackle.
According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Will Campbell is believed to have suffered a knee sprain in the first half of the Patriots' 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders Sunday. He'll receive an MRI tomorrow to confirm and the injury would "likely cause him to miss some time."
Campbell would leave the game after Rhamondre Stevenson got tackled into his right leg. It was the same leg that Campbell tore his MCL in a season ago, forcing him onto injured reserve. He would remain on the field for a little bit while he got checked out by members of the training staff before heading to the sideline.
He was replaced by first round rookie Caleb Lomu at left tackle . The Patriots also had running back TreVeyon Henderson, edge rusher Dre'Mont Jones and cornerback Charles Woods leave the game with injuries.
After the game, the rookie — who allowed just one pressure since entering the game — spoke about getting thrust into the starting lineup.
"That’s just one of the things that Vrabes and even this league is all about," Lomu said. "Lots of things can happen. Injuries are part of football, which sucks. You know, praying for everyone who has an injury, especially Will, but whatever happens, you got to prepare like a starter is what coach Vrabes tells us. And it’s completely true. Anything can happen. So prepare as a starter throughout the week, even if you’re not going to start, because things like this can happen."
Campbell would head to the locker room during the game, but would briefly return to the sideline to ride a stationary bike. After halftime, he wouldn't return to the sideline and would later be ruled out.
It was a great start to the 2026 season for the LSU alum, who has solidified himself as the cornerstone left tackle for the Patriots . He had only allowed 11 pressures and one sack through the first four-plus games. A year ago, Campbell was also playing well before an MCL tear against the Cincinnati Bengals forced him out for four games. After he would return to the active roster, he wasn't the same player and struggled in the postseason.
"I was ready to go," said Lomu, who played a career-high 47 snaps. "Always just like I said, preparing like a starter no matter what happens, you know, as soon as it happened, I was ready to go, do what I could do to help the team win."
Lomu, the Patriots' first round selection back in April, spent most of the year at right tackle in a backup role. Now, he'll have the opportunity to line back up at left tackle, the position he played at Utah during his collegiate career.
The Patriots already lost guards Mike Onwenu and Greg Van Roten earlier in the season, and may now lose Campbell for a few weeks. They could decide to activate Marcus Bryant off of injured reserve, who was placed on the list ahead of Week 1 and was already designated to return. They've yet to activate his 21-day practice window.
Players will return to the practice field Wednesday as they prepare for their next home game against the New York Jets.
