title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba Among 9 Seahawks in First Injury Report vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are preparing for a short week of practice as they get ready to face off against the Denver Broncos in Week 6's edition of Thursday Night Football.
The Seahawks did not practice on Monday, but they did release a report of players that would have practiced and would have sat if there was a session today.
#Seahawks didn't practice today, but here's an estimation of how the team would have practiced if they did on Monday injury report. Drake Thomas one to watch after exiting briefly yesterday with ankle injury. pic.twitter.com/76UIvBwJui
WR Irv Charles (knee), RB George Holani (ribs, knee)
Wide receiver Irv Charles is looking to make his debut with the Seahawks after being on injured reserve for the first five weeks of the season. Charles has not played since 2024 when he was with the New York Jets and the Seahawks traded a draft pick for him over the offseason, proving how much they value his special teams abilities.
As for Holani, he pops up on the injury report, but a full participation projection is a good sign that he is set to play for Thursday.
RB Zach Charbonnet (knee), QB Drew Lock (forearm), WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle), OL Beau Stephens (shoulder), DT Leonard Williams (ankle)

LB Chazz Surratt (calf), LB Drake Thomas (ankle)
Surratt has been dealing with a calf injury and has been out for the last two games. It's likely he will be out for a third straight week.

title: Seahawks Week 5 Snap Counts: Lineup Healthiest it's Been in 2026
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are licking their wounds after a gut-wrenching 32-29 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 5, ending a two-game win streak against their bitter NFC West rivals.
Seattle is now 3-2, the same record it had at this time last year before going 11-1 over its final 12 regular-season games and ultimately winning the Super Bowl. A repeat of that result, of course, isn’t guaranteed, as the Seahawks have a ton of work to do to become a championship-level team.
In terms of snap counts, not a ton changed from Week 4. A few players continue to see more usage as the season goes on, while others are seeing less as starters return from injury. Head coach Mike Macdonald continues to expect a lot from his defensive secondary and the unit’s leaders, while the splits change weekly on offense.
Here’s a look at the Seahawks’ offensive and defensive snap counts from their loss to the 49ers.
* All snap count statistics are courtesy of Pro Football Reference
LG Grey Zabel (63; 100%), LT Charles Cross (63; 100%), C Jalen Sundell (63; 100%), RT Abraham Lucas (63; 100%), QB Sam Darnold (63; 100%), TE AJ Barner (60; 95%), WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (53; 84%), WR Cooper Kupp (51; 81%), RB Emanuel Wilson (37; 59%), RG Christian Haynes (33; 52%), G Beau Stephens (30; 48%), WR Rashid Shaheed (29; 46%), RB George Holani (26; 41%), TE Eric Saubert (22; 35%), TE Elijah Arroyo (20; 32%), WR Tory Horton (11; 17%); FB Brady Russell (6; 10%)
The offensive line is once again stable outside of right guard. Haynes and Stephens continue to split snaps there while Anthony Bradford is out with an injury.
Barner saw his most snaps of any game this season, but he still only had three catches for 20 yards. Saubert and Arroyo also saw increased usage, as the Seahawks relied heavily on their tight ends.
Smith-Njigba still carried a heavy workload despite an ankle injury. The Seahawks superstar managed to push through it to still play the vast majority of snaps. Seattle’s running back split was about the same as in Week 4, leaning heavily toward Wilson. Macdonald doesn’t have much flexibility with rushers currently, so it should stay similar until Zach Charbonnet returns.
Shaheed surprisingly saw his fewest snaps of the season, despite it seeming like he was beginning to work into his role in the offense. That may be the biggest surprise of the week.
LB Ernest Jones IV (60; 100%), CB Josh Jobe (60; 100%), CB Devon Witherspoon (59; 98%), S Julian Love (58; 97%), DB/LB Nick Emmanwori (56; 93%), S Ty Okada (56; 93%), LB Drake Thomas (46; 77%), DL Leonard Williams (44; 73%), DL Byron Murphy II (41; 68%), OLB Uchenna Nwosu (40; 67%), OLB DeMarcus Lawrence (39; 65%), DL Jarran Reed (31; 52%), OLB Derick Hall (25; 42%), OLB Dante Fowler Jr. (9; 15%), DT Brandon Pili (8; 13%), CB Trevon Diggs (8; 13%), DL Mike Morris (7; 12%), DL Rylie Mills (5; 8%), CB Nehemiah Pritchett (4; 7%), S Rodney Thomas II (2; 3%), LB Tyrice Knight (2; 3%)
Jones, Josh, Witherspoon and Love all playing almost every snap is expected. Those are four of the team’s schematic and spiritual leaders, and Macdonald is going to keep them on the field as much as he can.
As for Emmanwori, he’s now fully ramped up from his offseason ankle surgery and is seeing a full share of work. Okada didn’t have a pitch count in his first game of the season coming off of injury, so that’s a good sign for his health moving forward.
The defensive line split has been about the same all season, and Williams playing 73% of the snaps despite coming out of Week 4 with an injury is a very good sign. Pili, Mills and Morris are the only defensive linemen who have their snap counts fluctuate with each game.

title: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold is Failing His Final Test
full_text:
Let me be clear before we get started here. This article isn’t about Drew Lock , Justin Herbert, C.J. Stroud, Joe Burrow, or whichever quarterback savior some Seattle Seahawks fans have in mind right now. Sam Darnold is our quarterback, and it’s going to take a lot to change that. But like I said last week, there’s a bigger conversation to have right now.
One year ago today, Sam Darnold was a legitimate MVP candidate. He was completing over 73% of his passes and had 9 touchdowns to 3 interceptions with 1,246 yards. He cooled off a bit, but still had a great season, and then cleaned his game up in week 18 and the postseason. During that crucial stretch, he had zero turnovers. He had it all figured out.
I find it shocking that we’ve regressed to the point we’re currently at, where a non-trivial portion of the fanbase doesn’t even want him to continue to be the starter . Perhaps that’s unfair, but Sam is definitely far less effective and explosive this season, so far. And it’s with a supporting cast and offense that, with a couple exceptions, is very similar to last year.
I understand interceptions. Sam Darnold has always thrown a lot of interceptions. Maybe some of the ones he’s thrown so far this year are egregious, but none of this should be unexpected. Nor is it an obstacle to him being a good, effective NFL quarterback. The thing that really bothers me is how he seems to lack confidence and composure on the field.
I don’t have a number or statistic that can back this up. All I can offer is what I see when I watch him on the field. I see a quarterback who is getting antsy in the pocket, is afraid to let the ball rip into tight windows, and looks to make low reward throws. Which might be okay, if not for the fact that he’s still turning it over at a high clip. It’s the worst of both worlds.
Darnold’s first full game this season, in Washington, had a couple interceptions . But I thought Sam looked healthy, confident, and willing to make the big time throws. The last two weeks, however, have been a different story. Did the picks on the first throws of both games spook him? Has his injury gotten worse due to an overly-aggressive return to the field?
Whatever the answer, a solution needs to be found. Because this current iteration of Darnold isn’t winning anything. The offense either needs to remove the turnovers from the equation, or bring back the big plays from last year, to get back on track. And Darnold needs it too, or else that monster contract (from Seattle or elsewhere) will be out the window.
Nothing can ever take 2025 away from Sam. He had a great season and won a super bowl. That test is in his back pocket. But right now, he doesn’t look like a quarterback worthy of a $55 million a year contract. And for him, you better believe that’s the real final test . I’m rooting for him, but games like the last two are hurting his case.

title: Mike Macdonald, Jaxon Smith-Njigba Slam Seahawks Over Turnovers
full_text:
Four turnovers and 21 points given up directly off those giveaways killed the Seattle Seahawks' chances of beating the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday.
The Seahawks lost to their bitter rivals at home 32-29, falling short on a last-gasp drive that ended with Cooper Kupp trying to extend a fourth-down catch beyond the first-down marker. But it never would have been that close without the giveaways.
“We have to stay out of our own way at the end of the day,” Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba said postgame . “We spotted them 21 points. Like I said, the defense played incredible; it’s on us to protect the ball and move the ball forward. We have to focus on that.”
Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold threw two bad interceptions. Running backs George Holani and Emanuel Wilson fumbled a total of three times, losing two of them.
“We need to grow quickly, in terms of complementary football, definitely taking care of the football,” head coach Mike Macdonald added. “Way too many giveaways at this point in the season, and we’ll look at those and see how we can get it fixed moving forward.”
The first Darnold pick came on the Seahawks' first drive, giving the 49ers the ball on Seattle's 18-yard line. That led to San Francisco taking a 7-0 lead. Wilson then fumbled on his own 9-yard line in the second quarter with the Seahawks leading 10-7, and the 49ers retook a 14-10 advantage.
Holani fumbled once in the second quarter, but he got back on it. Then, with the Seahawks attempting an outside run just before halftime, Holani fumbled in Seattle's own end zone. San Francisco recovered, taking a 21-13 lead into the break.
The 49ers needed touchdown drives of just 18 and 11 yards to score 21 points.
“We should be able to execute run plays,” Macdonald said. “We want to stay aggressive … But we’ve got to be able to execute our run game and hold onto the football. Straight up.”
When asked about how the team approached deciding whether to go back to Holani, who did have more touches in the game, Macdonald was blunt.
“We’re short on [running] backs. I can’t go out there and carry the ball, so. Nor do we want to.”
Macdonald said they aren't expecting Zach Charbonnet to return on a short week for their Week 6 Thursday night game against the Denver Broncos. That means, barring a free-agent signing, Wilson and Holani will likely be set for a larger workload once again.
Darnold now has five interceptions in his last three games and will have to improve drastically to keep the Seahawks from losing games they should win. The team now has 12 total giveaways in five games.
“I think we’ve got a tough team; I think we’re a connected team,” Macdonald said. “But in terms of playing complementary football, the way that we want to play here as Seahawks and become the team that we want to become, we’re not there yet.”

title: When Will Zach Charbonnet Return? Seahawks RBs Struggle With Injuries, Fumbles vs. 49ers
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks' running back room has underperformed during the 2026 season. There has not been power in numbers for the 12s. That was never more evident than during a 32-29 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 5.
Emanuel Wilson, the lead back, amassed just 61 yards on 20 carries. While he found the end zone on a two-yard run, Wilson looked overwhelmed by his massive workload. A fumble deep in Seahawks territory the second quarter was a major momentum shift that the Niners fully took advantage of.
Not to be outdone, George Holani had two negative rushing attempts against San Francisco's defensive front. Holani also had a key fumble and finished with seven rushing yards on four carries. Holani at least had 24 receiving yards on four catches.
Seattle offensive coordinator Brian Fleury needs a lifeline in the running game. Sam Darnold has been turnover-prone since returning from a hip injury. Darnold can't carry the offense by himself.
Help could be on the way sooner than later, luckily.
Zach Charbonnet recently returned to practice for the Seahawks. A return is right around the corner for Charbonnet after tearing his ACL during the postseason in January against the 49ers.
Fleury certainly sounded optimistic about having the former second-round pick back in the fold.
"It's exciting to see him out there," Fleury said this past week . "I mean, he's still getting up to speed, and obviously we don't have like a whole lot of reps to spare to give him if we know he's not playing. So, it's just kind of been some basic stuff, but it's exciting to have him out there."
Charbonnet could cut into Wilson's workload right away whenever he returns. It'd take a ramp-up before taking on any workhorse role.
With the short week before Thursday Night Football this coming Thursday against the Denver Broncos, Week 7 against the Kansas City Chiefs could be more realistic for a return. That game will be on Sunday Night Football.
Rookie Jadarian Price is currently on IR.
Price's first chance to return could come against the Chicago Bears during the first week of November.
So far, Price has had a similar problem that the team suffered on Sunday against San Francisco: he has problems holding the ball.
Price had two fumbles in his first three games. One was costly in the team's 33-31 loss to the Washington Commanders in Week 3.
Even when Price comes back, he may not be rushed back into a major role if Charbonnet is able to slow down the team's turnover woes.

title: Leonard Williams Ankle Injury Update: How Seahawks DT Played Through Scare vs. 49ers
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks defensive tackle Leonard Williams had an injury scare during the team's 30-23 win over the Los Angeles Chargers last week. It didn't prevent him from appearing against the San Francisco in a 32-29 loss at Lumen Field on Sunday afternoon.
The ankle injury may have slowed Williams down against the Niners, though. Williams had one assisted tackle and a quarterback hit on Brock Purdy.
As Williams had described before the game, he "heard a little bit of crunchiness" while he was walking off the field during the Chargers game.
"I think at first, just when it first happens and you're out there on the field, the adrenaline's pumping and you hear a little bit of crunchiness or something like that, you always think worst-case scenario. But then once you calm down, go in the training room and they start doing tests on you, you start realizing it's not as bad as you thought," Williams said .
After struggling against San Francisco, you have to wonder if Williams rushed back to the field too quickly.
Williams doesn't have the best luck in his injury recovery.
After electing to play against the Niners, Williams may now have to turn around and play against the Denver Broncos on just four days rest. The two teams clash in the Mile High City as part of Thursday Night Football this week.
Denver possesses one of the toughest interior offensive lines in the league. Even if Williams does play, he'll face a stiff test in the middle of the Broncos' protection.
Williams suffered what was believed to be a low ankle sprain against Los Angeles during a goal-line play.
Very few details were revealed publicly about the injury.
A Grade 1 ankle sprain typically takes at least a week, but up to a month of recovery time. That's the likeliest injury Williams went down with last week.
There's a few ways to get around Williams' injury, whether he sits or suits up against Denver this Thursday.
Seahawks head coach and defensive play-caller Mike Macdonald could get creative with disguised blitz packages to compensate for the hobbled tackle having limited mobility.
Macdonald may want to consider that anyway. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix struggles against heavy pressure.
Macdonald could also lean on Byron Murphy II opposite Jarran Reed as the primary interior pass-rusher.
Murphy had a pair of sacks, three TFLs, and three quarterback hits on Purdy this past Sunday.
Whether Williams sits or plays, Macdonald has good options to hedge with. We'll see what hand he plays in a few days.

title: 3 Observations After Seahawks Loss vs. 49ers
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are back in the loss column after falling to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 5 by a score of 32-29.
The Seahawks held a lead going into the fourth quarter, but they surrendered two scores, which ultimately cost them the win at home . Here are three key observations from the game.
With the Seahawks' run game in disarray, Sam Darnold has to play flawlessly as the team's starting quarterback. In the last three weeks, he hasn't really done that. Darnold threw an interception for the third straight game, marking five in the first five weeks. His two turnovers were a big catalyst behind the team's loss.
What made Darnold so successful in the Seahawks' playoff run last season was that he was able to take care of the football. If he is able to do that, the Seahawks' defense should be able to do enough to carry them to victory.
Unfortunately, his interceptions came at inopportune moments, which gave San Francisco short fields. One of them came in the first quarter, which opened up the scoring for the game. Emanuel Wilson fumbled in the second quarter, which also led to a quick touchdown for the Niners. It isn't just on Darnold, but as the quarterback, he is going to shoulder the bulk of the responsibility.
In brighter news, third-year defensive tackle Byron Murphy II sacked San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy twice and established his dominance throughout the game. Players like Murphy are going to make the Seahawks defense incredibly difficult to go up against week in and week out.
As the season goes along and offenses begin to deteriorate due to injury and fatigue, defenses will grow stronger. Murphy will be a big reason why if he can stay healthy.
While it's easy to look at this loss as a massive disappointment because the Seahawks aren't accustomed to losing very often, there is a grain of salt to be had. That's because they did play the 49ers, who are one of just two teams that have accumulated five wins in the first five weeks.
This is one of their tougher games on the schedule, and when the Niners came to Seattle last season, they also took the loss. The Seahawks learned from their mistakes and were able to come back and win in Week 18 in a must-win situation and again in the playoffs.
This won't be the last time they face off against the Niners. They'll get one more shot at them at the end of November, right after Thanksgiving, in a game they should be well prepared to win and get revenge.

title: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp Weighs in on Controversial Final Play vs. 49ers
full_text:
If not for a Jaxon Smith-Njigba drop on third down, the Seattle Seahawks wouldn’t have had to rely on a miracle fourth-down conversion to Cooper Kupp to try and save their eventual 32-29 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday.
But the Seahawks needed that final play to go in their favor, and without a camera angle that could conclusively see whether Kupp extended the ball beyond the first-down marker before going out of bounds, it didn’t.
The ruling on the field was that Kupp was short, and they didn’t have enough evidence to overturn it.
“I knew it was close, but yeah, clearly it was short,” Kupp said after the game . “So, just not enough there, and you’ve got to find a way to get that fourth down.”
Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold found Kupp about four yards away from the first-down marker. Kupp slipped a tackle and accelerated to the line to gain, where he was met by multiple 49ers defenders.
Kupp slid towards the sideline and tried to extend the football, but all the horizontal angles of the play made it difficult to tell if the ball crossed the marker before or after it was over the sideline.
Cooper Kupp is short and the @49ers take over! @SFvsSEA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/k9426I2gFe
Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald was asked about his thoughts on the play, and he was brief.
“I don’t know,” Macdonald said. “They said he was short, so you’ve got to live with it.”
The 49ers took over on downs, and they were able to kneel it out from there. The Seahawks only had one timeout remaining, and the game clock was under 50 seconds.
It’s a play that will undoubtedly live in infamy in the storied Seahawks-49ers rivalry that has already brought heaps of wild games. Seattle won the big ones that mattered last season, and San Francisco has once again won the first matchup of the season between the two teams.
The Seahawks fell to 3-2, losing two of their last three games. San Francisco advanced to 5-0, and they currently lead a tightly contested NFC West that also houses the Los Angeles Rams (2-2).
Week 6 will be critical for the Seahawks, as they’re on a short week before facing the Denver Broncos (3-2) on Thursday, Oct. 15. Seattle will have to quickly recover emotionally from a difficult, close loss.

title: 3 Winners & 3 Losers From Seahawks Heartbreaking Week 5 Loss to 49ers
full_text:
It was a sloppy game on Sunday as the Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers combined for seven turnovers. Each team continually capitalized on those mistakes, with 35 points being scored on those takeaways.
Unsurprisingly, that led to a back-and-forth contest as well, with four lead changes in the close contest. In the end, the 49ers escaped with a 32-29 win as Cooper Kupp came up just inches short of a first-down conversion on their final fourth-down play of the game.
Following the upsetting loss, here's a look back at which Seahawks players stood out as both winners and losers.
Seattle had a 10-7 lead in the second quarter and forced a punt right after taking the lead. They were backed up, but still could have tried to add to their lead. That didn't happen with Emanuel Wilson fumbling the ball away. San Francisco recovered the loss ball at the Seahawks' 11-yard line, which allowed them to score quickly and take the lead, 14-10. Wilson had the short touchdown early in the game but the fumble was a gut-punch that gave the 49ers plenty of momentum.
Seattle needed a big play to take back momentum and Nehemiah Pritchett delivered. With the Seahawks trailing 21-16, Pritchett picked off a pass from Brock Purdy, giving his offense a short field. They covered 23 yards on three plays, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba scoring on a 16-yard touchdown to take the lead back.
After Wilson's fumble, George Holani had a chance to steal some of his snaps and made two critical errors in the second quarter. His first was a fumble after gaining eight yards on a pass from Sam Darnold. He recovered the ball, but might have had a chance to score with a ton of open field in front of him. Instead, the drive stalled and they settled for a field goal.
Holani was given a chance to make up for his mistake, but made an even worse one to close out the half. The defense forced a punt with under 20 seconds to play, ending the 49ers chance to score before the half. Or so it seemed.
The Niners still scored as Holani fumbled in the end zone, with Gracen Holten recovering for a defensive touchdown. That sent the Seahawks into the half trailing 21-13.
49ERS RECOVER THE FUMBLE IN THE END ZONE @SFvsSEA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/lwDIn52XVj
There's no shortage of talent on the Seattle defensive line, but there's no denying that Byron Murphy is their most impactful player. He's coming off a breakout season that saw him record 62 tackles and seven sacks, and he just had his best game of the 2026 campaign.
Murphy was bullying his way into the offensive backfield, recording two sacks in the first half alone. Each of his sacks helped lead to a punt, allowing the Seahawks to stay in the game despite multiple mistakes in the first half.
He was also able to come up with a huge play near the end of the game. With things tied at 29, the 49ers were driving to take the lead with just over two minutes to play. Murphy stepped up and stopped Kaelon Black for a one-yard loss on third-and-one, forcing the Niners to settle for a field goal.
The Seahawks had a terrible start to the game, with Sam Darnold throwing an interception on third-and-10, giving the 49ers the ball in the red zone. That set them up for their opening touchdown, allowing them to go up 7-0.
In the second half, Darnold again gave the ball away quickly. This time, he was picked off at the SanFrancisco 44, but they were given even better field position when Elijah Arroyo was called for unneccesary roughness on the return. The 49ers missed their field goal, which bailed Darnold out, but these are mistakes he simply can't make.
Darnold did all he could to fight back in this one, but fell just short. One reason was a pass to a wide-open Jaxon Smith-Njigba that was thrown slightly behind JSN, who couldn't come down with the ball.
Seattle's offense was sloppy for much of the first three quarters, with four turnovers allowing the 49ers to take a 21-13 lead. The Seahawks fought back, however, thanks in large part to Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
The reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year continued to provide the fireworks, including a 16-yard touchdown with just under six minutes to play in the third quarter. JSN, who suffered an ankle injury earlier in the game, made a beautiful move after catching a short pass from Darnold to find the opening he needed to get into the end zone.
What a move by the reigning OPOY @SFvsSEA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GoZnRMz3om
Smith-Njigba finished with 102 yards on five receptions, but he's only going to remember the one he couldn't haul in, the final third-down play that was thrown behind him, but JSN nearly hauled in.

title: Dre Greenlaw Suspension Opens Door for 49ers Rookie
full_text:
The suspension of Dre Greenlaw is disappointing for the San Francisco 49ers, but it also opens the door to what the future could look like for the team. Rookie Jaden Dugger has been the 49ers' starting SAM linebacker, but that is a less prominent role.
With Greenlaw out, he is likely going to get his first start at WILL, which means playing the majority of the snaps in Week 6.
Dugger played 55.7% of the 49ers' snaps in their blowout win over the Los Angeles Rams in Week 1. He has not played that much since. In Week 2, Dugger played 30.5% of the defensive snaps and then played 37.9% of the snaps in Week 3.
He dipped to just 15 snaps and 22.7% of the snaps overall. This speaks to his role being dependent on the game script. However, he played a career-high 47 snaps and 75% of the snaps with Greenlaw out of the game. This is a much different role.
The 49ers could have kept him as the SAM and played Garrett Wallow more, which is what happened when Greenlaw went down earlier in the year. However, Wallow is going to miss time as well due to an injury. Now that he is going to be out for another game, it gives the rookie a chance to be a full-time starter for the first time.
The former fifth-round pick from Louisiana was known for his versatility in college. He aligned everywhere from the edge to linebacker and safety. The 49ers have been taking advantage of his versatility in his limited role, but this will provide him more of a chance to focus on a specific position.
The question becomes what happens if Dugger plays well. Week 5 was arguably his best game as an NFL player. He embraced the change in role. His athleticism and potential are hard to deny, and if things go right, the plan would be for the 49ers to let Greenlaw go this offseason and have Dugger step into a bigger role. If he can continue to play well to the point where it is not hurting the team, and he is growing into the role he will play next season, does the team really need to go back to Greenlaw? This could be a major opportunity.

title: Realistic or Not Realistic: Who Can the 49ers Add at Wide Receiver?
full_text:
New year, same story in Santa Clara: the 49ers can’t stay healthy.
San Francisco enters Week 6 with a receiver room stretched thin. Only two of the wideouts from the initial 53-man roster, Mike Evans and Jordan Watkins, got through Sunday’s game in Seattle without leaving with an injury. Brandin Cooks is also healthy, but he was signed after Week 2.
Head coach Kyle Shanahan has already said Deebo Samuel will miss multiple weeks with a hamstring injury. Jacob Cowing, a player who should already be feeling the heat, left Seattle banged up with an ankle issue.
That leaves the Niners to face the Washington Commanders on Monday night with Evans, Cowing (ankle), Cooks and Watkins. That’s thin help for one of the league’s best passing offenses, so here’s a look at who could come to aid the WR room.
Probability: 1% — Unrealistic
At his peak, Hill was as dynamic as any playmaker in the league. But he’s coming off a season-ending knee injury in 2025 and still has legal trouble hanging over him. San Francisco would likely prefer a player with less noise around him and no rehab to manage. And if Hill is fully healthy, he’s not a practice-squad candidate. He’d command a 53-man roster spot. I think that's where the 49ers would fall out of Tyreek signing race.
Probability: 50% — Realistic
If your first reaction was “who?”, fair enough. Skinner turned heads in the Jets’ 2025 preseason and spent the season on their practice squad, catching one pass for 10 yards and a two-point conversion in the regular season. He’s a 6'5" target who can win downfield, and he ran a 4.52 40-yard dash at his pro day. The concern is Shanahan’s long-standing reluctance to trust young receivers who haven’t mastered the nuances of his offense. Skinner got a workout in late September, but the team signed Dante Pettis instead.
Probability: 0.5% — Unrealistic
If Sunday’s win showed anything, it’s the value of a receiver like Evans, whose huge catch radius means the offense doesn’t have to rely on separation. Brock Purdy knows how to take advantage of that and isn’t shy about letting it fly. Hopkins is on the Georgia Tech coaching staff but has made it clear he isn’t retired. Shanahan loves his veterans, but this is a long shot.
Probability: 60% — Realistic
The 49ers don’t want to give up draft capital for a receiver. They’d rather save it for an edge rusher or an interior defensive lineman. Still, this fit makes too much sense for John Lynch not to at least call Minnesota. Shanahan values veterans, and a player like Jennings would need almost no time to learn the new playbook. He showed clear frustration Sunday, even with the Vikings off to a 5-0 start. He has just two catches for nine yards on the season, far below his production in recent years, which could open the door for a swap of late-round picks.
Probability: 0% — Unrealistic
If Beckham were still a free agent, Shanahan might consider him for the practice squad. But he’s on the Vikings’ practice squad, and I can’t see San Francisco putting him on the 53-man roster. In 2019 the Niners would have jumped at the chance. We’re a long way past that now.
Probability: 0% — Unrealistic
Getting Thomas would cost a second-round pick at minimum, whatever you think of how things have gone in Jacksonville. His draft classmate Marvin Harrison Jr. just went to Houston with a second-rounder as the main return to Arizona. Thomas has done more than Harrison, so that’s the floor for the Jaguars. If the Niners are spending a second, it should go toward a defensive lineman of Vita Vea or DeForest Buckner caliber.
Don’t expect a splash. Demarcus Robinson, Deebo Samuel and De’Zhaun Stribling are all due back this season, and that matters when weighing a move for a player who would count against the 53-man roster.

title: Kyle Shanahan Provides Discouraging Injury Update on Deebo Samuel
full_text:
Well, this was predictable.
The San Francisco 49ers will be without Deebo Samuel for "some time" after he exited the game against the Seattle Seahawks with a hamstring injury.
Kyle Shanahan provided the discouraging injury update on Samuel while on a conference call with reporters on Monday. Samuel injured his hamstring in the third quarter of the game.
The 49ers immediately ruled him out, which indicated that his injury would most likely keep him out for the next couple of games. Hamstring injuries are always annoying and tricky.
Players will think they're fine until they get on the field and undo everything. It wouldn't be shocking if Samuel wasn't seen again until after the 49ers' Week 8 Bye.
With Samuel out, this further thins the wide receiver position. This could force the 49ers to go out and add another player, but Shanahan thinks the 49ers are okay for now.
"I think we have enough. We’ve got three guys on practice squad also who can help. Anytime you lose this number of guys, four guys or five guys whatever it is, it's a huge challenge. But, we do have guys in this building who can do it and we'll always look," said Shanahan.
Brandin Cooks appears to be the No. 3 receiver for the 49ers, after Mike Evans and George Kittle. It seems he's overtaken Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins
Although those two are sure to be sprinkled into the offense. Cowing was surprisingly used a lot against the Seahawks, as he registered 17 routes run.
Watkins only clocked in eight routes run. His sweet two-catch, 60-yard performance against the Arizona Cardinals clearly didn't do much to help him earn an increased role.
It wouldn't be surprising if a newly added or practice squad player received more playing time than him. Shanahan favors veterans, which is why Cooks ran 12 routes and reeled in a touchdown.
The 49ers shouldn't feel compelled to make a big move at wide receiver. I know that Evans is still compromised, but they will be fine at the position.
They should be able to defeat the Washington Commanders and the Atlanta Falcons without being at full strength at receiver. Those are two very average to below-average teams.
It shouldn't be difficult to get wins over them. What the 49ers need is for their current players to step up. Get ready for more Cooks and Cowing.

title: Is 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw's One-Game Suspension Too Harsh?
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers will be without fiery linebacker Dre Greenlaw in Week 6 against the Washington Commanders.
The NFL has suspended Greenlaw for one game after he helmet-headbutted Seattle Seahawks' Ernest Jones, who didn't have his helmet on.
Greenlaw was ejected for his headbutt, so he'll essentially have cost himself a game and a half for his headbutt of Jones. The incident occurred on the Seahawks' sideline in the second quarter.
The Seattle players didn't take too kindly to Greenlaw's late hit on Sam Darnold, as he was rushing towards the sideline. A flock of Seahawks players surrounded Greenlaw and got in his face.
Greenlaw didn't appreciate that, especially Jones, so he answered with a headbutt. Given the context, was Greenlaw's one-game suspension too harsh?
Not at all. Under no circumstances can the NFL allow any player to helmet-headbutt another player without their helmet on.
Football helmets are brutal. They're part of why players have so many vicious bruises and body damage.
By suspending Greenlaw, the NFL is setting a precedent to ensure no one else will be tempted to replicate these actions. If they didn't suspend Greenlaw, players would know they could do it without consequence.
A fine wouldn't have done the job either. The NFL needed to suspend Greenlaw to send a clear message to everyone that this is NOT okay.
Greenlaw could've easily broken Jones' nose, delivered a facial fracture, or maybe even a concussion. That's how lethal a football helmet is. Suspending Greenlaw was a no-brainer for the league.
In fact, it was expected, which is why I listed it as one of my biggest takeaways from the 49ers' win over the Seahawks.
Don't forget that Greenlaw has a history of recklessness as well. The NFL surely took that into account as well.
Now, you may think Greenlaw was justified in his actions since an army of Seahawks players surrounded him. But let's not pretend the 49ers wouldn't have done the same.
Had 49ers players witnessed Brock Purdy take a late hit, they would've gotten in that Seahawks player's face as well. They have to rally to their leader. That's fine.
What isn't fine is Greenlaw helmet-headbutting a player without theirs on. Had he done it to someone who had their helmet on, then this would be a non-issue.
The 49ers will look to rookie Jaden Dugger, Luke Gifford, and Garrett Wallow to fill in for the suspended Greenlaw.

title: 5 49ers Whose Stock Dropped After Seahawks Victory
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers won a thrilling game against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. However, with such a tough win can come some ups and downs along the way. Which players on the 49ers saw their stock drop despite the win?
Colby has been much better in 2026 than he was in 2025. However, some of that could be competition-aided. It did not help that Byron Murphy is one of the best young defensive tackles in the NFL. Still, he had his way with Colby in this game, who allowed three pressures according to PFF. San Francisco also struggled to run the ball.
The 49ers' passing attack is Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle, and Mike Evans. Deebo Samuel has 206 yards this season, but 80 were on a hook and lateral that he did not even receive. Since Week 3, Jordan Watkins has two catches for 60 yards, and that is fifth on the team. Jacob Cowing has nine yards, and Brandon Cooks has seven yards. They are getting nothing from this group of players.
Black started the season looking hot. He recorded 14 rushing attempts for 65 yards in the 49ers' Week 1 win. It was looking like he was going to be a legitimate piece of the offense. Since then, he has had 23 carries for 71 yards. The good news is that his success rate is still high. They use him a lot in short-yardage situations. However, he is not as big a piece of the offense as expected, and he has not flashed any dynamic ability or passing game impact.
Greenlaw has been up and down all season. He has made big plays and has been a force downhill. Then, in space, he misses tackles. He has been reliable until he left the game early due to a silly ejection. Jaden Dugger flashed with Greenlaw out. The team is much more committed to Dugger than Greenlaw beyond this year. Can Dugger eat into Greenlaw’s snaps?
With all of the injuries along the edge rusher room, the team has started to lean into Okoronkwo playing more often. He had 48 snaps in Week 3 and then had 25 snaps the following week. However, with Mykel Williams back in the lineup, he was down to 14. He is not going to jump Romello Height or Keion White. So, when Nick Bosa returns, he might be inactive.

title: Brock Purdy and Fred Warner Sound Off on Mike Evans’ Impact for the 49ers
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are 5-0 to start the season after defeating the Seattle Seahawks 32-29 at Lumen Field.
What's more, San Francisco is 3-0 for the division too. The player on offense they can largely thank for maintaining that winning record is wide receiver Mike Evans .
Evans improved on Week 5's performance against the Denver Broncos to record his best game in a 49ers jersey. He caught seven passes for 113 yards and scored a touchdown, too.
"[He's] just a walking aura," linebacker Fred Warner said of Evans post-game. "I mean, I can't help it. Like, I'm on the sideline watching, dude, crazy stuff. I'm like, 'We have Mike Evans.' Like, I can't believe it.
"He's unreal. He really doesn't say anything. He just shows up every week and just works and then goes out there on Sunday and just dominates you. So, it's unbelievable. He's great.
"You know that he's a Hall of Fame receiver when we signed him, but just the hunger, and I think that's the character of our entire team. People kind of slept on our talent all along going into this year, but we've got guys who are ultra-talented but also could care less about what we've done in the past.
"We still are so eager to try to go out there and prove it every single time we step out there. So, you see that on the tape, you feel that in-game, and Mike's just the epitome of that."
It's not just the hunger to succeed as don't forget Evans has produced two fantastic games with two broken ribs.
Brock Purdy had his say on the Evans hype train, telling the media: "He's a dog. That's all I can say.
"He fights through stuff. He's competitive as heck, and he's going to go out there and obviously give the team every chance or everything that he's got, even if he's going through stuff.
"We saw that obviously the last couple weeks with him playing sort of injured, and even today. It's early in the season, (and) for a guy like him and where he's at in his career, to keep showing up for the team and myself, it's just a testament to his character and who he is.
"So, I'm extremely blessed to have him on our team and excited for the rest of the year together."
Evans may be 33 and his prime years are behind him, but he's proven once again why he will enter the Hall of Fame one day.

title: 5 49ers Who Stepped Up in Seahawks Win
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers won their most impressive performance of the season, beating the Seattle Seahawks 32-29. It took strong performances from a lot of unexpected names to get the job done. Who stepped up the most?
Evans has been excellent for the 49ers this year. However, whether it be blowouts or injuries, he has not put in a full effort yet. Sunday, we saw the entire skill set of Evans. The All-Pro receiver had seven catches for 114 yards and a touchdown. Evans dominated and averaged 4.35 yards per route run. His season total is 3.05. Anything above two is considered extremely good, which speaks to how well Evans has played. The 49ers made a great addition.
It is almost every week that Halton is being discussed as a player on the rise. The rookie from Oklahoma had three pressures and a forced fumble that he recovered for a touchdown. He is playing more than expected due to injuries around him, and he is taking advantage. You can call him a starter moving forward.
Green has consistently been asked to step up this year, and every time the team calls on him, he delivers. He allowed two receptions for five yards in coverage, and star receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba was 1-for-3 when he saw a pass with Green defending him. Green had a pick on one of those targets and added a second interception in the game. He has been a stock-up player all season.
With Marques Sigle on the sidelines, the team called on their former starter Malik Mustapha to jump into the lineup. Considering he was a former starter, the expectations were higher than for most backups. Still, Mustapha lived up to them and then some. Whether he is boosting his trade stock or competing to get back into the lineup, Mustapha made a strong case today.
Dugger has been the 49ers' third linebacker the entire season. So, when Dre Greenlaw was tossed from the game early, the team threw even more responsibility on the rookie linebacker. Dugger lived up to the hype so far. He added six tackles and a sack. For a fifth-round rookie who is new to the position, there is a lot to like in his progression so far this season.

title: 49ers Grades After 32-29 Win Over Seahawks: Mike Evans Dominates Seattle
full_text:
SEATTLE -- The 49ers just beat the Seattle Seahawks 32-29. Here are the 49ers' grades for this performance.
Brock Purdy was clutch against an elite defense, and he gets credit for that. When the game was tight in the fourth quarter, Purdy played his best because he threw repeatedly to Mike Evans, his only good wide receiver. That was smart. Earlier in the game, Purdy got intercepted because he forced a pass to his worst wide receiver, Jacob Cowing. That was not smart. Overall, Purdy did the best he could with a depleted supporting cast, and eventually found the Seahawks' weakest link -- cornerback Josh Jobe. As opposed to Sam Darnold, who essentially lost the game for the Seahawks with his two turnovers. Purdy didn't have to win this game -- he just had to let the Seahawks lose it, and they did.
Kaelon Black continued to struggle, but Christian McCaffrey averaged a whopping 6.2 yards per carry without Kyle Juszczyk leading the way. It's almost as if Juszczyk's impact on the offense is extremely overstated. The 49ers didn't miss him at all in this game.
The 49ers had just one quality wide receiver -- Mike Evans -- but he was all they needed. He finished the game with 7 catches for 113 yards and a touchdown. And when the 49ers needed to put together their first long touchdown drive of the game, they called his number repeatedly and he came through. As long as Evans stays healthy, the 49ers offense will be extremely difficult to stop unless the opposing team has three outstanding cornerbacks. Still, Deebo Samuel left the game with a hamstring injury that could sideline him for a few weeks, which means the 49ers desperately need to trade for a wide receiver, preferably a young, fast one who can replace Jacob Cowing in three-receiver formations and on special teams.
George Kittle came down with flu-like symptoms last night and struggled as a receiver in this game -- just 24 receiving yards on five catches. But he and Luke Farrell were a big reason that McCaffrey was so successful running the ball. Unfortunately for the 49ers, Farrell is a horrendous receiver.
I guess this group isn't the best offensive line in the league. Today, they faced their first real test, and gave up three sacks. Left guard Connor Colby in particular gave up two. He remains the weakest link on this line. Still, this group more than held its own in the run game.
This group is playing so much better than it has any business playing. Gracen Halton forced a fumble at the goal line and recovered it in the end zone for a touchdown. He looks like he's going to be a great player one day. Osa Odighizuwa, Sebastian Valdez, Keion White and Mykel Williams played well, too. Suddenly, the defensive line doesn't look like the position the 49ers need to upgrade before the trade deadline, particularly if Nick Bosa comes back. They need a wide receiver instead.
Draymond Greenlaw got ejected after hitting Sam Darnold out of bounds and then head-butting a Seahawks player who wasn't wearing his helmet. Greenlaw is entirely too old to continue making that same mistake. He really is the 49ers' version of Draymond Green. He might get suspended for next week's game against the Commanders. And if he can't play, the 49ers will still win, because they have Fred Warner, one of the best linebackers of all time. Of course, he recorded 10 tackles and a forced fumble in this game. Just another day at the office for him.
Renardo Green is becoming an All-Pro cornerback. Today, he intercepted two passes and broke up three. No wonder the 49ers don't have Deommodore Lenoir shadow the other team's best receiver -- he's the second-best cornerback on the team. No disrespect to him, but Green is better. Lenoir gave up a long catch to Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the first half. And despite how well this group played, the Seahawks were one dopped Smith-Njigba pass on the final drive away from tying the game. These teams are so evenly matched.
The 49ers need a new punt returner. Jacob Cowing muffed a punt and the Seahawks recovered it, which kept them in the game. The 49ers might also need a new kicker. Eddy Pineiro missed another kick today, and now has missed five this season. He's becoming the new Jake Moody.
Raheem Morris' defense won the game. It forced four turnovers, held the Seahawks to five field goals, and got the game-winning stop at the end when it pushed Cooper Kupp out of bounds an inch before the first-down marker on fourth-and-10. To be fair, the defense got to face two of the worst running backs you'll ever see in the NFL because the Seahawks arrogantly thought they could replace Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker. Still, Raheem Morris has been an outstanding hire, and he's a huge reason the 49ers remain undefeated. In hindsight, he was one of the best hires of the offseason for any team.
Kyle Shanahan's offense was another story. It had just two drives of 25 or more yards. They had touchdown drives of 18 and 11 yards. Their defense scored a touchdown. Their run game worked when Christian McCaffrey got the ball but Shanahan didn't stick with him. Other than that, nothing Shanahan called worked particularly well until he put Evans on Jobe in the fourth quarter. That was the game-winning matchup for the 49ers. Give Shanahan credit for finding it eventually. In the future, he needs to do a better job of using Purdy's legs and getting him out of the pocket and establishing someone other than Evans as a threat in the passing game. Still, it's been two weeks in a row that Shanahan has saved his best for the end of the game. That's clutch. His team clearly is the best one in the NFC.

title: 7 Biggest Takeaways From 49ers' Week 5 Win Over Seahawks
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers went into Lumen Field to defeat the Seattle Seahawks 32-29. There were a lot of highs and lows for both teams in this contest.
But it had everything you'd expect from a divisional game between the two best teams in the NFL. Let's unpack the biggest takeaways from the 49ers' Week 5 win over the Seahawks.
It was for games like this. The 49ers were desperately missing a true No. 1 receiver in their last two games against the Seahawks. Mike Evans was a massive difference-maker in this game.
He reeled in seven catches for 113 yards, one touchdown, and a two-point conversion. Every time Brock Purdy targeted him, he almost always came down with the ball.
Their connection is insane, especially on the first two throws from Purdy, which were dimes. Evans was Mr. Reliable today. He carried the 49ers' offense, and with fractured ribs. What a monster.
Ever since Nick Bosa was put on the shelf with a calf injury, the 49ers haven't been able to rush the passer effectively. That all changed in this game, as it was very well alive.
Sam Darnold was sacked a whopping five times. He was pressured on a bunch of drop backs, causing him to make mistakes. Osa Odighizuwa, Keion White, and Sebastian Valdez all stood out today. They played a key role in today's win.
And so did rookie Gracen Halton. He deserves his own recognition for this game. The rookie had a dream breakout game. Not only did he register a sack, but he forced a fumble and recovered it in Seattle's end zone.
He caused the biggest turning point in the game right before halftime. Halton has been showing a ton of promise all year, and after a performance like that, he's officially arrived as an impactful player the 49ers rely on.
As great as Dre Greenlaw's energy and emotion are, he can sometimes be his own worst enemy. Greenlaw was ejected after headbutting Ernest Jones, who didn't have his helmet on, while on Seattle's sideline.
The NFL might suspend Greenlaw for that. I'd be surprised if they don't. The league can't let a player helmet-headbutt another without their own. It's insanely reckless, so I fully expect Greenlaw to be suspended for at least one game.
Injuries continue to stack up for the 49ers, with Deebo Samuel as the latest injury. He hurt his hamstring in the third quarter on the play where he fumbled the ball.
The 49ers ruled Samuel out of the game immediately. Given how quickly he was ruled out, you could probably expect Samuel to be out for weeks. He might've torn it. Either way, hamstring injuries take time and are very tricky. Expect him to miss time.
What's wrong with Eddy Pineiro ? First, he was struggling to connect on easy extra-point attempts. Now, he's missing field goals that he'd casually make last year in a pivotal game.
It's time to be concerned about him. Thankfully, he made the game-winning field goal to force Seattle's offense to respond in the final two minutes. If he had missed that, he would've struggled to come back from it.
I think it's officially fair to ask this question now. Raheem Morris has the 49ers' secondary playing at a different level. Robert Saleh couldn't do much with them last year.
That is the biggest difference between the two, along with more trickery from Morris. His defense is not as easy to decipher as Saleh's. He forces quarterbacks to spend more time figuring out what's going on.
That's part of what led Darnold to get sacked and make mistakes. The crazy part is the 49ers don't have Bosa. Just imagine how unleashed it'll look with him back, especially if they add another pass rusher via trade.

title: Why Baker Mayfield Shouldn’t Start for Buccaneers Against Steelers
full_text:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers starting quarterback Baker Mayfield seems to be recovering well from his dislocated thumb suffered in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings.
However, it may not be the wisest of decisions to bring him back this quickly when the Bucs face off against the Pittsburgh Steelers after a long break when they beat the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football.
After starting the season 0-4 with three of those losses coming with Mayfield at the helm of the offense, the Bucs were finally able to get their first victory with Jalon Daniels commanding the offense.
It wasn't the most spectacular outing for Daniels, but he was able to provide a spark that helped the offense look competent — something they haven't looked like all season.
Daniels performed admirably in his first start, a loss to the Green Bay Packers, but was able to lift the offense against the Cowboys. His charismatic energy, passion, and love for the game seemed to reverberate throughout the rest of the team. That instilled confidence in every player around him.
Everything about the offense seemed to run smoothly, sparking the Bucs to score their second-most points of the season.
Inserting Mayfield at less than 100% against the Steelers would be a disservice given the spark that Daniels has brought to this team.
Mayfield signed a massive extension this past offseason, so bringing him back and putting him in a position to further injure the same injury or worse could put the future of their franchise quarterback in jeopardy.
With the dislocation being on his throwing hand, life will be difficult for Mayfield when it comes to gripping the ball, which will lead to decreased ball security and velocity on his throws.
With further injury and heightened risk of turnover prevalent in rushing Mayfield back against the Steelers in Week 6, it would be smart for the Bucs to continue letting him rehab no matter how much he pushes to return sooner.
The season isn't a complete loss yet, with Tampa Bay still within shouting distance of the NFC South lead.
Taking one step forward after a win, only to take two steps back by playing his injury and rehab wrong, would further put pressure on the front office and coaching staff.

full_text:
Even after the Tampa Bay Buccaneers shut down the Dallas Cowboys' prolific offense on the road last Thursday night to secure their first victory of the year, it's tough to suggest that vibes in Tampa Bay are high considering how low they were just a few days ago.

title: Was Mike Evans Right to Leave Buccaneers for 49ers?
full_text:
Some players are franchise legends for their entire career and make their name with just one team. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers know what that's like — linebacker Lavonte David was one of those players, and he retired in 2025 after 14 seasons in red and pewter.
The Bucs also thought wideout Mike Evans was going to be one of those players — and so did he. When Evans re-signed with the Bucs before the start of the 2024 season, he famously declared that he was set to be a "Buc for life." Two years later, he was gone.
Evans decided to spurn the Bucs in free agency and sign with the San Francisco 49ers instead, leaving the team after 12 years of service. There's been plenty of talk about that move ever since it happened, and now that we're five weeks into the season, we're getting a clearer look at where Evans and the Bucs currently stand.
The look? Tampa Bay is 1-4 and staring at oblivion, and Evans and the 49ers are 5-0 and looking toward the Super Bowl.
So, was Evans right in leaving the Buccaneers to chase glory at the end of his career? It sure looks like it right now.
There's no doubt that being a one-franchise player would have meant a lot to Evans. But there are things that matter more, and he's on a better track to achieve those things in San Francisco than he would have been in Tampa Bay.
Evans wants to be a Hall of Famer. To do that, he needs more production, he needs to be in the public eye more often and he needs to be on a team that could potentially win him a ring in the future. There was a time with Tom Brady that the Bucs hit on all three of those requirements, but that time is far gone.
The Bucs are not a Super Bowl-caliber team. They also have multiple wide receivers on their roster to share targets with, so Evans wouldn't have gotten the share he wanted, and with Brady gone and the Bucs middling, Evans likely wouldn't have gotten the exposure required for a Hall of Fame bid.
Even worse? The Buccaneers could be staring at a rebuild next season. If head coach Todd Bowles is fired (and maybe even general manager Jason Licht), the Bucs will be starting from scratch, and Evans could have simply been on his way out regardless. Retiring as a member of the team and continuing to make his case as a Hall of Famer now seems entirely impossible, and that the gamble Evans made here was right.
Whether it was because of what happened at the end of 2025 and the infamous third-and-28 or because he simply wanted a change of scenery, Evans was certainly right to separate from Tampa Bay. And he's proved it already in Week 5 of the regular season.
The Bucs face off against the Steelers in Week 6 to try to move to 2-4 on the year. Evans and the 49ers face off against the Washington Commanders to try and move to 6-0.

title: Week 5 NFC South Update: Are the Buccaneers Still Last in the Division?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got their big win in Week 5 out of the way early, beating the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 at AT&T Stadium.
They got to have the rest of the week off and sit back on Sunday while the rest of the league played its Sunday slate. Two other teams in the NFC South played their games, while the Carolina Panthers took the Sunday off too — they were on their bye week, though.
Here's how the Atlanta Falcons and the New Orleans Saints did, and where the Bucs sit in the division — their win changed some things around in the NFC South.
The Panthers technically lead the division because they did not play a game on Sunday, so they still sit at 2-2.
The Atlanta Falcons played a close overtime thriller with the Baltimore Ravens, but they lost 30-23 after a backbreaking Tua Tagovailoa interception late in overtime. As a result, they sit in second with the same amount of wins as Carolina but with an extra loss due to the bye-week discrepancy.
The New Orleans Saints lost their game against the Minnesota Vikings 23-13, which drops them to 1-4 on the year. That game propelled the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to third place in the division, not last, due to New Orleans' NFC South loss against the Falcons and their much poorer point differential.
The craziest thing? With Atlanta's loss on Sunday night, the Bucs are just one game back from the NFC South lead. It would be a surprising turn of events, but if Tampa Bay were to get something going here quickly, the division would still be very much in reach for the Bucs.
That turnaround continues next Sunday. The Bucs face off against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and they'll try to beat them in Raymond James Stadium to move to 2-4 on the year. A win would be great for Tampa Bay's upward projection, but a loss would plummet them to 1-5 and put most in the organization right back in the hot seat.

title: 3 Buccaneers Players Who Could Be Traded Before Deadline
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers may be coming off a win, but things still don't look great for them heading into the rest of the season. The team is 1-4, and if things go poorly, it could be staring at a rebuild next year with a new head coach.
If that's the case, general manager Jason Licht may want to get some new draft capital. Licht almost never trades midseason , but what if he did? And if he needed some draft picks, which Buccaneers players would he be willing to give up? Who would teams want?
We tried to answer all these questions with three potential Bucs players who could be moved before the deadline:
If the Bucs don't play well leading up to the deadline, they'd probably be down to get anything they could from Chris Godwin. Godwin is 30 years old and isn't getting a ton of use in Zac Robinson's scheme, and there are probably a few teams that wouldn't mind his veteran presence and experience at the position — and maybe a few that would utilize him just a bit more.
Godwin is currently playing on a $22 million deal this year after signing a three-year deal for that much on average. But his last deal is a team option, so any team that traded for Godwin could either extend him to the tune of $22 million more or simply let him walk. Godwin could be a rental for any team looking to take themselves over the line, and the Bucs could get a little capital on top.
Gainwell is another player the Bucs haven't been using much. He's only ran the ball 17 times for 44 yards, just 2.6 yards per carry — he's also only caught 11 passes for 54 yards and a touchdown.
RB-needy teams could easily call about Gainwell if needed. The Bucs have Sean Tucker available and Tucker has looked good in his limited snaps, so he could slide right into that RB2 postion (and he's be a lot cheaper). Any team that wants Gainwell would have to take on his two-year, $14 million contract, which he's currently in the first year of.
This one doesn't feel particularly likely, because the Bucs' pass rush hasn't been great. But if Tampa Bay really wants some capital back before what could be a rebuilding year next year, Diaby wouldn't be a bad player to move.
Diaby is on a contract year as it stands and will be a free agent in March. As a result, any team picking him up wouldn't have to worry about taking on a big contract and could instead watch him to see how he plays — if he pays well, they can extend him, and if not, he'd be a quick rental.
Diaby has five solo tackles and a pick without any sacks so far this season. The Bucs probably want to keep him around for now, but it might be wise to simply listen if a team comes calling.

title: Would Jason Licht Realistically Trade Any Buccaneers Players?
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is approaching. We're exactly one month away, and so any talks or significant developments on the trade market are beginning to fester as we approach Week 6 of the regular season and teams are more in-tune with what they need.
It's been a big week for trades, with center Cam Jurgens heading from Philidelphia to Baltimore and Arizona Cardinals wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. allegedly headed... somewhere after Sunday's slate. More trades will be soon to come, and all 32 teams likely have players that could be dealt this season.
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are 1-4 heading into Week 6. Things looked particularly dire before the team's 24-16 win over the Cowboys on Thursday Night Football, but with a win, the Bucs can seek to become the second team in NFL history to make the playoffs off a 0-4 start.
Do they need firepower to do that? Should general manager Jason Licht go all in and make a trade? Should the Bucs begin their rebuild early and try to get rid of some veterans for extra capital?
Almost certainly not. There are a few reasons, but we'll start with the biggest one — Licht isn't really a big trader.
He's only made one in-season trade during his entire tenure as Bucs GM, and that was when he gave the New York Jets a sixth-round pick in exchange for defensive tackle Steve McLendon in 2020. He's also not a huge fan of giving high value — the most he's ever exchanged for a player is a third-round pick when he traded for edge rusher Jason Pierre-Paul in 2018.
On the flip side, Licht has a bit more recent history dealing aging players to get capital, but never during the season — he flipped cornerback Carlton Davis to the Detroit Lions in 2024 before the season started to get a third-round pick back from them.
The Bucs have a few aging veterans on the team, but they tend to like all of them. Some options, like wideout Chris Godwin Jr., have a contract far greater than their ability, so other teams probably wouldn't bite on a trade for any of Tampa Bay's mainstays.
The Bucs also went into this season believing they were competitive, and even at a 0-4 start, they likely still believe that. The Bucs will try and turn things around from a disastrous start, and with that in mind, they're very likely to stay put at the trade deadline and try to make things work with the talent they have — and they aren't in the mindset of rebuilding.
The Bucs will try plenty of things over the next few weeks to try and get things going in Tampa Bay. Just don't expect trades to be one of them.

title: Why Todd Bowles Was Crouched In Pain After Buccaneers Sealed the Win
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers pulled off the improbable.
They went on the road as a 0-4 team in primetime with an undrafted rookie quarterback and won against one of the best offenses in the league, the Dallas Cowboys.
It was a thrilling game for the Bucs, who had to fight to the very end to make sure they were able to get their first win.
Once the Bucs sealed the victory with an interception by Alex Anzalone, head coach Todd Bowles could be seen kneeling down in some pain. That caused many to show concern, but we now know exactly what occurred and that Bowles will be okay.
According to ESPN's Jenna Laine, Bowles confirmed that it wasn't anything serious and that he just caught a helmet to the gut that caused him to go down to one knee.
I’m told that Todd Bowles is OK. Several of you asked. I was concerned as well. I’m not in Dallas but just heard back. He said he caught a celebration helmet to the gut but says he’ll be OK. That’s why he was crouched over like this. pic.twitter.com/cDwSSsAETj
For a moment, those who have been critical of Bowles forgot about the football side of things and hoped that he didn't suffer some type of medical emergency.
It's great to get some clarity on the situation, even though we knew Bowles was okay since he spoke with the media following the game.
Bowles coached his tail off in the matchup, showing signs of what this team could be if it all comes together.
The offense did what it was supposed to do by running the ball for a whopping 241 yards. And the defense, while still struggling to get pressure, was able to play CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens tight. The defense also showed up big time by winning the turnover battle with two interceptions and a fumble recovery on special teams.
While the win is big for how the team moves forward, it's impossible to ignore that they did this against one of the worst defenses in the league.
The road ahead doesn't get much easier for the Bucs, but if they are able to carry over this type of play and confidence as a team, they could find themselves right back in the mix of the NFC South.
The Bucs now have over a week until their next game, when they return home to Raymond James Stadium to face off against Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers.

title: Buccaneers Rookie Quarterback Makes NFL History With Cowboys Win
full_text:
It took awhile, but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers finally have their first win of the season.
The Bucs defeated the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 on Thursday Night Football to move to 1-4 on the year. They did it with undrafted free agent Jalon Daniels under center, who is filling in for QB Baker Mayfield as Mayfield recovers from a dislocated thumb he suffered against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3.
Daniels played well against the Cowboys, completing 76% of his passes for 178 yards and a touchdown. But he also made history when he beat Dallas at AT&T Stadium, and it's a record that will never be broken.
Per FOX Sports' Greg Auman, Daniels is the only quarterback outside of the NFL's strike year in 1987 to ever defeat the Dallas Cowboys in a regular season football game.
Tampa Bay’s Jalon Daniels is the first undrafted rookie QB ever to beat the Cowboys, aside from a strike game with replacement players in 1987.
That stat makes sense — UDFA rookies rarely ever start football games anyway. Daniels is the first UDFA rookie to start for a team before Week 4 since the 1970 NFL-AFL merger. There have been just 10 UDFA rookie quarterbacks to start a game since 2013 — of those 10, one of them was Kendall Hinton, a wide receiver who had to play emergency QB.
Daniels has done a decent job filling in for Mayfield so far. Daniels has thrown two touchdowns and three interceptions on 55 attempts for 337 yards, and on top of that, he's rushed for  87 yards on 16 carries.
Daniels is set to start another game two Sundays from now against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 6. With Mayfield already looking to come back from his dislocated thumb, Daniels will likely have one more week to show his worth and cement himself as Tampa Bay's backup for the foreseeable future when the Steelers come to Tampa Bay.
The Bucs and Daniels will play the Steelers on Oct. 18. The Bucs have alternated wins and losses against the Steelers since 2002, so maybe Daniels will help continue that trend two Sundays from now.

title: Buccaneers Reveal Who They're Planning to Start at Quarterback vs. Steelers
full_text:
It took a while, but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers officially got their first win on Thursday night.
Tampa Bay bested the Cowboys 24-16 to move to 1-4 on the year. There's still a lot of work to do and things to clean up, but Tampa Bay ran the ball exceptionally well and the defense showed up in a big way to help secure the victory.
The first win of the season didn't come with starting quarterback Baker Mayfield, though. It came with backup quarterback Jalon Daniels under center, who executed the offense well and took care of the football to help Tampa Bay win. Daniels is now 1-1 as a starter in Tampa Bay — but with a long week off and the Pittsburgh Steelers coming two Sundays from now, will he get to play a third game?
Head coach Todd Bowles spoke to media on Friday after the win, and he revealed who the Bucs are planning to go with against the Steelers — for now.
Bowles confirmed to the media that while he still needs to see what Mayfield looks like and how he can grip the football after the stitches in his thumb were removed, he's planning on going with Daniels against the Steelers at the moment.
"Right now, we plan on starting Jalon Daniels against the Steelers," Bowles said.
Todd Bowles says that he’ll see what Baker Mayfield looks like when he comes in and how he’s able to grip the ball, but the team is planning on starting Jalon Daniels again against the Steelers
Starting two games and appearing at the end of one, Daniels has thrown two touchdowns and three interceptions on 55 attempts for 337 yards. Daniels has also been a significant threat on the ground, already amassing 87 yards on 16 carries.
Despite Daniels being the plan for Week 6, it will be interesting to see if Mayfield begins to practice or has an outside shot at playing against Pittsburgh. Mayfield has been campaigning to play the game, per NFL insider James Palmer, and if the medical staff thinks he can grip the football well enough, Bowles may be faced with the decision to rest Mayfield or to let him get back in after the team has gotten its first win of the season.
Coach Baker Mayfield could return to player Baker Mayfield next week against the Steelers. I'm told Mayfield is pushing to play but it's 10 days out and it's too early for the Bucs to know medically if he can go. The stitches were taken out Monday and it's a matter of his thumb…
Mayfield has started three games for Tampa Bay and has thrown for 615 yards on 96 attempts with two touchdowns and two interceptions.
The Bucs have the rest of the week off before preparing for the Steelers, who they'll play on Oct. 18. That's plenty of time for Mayfield to recover, but it's also plenty of time for the Bucs to continue game planning with Daniels and the skill set he has as he goes into what is currently set to be his third NFL start.

title: Cam Ward Beats David Carr, Tim Couch and Other Busts for Worst Record in First 22 Starts in NFL History
full_text:
After Sunday's 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans , QB Cam Ward has the fewest wins across 22 starts of any NFL quarterback to begin their career.
In Ward's rookie campaign, he led the Titans to a 3-14 record. The last time Ward guided Tennessee to a win was in December against the Kansas City Chiefs without QB Patrick Mahomes, since the Titans have lost seven straight with Ward at the helm, including a 0-5 start, to begin the 2026 season.
In Sunday's blowout loss to Houston, Titans fans poured boos over the field and held up signs showing their frustrations .
Although football is the ultimate team sport, in recent years, a quarterback's win-loss record has become just as much a position stat as ERA is to pitchers in baseball. Whether or not the blame should fall on the shoulders of the 24-year-old quarterback, the numbers contextualize how medicore Ward's career has been.
Let's take a look at the short list of losing NFL quarterbacks who have started their careers with more wins than Ward.
Former University of Kentucky great, QB Tim Couch, like Ward, was drafted number one in the 1999 NFL Draft to the newly expanded Cleveland Browns.
In 1996, the Browns moved to Baltimore, becoming the Baltimore Ravens. After three years of no football in northern Ohio, the Cleveland Browns were reinstated as an expansion franchise.
Couch made his first career start in Week 2 against the newly rebranded Tennessee Titans; the Browns lost 9-26. Cleveland would only win two games in Couch's rough rookie season, one less than Ward's rookie campaign.
In his sophomore season, Couch led the Browns to a 2-1 start before going on a four-game losing streak. A broken thumb sidelined Couch for missing the remainder of the season.
In 2001, Couch made his 22nd start and lost, going 4-18 in that stretch, earning one more than Ward to begin his career.
Unfortunately, Coach would retire at the age of 26 due to major injuries. He finished his career with the Browns, going 22-37 as a starter, throwing 67 interceptions to 64 touchdowns.
Today, Couch is remembered as the beginning of the Browns' carousel of quarterbacks .
Drafted sixth overall by the Cincinnati Bengals, QB David Klingler was a standout at the University of Houston. The Bengals selected Klingler to be the successor to franchise legend QB Boomer Esaison.
After a rocky start of 4-7, Cincinnati benched Esaison in favor of Klingler. The rookie struggled, losing his first three starts before finally earning his first and only win as a rookie.
The Bengals traded Esaison to the New York Jets, and Klingler was named the full-time starter, but he continued to underperform. In his first 22 starts, he only earned four wins, which is one more win than Ward.
Klingler was benched for good in 1994 after going 0-7 to start the season. Over the next three seasons, Klingler only appeared in five games as a backup.
He finished his career with a 4-20 record, throwing 22 interceptions and 16 touchdowns.
The Houston Texans selected QB David Carr first overall in the 2002 NFL Draft. The Texans were given the first pick because they were an expansion team, bringing football back to Houston since the Oilers left in 1996 for Tennessee.
Similar to Ward, Carr was named the day-one starter as the number one pick. In his NFL debut, Carr steered the newly formed Texans to a 19-10 victory over in-state opponent the Dallas Cowboys.
Carr ended his rookie season with a 4-12 record, earning one more win than Ward despite finishing the season without a touchdown over the final six games. In 2003, Carr made his 22nd start in his sophomore season and lost, finishing with a 6-16 record in that span.
Carr continued to quarterback the Texans for the next several seasons with little success. He made his final start in 2007 as a member of the Carolina Panthers before spending four years as a backup.
In 2012, Carr retired a Super Bowl champion as a backup for Eli Manning. Carr finished his career with a 23-56 record as a starter, throwing 71 interceptions to 65 touchdowns as a pro.
Carr holds an NFL record for the most sacks taken in a single season with 76 , which came in his rookie season.
Coming out of Washington State, QB Ryan Leaf was considered worthy of the first overall pick in the 1998 NFL Draft over Hall of Famer Peyton Manning. Ultimately, the Colts chose Manning, and Leaf was selected second to the San Diego Chargers.
In 1998, Leaf was a Week 1 starter, like Ward. He won his first two starts over the Bills and Titans before getting benched in Week 10 due to a sour performance against the Broncos.
Leaf would appear in one more game in Week 15 as a backup; he finished his rookie season 3-9 as a starter.
Over the next two seasons, Leaf would only make nine more starts before flaming out with the Dallas Cowboys in 2001. Although Leaf was one start shy of 22 career starts, he still earned one more win than Ward.
Across his three seasons as a pro, Leaf went 4-17 as a starter and had a horrendous 14-36 touchdown-to-interception ratio. He was out of the NFL by the age of 25.
Today, Leaf is widely regarded as one of the biggest busts in recent NFL history.
